records.title: CALGB 9344 (INT 0148)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2003
records.body: Women with operable node-positive breast cancer after lumpectomy or mastectomy with axillary sampling and negative margins; systemic therapy began within 84 days, and breast radiotherapy was required after lumpectomy. The HER2 correlative report used 1,322 obtained specimens from 1,500 randomly selected participants; other parent-protocol criteria were not filed Cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² + doxorubicin 60, 75 or 90 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks ×4, then paclitaxel 175 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks ×4 or observation; factorial 3×2 comparison (about 3 vs 6 months of chemotherapy) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, toxicity Escalating doxorubicin above 60 mg/m² did not improve DFS or OS and increased long-term cardiotoxicity; adding paclitaxel reduced recurrence (HR 0.83, P=.0023) and death (HR 0.82, P=.0064). Receptor-status and HER2 companion findings were unplanned or correlative and are not treatment-selection proof.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2003;21:976-983   N Engl J Med 2007;357:1496-1506 HER2 predictive companion analysis 17928597

records.title: CALGB 9741
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2003
records.body: Women with completely resected T0-3 N1-2 M0 primary breast adenocarcinoma after lumpectomy plus axillary dissection or modified radical mastectomy, with negative invasive margins and no non-axillary metastases; chemotherapy began within 84 days. Normal bilirubin, ECG/chest radiograph and per-cycle blood-count thresholds were required; age and performance-status criteria were not stated Dose-dense AC → paclitaxel (Q2W with G-CSF) vs conventional Q3W scheduling, in a 2×2 also comparing sequential (doxorubicin → paclitaxel → cyclophosphamide) vs concurrent (AC → paclitaxel); adjuvant Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, toxicity Dose-dense treatment improved DFS (RR 0.74, P=.010; 4-year DFS 82% vs 75%) and OS (RR 0.69, P=.013), with no sequence effect or density-by-sequence interaction. This first report had 36 months' median follow-up and only 315 of 515 expected events, so the survival estimate was not fully mature.

records.title: NSABP B-28
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2005
records.body: Resected operable invasive breast adenocarcinoma, cT1-3 cN0-1 cM0, confined to breast/ipsilateral axilla with at least one pathologically positive axillary node; lumpectomy with free margins plus axillary dissection or modified radical mastectomy. Randomisation within 63 days of diagnosis, adequate marrow/hepatic/renal function and 10-year non-cancer life expectancy were required; prior breast cancer/DCIS or prior therapy for this cancer were excluded Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² IV + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV Q3W ×4, followed by paclitaxel 225 mg/m² IV over 3 hours Q3W ×4, vs AC alone; adjuvant, node-positive Primary: disease-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: recurrence-free interval Adding paclitaxel after AC improved DFS (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72–0.95, P=.006; 5-year DFS 76% vs 72%) but not OS (RR 0.93, 95% CI 0.78–1.12, P=.46). There was no evidence that hormone-receptor subgroup effects differed (DFS interaction P=.30); they should not be used as predictive evidence.

records.title: ECOG E1199
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2008
records.body: Women with operable breast adenocarcinoma, no distant metastases, T1-3 N1-2 or high-risk T2-3 N0 disease. Reported ineligibility included margin <1 mm, fewer than six nodes removed, T4/N3 or pre-registration metastases. Other protocol criteria were in an unfiled supplement; 26 of 102 ineligibility reasons were unspecified After AC ×4: paclitaxel vs docetaxel, each given weekly vs every 3 weeks (2×2 taxane type × schedule); adjuvant Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety The factorial main effects of taxane type and schedule on DFS were null, and a taxane-by-schedule interaction complicated interpretation. Weekly paclitaxel improved DFS and OS vs paclitaxel Q3W; docetaxel Q3W improved DFS only. The eligible efficacy population was 4,950 of 5,052 enrolled patients.

records.title: US Oncology 9735
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2006
records.body: Women aged 18-75 with completely excised stage I-III invasive breast cancer, tumour >=1.0 and <7.0 cm, Karnofsky score >=80 and no metastatic disease; no neoadjuvant chemotherapy or prior chemotherapy/hormonal therapy for this cancer. Baseline marrow, hepatic and renal thresholds applied; pregnancy/lactation, serious infection and significant comorbidity were excluded TC ×4 (docetaxel 75 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²) vs AC ×4 (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²), each IV Q3W; adjuvant Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety At 7 years, TC improved DFS versus AC (81% vs 75%; HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.56–0.98, P=.033) and OS (87% vs 82%; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.50–0.97, P=.032). The comparator was 4 cycles of AC, so this trial does not establish TC against contemporary anthracycline–taxane regimens.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2006;24:5381-5387   J Clin Oncol 2009;27:1177-1183 7-yr OS update 19204201

records.title: ABC trials (USOR 06-090, NSABP B-46-I/USOR 07132, NSABP B-49; NRG Oncology)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · III · 2017
records.body: Women with resected HER2-negative high-risk early breast cancer: pT1-3 node-positive (including pN1mi), or pN0 with ER/PgR-negative disease, tumour >2.0 cm, or T1c ER/PgR-positive grade 3 or elevated Oncotype DX recurrence score; metastatic disease, T4 or supraclavicular nodes excluded TC6 (docetaxel 75 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² q21d × 6 cycles) vs TaxAC regimens × 6 cycles (TAC6: docetaxel 75, doxorubicin 50, cyclophosphamide 500 mg/m² q21d; or AC q3w×4 → weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m² ×12; or dose-dense AC q2w×4 → weekly paclitaxel 80 mg/m² ×12 or paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q2w×4) Primary: Invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: Recurrence-free interval, Disease-free survival–DCIS, Overall survival, Toxicity At 6.9 years median follow-up, noninferiority of TC6 to TaxAC was not demonstrated for IDFS: ITT HR 1.14 (80% CI 1.04–1.25), upper boundary exceeding the prespecified 1.18 inferiority threshold; 5-year IDFS 85.1% (TC6) vs 86.7% (TaxAC). RFI favoured TaxAC (HR 1.38, 95% CI 1.16–1.65; P = .0003; 5-year RFI 88.2% vs 91.0%), with significant heterogeneity by hormone receptor status (P = .02) favouring TaxAC in receptor-negative disease (RFI HR 1.90, IDFS HR 1.30). OS did not differ (HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.87–1.26; P = .64; 5-year OS 91.8% vs 92.4%). TaxAC reduced recurrences as first events (P = .0012) but increased leukemias (P = .03) and non-breast-cancer deaths (P = .003), suggesting recurrence reductions were offset by late leukemias and unrelated deaths.
records.keywords: Blum et al. J Clin Oncol 2017;35:2647-2655   Geyer et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;42:1344-1349  38335467

records.title: EBCTCG chemohormonal therapy 15-year overview
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · N/A · 2005
records.body: Women with early breast cancer in 194 unconfounded randomised adjuvant trials begun by 1995 of >1 month chemotherapy (single-agent, poly-, anthracycline vs CMF, longer vs shorter), tamoxifen (any duration vs none) or ovarian ablation/suppression (age <50) vs none; few women ≥70 entered chemotherapy trials; no taxanes, trastuzumab, raloxifene or modern aromatase inhibitors About 6 months anthracycline-based polychemotherapy (FAC or FEC) or 6–12 months CMF vs no adjuvant chemotherapy or each other; about 5 years vs 1–2 years vs no tamoxifen; ovarian ablation (surgery/irradiation) or LHRHI suppression vs none in women <50 Primary: First recurrence (at any site). Secondary: Breast cancer mortality, Overall mortality, Cause-specific mortality before recurrence, Second cancer incidence In this meta-analysis of 194 randomised trials, about 6 months of anthracycline-based polychemotherapy reduced the annual breast cancer death rate by about 38% (SE 5) below age 50 and 20% (SE 4) at age 50–69, largely irrespective of ER status, nodal status or tamoxifen use, and was more effective than CMF (breast cancer mortality 2p<0.00001). In ER-positive disease, about 5 years of tamoxifen reduced annual breast cancer mortality by 31% (SE 3), with 5 years significantly better than 1–2 years (2p=0.01); 10 vs 5 years remained uninformative. Ovarian ablation/suppression reduced recurrence (2p<0.00001) and breast cancer mortality (2p=0.004), appearing effective mainly without other systemic therapy. Fatal toxicity was small: anthracycline excess heart/leukaemia deaths and tamoxifen uterine-cancer/pulmonary-embolus deaths each ~0.2% over 6–8 years
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group. Lancet 2005;365:1687-1717

records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis of polychemotherapy regimens
records.subtitle: General Principles · Chemotherapy backbone — anthracycline/taxane regimens & dose-density · N/A · 2012
records.body: Women with early breast cancer in 123 randomised adjuvant trials begun 1973–2003, comparing taxane-based vs non-taxane regimens, anthracycline-based regimens vs CMF or each other, higher vs lower anthracycline dose, or polychemotherapy vs none; trials of stem-cell rescue or dose-density-only variation excluded Meta-analysis, not a two-arm trial: taxane-plus-anthracycline-based regimens vs the same or more non-taxane chemotherapy; anthracycline-based regimens (standard 4AC: 4 cycles A60 C600 iv 3-weekly; higher-dose CAF/CEF) vs standard/near-standard CMF (6 cycles C300x14 M40x2 F500x2 4-weekly) or no chemotherapy Recurrence, distant recurrence, breast-cancer mortality, overall mortality, acute mortality, acute-myeloid-leukaemia mortality, cardiac mortality In unconfounded trials adding four separate taxane cycles to a fixed anthracycline-based control regimen, breast cancer mortality was reduced (RR 0·86, SE 0·04, 2p=0·0005); 8-year breast cancer mortality 21·1% taxane vs 23·9% control. When four extra taxane cycles were counterbalanced by roughly doubling non-taxane chemotherapy in controls, there was no significant difference (RR 0·94, SE 0·06, 2p=0·33). Standard 4AC and standard CMF were equivalent (RR 0·98, SE 0·05, 2p=0·67), but higher-cumulative-dose regimens (CAF/CEF) beat CMF (RR 0·78, SE 0·06, 2p=0·0004); these cross-regimen comparisons are indirect. The 'about one-third' mortality reduction is an indirect product (0·775×0·825=0·64), not a head-to-head estimate. Excess AML and cardiac mortality (cardiac RR 1·56, 2p=0·02) noted; taxane trial follow-up beyond year 8 was limited
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group. Lancet 2012;379:432-444

records.title: NSABP B-18 & B-27
records.subtitle: General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · III · 2008
records.body: B-18: operable palpable T1-3 N0-1 M0 breast cancer. B-27: women with primary operable T1c-3 N0-1 M0 or T1-3 N1 M0 breast cancer. Diagnosis was by core biopsy or fine-needle aspiration; written consent was required. Other trial-specific inclusion/exclusion criteria were in prior reports and were not reproduced in the bound publication B-18: preoperative vs postoperative AC ×4 (doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m², Q3W). B-27: preoperative AC ×4 then surgery, ± docetaxel 100 mg/m² Q3W ×4 given either before surgery (neoadjuvant) or after (adjuvant); tamoxifen 20 mg/d ×5 years in all Overall survival, disease-free survival, relapse-free interval, response rate, pathological complete response rate, breast-conserving surgery rate, first failure Giving the same AC before rather than after surgery did not improve long-term DFS or OS in B-18 but increased breast conservation. In B-27, adding preoperative docetaxel doubled pCR (13% to 26%, P<.001) without improving DFS (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.78–1.08, P=.29). pCR was prognostic for individual patients, but these trials did not validate it as a trial-level surrogate.

records.title: EBCTCG neoadjuvant meta-analysis
records.subtitle: General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · N/A · 2018
records.body: Randomized operable early-breast-cancer trials begun before 2005 comparing chemotherapy started preoperatively with the identical regimen started after surgery; trials with different postoperative chemotherapy, including B-27, were excluded. IPD covered 10 of 16 eligible trials. Trial-level stage, exclusions, laboratory criteria and the appendix were not filed Neoadjuvant chemotherapy vs identical adjuvant chemotherapy Response, breast-conserving therapy, local recurrence, distant recurrence, breast-cancer mortality, overall mortality Compared with the identical adjuvant regimen, neoadjuvant chemotherapy increased breast-conserving therapy (65% vs 49%) and 15-year local recurrence (21.4% vs 15.9%; RR 1.37, P=.0001). Distant recurrence, breast-cancer mortality and all-cause mortality did not differ. The trials largely predated taxanes and trastuzumab.

records.title: CTNeoBC pooled analysis
records.subtitle: General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · N/A · 2014
records.body: 2014 pool: neoadjuvant studies with >=200 primary-breast-cancer patients, surgery after chemotherapy, pCR/EFS/OS data and >=3 years median follow-up; postoperative-treatment patients, HER2-negative NOAH and patients never starting treatment were excluded. 2023 HER2-positive reanalysis required randomized anti-HER2 neoadjuvant trials with >=100 patients and the same outcomes/follow-up; trial-level criteria were not filed Neoadjuvant chemotherapy ± trastuzumab (pCR vs no pCR; patient- & trial-level analysis) Pathological complete response rate, event-free survival, overall survival Across 12 neoadjuvant trials, pCR in breast and nodes was strongly associated with better patient-level EFS and OS, especially in TNBC and HER2-positive/HR-negative disease. Treatment-induced pCR differences did not predict treatment effects on EFS or OS at trial level; the HER2-positive re-analysis likewise showed strong patient-level associations but weak trial-level R², so pCR was not validated as a trial-level surrogate.
records.keywords: Lancet 2014;384:164-172   J Clin Oncol 2023;41:2988-2997 HER2+ re-evaluation 36977286

records.title: Residual Cancer Burden (Symmans)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Neoadjuvant therapy — timing & pathological response · N/A · 2017
records.body: Five institutional cohorts of primary breast cancer treated with neoadjuvant chemotherapy and surgery, spanning TNBC, HR-positive/HER2-negative and HER2-positive disease. Exclusions included prior invasive cancer, diagnostic excision before therapy, <75% of planned chemotherapy, additional/adjuvant systemic therapy beyond endocrine/HER2 therapy, inflammatory or stage IV disease, incomplete treatment, or unresectability; cohort-specific criteria were not stated Residual Cancer Burden index after NACT (RCB-0/pCR, RCB-I, RCB-II, RCB-III) Primary: relapse-free survival. Secondary: distant relapse-free survival, overall survival Residual Cancer Burden graded prognosis after neoadjuvant chemotherapy, but its relationship with 10-year RFS varied by phenotype. It was independently prognostic in TNBC and trastuzumab-treated HER2-positive disease, while HR-positive/HER2-negative class rates were non-monotonic and chemotherapy-only HER2-positive RCB-II and RCB-III rates did not separate.

records.title: SUPREMO (MRC/EORTC BIG 2-04)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Adjuvant radiation therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Unifocal stage II intermediate-risk breast cancer after mastectomy, axillary surgery and systemic therapy; defined as pT1N1, pT2N1, or pT3N0 (2010 amendment) or pT2N0 with grade 3, lymphovascular invasion or both, minimum clear margin 1 mm; neoadjuvant chemotherapy allowed after 2010 amendment Postmastectomy chest-wall irradiation 40 Gy/15 fractions to 50 Gy/25 fractions vs no chest-wall irradiation; both with recommended anthracycline-based (± taxane) chemotherapy, trastuzumab per local policy, and ≥5 years endocrine therapy for ER-positive disease Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Chest-wall recurrence, Regional recurrence, Disease-free survival, Distant metastasis-free survival, Cause of death, Short-term radiation-related adverse events, Long-term radiation-related adverse events, Quality of life, Cost-effectiveness Chest-wall irradiation did not improve overall survival after mastectomy in intermediate-risk early breast cancer: 10-year OS 81.4% vs 81.9%, HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.82–1.30, P=0.80); median follow-up 9.6 years. Chest-wall recurrence rare (1.1% vs 2.5%, HR 0.45, 95% CI 0.20–0.99); DFS and DMFS did not differ. Exploratory subgroup: worse OS with irradiation in triple-negative disease (HR 1.91, 95% CI 1.06–3.46). Toxicity mild; grade ≥2 lung events 13 vs 5; cardiac death ≤1% both arms. 5-year QOL (UK substudy, 947 baseline responders): chest wall symptoms modestly worse with irradiation (effect estimate 1.99, 95% CI 0.36–3.62, p=0.017), improving over years 1–5; clinically meaningful worsening at 5 years 13% vs 9%; no significant differences in other QOL domains. Exploratory subgroup: worse chest wall symptoms after SLNB plus axillary clearance with irradiation (difference –5.29, 95% CI –8.53 to –2.05, p=0.0015).
records.keywords: Kunkler et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393:1771-1783   Velikova et al. Lancet Oncol 2026;27:959-72  42508432

records.title: EBCTCG regional node radiotherapy individual patient data meta-analysis
records.subtitle: General Principles · Adjuvant radiation therapy · N/A · 2023
records.body: Women with early breast cancer in randomised trials (or laterality-based allocation in the DBCG study) of regional node radiotherapy versus none; trials began before Jan 1, 2009; surgery, breast/chest-wall radiotherapy and systemic therapy had to be identical between groups Regional node radiotherapy (internal mammary chain, supraclavicular fossa, or axilla, alone or in any combination) vs no regional node radiotherapy, both on a background of identical breast/chest-wall radiotherapy, surgery and systemic therapy; DBCG study allocated internal mammary chain irradiation by tumour laterality (right-sided irradiated, left-sided not) Primary: Recurrence at any site, Breast cancer mortality, Non-breast-cancer mortality, All-cause mortality. Secondary: Distant recurrence, Locoregional recurrence, Heart disease mortality, Contralateral breast cancer incidence, Second cancer incidence, Lymphoedema Regional node radiotherapy significantly reduced breast cancer mortality and all-cause mortality in trials done after the 1980s, but not in older trials. In the eight newer trials (12 167 patients, 1989–2008): recurrence RR 0·88 (95% CI 0·81–0·95), breast cancer mortality RR 0·87 (0·80–0·94), all-cause mortality RR 0·90 (0·84–0·96), with no significant effect on non-breast-cancer mortality (0·97, 0·84–1·11). Estimated 15-year absolute breast cancer mortality reductions: 1·6% node-negative, 2·7% with one to three positive nodes, 4·5% with four or more. In the eight older trials (2157 patients, 1961–78), non-breast-cancer mortality was significantly increased (RR 1·42, 1·18–1·71), risk mainly after year 20, with net increase in all-cause mortality (1·17, 1·04–1·31). Axillary radiotherapy lymphoedema in MA.20: 8·3% vs 4·5%
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group et al. Lancet 2023;402:1991-2003

records.title: EBCTCG overview of local therapy trials (radiotherapy and extent of surgery in early breast cancer)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Adjuvant radiation therapy · 2005
records.body: Early breast cancer; women in unconfounded randomised trials of local therapy beginning by 1995 (radiotherapy vs no radiotherapy, more vs less surgery, or more surgery vs radiotherapy); only trials with no planned difference in systemic therapy between groups; sentinel-node-biopsy studies not available Pooled randomised comparisons, not one regimen: radiotherapy vs no radiotherapy with the same surgery (post-BCS, generally breast only, or post-mastectomy to chest wall and regional nodes) vs more vs less surgery with the same radiotherapy vs more surgery vs less surgery plus radiotherapy; systemic therapy, where given, identical in both arms Isolated local recurrence, Breast cancer mortality, Overall mortality, Incidence of second primary cancers, Non-breast-cancer mortality In these trials, local treatments that substantially reduce locoregional recurrence would, absent other causes of death, avoid about one breast cancer death over 15 years for every four local recurrences avoided and should reduce 15-year overall mortality (EBCTCG conclusion). Among 25,000 women in comparisons cutting 5-year local recurrence risk by >10%, 5-year recurrence was 7% vs 26% and 15-year breast cancer mortality 44.6% vs 49.5% (absolute reduction 5.0%, SE 0.8, 2p<0.00001). Post-BCS radiotherapy: 15-year breast cancer mortality 30.5% vs 35.9% (reduction 5.4%, SE 1.7); post-mastectomy radiotherapy in node-positive disease: 54.7% vs 60.1% (reduction 5.4%, SE 1.3). Radiotherapy increased contralateral breast cancer (rate ratio 1.18) and mortality from heart disease (1.27) and lung cancer (1.78), mainly in older regimens.
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group. Lancet 2005;366:2087-2106

records.title: NSABP B-51 / RTOG 1304
records.subtitle: General Principles · Adjuvant radiation therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Breast cancer, clinical stage T1–T3, N1 (biopsy-proven movable ipsilateral level I–II axillary nodes), M0, operable; ypN0 in all removed nodes after ≥8 weeks of anthracycline- and/or taxane-based neoadjuvant chemotherapy (anti-HER2 therapy required for HER2-positive tumors unless contraindicated); axillary staging by sentinel-node biopsy (≥2 nodes) or dissection Regional nodal irradiation: 50 Gy in 25 fractions to retained level I–III axillary, supraclavicular and internal mammary nodes (first 3–4 intercostal spaces) plus chest wall (post-mastectomy) or whole breast (post-lumpectomy) vs no regional nodal irradiation: no irradiation after mastectomy or whole-breast 50 Gy in 25 fractions plus boosts of 12–14 Gy in 6–7 fractions after lumpectomy; assigned after neoadjuvant chemotherapy and ypN0 surgery Primary: Invasive breast cancer recurrence-free interval. Secondary: Locoregional recurrence-free interval, Distant recurrence-free interval, Disease-free survival, Overall survival, Safety Adjuvant regional nodal irradiation did not decrease the risk of invasive breast cancer recurrence or death from breast cancer in patients with negative axillary nodes after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. In the intention-to-treat primary-event analysis of 1556 patients (median follow-up 59.5 months), 5-year invasive breast cancer recurrence-free interval was 92.7% with RNI vs 91.8% without (HR 0.88; 95% CI 0.60–1.28; P=0.51); a prespecified time-driven final analysis included 109 events (50 vs 59) versus the 172 planned. No benefit in locoregional recurrence-free interval (HR 0.57), distant recurrence-free interval (HR 1.00), disease-free survival (HR 1.06) or overall survival (HR 1.12; 5-year 93.6% vs 94.0%). No deaths related to protocol-specified therapy and no unexpected adverse events; grade 3 events 10.0% vs 6.5% (radiation dermatitis 5.7% vs 3.3%); grade 4 events 0.5% vs 0.1%
records.keywords: Mamounas et al. N Engl J Med 2025;392:2113-24

records.title: EBCTCG adjuvant bisphosphonate meta-analysis
records.subtitle: General Principles · Bone-targeted adjuvant therapy (bisphosphonates) · N/A · 2015
records.body: Early breast cancer; adjuvant setting; women in unconfounded randomised trials begun before 2008 comparing a bisphosphonate of any type, dose and schedule vs no-bisphosphonate control (open label or placebo), all other treatments similar; menopausal status (postmenopausal natural or induced by LHRH analogue or oophorectomy) a prespecified primary subgroup; ongoing trials and trials without recorded recurrence contributed no outcome data Adjuvant bisphosphonate of any type, dose and schedule (clodronate or aminobisphosphonates: zoledronic acid, ibandronate, pamidronate, risedronate; mean scheduled duration 3.4 years, 97% of women in trials of 2–5 years) vs no bisphosphonate (open-label or placebo control) Primary: any recurrence, distant recurrence, breast cancer mortality. Secondary: all-cause mortality, death without recurrence, bone recurrence as first distant recurrence, other first (extraskeletal) distant recurrence, locoregional recurrence as first event, contralateral new primary breast cancer as first event, any bone fractures Adjuvant bisphosphonates reduced bone recurrence and improved breast cancer survival, but definite benefit was confined to women postmenopausal when treatment began. Overall, bone recurrence fell (RR 0.83, 95% CI 0.73–0.94; 10-yr 7.8% vs 9.0%); coprimary reductions were not significant for any recurrence (RR 0.94, 0.87–1.01; 2p=0.08) and borderline for distant recurrence (0.92, 0.85–0.99) and breast cancer mortality (0.91, 0.83–0.99). Among 11767 postmenopausal women, breast cancer mortality RR 0.82 (0.73–0.93; 10-yr 14.7% vs 18.0%) and bone recurrence RR 0.72 (0.60–0.86); premenopausal women showed no apparent effect, although heterogeneity by menopausal status was barely significant (2p=0.06 for trend). There was no significant effect on extra-osseous distant recurrence, locoregional recurrence, contralateral breast cancer or non-breast cancer mortality. Fractures were reduced (RR 0.85, 0.75–0.97; data from 71% of women); osteonecrosis of the jaw could not be assessed.
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group (EBCTCG). Lancet 2015;386:1353-1361

records.title: SUBITO
records.subtitle: General Principles · High-dose chemotherapy & autologous stem-cell transplant · III · 2026
records.body: Stage IIIA-C, HER2-negative breast cancer with homologous recombination deficiency (germline BRCA1/2 mutation or HRD tumour testing), newly diagnosed, age 18-66 (Netherlands + France) Intensified alkylating chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell rescue (dose-dense AC then high-dose cyclophosphamide–thiotepa–carboplatin + ASCT) vs standard-of-care (dose-dense AC then carboplatin–paclitaxel) followed by adjuvant olaparib ×1 year Primary: overall survival. Secondary: recurrence-free survival, pathological complete response rate, toxicity, quality of life, cost-effectiveness Intensified chemotherapy with autologous stem-cell rescue did not improve 4-year OS, RFS or pCR versus chemotherapy plus olaparib in this small HRD stage III trial. The null superiority result is not equivalence, and intensified treatment markedly increased grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia, febrile neutropenia and serious adverse events; olaparib's independent contribution was not tested.

records.title: SENOMAC
records.subtitle: General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · III · 2024
records.body: Clinically node-negative T1–3 breast cancer with 1–2 sentinel-node macrometastases (>2 mm); mastectomy or BCS; ~89% received nodal radiotherapy Completion axillary-lymph-node dissection vs sentinel-node biopsy only (omission of completion ALND); adjuvant systemic therapy and radiotherapy per national guidelines Primary: overall survival. Secondary: recurrence-free survival, breast-cancer-specific survival, arm morbidity, quality of life Omitting axillary dissection was non-inferior for 5-year recurrence-free survival in the 2024 publication (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.66–1.19; margin 1.44). The primary overall-survival endpoint matured only in the 2026 conference abstract (HR 0.84, 0.64–1.12), so publication and abstract maturity should remain distinct; omission improved arm symptoms and function.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2024;390:1163-1175  38598571 J Clin Oncol 2026;44(suppl):LBA503 (ASCO 2026 abstract) overall survival & arm morbidity

records.title: ACOSOG Z0011 (Alliance)
records.subtitle: General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · III · 2011
records.body: Clinical T1-T2 breast cancer, no palpable adenopathy, 1-2 positive sentinel nodes, lumpectomy + whole-breast irradiation Randomised after a positive sentinel node to sentinel lymph node dissection (SLND) alone (no further axillary surgery) vs completion axillary lymph node dissection (ALND, levels I–II). Both arms received breast-conserving surgery, whole-breast tangential-field radiotherapy, and adjuvant systemic therapy (chemotherapy and/or endocrine therapy) at the treating team's discretion; no protocol-specified systemic regimen or dose Primary: overall survival, surgical morbidity. Secondary: disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival, locoregional recurrence Sentinel-node dissection alone was non-inferior to axillary dissection for 10-year OS (86.3% vs 83.6%; HR 0.85; upper confidence limit 1.16; margin 1.3). DFS and locoregional recurrence did not differ, but the trial closed early, accrued fewer deaths than planned and the completed-follow-up OS analysis was not prespecified.

records.title: AMAROS
records.subtitle: General Principles · Axillary management — surgical de-escalation · III · 2014
records.body: Clinically node-negative (no palpable lymphadenopathy) T1–2 primary invasive breast cancer (initially unifocal ≤3 cm; amended Feb 2008 to include ≤5 cm and/or multifocal) with a tumour-positive sentinel node; ~82% breast-conserving surgery, ~18% mastectomy; 34 centres, 9 European countries; enrolled 2001–2010. Median follow-up 6.1 years (IQR 4.1–8.0) in sentinel-node-positive patients. EORTC 10981-22023; NCT00014612 Randomised before sentinel-node biopsy to axillary lymph-node dissection (levels I–II, ≥10 nodes) within 12 weeks vs axillary radiotherapy (levels I–III plus medial supraclavicular fossa; 25 × 2 Gy) starting within 12 weeks; allocated treatment delivered only if the sentinel node was positive. Breast surgery and adjuvant systemic therapy were given in both arms Primary: axillary recurrence. Secondary: axillary recurrence-free survival, disease-free survival, overall survival, shoulder mobility, lymphoedema, quality of life Axillary radiotherapy and dissection produced very low 5-year axillary-recurrence rates, but formal non-inferiority of radiotherapy was not established because the confidence interval crossed the HR margin. DFS and OS did not differ; radiotherapy caused substantially less clinical lymphoedema at 1, 3 and 5 years.

records.title: CALOR
records.subtitle: General Principles · ISOLATED locoregional recurrence · III · 2014
records.body: Women with a histologically confirmed, completely excised first isolated locoregional recurrence after unilateral breast cancer treated by mastectomy or lumpectomy; no distant metastases, available recurrence hormone-receptor status and fitness for chemotherapy; prior adjuvant chemotherapy was allowed Physician-selected adjuvant chemotherapy (at least 2 cytotoxic drugs for 3-6 months recommended) vs No chemotherapy; endocrine therapy for HR-positive recurrence, radiotherapy as indicated and optional HER2-directed therapy in both arms Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Sites of first recurrence, Second non-breast malignancies, Causes of death without breast cancer relapse, Serious adverse events Adjuvant chemotherapy improved DFS after complete excision of isolated locoregional recurrence: 5-year DFS 69% vs 57% (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.35-0.99) at 4.9 years median follow-up. DFS HRs were 0.32 (95% CI 0.14-0.73) for ER-negative recurrence and 0.94 (0.47-1.89) for ER-positive recurrence; these prespecified subgroup analyses were exploratory (nominal interaction P=0.046), and ER-positive benefit remains uncertain. Five-year OS was 88% vs 76% (HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.19-0.89), a secondary analysis without multiplicity control. Accrual stopped early at 162 of 265 planned patients. Serious adverse events occurred in 12/81 (15%) chemotherapy recipients; routine adverse events were not collected.

records.title: MINDACT (EORTC 10041/BIG 3-04)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · III · 2016
records.body: Primary invasive early-stage breast cancer (stage T1, T2 or operable T3); initially node-negative, amended August 2009 to allow up to three positive axillary nodes; women aged 18-70; genomic risk by 70-gene signature (MammaPrint) and clinical risk by modified Adjuvant! Online Discordant clinical/genomic-risk patients randomized to adjuvant chemotherapy vs no chemotherapy, based on use of either clinical risk or genomic risk to direct the decision; concordant low-risk received no chemotherapy, concordant high-risk received chemotherapy; optional further randomizations: anthracycline-containing regimen vs docetaxel-capecitabine, and tamoxifen-letrozole vs letrozole only (regimen details in unfiled supplement) Primary: Survival without distant metastasis (5-year event-free rate). Secondary: Proportion receiving chemotherapy by clinical risk vs genomic risk, Overall survival, Disease-free survival The primary noninferiority objective was met: women at high clinical risk but low genomic risk who received no chemotherapy had 5-year survival without distant metastasis of 94.7% (95% CI 92.5-96.2), lower bound above the 92% noninferiority boundary (primary-test population, n=644; median follow-up 5.0 years). In the randomized ITT comparison in this discordant group, chemotherapy gave 95.9% vs 94.4% without (adjusted HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.50-1.21); the study was not powered to assess the statistical significance of these differences. Genomic-risk guidance would avoid chemotherapy in 46.2% of high-clinical-risk patients at a cost of a 5-year metastasis risk 1.5 percentage points higher; long-term follow-up is ongoing.
records.keywords: Cardoso et al. N Engl J Med 2016;375:717-29

records.title: TAILORx
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · III · 2018
records.body: Hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative, axillary node-negative breast cancer in women aged 18–75 meeting NCCN guidelines for recommendation or consideration of adjuvant chemotherapy; randomized stratum defined by 21-gene recurrence score 11–25; full inclusion/exclusion criteria in an unfiled supplement Recurrence score 11–25 randomized to endocrine therapy alone (median 5.4 years) vs chemotherapy followed by endocrine therapy; scores ≤10 assigned endocrine therapy only and ≥26 chemoendocrine therapy non-randomly; agent doses/schedules and durations per unfiled supplement (docetaxel–cyclophosphamide in 56% and anthracycline-containing regimens in 36% of chemotherapy-treated) Primary: Invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: Freedom from recurrence of breast cancer at a distant site, Freedom from recurrence of breast cancer at a distant or local-regional site, Overall survival In 6711 women with hormone-receptor-positive, HER2-negative, node-negative breast cancer and a midrange recurrence score of 11–25, endocrine therapy alone was noninferior to chemoendocrine therapy for invasive disease-free survival (HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.94–1.24), providing evidence that adjuvant chemotherapy was not beneficial in these patients. At 9 years: invasive DFS 83.3% vs 84.3%, freedom from distant recurrence 94.5% vs 95.0%, OS 93.9% vs 93.8%. Noninferiority testing used a null hypothesis of no difference with one-sided 10% type I error. Age/recurrence-score interactions were exploratory: some chemotherapy benefit in women ≤50 yr with scores 16–25 (9-yr distant recurrence percentage-point differences 1.6 for scores 16–20, 6.5 for 21–25), with similar OS and no demonstrated OS advantage
records.keywords: Sparano et al. N Engl J Med 2018;379:111-121

records.title: RxPONDER
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · III · 2021
records.body: HR-positive, HER2-negative, noninflammatory breast cancer, nodal stage N1 (one to three positive axillary nodes) without distant metastasis; adjuvant setting after primary surgery (sentinel-node biopsy or axillary-node dissection); 21-gene recurrence score 0–25 on primary tumor (score >25 ineligible); eligible for taxane- and/or anthracycline-containing chemotherapy; women at least 18 years old Randomized 1:1 to chemotherapy followed by endocrine therapy (chemoendocrine) vs endocrine therapy only (adjuvant); each participant followed for 15 years Primary: Invasive disease-free survival (effect of chemotherapy and its interaction with the recurrence score). Secondary: Distant relapse-free survival, Overall survival In N1, HR+/HER2− breast cancer with recurrence score 0–25, adjuvant chemotherapy did not significantly improve invasive disease-free survival overall (5-yr 92.2% vs 91.0%; HR 0.86, 95% CI 0.72–1.03; P=0.10), and the treatment-by-continuous-recurrence-score interaction was null (P=0.35). In prespecified analyses, menopausal status interacted with chemotherapy benefit (P=0.008): no iDFS benefit in postmenopausal women (HR 1.02; 95% CI 0.82–1.26) but benefit in premenopausal women (HR 0.60; 95% CI 0.43–0.83), including distant relapse-free survival (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.39–0.87); menopausal analyses require caution. Recurrence score remained independently prognostic (HR 1.05 per unit). Overall survival not mature at this interim analysis (median follow-up 5.3 yr); no safety results reported in this publication
records.keywords: Kalinsky et al. N Engl J Med 2021;385:2336-2347

records.title: Paik et al. (NSABP B-20 21-gene recurrence score chemotherapy-benefit analysis)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · N/A · 2006
records.body: Node-negative, ER-positive primary invasive breast cancer in parent NSABP B20, randomized to adjuvant tamoxifen ± CMF/MF; correlative cohort required an archived tumor block with ≥5% tumor, RNA ≥0.5 μg and adequate RT-PCR signal (651 of 2,299 clinically eligible assay-evaluable) Parent B20 randomization: tamoxifen ×5 years alone vs tamoxifen ×5 years plus CMF or MF chemotherapy (chemotherapy arms combined for this analysis); 21-gene recurrence score assayed on archived tumor Primary: Freedom from distant recurrence. Secondary: Freedom from any relapse, Overall survival In this retrospective correlative analysis of 651 assay-evaluable NSABP B20 patients, the 21-gene recurrence score (RS) predicted magnitude of chemotherapy benefit: interaction between chemotherapy and RS (continuous) was significant (P=.038). High-RS (≥31) tumors had large chemotherapy benefit (RR 0.26; 95% CI 0.13–0.53; 10-yr distant recurrence absolute decrease 27.6%, SE 8.0%); low-RS (<18) tumors had minimal if any benefit (RR 1.31; 95% CI 0.46–3.78); intermediate-RS benefit unclear (RR 0.61; 95% CI 0.24–1.59, clinically important benefit not excluded). This does not prospectively validate a treatment-selection rule; tamoxifen-arm samples had partly been used in assay development.
records.keywords: Paik et al. J Clin Oncol 2006;24:3726-3734

records.title: OPTIMA
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · III · 2026
records.body: High clinical-risk ER+/HER2- early breast cancer (0-9 involved nodes; 73% pN1; T>=30 mm if node-negative); women & men >=40 Standard chemotherapy → endocrine therapy (control) vs Prosigna (PAM50) ROR-directed: ROR >60 → chemo→ET, ROR <=60 → endocrine therapy alone; premenopausal ET included ovarian function suppression Primary: invasive breast-cancer-free survival In the bound ASCO 2026 abstract, Prosigna-directed treatment met the stated non-inferiority criterion for 5-year invasive breast-cancer-free survival, with 3.9 years' median follow-up and 280 events. The abstract-only, relatively immature result supports chemotherapy de-escalation in the tested population but does not establish long-term safety of omission.

records.title: ASTER 70s
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · III · 2025
records.body: Women aged 70 years and older with oestrogen receptor-positive (≥10% by immunohistochemistry) HER2-negative primary breast cancer or isolated local relapse after complete surgery, before any systemic treatment; adjuvant setting; GGI high-risk tumour on central RT-PCR testing required for randomisation; any tumour size, nodal status or medical history; neoadjuvant treatment not permitted Four cycles intravenously every 3 weeks of doxorubicin 60 mg/m², non-pegylated liposomal doxorubicin 60 mg/m² or docetaxel 75 mg/m², each combined with cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² with mandatory G-CSF primary prophylaxis against febrile neutropenia, followed by hormonotherapy (tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitor or sequence of the two) for 5 years, vs hormonotherapy alone for 5 years (1:1 randomisation) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival, breast-cancer-specific survival, safety, quality of life Adding adjuvant chemotherapy conferred no survival benefit in women aged 70 years and older with GGI high-risk ER-positive HER2-negative breast cancer (8-year OS 72·7% vs 68·3%; HR 0·83, 95% CI 0·63–1·11; stratified log-rank p=0·2100; median follow-up 7·8 years, ITT); no significant differences in invasive disease-free survival or breast cancer-specific survival and no differential subgroup effect. Grade ≥3 adverse events in 183 (34%) of 541 vs 52 (9%) of 548, including one treatment-related death with chemotherapy; time to definitive quality-of-life deterioration was shorter with chemotherapy. The wide CI does not prove equivalence nor exclude a smaller benefit

records.title: NCIC CTG MA.27
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Genomic assays & chemotherapy de-escalation · III · 2013
records.body: Hormone receptor–positive primary invasive breast cancer (histologically confirmed, adequately excised), postmenopausal (age ≥60, or 45–59 with menses ceased >12 months or postmenopausal FSH, or bilateral oophorectomy); adjuvant first-line, randomized >3 weeks and <3 months after chemotherapy completion; excluded prior tamoxifen, receptor-negative tumor, metachronous contralateral primary, or prior cancer except nonmelanoma skin/cervical carcinoma in situ Exemestane 25 mg daily vs anastrozole 1 mg daily, planned maximum 5 years in event-free patients or until unacceptable toxicity (open-label; early celecoxib factorial randomization discontinued) Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant disease-free survival, incidence of contralateral new primary breast cancer, clinical and laboratory safety, disease-specific survival Neither exemestane nor anastrozole was superior for breast cancer outcomes as 5-year initial adjuvant therapy by two-way test; exemestane should be considered another up-front option. 4-year EFS 91.0% on exemestane vs 91.2% on anastrozole (350 vs 343 events; stratified HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.87–1.18, P=.85) at median follow-up 4.1 years. OS similar (208 vs 224 deaths; HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.77–1.13, P=.46), as were distant disease–free and disease-specific survival. 31.6% discontinued treatment. Osteoporosis less frequent on exemestane (31% vs 35%; P=.001); atrial fibrillation more frequent (72 vs 46; P=.02); no treatment-related deaths. Fewer deaths in minority women on exemestane (HR 0.38) was exploratory and needs confirmation
records.keywords: Goss et al. J Clin Oncol 2013;31:1398-1404

records.title: MA.17 (NCIC CTG)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2003
records.body: Postmenopausal women with histologically confirmed primary breast cancer; ER- and/or PR-positive (10 fmol per milligram of protein or positive immunohistochemical/immunocytochemical result); disease-free after 4.5–6 years of adjuvant tamoxifen discontinued less than 3 months before enrollment; excluded prior or concurrent other cancer (except skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ) and concomitant hormone-replacement therapy or SERM Letrozole 2.5 mg orally daily for five years vs matching placebo (double-blind), after completion of adjuvant tamoxifen; treatment stopped for serious intercurrent illness, unacceptable toxic effects, recurrence, or patient request Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life, long-term safety Extended letrozole after about 5 years of tamoxifen significantly improved disease-free survival at the first interim analysis: 4-year DFS 93% vs 87% (HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.43–0.75; P=0.00008), with 75 vs 132 recurrences or new contralateral cancers; OS was not significant (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.48–1.21; P=0.25; 31 vs 42 deaths). The DSMC stopped the trial early at 2.4 years median follow-up, so this report establishes an early recurrence benefit rather than a mature survival effect, and leaves optimal treatment duration and long-term toxicity undefined. Low-grade hot flashes, arthritis, arthralgia and myalgia were more frequent with letrozole; new osteoporosis 5.8% vs 4.5% (P=0.07) with similar fracture rates; vaginal bleeding was less frequent
records.keywords: Goss et al. N Engl J Med 2003;349:1793-1802

records.title: NSABP B-33
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2008
records.body: Postmenopausal women with clinical T1-3 N0-1 M0 ER and/or PgR-positive invasive breast cancer, disease-free after tamoxifen for 57 to 66 months; randomized less than 180 days after tamoxifen completion Exemestane 25 mg/d orally for 5 years vs placebo for 5 years, after ~5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, relapse-free survival, bone mineral density, blood lipid profile, quality of life, safety Despite premature closure and substantial crossover, further endocrine therapy with exemestane resulted in 4-year DFS of 91% vs 89% (HR 0.68, P=.07), a non-statistically significant improvement, and improved relapse-free survival (4-year RFS 96% vs 94%; HR 0.44, P=.004); authors conclude exemestane may provide another extended adjuvant option after 5 years of tamoxifen. OS not significantly different (16 vs 13 deaths; too few for conclusions). Accrual stopped early (1,598 of 3,000 planned) and 44% of placebo patients crossed over after unblinding, truncating inference; exploratory nodal subgroup results do not define a predictive population. No treatment-related deaths; grade 3 toxicity 9% vs 6% (P=.03); MENQOL differences small and non-significant
records.keywords: Mamounas et al. J Clin Oncol 2008;26:1965-1971

records.title: BIG 1-98
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2005
records.body: Operable invasive breast cancer, adjuvant endocrine setting, in postmenopausal women with tumors positive for estrogen receptors, progesterone receptors, or both; primary surgery with clear margins required; excluded metastatic disease, previous or concurrent cancer (other than adequately treated noninvasive breast or cervical cancer or skin carcinoma within 5 years), and prior adjuvant antiestrogen therapy for at least 1 month Letrozole 2.5 mg daily ×5 years vs tamoxifen 20 mg daily ×5 years; sequential arms: letrozole ×2 years → tamoxifen ×3 years and tamoxifen ×2 years → letrozole ×3 years; this analysis compares letrozole-initial vs tamoxifen-initial groups (sequential arms censored at switch +30 days) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, systemic disease-free survival, safety, disease-free survival excluding second nonbreast cancers, time to recurrence, time to distant recurrence At long term follow up with a median of 12.6 years, initial letrozole vs tamoxifen showed continued, modest, slightly attenuated benefit; DFS HR 0.91 (95% CI 0.81-1.01; P=.08; core 25.8-month analysis HR 0.81, P=0.003). Distant recurrence-free interval HR 0.85 (0.72-1.005; P=.057); OS HR 0.89 (0.77-1.02; P=.087); breast cancer mortality HR 0.89 (0.74-1.07; P=.20). Contralateral breast cancer lower with letrozole years 0-5 (HR 0.62) and 5-10 (0.47), reversed beyond 10 (1.35; interaction P=.005). LTFU safety: no between-arm difference in MI, cerebrovascular events, osteoporosis or fractures; more thromboembolic and other cardiac events with letrozole. Letrozole→tamoxifen sequence approximated letrozole monotherapy (14-year DFS 35.5% vs 36.2%). Weighted ITT analyses; follow-up attenuated for ~30% of eligible patients; 25.2% of tamoxifen patients crossed over. Treatment-period safety (2005): more fractures (5.7% vs 4.0%) and grade 3-5 cardiac events (2.1% vs 1.1%) with letrozole
records.keywords: Breast International Group (BIG) 1-98 Collaborative Group. N Engl J Med 2005;353:2747-2757   Ruhstaller et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:105-114  30475668

records.title: ATAC
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2002
records.body: Postmenopausal women with operable early breast cancer eligible for 5 years of adjuvant endocrine therapy, randomized to anastrozole, tamoxifen, or their combination; the efficacy interpretation is concentrated in the hormone-receptor-positive subset; receptor-negative or unknown status allowed; excluded: metastatic disease, neoadjuvant chemotherapy, prior adjuvant or preventive hormonal therapy, previous breast cancer Anastrozole 1 mg/day plus tamoxifen placebo versus tamoxifen 20 mg/day plus anastrozole placebo versus the combination, each planned for 5 years or until recurrence; the combination arm was stopped after the first analysis Primary: disease-free survival, adverse events. Secondary: time to recurrence, distant recurrence, contralateral breast cancer, death after recurrence, death without recurrence, overall survival, fractures, serious adverse events At 10-yr median follow-up, anastrozole remained superior to tamoxifen: DFS HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.78–0.95) and time to recurrence HR 0.79 in HR-positive disease; contralateral breast cancer HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.45–0.85). Absolute recurrence difference widened from 2.7% at 5 yr to 4.3% at 10 yr and persisted after treatment (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.67–0.98), though smaller after 8 yr; OS did not differ (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.84–1.06). First analysis (median 33.3 mo): combination not better than tamoxifen (DFS HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.89–1.18) and worse than anastrozole. First-analysis safety: fewer endometrial cancers, vaginal bleeding/discharge, ischaemic cerebrovascular and VTE events with anastrozole, but more musculoskeletal disorders (27.8% vs 21.3%) and fractures (5.9% vs 3.7%; hip fractures not increased). At 10 yr, excess fractures were confined to active treatment (451 vs 351; after, 110 vs 112); treatment-related SAEs were fewer (223 vs 369)
records.keywords: Baum et al. Lancet 2002;359:2131-2139   Cuzick et al. Lancet Oncol 2010;11:1135-1141  21087898

records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis: adjuvant tamoxifen
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · N/A · 2011
records.body: Women with early breast cancer in unconfounded randomised trials of adjuvant tamoxifen versus no tamoxifen; ductal carcinoma in situ trials excluded; ER positive defined as ≥10 fmol/mg cytosol protein, lower values ER-poor/negative; principal efficacy analyses in ER-positive disease (n=10 645), median follow-up 13 years About 5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen vs no adjuvant tamoxifen; most trials exactly 5 years, four of 3 years, three trials re-randomising some women at year 2 or 5; daily doses tested 20, 30 or 40 mg Breast cancer recurrence, breast cancer mortality, all-cause (any) mortality, mortality by cause, second cancer incidence (contralateral breast, uterine cancer) 5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen roughly halved the recurrence rate during years 0–4 (RR 0·53 [SE 0·03]) and reduced it by a third during years 5–9 (RR 0·68), cutting 15-year recurrence by 13·2% and breast-cancer mortality by about a third throughout 15 years (overall RR 0·70; 0·71 years 0–4, 0·66 years 5–9, 0·68 years 10–14), with 15-year mortality gain 9·2% (24% vs 33% at year 15). RR was approximately independent of PR status, age, nodal status and chemotherapy. Benefit substantial even at ER 10–19 fmol/mg (RR 0·67); no effect in ER-poor disease (recurrence RR 0·97, 95% CI 0·88–1·07). Non-breast-cancer mortality little affected despite small absolute increases in thromboembolic and uterine cancer mortality (only in women older than 55); uterine cancer incidence RR 2·40; contralateral breast cancer reduced (15-year 6·5% vs 9·8%). About 80% compliance, ~18% stopping within 2 years, so full-compliance benefit would be somewhat greater
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group. Lancet 2011;378:771-784

records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis: aromatase inhibitor vs tamoxifen in postmenopausal women
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · N/A · 2015
records.body: Postmenopausal women with ER-positive early breast cancer receiving about 5 years of adjuvant endocrine therapy; individual patient data from nine randomised trials begun by 2005 comparing aromatase-inhibitor versus tamoxifen schedules; trials in premenopausal women with ovarian suppression not included 5 years of aromatase inhibitor vs 5 years of tamoxifen; 5 years of aromatase inhibitor vs 2–3 years of tamoxifen→aromatase inhibitor to year 5; 2–3 years of tamoxifen→aromatase inhibitor to year 5 vs 5 years of tamoxifen; additionally 5 years AI vs 2 years AI→tamoxifen to year 5 and 2 years AI→tamoxifen to year 5 vs 5 years tamoxifen (BIG 1-98) Primary: any recurrence of breast cancer, breast cancer mortality, death without recurrence, all-cause mortality. Secondary: second primary cancer incidence, site of second primary cancers, bone fracture Aromatase inhibitors reduce recurrence rates by about 30% (proportionately) versus tamoxifen while treatments differ, but not thereafter; 5 years of an aromatase inhibitor reduces 10-year breast cancer mortality by about 15% versus 5 years of tamoxifen (12·1% vs 14·2%; RR 0·85, 0·75–0·96), hence by about 40% versus no endocrine treatment — an indirect estimate (product of RRs, table). Aggregated across comparisons, breast cancer mortality RR 0·86 (0·80–0·94) and all-cause mortality RR 0·88 (0·82–0·94); RRs differed little by age, BMI, stage, grade, PR or HER2 status. Fewer endometrial cancers (10-year 0·4% vs 1·2%; RR 0·33) but more bone fractures (5-year 8·2% vs 5·5%; RR 1·42); non-breast-cancer mortality similar. Intention-to-treat analyses with tamoxifen-arm crossover understate AI superiority.
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group. Lancet 2015;386:1341-1352

records.title: ATLAS
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2013
records.body: Early breast cancer (all detected disease removable) in women clinically disease-free after about 5 years of adjuvant tamoxifen (median 5·0 years, IQR 4·8–5·2), still on tamoxifen or stopped within the past year; any local recurrence removed and no distant recurrence detected; no restrictions on age, surgery, histology, nodal or ER status, but main efficacy analyses restricted to ER-positive disease; contraindications to continuing tamoxifen precluded entry Continue adjuvant tamoxifen (Nolvadex 20 mg once daily) to 10 years, stopping only if a definite contraindication emerged, vs stop at 5 years (open control, no placebo) Primary: overall mortality. Secondary: recurrence, breast cancer mortality, endometrial cancer, pulmonary embolus, stroke, ischaemic heart disease, second cancer incidence Continuing tamoxifen to 10 years further reduced recurrence (RR 0·84, 95% CI 0·76–0·94; years 5–14: 21·4% vs 25·1%) and breast-cancer mortality (12·2% vs 15·0%; absolute reduction 2·8%), and reduced overall mortality (639 vs 722 deaths), with benefit emerging mainly after year 10 (breast-cancer mortality RR 0·71 ≥10 years vs 0·97 in years 5–9); no effect in ER-negative disease; cost of more endometrial cancer (years 5–14: 3·1% vs 1·6%; mortality 0·4% vs 0·2%) and pulmonary embolus (RR 1·87)

records.title: TEXT & SOFT
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2014
records.body: Premenopausal women with resected invasive early breast cancer with ≥10% estrogen receptor- and/or progesterone receptor-expressing cells by local determination; adjuvant endocrine therapy setting; SOFT enrolled no-chemotherapy patients within 12 weeks of definitive surgery and prior-chemotherapy patients within 8 months of final dose after documented premenopausal estradiol; TEXT randomized all within 12 weeks of surgery, chemotherapy concurrent with ovarian function suppression Exemestane 25 mg orally daily plus ovarian suppression (triptorelin 3.75 mg IM every 28 days; bilateral oophorectomy or ovarian irradiation allowed after at least 6 months of triptorelin) vs tamoxifen 20 mg orally daily plus ovarian suppression; protocol-assigned endocrine therapy for 5 years from randomization Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: time interval without breast cancer, time interval before a recurrence of breast cancer at a distant site, overall survival, quality of life, safety Exemestane + OFS reduced recurrence endpoints vs tamoxifen + OFS, with benefit persisting in the final analysis (16-year median follow-up, ITT 4,690): 15-year DFS 74.9% vs 71.3% (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.73–0.92, P<0.01) and DRFI 86.5% vs 83.9% (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71–0.97, P=0.02); primary 68-month analysis 5-year DFS 91.1% vs 87.3% (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.60–0.85). OS did not differ at 15 years (87.8% vs 87.0%, HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.80–1.11). In HER2-negative disease (secondary analysis) OS HR 0.89 (95% CI 0.74–1.06); authors conclude most women gain no long-term OS advantage but higher-risk subgroups may (age <40 OS +3.6%–3.8%; grade 3 OS +5.8%) — subgroup/exploratory. Grade 3/4 AEs 30.6% vs 29.4%; osteoporosis 13.2% vs 6.4%; no grade 5 events; deaths without breast/second cancer rare and not higher with exemestane.
records.keywords: Pagani et al. N Engl J Med 2014;371:107-118   Pagani et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:1376-1382  36521078 Francis et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37:1367-1385  42229584

records.title: SOFT
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2015
records.body: Premenopausal women with operable hormone-receptor-positive early breast cancer (ER or PR expressed in at least 10% of cells); women remaining premenopausal after (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy enrolled within 8 months of completing it once premenopausal estradiol confirmed, chemotherapy-naive women randomized within 12 weeks of surgery; prior mastectomy or breast-conserving surgery with axillary dissection or sentinel-node biopsy Tamoxifen 20 mg daily orally vs tamoxifen plus ovarian suppression vs exemestane 25 mg daily orally plus ovarian suppression, all for 5 years from randomization; ovarian suppression by triptorelin 3.75 mg intramuscularly every 28 days, bilateral oophorectomy, or ovarian irradiation Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: freedom from breast cancer, freedom from distant recurrence, overall survival, adverse events At 12 years (database lock May 2021), SOFT shows sustained significant DFS improvement with OFS added to tamoxifen (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.69-0.98; 12-yr DFS 71.9% tamoxifen, 76.1% tamoxifen+OFS, 79.0% exemestane+OFS); OS improved with tamoxifen+OFS (HR 0.78, 0.60-1.01; 86.8%, 89.0%, 89.4%), exemestane+OFS benefit emerging after year 5 (HR 0.80, 0.62-1.04); prior-chemotherapy HER2-negative 12-yr OS 78.8/81.1/84.4%. Benefit more apparent with higher baseline recurrence risk; no-chemotherapy cohort 12-yr OS exceeded 95% in all arms. Earlier cuts: at 5.6 years DFS not significant (5-yr 86.6% vs 84.7%; HR 0.83, 0.66-1.04); at 8 years DFS 83.2% vs 78.9% (HR 0.76, 0.62-0.93), OS 93.3% vs 91.5% (HR 0.67, 0.48-0.92). Women remaining premenopausal after chemotherapy: 5-yr freedom from breast cancer 82.5% vs 78.0%. SOFT/TEXT pooled: exemestane+OFS 8-yr DFS 86.8% vs 82.8% (HR 0.77), no OS difference. Grade >=3 AEs 31.3% vs 23.7%; osteoporosis (T score <-2.5) 5.8% vs 3.5% with OFS

records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis: extended adjuvant aromatase inhibitor therapy
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · N/A · 2025
records.body: Postmenopausal women with oestrogen receptor-positive early breast cancer, recurrence-free after completing at least 5 years of tamoxifen, aromatase inhibitor treatment, or tamoxifen then aromatase inhibitor; women with ER-negative/PR-positive or unknown ER tumours excluded, as were those not reaching landmark treatment divergence Further aromatase inhibitor treatment (letrozole, anastrozole or exemestane) for 2–3 years or 5 years vs no further adjuvant endocrine therapy (four trials placebo-controlled, eight open control) Primary: Recurrence of invasive breast cancer (local, distant, or new contralateral), Breast cancer mortality, Mortality from other causes, All-cause mortality. Secondary: Time to first distant recurrence, Bone fractures, Cardiovascular deaths, Site-specific second primary cancers Further AIT after at least 5 years of endocrine therapy reduced recurrence, including distant recurrence, but breast cancer mortality was reduced only non-significantly. Allocation to 5 further years of AIT after some previous AIT: any recurrence RR 0·71 (11·6% vs 15·2% years 5–15), distant recurrence RR 0·73 (6·6% vs 8·6%), breast cancer mortality RR 0·90 (4·4% vs 5·0%). Among 5710 women with 5 prior years of AIT (10 vs 5 years total; median follow-up 7·1 years): any recurrence 12·2% vs 15·4% (RR 0·74), distant recurrence 6·9% vs 8·8% (RR 0·75). Absolute recurrence reduction greater for node-positive (16·3% vs 20·1%) than node-negative (9·1% vs 11·8%). 5 further years increased 5-year fracture risk (4·6% vs 3·4%, RR 1·35). Non-adherence was widespread (39·0% AIT vs 37·6% placebo). Longer follow-up needed to assess mortality
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group. Lancet 2025;406:603-614

records.title: lidERA (BC)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2026
records.body: ER+/HER2- stage I-III early breast cancer after surgery +/- (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy Giredestrant 30 mg PO once daily vs standard-of-care endocrine therapy (anastrozole/letrozole/exemestane or tamoxifen) for 5 years; premenopausal pts on giredestrant or AI received an LHRH agonist Invasive disease-free survival, distant recurrence-free interval Giredestrant iDFS effects were directionally consistent in premenopausal and postmenopausal patients, with similar distant-recurrence-free trends. The linked ASCO 2026 menopausal-status subgroup abstract does not contain the full primary trial report and cannot establish the overall primary result or mature benefit–risk profile.

records.title: POSITIVE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · N/A · 2023
records.body: Women aged 42 years or younger with stage I, II, or III hormone receptor–positive breast cancer (receptor-positivity cutoff 1% or higher) who had received adjuvant endocrine therapy for 18–30 months and wished to temporarily discontinue it to attempt pregnancy; prior chemotherapy with or without fertility preservation allowed; no clinical evidence of recurrence (single-arm) temporary interruption of adjuvant endocrine therapy, discontinued within 1 month before enrollment with a 3-month washout before attempting pregnancy, for up to 2 years to allow conception, delivery and breast-feeding, then strongly recommended resumption to complete planned 5–10 years; assisted reproductive technology allowed; fertility assessment encouraged if no pregnancy after 1 year vs external control cohort of 1499 SOFT/TEXT patients (non-randomised, bootstrap-matched) Primary: Number of breast cancer events during follow-up. Secondary: Freedom from a breast cancer event, Freedom from distant recurrence, Ability to become pregnant, Pregnancy outcomes, Birth outcomes, Breast-feeding, Use of assisted reproductive technology, Resumption of endocrine therapy, Distant recurrences Temporary interruption of endocrine therapy to attempt pregnancy did not confer a greater short-term risk of breast cancer events than an external control cohort among select women with previous HR-positive early breast cancer. 44 events occurred over 1638 patient-years (median follow-up 41 months), within the prespecified safety threshold of 46; 3-year incidence 8.9% vs 9.2% in controls (bootstrap-matched difference −0.2 points; HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.57–1.15). Among 497 women followed, 74.0% had at least one pregnancy and 63.8% at least one live birth. Longer-term safety unresolved: median follow-up only 3.4 years vs protocol-specified 10-year follow-up.
records.keywords: Partridge et al. N Engl J Med 2023;388:1645-1656

records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis: aromatase inhibitors vs tamoxifen with ovarian suppression in early breast cancer
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · N/A · 2022
records.body: Premenopausal women with ER-positive operable early-stage breast cancer receiving ovarian suppression (goserelin or triptorelin) or ablation; ER positivity defined as expression in at least 1% of tumour cells by IHC (ABCSG XII: Reiner score ≥3); women with ER-negative, PR-positive tumours excluded Aromatase inhibitor (anastrozole in ABCSG XII, exemestane in SOFT and TEXT, letrozole in HOBOE) plus ovarian suppression (triptorelin or goserelin at licensed doses, or oophorectomy/ovarian irradiation in SOFT/TEXT) vs tamoxifen plus the same ovarian suppression; endocrine therapy for 5 years (SOFT, TEXT, HOBOE) or 3 years (ABCSG XII) Primary: any breast cancer recurrence, distant recurrence, breast cancer mortality, death without recurrence, all-cause mortality. Secondary: second primary cancer incidence, endometrial cancer, bone fracture With ovarian suppression, aromatase inhibitors reduced recurrence versus tamoxifen (RR 0.79; 5-year absolute risk 6.9% vs 10.1%; 10-year 14.7% vs 17.5%) and distant recurrence (RR 0.83), but did not reduce breast-cancer or all-cause mortality at a median 8.0 years' follow-up; longer follow-up is needed to assess mortality impact. Fractures were more frequent with aromatase inhibitors (227 [6.4%] of 3528 vs 180 [5.1%] of 3502); non-breast-cancer deaths and endometrial cancers were rare.
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group. Lancet Oncol 2022;23:382-392

records.title: MA.17R
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2016
records.body: Postmenopausal women with primary breast cancer, disease-free after 4.5–6 yr of adjuvant aromatase-inhibitor therapy (mostly preceded by tamoxifen), randomized within 2 yr of completing the AI; hormone-receptor-positive primary tumour required (unknown status only for MA.17 participants); ECOG performance status <3, minimum life expectancy ≥5 yr; no exclusion on age alone Extended letrozole 2.5 mg orally once daily × 5 yr vs placebo orally once daily × 5 yr; treatment discontinued for serious intercurrent illness, unacceptable toxic effects, disease recurrence or patient request Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, incidence of contralateral breast cancer, quality of life, long-term safety Extending adjuvant aromatase inhibitor to 10 years significantly improved disease-free survival and lowered contralateral breast cancer incidence vs placebo, but did not improve overall survival. At median follow-up 6.3 yr, 5-yr DFS 95% vs 91% (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.48–0.91); annual contralateral breast cancer incidence 0.21% vs 0.49% (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.22–0.81); 5-yr OS 93% vs 94% (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.73–1.28). Cost: bone fractures 14% vs 9%, new-onset osteoporosis 11% vs 6%, bone pain 18% vs 14%; no significant QoL differences on most subscales
records.keywords: Goss et al. N Engl J Med 2016;375:209-219

records.title: NRG Oncology/NSABP B-42
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2019
records.body: Postmenopausal women with hormone receptor-positive stage I-IIIA breast cancer, disease-free after 5 years of endocrine therapy with an aromatase inhibitor or tamoxifen for no more than 3 years followed by an AI; excluded history of nontraumatic osteoporotic fracture, bilateral breast cancer and other malignancies unless disease-free at least 5 years Letrozole 2.5 mg orally once daily for 5 years vs matching placebo orally once daily for 5 years; study drug discontinued for grade ≥1 stroke/TIA, grade ≥2 acute coronary syndrome or cerebrovascular ischaemia, grade ≥3 myocardial infarction or peripheral/visceral arterial ischaemia, or osteoporotic fracture with T score <−2.5 on osteoporosis therapy Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, breast cancer-free interval, distant recurrence, osteoporotic fracture, arterial thrombotic events, recurrence-free interval Primary endpoint was negative at the definitive analysis (median follow-up 6.9 yr): DFS HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73–0.999; p=0.048 vs alpha 0.0418; 7-yr DFS 84.7% letrozole vs 81.3% placebo. In the unplanned 10-yr update (median follow-up 10.3 yr; 940 DFS events) extended letrozole improved DFS (75.9% vs 72.6%; HR 0.85, 0.74–0.96; P=.01), breast cancer-free interval (HR 0.75, 0.62–0.91) and distant recurrence (HR 0.72, 0.55–0.92; benefit only between years 4 and 7.4). OS unchanged at 10 yr (86.1% vs 86.2%; HR 0.97, 0.82–1.15); at the definitive cut 7-yr OS was 92.3% vs 91.8% (HR 1.15, 0.92–1.44). Recurrence-free interval also favoured letrozole (HR 0.80, 0.64–0.99). Osteoporotic fractures and arterial thrombotic events did not differ at 10 yr; at the definitive cut arterial thrombotic events rose after 2.5 yr (HR 1.85, 1.18–2.88) and grade 3–5 toxicity was similar. Careful risk–benefit assessment is required before recommending extended letrozole.

records.title: IDEAL (Investigation on the Duration of Extended Adjuvant Letrozole treatment); BOOG 2006-05
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Postmenopausal women with early-stage hormone receptor-positive (ER- and/or PR-positive in ≥10% of nuclei) breast cancer who had completed five years (±3 months) of any adjuvant endocrine therapy no longer than two years before randomisation; disease-free at randomisation, WHO performance status 0 or 1 Extended adjuvant letrozole 2.5 mg once daily for 2.5 years vs letrozole 2.5 mg once daily for 5 years, after 5 years of prior adjuvant endocrine therapy; 1:1 randomization, open label Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, distant metastasis-free interval, new primary breast cancer, safety Extending letrozole from 2.5 to 5 years after 5 years of prior endocrine therapy did not improve DFS (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.74–1.16; median follow-up 6.6 years), OS (HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.78–1.38) or distant metastasis-free interval (HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.78–1.45). Second primary breast cancer, a secondary endpoint, was less frequent with 5 years (1.1% vs 3.1%; HR 0.39), and preplanned subgroups showed no benefiting subgroup. Grade 3–4 events comprised 10.0% vs 8.8% of adverse events; 23.5% vs 17.3% discontinued for toxicity.
records.keywords: Blok et al. J Natl Cancer Inst 2018;110:40-48

records.title: ABCSG-16 / SALSA
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2021
records.body: Postmenopausal women aged 80 years or younger with histologically verified invasive hormone-receptor-positive early breast cancer (stage I, II or III) without evidence of recurrence; all had received 5 years (±12 months) of adjuvant endocrine therapy with tamoxifen, an aromatase inhibitor, or both sequentially, completed up until 12 months before randomisation Anastrozole 1 mg orally once daily for 2 additional years (total 7 years) vs 5 additional years (total 10 years) after prior endocrine therapy; no dose modification, temporary interruption ≤3 months permitted Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, contralateral breast cancer, second primary cancer, clinical bone fracture Extending anastrozole from 2 to 5 additional years after 5 years of prior endocrine therapy did not improve DFS in the 3208 patients still on trial and disease-free at the 2-year landmark (73.9% vs 73.6%; HR 0.99) or OS (87.3% vs 87.5%; HR 1.02). Clinical fractures were more frequent with 5 years (6.3% vs 4.7%; HR 1.35); serious-adverse-event comparisons covered unequal exposure periods.
