records.title: EBCTCG meta-analysis: ovarian function suppression (OFS) in early breast cancer
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · N/A · 2026
records.body: Premenopausal women younger than 55 years with ER-positive or ER-unknown early breast cancer randomised to OFS vs no OFS in 23 trials recruiting 1948–2014; where menopausal status was unavailable, assumed premenopausal if trial eligibility required it (only younger than 50 years if unrestricted); women aged 55 or older, postmenopausal or ER-negative excluded OFS by ovarian ablation (surgery or irradiation) or pharmacological GnRHa (mostly 2–5 years) vs no OFS; other adjuvant therapy the same in both arms (none, chemotherapy, or 2–5 years of tamoxifen, or both) Primary: Invasive breast cancer recurrence, Breast cancer mortality, Other mortality, All-cause mortality For premenopausal women with ER-positive early breast cancer, even if chemotherapy or tamoxifen are given, OFS significantly reduces the 15-year risk of recurrence and death. Across 23 randomised trials (15 075 women), OFS reduced recurrence (RR 0·82, 95% CI 0·77–0·87; 15-year risk 36·5% vs 41·9%) and breast cancer mortality (RR 0·86, 0·80–0·93; 15-year risk 31·3% vs 34·4%). Benefit was larger with confirmed than unconfirmed premenopausal status after chemotherapy (heterogeneity p=0·0004); with unconfirmed status there was little apparent effect on breast cancer mortality (RR 0·96, 0·88–1·05). Adding OFS to tamoxifen reduced recurrence (RR 0·79, 0·70–0·91) but breast cancer mortality reduction was non-significant (RR 0·84, 0·69–1·02; p=0·080). Women younger than 45 years on tamoxifen had lower distant recurrence (RR 0·77, 0·64–0·93), breast cancer (RR 0·74, 0·58–0·94) and all-cause (RR 0·72, 0·57–0·90; 10-year mortality 9·4% vs 12·2%) mortality. No increase in deaths without recurrence; OFS was consistently associated with more higher grade hot flushes, and patient-level toxicity data were not sought
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group. Lancet 2026;407:1699-1711

records.title: FATA-GIM3
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Postmenopausal women with histologically confirmed invasive, completely resected ER- or PR-positive (≥10% of cells or ≥10 fmol/mg) early breast cancer, any tumour size and nodal status; HER2-positive allowed if trastuzumab feasible; adjuvant/neoadjuvant setting; excluded recurrent or metastatic disease, prior tamoxifen, hormone replacement therapy, and other malignancy within 10 years Oral anastrozole 1 mg/day, exemestane 25 mg/day or letrozole 2·5 mg/day for 5 years (upfront) vs oral tamoxifen 20 mg/day for 2 years → assigned aromatase inhibitor for 3 years (switch); permanent discontinuation per investigator judgment, unacceptable toxicity, patient choice or recurrence Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, toxicity 5 years of aromatase inhibitor was not superior to 2 years of tamoxifen followed by 3 years of aromatase inhibitor, and no aromatase inhibitor was superior to the others in efficacy. At median follow-up 60 months, 5-year DFS 88.5% switch vs 89.8% upfront (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.73–1.08; p=0.23); 5-year OS 95.3% vs 96.8% (HR 0.72, 0.51–1.00; p=0.052). DFS by drug: anastrozole 90.0%, exemestane 88.0%, letrozole 89.4% (p=0.24); pairwise comparisons not done. Comparisons underpowered (power 0.59; fewer events than planned). No unexpected serious adverse reactions or treatment-related deaths; grade 3–4 musculoskeletal events 130 (7%) of 1761 switch vs 128 (7%) of 1766 upfront; grade 1 musculoskeletal events more frequent upfront (924 [52%] of 1766 vs 745 [42%] of 1761)
records.keywords: De Placido et al. Lancet Oncol 2018;19:474-485

records.title: FACE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · III · 2017
records.body: Postmenopausal women with HR-positive, node-positive early breast cancer (stage IIA to IIIC) within 12 weeks after breast surgery or completion of adjuvant chemotherapy; neoadjuvant chemotherapy or adjuvant trastuzumab allowed; excluded metastatic or inflammatory BC, contralateral BC, prior neoadjuvant endocrine or adjuvant antiestrogen therapy >1 month, and Child-Pugh C cirrhosis Adjuvant letrozole 2.5 mg orally once daily vs anastrozole 1 mg orally once daily, until disease recurrence/relapse or for a maximum of 5 years Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to distant metastases, distant disease-free survival, safety Letrozole did not demonstrate significantly superior efficacy or safety compared with anastrozole as adjuvant therapy in postmenopausal patients with HR-positive, node-positive eBC. 5-year DFS 84.9% letrozole vs 82.9% anastrozole (HR 0.93; 95% CI 0.80 to 1.07; P = .3150); 5-year OS 89.9% vs 89.2% (HR 0.98; 95% CI 0.82 to 1.17; P = .7916); exploratory analyses showed similar DFS across all subgroups, including obese patients. Trial terminated early (September 2014) for lower-than-expected DFS events; final analysis at 709 vs 959 planned events. Safety profiles similar; no new safety concerns; most common grade 3-4 AE arthralgia 3.9% vs 3.3%; AE-related discontinuation 15.1% vs 14.3%
records.keywords: Smith et al. J Clin Oncol 2017;35:1041-1048

records.title: ELPh (Exemestane and Letrozole Pharmacogenetics) trial
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant endocrine therapy · N/A · 2012
records.body: Postmenopausal women with stage 0 to III HR-positive breast cancer initiating adjuvant AI therapy; prior tamoxifen permitted but no prior AI allowed; all indicated surgery, chemotherapy and radiation completed before enrollment Exemestane 25 mg daily vs letrozole 2.5 mg daily, each for 2 years; after protocol amendment, patients with intolerable AI-associated symptoms discontinued and could cross over to the other AI after a 2- to 8-week washout Primary: persistence with the second AI medication. Secondary: discontinuation of initial AI therapy because of toxicity, discontinuation of initial AI therapy because of musculoskeletal toxicity, time to treatment discontinuation, change in HAQ and pain VAS scores Premature discontinuation of initial AI therapy because of symptoms is common, and more than one third of patients may tolerate a different AI. Of 503 enrolled women, 32.4% discontinued initial AI within 2 years because of adverse effects; 24.3% because of musculoskeletal symptoms. Median time to discontinuation for any symptom was 6.1 months, shorter with exemestane than letrozole (HR 1.5; 95% CI 1.1 to 2.1; P = .02). Younger age (HR 1.4) and taxane chemotherapy (HR 1.9) predicted discontinuation. Of 83 patients who switched AI, 38.6% continued the alternate AI for a median of 13.7 months. Descriptive exploratory analysis; cross-over was optional, so motivated patients may be over-represented, and no predictors of second-AI persistence were identified
records.keywords: Henry et al. J Clin Oncol 2012;30:936-942

records.title: monarchE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors · III · 2020
records.body: Adults with HR-positive/HER2-negative, node-positive, high-risk early breast cancer after surgery; cohort 1: ≥4 positive axillary nodes or 1-3 plus grade 3 disease and/or tumour ≥5 cm; cohort 2: 1-3 nodes, grade <3, tumour <5 cm and central Ki-67 ≥20%; node-negative, metastatic and, after amendment, inflammatory breast cancer were excluded, while chemotherapy and radiotherapy were optional Abemaciclib 150 mg orally twice daily for 2 years + physician’s choice of adjuvant endocrine therapy for 5-10 years vs endocrine therapy alone for 5-10 years Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: distant relapse-free survival, overall survival, invasive disease-free survival in Ki-67-high disease, quality of life, safety, pharmacokinetics Adding 2 years of abemaciclib to endocrine therapy improved the primary iDFS endpoint: at the 2020 preplanned interim analysis (median follow-up approximately 15.5 months), HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.60-0.93); 2-year iDFS 92.2% vs 88.7%. At the alpha-controlled primary OS analysis (median follow-up 6.3 years), OS improved: HR 0.842 (95% CI 0.722-0.981); 7-year OS 86.8% vs 85.0%. Updated 7-year iDFS 77.4% vs 70.9% (HR 0.734, 95% CI 0.657-0.820) and DRFS 80.0% vs 74.9% (HR 0.746, 95% CI 0.662-0.840), both descriptive. In the 2023 safety update (during treatment or ≤30 days after study-treatment discontinuation), grade ≥3 adverse events were 49.9% vs 16.9% and serious adverse events 15.5% vs 9.1%; grade 3-4 neutropenia was 19.6% vs 0.9% and diarrhoea 7.8% vs 0.2%; venous thromboembolic events occurred in 2.5% vs 0.7%. Long-term data showed no delayed toxicity. In the 2020 report, two deaths on treatment or within 30 days (diarrhoea, pneumonitis) were considered possibly treatment-related.
records.keywords: Johnston et al. J Clin Oncol 2020;38:3987-3998   Johnston et al. Lancet Oncol 2023;24:77-90  36493792 Johnston et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37:155-165  41110697

records.title: NATALEE
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors · III · 2024
records.body: Adults with HR-positive/HER2-negative AJCC stage II-III early breast cancer; stage III or IIB was eligible irrespective of nodal status; stage IIA required ≥1 positive node, or node-negative grade 3 disease, or node-negative grade 2 disease with Ki-67 ≥20% or high genomic risk (Oncotype DX score ≥26, or high-risk Prosigna/PAM50, MammaPrint or EndoPredict); prior endocrine therapy for ≤12 months was allowed Ribociclib 400 mg orally once daily on days 1-21 of 28-day cycles for 3 years + letrozole 2.5 mg/day or anastrozole 1 mg/day for 5 years vs the same endocrine therapy alone; men and premenopausal women received goserelin 3.6 mg every 28 days Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: distant disease-free survival, recurrence-free survival, distant recurrence-free survival, overall survival, safety, quality of life, pharmacokinetics Adding 3 years of ribociclib to a nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor improved iDFS, with benefit persisting beyond the 3-year treatment window at the prespecified 5-year follow-up. In this descriptive analysis (median follow-up 55.4 months), 5-year iDFS was 85.5% vs 81.0% (HR 0.716, 95% CI 0.618-0.829), an absolute difference of 4.5 percentage points (2.7 at 3 years); DDFS HR 0.709 (95% CI 0.608-0.827). Exploratory N0 subgroup: HR 0.606 (95% CI 0.372-0.986). OS remained immature and descriptive, a numerical trend only (HR 0.800, 95% CI 0.637-1.003; 137 vs 163 deaths). No new safety signals at 5 years; second primary malignancies 2.7% vs 3.0%. In the 2024 primary report’s 36-month safety window, grade ≥3 neutropenia was 43.8% vs 0.8%, grade 3-4 liver events 8.3% vs 1.5%, and 18.9% discontinued ribociclib because of adverse events.
records.keywords: Slamon et al. N Engl J Med 2024;390:1080-1091   Crown et al. ESMO Open 2025;10:105858  41320342

records.title: PALLAS
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors · III · 2021
records.body: Adults with completely resected stage II-III HR-positive/HER2-negative early breast cancer enrolled within 12 months of diagnosis and starting endocrine therapy within 6 months before randomisation; adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy was allowed. Palbociclib 125 mg orally once daily on days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle ×2 years + standard adjuvant endocrine therapy (tamoxifen or aromatase inhibitor ± LHRH agonist) for ≥5 years vs endocrine therapy alone for ≥5 years (open-label) Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival excluding second non-breast primaries, distant recurrence-free survival, locoregional recurrence-free survival, overall survival, safety, translational science, adherence, quality of life At the planned second interim analysis (67% of expected events; median follow-up 23.7 mo), adding 2 years of palbociclib to adjuvant endocrine therapy did not improve iDFS in stage II–III HR-positive/HER2-negative disease (3-year 88.2% vs 88.5%; HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.76–1.15). The futility boundary was crossed and palbociclib was discontinued; the authors state the regimen cannot be recommended in the adjuvant setting. Secondary analyses do not establish benefit: 3-year distant RFS 89.3% vs 90.7% (HR 1.00); OS immature; post-hoc subgroups, including high clinical risk, showed no benefit. 42% stopped palbociclib early, mainly for adverse events. Grade 3–4 neutropenia 61.3% vs 0.3%; febrile neutropenia 1.0% vs none; serious AEs 12.4% vs 7.6%; no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: PENELOPE-B
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- EBC · Adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitors · III · 2021
records.body: HR-positive/HER2-negative residual invasive breast cancer after taxane-containing neoadjuvant chemotherapy (>=16 weeks, including 6 weeks of a taxane), with high relapse risk by CPS-EG score (>=3, or 2 with ypN+ after amendment 3), no distant disease and surgery completed. Randomized treatment began after local therapy; excluded prior CDK4/6 inhibitor Palbociclib 125 mg orally once daily on days 1–21 of each 28-day cycle ×13 cycles (~1 year) + endocrine therapy vs placebo + endocrine therapy (standard endocrine therapy per investigator for ≥5 years in both arms) Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival excluding second non-breast primaries, distant disease-free survival, overall survival, locoregional relapse-free interval, safety, compliance One year of palbociclib added to endocrine therapy did not improve iDFS in high-risk residual HR-positive/HER2-negative disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy (stratified HR 0.93, 95% repeated CI 0.74–1.17; weighted P=.525; median follow-up 42.8 mo); 3-year iDFS 81.2% vs 77.7%. iDFS excluding second nonbreast primaries was similar (HR 0.93); LRRFI (HR 0.83) and interim OS (131 deaths; HR 0.87, P=.420; 3-year OS 93.6% vs 90.5%) did not differ significantly. Subgroup and secondary findings do not establish a benefiting population; a nominal LRRFI signal in NACT non-responders (n=200) had a negative interaction test. Grade 3–4 AEs 79.6% vs 20.1%, mainly neutropenia (70.0% vs 1.0%); dose reduction 47.6% vs 1.8%. Serious AEs 9.1% overall with no arm difference; eight fatal SAEs (two palbociclib, six placebo), both palbociclib deaths not related to study drug.
records.keywords: Loibl et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:1518-1530

records.title: PALOMA-2
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · First-line — CDK4/6 inhibitor + endocrine therapy · III · 2016
records.body: ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer in postmenopausal women; first-line, no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease; measurable disease per RECIST 1.1 or bone-only disease; prior (neo)adjuvant nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor allowed unless disease recurred during it or within 12 months after completing it; excluded advanced, symptomatic visceral spread at risk of short-term, life-threatening complications Palbociclib 125 mg orally daily, 3 weeks on/1 week off (4-week cycles) + letrozole 2.5 mg orally daily continuously vs matching placebo + letrozole 2.5 mg orally daily continuously; treatment until RECIST 1.1 progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, duration of response, clinical benefit response, patient-reported outcomes, pharmacokinetic effects, safety, tissue biomarker assessments Palbociclib plus letrozole significantly prolonged PFS vs letrozole alone in previously untreated ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, with higher myelotoxicity; final OS was not significantly improved. Investigator-assessed median PFS 24.8 vs 14.5 mo (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.46 to 0.72) at median follow-up of 23 mo; central review supportive (HR 0.65). ORR (all randomized) 42.1% vs 34.7% (P=0.06); clinical benefit response 84.9% vs 70.3%. Final OS (median follow-up 90.1 mo): 53.9 vs 51.2 mo (HR 0.96; 95% CI 0.78 to 1.18); unequal loss to follow-up (13.3% vs 21.2%) limited interpretation; with recovered data 53.8 vs 49.8 mo (HR 0.92). Time to subsequent chemotherapy 38.1 vs 29.8 mo (HR 0.73). Grade 3 or 4 neutropenia 66.4% vs 1.4%, leukopenia 24.8% vs 0%; febrile neutropenia 1.8% vs none; no evidence of cumulative toxicity. AE discontinuation 9.7% vs 5.9%; on-treatment deaths 10 (2.3%) vs 4 (1.8%); one placebo-arm death treatment related.

records.title: MONALEESA-2
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · First-line — CDK4/6 inhibitor + endocrine therapy · III · 2016
records.body: Postmenopausal women with breast cancer; recurrent or metastatic, no previous systemic therapy for advanced disease; locally confirmed HR-positive, HER2-negative; measurable disease (RECIST 1.1) or at least one predominantly lytic bone lesion; excluded prior CDK4/6 inhibitor, prior (neo)adjuvant nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitor unless disease-free interval >12 months, inflammatory breast cancer, CNS metastases, cardiac disease or dysfunction including QTcF >450 msec Ribociclib 600 mg/day orally, 3 weeks on/1 week off (28-day cycles) + letrozole 2.5 mg/day continuously vs placebo + letrozole; double-blind; until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or discontinuation Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, overall response rate, clinical benefit rate, safety, quality of life, time to first subsequent chemotherapy, chemotherapy-free survival At the preplanned interim analysis, adding ribociclib to letrozole as first-line therapy significantly prolonged PFS and increased overall response vs placebo plus letrozole, with more myelosuppression. Median PFS not reached vs 14.7 mo (HR 0.56; 95% CI 0.43–0.72), meeting the prespecified superiority boundary; blinded independent review HR 0.59 (95% CI 0.41–0.85). Updated analysis: median PFS 25.3 vs 16.0 mo (HR 0.57). ORR among patients with measurable disease 52.7% vs 37.1%. Final OS analysis (400 deaths; median follow-up 80 mo): OS significantly longer, median 63.9 vs 51.4 mo (HR 0.76; 95% CI 0.63–0.93); no new safety signals. Grade 3/4 neutropenia 59.3% vs 0.9%, leukopenia 21.0% vs 0.6%, ALT increase 9.3% vs 1.2%; febrile neutropenia 1.5% vs none; Four ribociclib patients met Hy's law criteria, all resolving after stopping ribociclib; QTcF >480 msec 3.3% vs 0.3%. One sudden death was considered ribociclib-related. Discontinuation for adverse events 7.5% vs 2.1%.

records.title: MONALEESA-7
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · First-line — CDK4/6 inhibitor + endocrine therapy · III · 2018
records.body: First-line pre/perimenopausal HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer; age 18–59; no prior endocrine therapy for advanced disease, up to one prior line of chemotherapy for advanced disease allowed; no prior CDK4/6 inhibitor; excluded inflammatory breast cancer, CNS metastases, symptomatic visceral disease, QTcF >450 ms Ribociclib 600 mg once daily 3 weeks on / 1 week off + endocrine therapy (tamoxifen 20 mg once daily or a non-steroidal aromatase inhibitor [letrozole 2.5 mg or anastrozole 1 mg once daily]) + goserelin 3.6 mg SC vs placebo + same endocrine therapy + goserelin; to progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival 2, objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, time to response, duration of response, time to chemotherapy, performance-status deterioration, quality of life, safety Ribociclib plus endocrine therapy improved PFS (23.8 vs 13.0 months; HR 0.55) in premenopausal or perimenopausal women. At the second interim OS analysis (median follow-up 34.6 months), OS was significantly longer (not reached vs 40.9 months; HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.54–0.95; 42-month OS 70.2% vs 46.0%). At the primary PFS analysis (median follow-up 19.2 months), PFS benefit was seen with both tamoxifen (HR 0.59) and NSAI (HR 0.57) partners; overall response was 41% vs 30%, and time to definitive QoL deterioration favoured ribociclib (HR 0.70). OS HR was 0.70 with NSAI and 0.79 (95% CI 0.45–1.38) with tamoxifen; exploratory PFS on second-line therapy HR 0.69. Grade 3/4 neutropenia occurred in 63.5% vs 4.5% at the OS cut; QTcF >480 ms in 7% vs 1%, and in the ribociclib group a QTcF increase >60 ms was more frequent with tamoxifen (16%) than with an NSAI (7%); no treatment-related deaths occurred.

records.title: MONALEESA-3
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · First-line — CDK4/6 inhibitor + endocrine therapy · III · 2018
records.body: First/second-line postmenopausal women or men with HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer; treatment naive (de novo or relapse >12 months after (neo)adjuvant endocrine therapy) or up to one line of endocrine therapy for advanced disease, including relapse on or within 12 months of (neo)adjuvant endocrine therapy; no prior chemotherapy for advanced disease, fulvestrant or CDK4/6 inhibitor; no inflammatory breast cancer or symptomatic visceral disease Ribociclib 600 mg once daily 3 weeks on / 1 week off + fulvestrant 500 mg IM (days 1, 15, 29, then monthly) vs placebo + fulvestrant 500 mg IM; to progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival 2, objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, time to chemotherapy, safety Ribociclib plus fulvestrant improved PFS (20.5 vs 12.8 months; HR 0.59) and, at the protocol-specified second interim analysis (final per protocol), significantly improved OS: median not reached vs 40.0 months; 42-month OS 57.8% vs 45.9%; HR 0.72. In exploratory subgroup analyses, PFS benefit was consistent in treatment-naive patients (HR 0.577) and after up to one line of endocrine therapy for advanced disease (HR 0.565). In a descriptive update, first-line median PFS was 33.6 vs 19.2 months. ORR in measurable disease was 40.9% vs 28.7%. Grade 3 neutropenia occurred in 46.6% vs 0% and grade 4 in 6.8% vs 0%; febrile neutropenia 1.0% vs 0%. QTcF >480 ms occurred in 5.6% vs 2.5%, with no torsades de pointes; grade 3 and 4 ALT elevation occurred in 6.6% and 1.9% with ribociclib, with two confirmed Hy's law cases. One death from acute respiratory distress syndrome was suspected to be treatment-related. No new safety signals emerged at the OS analysis.

records.title: MONARCH 3
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · First-line — CDK4/6 inhibitor + endocrine therapy · III · 2017
records.body: Advanced breast cancer (metastatic, or locoregionally recurrent not amenable to curative surgery/radiotherapy); postmenopausal women, no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease; HR-positive, HER2-negative; measurable or non-measurable bone-only disease, prior (neo)adjuvant endocrine therapy only if disease-free interval >12 months; excluded visceral crisis, lymphangitic spread, leptomeningeal carcinomatosis, inflammatory breast cancer, CNS metastases, prior everolimus or CDK4/6 inhibitor Abemaciclib 150 mg orally twice daily continuous + nonsteroidal AI (anastrozole 1 mg or letrozole 2.5 mg orally daily, physician's choice) in 28-day cycles vs matching placebo + nonsteroidal AI; until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, clinical benefit rate, safety, tolerability, overall survival, quality of life, pharmacokinetics, biomarker analyses, chemotherapy-free survival Abemaciclib plus a nonsteroidal AI significantly improved PFS and ORR vs the AI alone and was an effective initial treatment with a tolerable safety profile. At the prespecified interim analysis (194 PFS events; median follow-up 17.8 mo), investigator-assessed PFS HR was 0.54 (95% CI 0.41-0.72; P=.000021); at 8.1-yr median follow-up PFS HR 0.535 (nominal), median 29.0 vs 14.8 mo. ORR in measurable disease 59.2% vs 43.8% (P=.004); ITT clinical benefit rate 78.0% vs 71.5% (P=.101). Final OS (8.1 yr) was not statistically significant: median 66.8 vs 53.7 mo; HR 0.804 (95% CI 0.637-1.015); visceral subgroup HR 0.758, also non-significant. Exploratory chemotherapy-free survival 46.7 vs 30.6 mo. Interim grade 3 or 4 neutropenia 21.1% vs 1.2%, diarrhea 9.5% vs 1.2%; serious AEs 27.5% vs 14.9%; AE discontinuation 19.6% vs 2.5%; deaths from AEs on treatment or within 30 days 8 (2.4%) vs 2 (1.2%). At 8.1 yr: any-grade diarrhea 83.5%, VTE 7.6% vs 1.2%, ILD 7.0% vs 0.6%; no new safety signals.

records.title: RIGHT Choice
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · First-line — CDK4/6 inhibitor + endocrine therapy · II · 2024
records.body: Premenopausal women 18-59 with recurrent or metastatic breast cancer not amenable to curative therapy; first-line, no prior systemic therapy for ABC, adjuvant AI allowed if treatment-free interval >12 months; progesterone or estrogen (>10%) receptor-positive, HER2-; combination CT indicated for symptomatic visceral metastases, rapid progression/impending visceral compromise, or markedly symptomatic nonvisceral disease; excluded liver metastases with bilirubin >1.5x ULN or AST/ALT >5x ULN Ribociclib 600 mg orally once daily, 3 weeks on/1 week off + letrozole 2.5 mg or anastrozole 1 mg orally once daily + goserelin 3.6 mg subcutaneous implant on day 1 of each 28-day cycle vs investigator's choice of combination CT (docetaxel + capecitabine, paclitaxel + gemcitabine, or capecitabine + vinorelbine); treatment until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or discontinuation for any other reason Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: time to treatment failure, 3-month treatment failure rate, overall response rate, clinical benefit rate, time to response, overall survival, health-related quality of life, safety First-line ribociclib plus ET showed a significant PFS benefit, similar response rates and better tolerability vs combination CT in clinically aggressive HR+/HER2- ABC. Final analysis (median follow-up 37.0 mo; 132 events): median PFS 21.8 vs 12.8 mo; HR 0.61 (95% CI 0.43-0.87); one-sided P=.003. Median TTF 18.6 vs 9.1 mo (HR 0.50). Unconfirmed ORR 66.1% vs 61.8%; median TTR 4.9 vs 3.2 mo (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.55-1.06). The study was not powered for secondary endpoints; OS was immature (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.56-1.52). In exploratory subgroups, PFS benefit was smaller in visceral crisis and recurrent disease. The design was open-label. All-cause grade 3 or 4 AEs occurred in 79.5% vs 73.0%, including neutropenia in 59.8% vs 36.0%; grade ≥3 QTc prolongation in 1.8% (ribociclib) and grade ≥3 febrile neutropenia in 3.0% (CT only). Treatment-related AEs led to discontinuation in 6.3% vs 27.0%.

records.title: FALCON
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · First-line endocrine therapy — foundation · III · 2016
records.body: Postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer, endocrine therapy-naive; no prior hormonal therapy, one prior cytotoxic line allowed; life-threatening visceral disease excluded Fulvestrant 500 mg IM (two 5 mL injections) on days 0, 14 and 28, then every 28 days, with anastrozole placebo daily vs anastrozole 1 mg orally daily with fulvestrant placebo on the same schedule; both arms until progression or discontinuation criterion Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Objective response rate, Duration of response, Expected duration of response, Clinical benefit rate, Duration of clinical benefit, Expected duration of clinical benefit, Overall survival, Quality of life, Safety First-line fulvestrant 500 mg significantly improved investigator-assessed PFS versus anastrozole in the ITT population (HR 0.797, 95% CI 0.637–0.999, p=0.0486); median PFS 16.6 vs 13.8 months. ORR was similar in measurable disease (46% [89/193] vs 45% [88/196]). Interim OS was immature (median not reached; HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.63–1.22, p=0.4277). A prespecified exploratory non-visceral subgroup showed a larger PFS effect (HR 0.59; visceral interaction post hoc, p=0.0092), not supporting a predictive claim. Grade ≥3 AEs 22% (51/228) vs 18% (41/232); AE deaths 3% each arm, none attributed to treatment.

records.title: SONIA
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · CDK4/6-inhibitor sequencing & continuation · III · 2024
records.body: Women with HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer; first-line, no previous systemic therapy for advanced disease; HR+ defined as ER and/or PR expression >10%; any menopausal status (pre-/perimenopausal with LHRH agonist), prior (neo)adjuvant NSAI allowed unless recurrence during or ≤12 months after completing it, measurable or evaluable disease; excluded visceral disease requiring chemotherapy, symptomatic CNS metastases and prior CDK4/6i CDK4/6i-first: NSAI (letrozole or anastrozole) + CDK4/6i (palbociclib, ribociclib or abemaciclib; physician's choice) first-line → fulvestrant second-line vs CDK4/6i-second: NSAI first-line → fulvestrant + CDK4/6i second-line; switch to second line mandated within 28 days of RECIST progression on first line; all agents given per standard of care Primary: progression-free survival after two treatment lines (PFS2). Secondary: overall survival, PFS1, quality of life, toxicity, cost-effectiveness, objective response rate, biomarkers, pharmacokinetics, cognitive functioning, CDK4/6i treatment duration, CDK4/6i drug costs, chemotherapy-free survival, subsequent anticancer therapy At the primary analysis (median follow-up 37.3 mo), first-line CDK4/6i gave no statistically significant or clinically relevant PFS2 benefit over second-line use (31.0 vs 26.8 mo; HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.74–1.03); second-line non-inferiority was met against a possibly lenient 1.54 margin. At the prespecified update (median follow-up 58.5 mo), PFS2 was 31.9 vs 26.7 mo (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.71–0.94; P = .01). First-line use did not improve OS (47.9 vs 48.1 mo; HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.77–1.07) but increased treatment-related and financial toxicity. PFS1 favoured first-line use (24.7 vs 16.1 mo; HR 0.59); FACT-B quality of life did not differ. Post hoc, OS favoured first-line in premenopausal (HR 0.53) but not postmenopausal patients (HR 1.00; interaction P = .01). At the update, CDK4/6i exposure was 23.0 vs 8.5 mo and grade ≥3 AEs 3400 vs 2242 (≥1 in 86.4% vs 75.7%); earlier, serious AEs 299 vs 273 and €27,078 more drug cost per patient. Open-label; 91% palbociclib.

records.title: PALOMA-3
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · Second-line & beyond — CDK4/6 after endocrine progression · III · 2015
records.body: HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, any menopausal status; progression during or within 1 month after prior endocrine therapy for metastatic disease or within 12 months after adjuvant therapy (postmenopausal: aromatase inhibitor; pre/perimenopausal adjuvant: tamoxifen); one prior chemotherapy line for advanced disease allowed; excluded prior fulvestrant or everolimus, uncontrolled brain metastases, symptomatic visceral spread at risk of life-threatening complications Palbociclib 125 mg orally daily for 3 weeks, then 1 week off, + fulvestrant 500 mg IM every 14 days for the first three injections, then every 28 days vs matching placebo + fulvestrant; pre/perimenopausal patients also received goserelin every 28 days for the duration of study treatment; treatment until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, survival probability at 1, 2 and 3 years, objective response, duration of response, rate of clinical benefit, patient-reported outcomes (EQ-5D, EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-BR23), pharmacokinetics, safety, time to end of immediate subsequent therapy, time to chemotherapy Palbociclib plus fulvestrant prolonged PFS vs fulvestrant alone in HR-positive advanced breast cancer progressing on prior endocrine therapy, regardless of menopausal status; the primary endpoint was met at the preplanned interim analysis. Investigator-assessed median PFS 9.2 vs 3.8 mo (HR 0.42; 95% CI 0.32–0.56); blinded central audit consistent (HR 0.27). CBR 34.0% vs 19.0%; ORR 10.4% vs 6.3% (P=0.16). Final OS (median follow-up 44.8 mo) was not significant: 34.9 vs 28.0 mo (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.64–1.03); 16% of placebo patients later received a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Endocrine-sensitive subgroup OS 39.7 vs 29.7 mo (HR 0.72); intrinsic endocrine resistance HR 1.14 (interaction P=0.12). Global QoL (QLQ-C30) was maintained with palbociclib, deteriorated with placebo. Updated safety: grade 3/4 neutropenia 70% vs none, febrile neutropenia 1% vs none; primary analysis: leukopenia 25.2% vs 0.6%, serious thromboembolic events in 4 palbociclib patients (three pulmonary emboli), none with placebo.

records.title: MONARCH 2
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · Second-line & beyond — CDK4/6 after endocrine progression · III · 2017
records.body: Women with HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer (inoperable locally advanced or metastatic), any menopausal status (pre/perimenopausal with GnRH agonist); progression on neoadjuvant/adjuvant ET, ≤12 months after adjuvant ET, or on ET for advanced disease; no more than one ET and no chemotherapy for advanced disease; measurable or nonmeasurable bone-only disease; excluded prior fulvestrant, everolimus or CDK 4 and 6 inhibitors, visceral crisis, CNS metastasis Abemaciclib 150 mg orally twice daily, continuous (starting dose amended from 200 mg twice daily, with mandatory reduction to 150 mg for patients on 200 mg) + fulvestrant 500 mg IM on days 1 and 15 of cycle 1, then day 1 of each 28-day cycle vs placebo twice daily + fulvestrant (same schedule); until progression, death or withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, clinical benefit rate, safety, tolerability, overall survival, quality of life, pharmacokinetics, disease control rate, change in tumor size, chemotherapy-free survival Abemaciclib 150 mg twice daily plus fulvestrant significantly improved PFS and ORR vs placebo plus fulvestrant, with a tolerable safety profile, in HR+/HER2− ABC progressing on ET. Median investigator-assessed PFS 16.4 vs 9.3 mo (HR 0.553; 95% CI 0.449–0.681) at median follow-up 19.5 mo; blinded central review consistent (HR 0.460); final cut 16.9 vs 9.3 mo (HR 0.539). ORR 35.2% vs 16.1% (ITT) and 48.1% vs 21.3% in patients with measurable disease. Final OS confirmed benefit (80-mo median follow-up; post hoc after interim significance): 45.8 vs 37.3 mo (HR 0.784; 95% CI 0.644–0.955). Exploratory chemotherapy-free survival HR 0.674. Diarrhea 86.4% vs 24.7% (grade 3 13.4% vs 0.4%), typically in the first cycle; final cut 87.1% vs 27.8% (grade 3 14.5%), no new safety signals. Grade 3 neutropenia 23.6% vs 1.3%. AEs led to abemaciclib discontinuation in 15.9% vs 3.1% and dose reduction in 42.9% vs 1.3%. Three treatment-related deaths (0.7%) occurred with abemaciclib, two from sepsis.

records.title: postMONARCH
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · Second-line & beyond — CDK4/6 after endocrine progression · III · 2025
records.body: HR+, HER2− advanced breast cancer; radiologic progression on CDK4/6i plus aromatase inhibitor as initial therapy for advanced disease, or recurrence on/after adjuvant CDK4/6i plus ET (no restriction on interval after adjuvant CDK4/6i); no intervening systemic therapy after CDK4/6i progression; excluded: CDK4/6i in more than one setting, chemotherapy for metastatic disease, prior SERD (e.g. fulvestrant) or PI3K/mTOR/AKT inhibitor, visceral crisis, symptomatic/untreated CNS metastases Abemaciclib 150 mg orally twice daily + fulvestrant 500 mg IM on days 1 and 15 of cycle 1, then every 4 weeks vs matched placebo twice daily + fulvestrant (same schedule); GnRH analog for men and premenopausal women; until disease progression, death or discontinuation for other reasons Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, PFS by blinded independent central review, objective response rate, safety, clinical benefit rate, PFS by ctDNA biomarker status Abemaciclib plus fulvestrant significantly improved PFS after progression on prior CDK4/6i plus ET in HR+, HER2− ABC, although the absolute median gain was modest. Significance was reached at the prespecified interim analysis (169 events; HR 0.66). At the primary analysis (258 events), investigator-assessed PFS HR was 0.73 (95% CI 0.57–0.95; nominal P = .017); median 6.0 vs 5.3 mo; 6-month PFS 50% vs 37%. BICR-assessed PFS was supportive (HR 0.55; median 12.9 vs 5.6 mo), despite notable investigator/BICR discordance. ORR in measurable disease was 17% vs 7% (nominal P = .015). OS was immature (40 vs 37 deaths). In exploratory biomarker analyses the effect was consistent with or without ESR1 or PIK3CA mutations. Grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 55% vs 20% (grade ≥3 neutropenia 24.9% with abemaciclib) and SAEs in 24% vs 11%. AE-related discontinuation was 6% vs none. AEs led to death in four (2%) vs two (1%) patients; one abemaciclib-arm death (pneumonia) was judged treatment-related.
records.keywords: Kalinsky et al. J Clin Oncol 2024;43:1101-1112

records.title: MAINTAIN (Kalinsky)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · Second-line & beyond — CDK4/6 after endocrine progression · II · 2023
records.body: HR+/HER2- metastatic or unresectable breast cancer, histologically or cytologically confirmed; progression on ET and any CDK4/6i, intervening treatment allowed, ≤1 previous chemotherapy line for MBC; women and men, premenopausal eligible if gonadotropin-releasing hormone started ≥2 weeks before ET; baseline corrected QT interval ≤450 ms; previously treated brain metastases eligible only if asymptomatic, stable ≥4 weeks and off corticosteroids Switched ET + ribociclib 600 mg once daily 21 days on/7 days off vs switched ET + placebo (double-blind); ET switched from pre-randomization ET: fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly C1D1, C1D15, then D1 every 4 weeks if previous exemestane, exemestane 25 mg once daily if previous fulvestrant (September 2018 amendment), fulvestrant encouraged if neither Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, adverse events, blood markers including ctDNA detection Switching ET and adding ribociclib significantly improved PFS vs switched ET plus placebo in HR+/HER2- MBC after progression on a CDK4/6i and different ET. Median PFS 5.29 vs 2.76 mo; HR 0.57 (95% CI 0.39-0.85); P=.006; 6-mo PFS 41.2% vs 23.9%, 12-mo 24.6% vs 7.4% (median follow-up 18.2 mo). ORR 20% vs 11% among 70 with measurable disease (P=.51); CBR 43% vs 25% (P=.06). 86.5% had prior palbociclib; prior ribociclib or abemaciclib was under-represented, and subgroup analyses are exploratory. In an exploratory ctDNA analysis of the fulvestrant subgroup, benefit was limited to ESR1 wild-type patients (HR 0.30) and not seen with ESR1 mutation (HR 1.22). With ribociclib, grade III neutropenia 38%, grade IV 2%, febrile neutropenia in 2 patients; dose interruptions 53% vs 20%. Treatment-related deaths 2 vs 1.

records.title: BOLERO-2
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · PI3K / AKT / mTOR pathway-targeted therapy · III · 2012
records.body: Postmenopausal women with ER-positive, HER2-nonamplified advanced breast cancer; refractory to prior letrozole or anastrozole (recurrence during or within 12 months after end of adjuvant treatment or progression during or within 1 month after end of treatment for advanced disease); recurrence or progression on most recent systemic therapy documented; a single prior chemotherapy regimen for advanced disease allowed; excluded brain metastases history, prior exemestane or mTOR inhibitors Oral everolimus 10 mg daily + exemestane 25 mg daily vs matching placebo + exemestane 25 mg daily (double-blind); until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, overall response rate, clinical benefit rate, time to deterioration of ECOG performance status, safety, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, QLQ-BR23), changes in bone marker levels Adding everolimus to exemestane improved PFS in HR-positive advanced breast cancer previously treated with nonsteroidal aromatase inhibitors but did not significantly improve OS. At the final PFS analysis (510 local PFS events; median follow-up 17.7 mo), median PFS was 7.8 vs 3.2 mo by local assessment (HR 0.45; 95% CI 0.38-0.54) and 11.0 vs 4.1 mo by central assessment (HR 0.38; 95% CI 0.31-0.48), consistent across prospectively defined subgroups. Final local ORR 12.6% vs 1.7%; CBR 51.3% vs 26.4%. Final OS (410 deaths; median follow-up 39.3 mo): 31.0 vs 26.6 mo (HR 0.89; 95% CI 0.73-1.10; P=0.14); poststudy chemotherapy 53% vs 63%. Time to deterioration of ECOG PS and of QoL did not differ significantly. Final PFS-cut grade 3 stomatitis 8% vs <1%, anemia 7% vs <1%, hyperglycemia 5% vs <1%, pneumonitis 3% vs 0%; OS-cut serious AEs 33% vs 16%, AE discontinuation 29% vs 5%, on-treatment AE deaths 1.7% vs 0.4%, one pneumonia death with exemestane alone.

records.title: SOLAR-1
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · PI3K / AKT / mTOR pathway-targeted therapy · III · 2019
records.body: HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer, men or postmenopausal women; relapse/progression on/after aromatase inhibitor (neo/adjuvant or advanced), no prior chemotherapy for advanced disease; central tumour-tissue PIK3CA-mutated (primary) or non-mutated cohort; excluded prior fulvestrant or PI3K/AKT/mTOR inhibitor, type 1 or uncontrolled type 2 diabetes (FPG >140 mg/dL or HbA1c >6.4%), (amendment) endocrine-sensitive relapse ≥12 mo after adjuvant endocrine therapy untreated for advanced disease Alpelisib 300 mg orally daily (continuous) + fulvestrant 500 mg IM days 1 and 15 of cycle 1, then day 1 of each 28-day cycle vs placebo + fulvestrant (same schedule), double-blind, randomized within each PIK3CA cohort; until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent or death Primary: progression-free survival (PIK3CA-mutated cohort). Secondary: overall survival (PIK3CA-mutated cohort), progression-free survival (non-mutated cohort), overall survival (non-mutated cohort), progression-free survival by ctDNA level, overall response, clinical benefit, PFS2, time to chemotherapy, overall survival in plasma ctDNA PIK3CA-mutated patients, safety Alpelisib–fulvestrant significantly prolonged PFS and increased overall response vs placebo–fulvestrant in PIK3CA-mutated, HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer after prior endocrine therapy. Mutated cohort (median follow-up 20.0 mo): median PFS 11.0 vs 5.7 mo; HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.50–0.85; P<0.001); blinded independent review of a 50% audit subset, HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.32–0.71). Overall response 26.6% vs 12.8%; clinical benefit 61.5% vs 45.3%. Final OS (23 April 2020 cut-off) did not cross the prespecified boundary: 39.3 vs 31.4 mo; HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.64–1.15); lung/liver metastases HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.46–1.00). In the cohort without PIK3CA mutations, proof-of-concept criteria were not met (HR 0.85; 95% CI 0.58–1.25; earlier data cutoff). In the safety population, grade 3/4 hyperglycemia 36.6% vs 0.7% and rash 9.9% vs 0.3%; grade 3 diarrhea 6.7% vs 0.3%; serious AEs 34.9% vs 16.7%; discontinuation of alpelisib vs placebo for AEs 25.0% vs 4.2%; no new signals with longer follow-up.

records.title: CAPItello-291
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · PI3K / AKT / mTOR pathway-targeted therapy · III · 2023
records.body: HR-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced (primary inoperable) or metastatic breast cancer; progression during AI for metastatic disease or during/within 12 months after (neo)adjuvant AI, with or without prior CDK4/6 inhibitor (protocol minimum 51% CDK4/6 inhibitor-pretreated); not selected by AKT pathway status; up to two prior endocrine and one chemotherapy line for advanced disease; excluded prior fulvestrant/SERD or AKT, PI3K or mTOR inhibitor, and insulin-treated diabetes or HbA1c ≥8.0% Capivasertib 400 mg orally twice daily, 4 days on/3 days off, plus fulvestrant 500 mg IM every 14 days for the first three injections then every 28 days vs matching placebo plus fulvestrant (double-blind); LHRH agonist for pre/perimenopausal women; until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent or death Primary: progression-free survival in the overall population, progression-free survival in AKT pathway-altered tumors. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, safety, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30), time to deterioration of global health status/quality of life, PFS2, time to first subsequent chemotherapy or death Adding capivasertib to fulvestrant significantly prolonged PFS vs fulvestrant alone in HR-positive advanced breast cancer progressing during or after AI therapy, with or without a CDK4/6 inhibitor. Median PFS 7.2 vs 3.6 mo overall (HR 0.60; 95% CI 0.51-0.71) and 7.3 vs 3.1 mo in AKT pathway-altered tumors (HR 0.50; 95% CI 0.38-0.65). Final OS was not significantly improved (altered HR 0.83; 95% CI 0.63-1.10; overall HR 1.00; 95% CI 0.83-1.19). PFS2 (HR 0.68 altered; 0.85 overall) and exploratory time to first subsequent chemotherapy or death were prolonged. In an exploratory analysis of AKT pathway-nonaltered tumors (unknown status excluded), PFS HR was 0.79 (95% CI 0.61-1.02). Median time to deterioration of global health status/QoL 24.9 vs 12.0 mo (HR 0.70; 95% CI 0.53-0.92). Grade ≥3 rash 12.1% vs 0.3%, diarrhea 9.3% vs 0.3%, hyperglycemia 2.3% vs 0.3%; AE-related discontinuation 13.0% vs 2.3%. Fatal AEs in 4 vs 1 patients, none considered related to capivasertib or fulvestrant.

records.title: INAVO120
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · PI3K / AKT / mTOR pathway-targeted therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Hormone receptor-positive (≥1% ER or PR), HER2-negative locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer; first-line after relapse during or within 12 months after completing adjuvant endocrine therapy; PIK3CA mutation by local tumour tissue/ctDNA or central ctDNA testing; fasting glucose <126 mg/dL, HbA1c <6.0%, RECIST 1.1 measurable disease; excluded de novo metastatic disease, evaluable bone-only disease and diabetes requiring ongoing treatment Inavolisib 9 mg orally once daily days 1–28 + palbociclib 125 mg orally once daily days 1–21 + fulvestrant 500 mg IM days 1 and 15 of cycle 1 then approximately every 28 days (28-day cycles) vs placebo once daily + the same palbociclib–fulvestrant; LHRH agonist for premenopausal/perimenopausal women and men; until disease progression, unacceptable toxic effects, withdrawal of consent or death Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, confirmed objective response, best overall response, clinical benefit, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, safety, unacceptable side effects, pharmacokinetics Adding inavolisib to first-line palbociclib–fulvestrant significantly prolonged PFS and, at the final analysis, OS in PIK3CA-mutated, HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer, with more toxic effects but a low rate of discontinuation for adverse events. Updated descriptive PFS (median follow-up 34.2 vs 32.3 mo): 17.2 vs 7.3 mo (HR 0.42; 95% CI 0.32–0.55). Final OS: 34.0 vs 27.0 mo (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.48–0.94; P=0.02, boundary P<0.0469). ORR 62.7% vs 28.0%; median DoR 19.2 vs 11.1 mo. Subgroup analyses were underpowered, with apparent lack of benefit in patients older than 65 years. Hyperglycemia 63.4% vs 13.5% (grade 3/4 6.8% vs 0%); grade 3/4 stomatitis 5.6% vs 0%, diarrhea 3.7% vs 0%, neutropenia 82.6% vs 80.4%. Serious AEs 27.3% vs 13.5%; grade 5 AEs 3.7% vs 1.2%, none considered related to trial agents by investigators and none new since the primary analysis; AE-related discontinuation of inavolisib vs placebo 6.8% vs 0.6%.

records.title: VIKTORIA-1
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · PI3K / AKT / mTOR pathway-targeted therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Adults (including pre/perimenopausal with induced menopause) with HR-positive/HER2-negative, PIK3CA wild-type (central testing) metastatic or locally advanced breast cancer progressing during or after CDK4/6 inhibitor plus NSAI; ECOG 0-1 with measurable RECIST v1.1 disease; excluded prior PI3K/AKT/mTOR inhibitor, advanced-setting chemotherapy/ADC, >2 prior ET lines, and uncontrolled diabetes Gedatolisib 180 mg IV on days 1, 8, 15 of each 28-day cycle + palbociclib 125 mg PO daily days 1-21 + fulvestrant 500 mg IM days 1 and 15 of cycle 1 then q4w vs gedatolisib 180 mg IV days 1, 8, 15 q28d + fulvestrant 500 mg IM as above vs fulvestrant 500 mg IM days 1 and 15 of cycle 1 then every 4 weeks Primary: Progression-free survival by blinded independent central review. Secondary: Overall survival, Objective response, Duration of response, Safety, Quality of life, Pharmacokinetics In PIK3CA wild-type HR+/HER2- advanced breast cancer after CDK4/6 inhibitor plus NSAI, both gedatolisib combinations improved BICR-assessed PFS versus fulvestrant alone (hierarchical primary testing). Median PFS 9.3 vs 2.0 months (stratified HR 0.24, 95% CI 0.17-0.35; P < .001) with the triplet and 7.4 months (HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.24-0.48; P < .001) with the doublet. Confirmed ORR 31.5%, 28.3% and 1.0%, respectively; median DOR 17.5 and 12.0 months. Interim OS did not cross prespecified boundaries (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.43-1.12 and HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.46-1.19). Grade 3 neutropenia 52.3% with the triplet; two treatment-related deaths (pneumonia, hepatic failure), both in the triplet group

records.title: evERA Breast Cancer
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · PI3K / AKT / mTOR pathway-targeted therapy · III · 2026
records.body: ER-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced unresectable or metastatic breast cancer; after CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy (progression after ≥6 months for advanced disease, or recurrence during/within 12 months after adjuvant use); ESR1-mutation enriched (no detectable mutation capped at ~40%); excluded progression during more than two prior endocrine lines, prior chemotherapy for advanced disease or prior oral SERD Giredestrant 30 mg orally once daily plus everolimus 10 mg orally once daily vs investigator's-choice standard endocrine therapy (exemestane; fulvestrant or tamoxifen added after a protocol amendment) plus everolimus, each until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; LHRH agonist for premenopausal/perimenopausal women and men Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, duration of response, safety, progression-free survival without detectable ESR1 mutation, overall survival without detectable ESR1 mutation An all-oral giredestrant–everolimus regimen significantly prolonged PFS vs standard endocrine therapy–everolimus after a CDK4/6 inhibitor, mainly in ESR1-mutated tumors; adverse event incidence was similar. ESR1-mutated (n=207): median PFS 10.0 vs 5.5 mo; HR 0.38 (95% CI 0.27–0.54). Overall population: 8.8 vs 5.5 mo; HR 0.56 (95% CI 0.44–0.71), to be read in light of ESR1-enriched enrolment (55.5% ESR1-mutated). Without detectable ESR1 mutation (exploratory): 5.7 vs 5.5 mo; HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.59–1.18). Interim OS immature and boundaries not crossed: HR 0.62 (95% CI 0.38–1.02) ESR1-mutated, 0.69 (95% CI 0.47–1.00) overall. ORR 26.6% vs 13.8% in ESR1-mutated measurable disease (not multiplicity-adjusted). Serious AEs 29.1% vs 23.1%; everolimus discontinuation for AEs 17.0% vs 11.8%; fatal AEs 2.7% in each group; bradycardia 3.8% vs 0.5%, all grade 1.

records.title: EMERALD
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · ESR1-mutant disease & next-generation oral SERDs · III · 2022
records.body: ER-positive (≥1% IHC)/HER2-negative locoregionally recurrent or metastatic breast adenocarcinoma, postmenopausal women or men; progression during or within 28 days after one or two endocrine lines for advanced disease (adjuvant progression within 12 months counted), prior CDK4/6 inhibitor with fulvestrant or AI required, ≤1 prior chemotherapy; ESR1 by ctDNA, not required; measurable or bone-only lytic/mixed disease; excluded symptomatic visceral disease, cardiovascular events within 6 months Elacestrant 400 mg orally once daily vs investigator's-choice SOC endocrine monotherapy (fulvestrant, anastrozole, letrozole or exemestane, dosed per labeling; a different agent from prior therapy recommended) Primary: progression-free survival in all patients, progression-free survival in patients with ESR1 mutation. Secondary: overall survival in all patients, overall survival in patients with ESR1 mutation, progression-free survival in patients without ESR1 mutation, overall survival in patients without ESR1 mutation, investigator-assessed progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, clinical benefit rate, 6-month and 12-month PFS rates, safety, tolerability Elacestrant significantly prolonged BICR-assessed PFS vs SOC endocrine monotherapy in both all patients and those with ESR1 mutation, with manageable safety. PFS HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.55–0.88) overall and 0.55 (95% CI 0.39–0.77) with ESR1 mutation; 12-month PFS 22.3% vs 9.4% and 26.8% vs 8.2%, respectively. Median PFS was 2.8 vs 1.9 mo overall and 3.8 vs 1.9 mo with ESR1 mutation, after an initial drop in both arms. Interim OS was not significant at the allocated alpha: HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.54–1.04) overall and 0.59 (95% CI 0.36–0.96) with ESR1 mutation; final OS pending. PFS benefit was smaller without detectable ESR1 mutation (not a primary endpoint; interpret with caution). Grade 3/4 AEs 27.0% vs 20.5%; nausea 35.0% vs 18.8% (grade 3/4 2.5% vs 0.9%); AE-related discontinuation 6.3% vs 4.4%; no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: EMBER-3

records.body: ER-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer; progression on an aromatase inhibitor, alone or with a CDK4/6 inhibitor, as neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapy, within 12 months after adjuvant therapy, or on first-line treatment for advanced disease, with no other prior therapy for advanced disease; ESR1 status centrally assessed in pretreatment ctDNA; excluded visceral crisis, symptomatic or untreated brain metastases, inflammatory breast cancer Imlunestrant 400 mg orally once daily vs investigator's choice of standard endocrine monotherapy (exemestane 25 mg orally once daily or fulvestrant 500 mg IM on days 1 and 15 of cycle 1, then day 1 of each subsequent 28-day cycle) vs imlunestrant 400 mg once daily + abemaciclib 150 mg orally twice daily (arm added by early amendment); GnRH agonist for premenopausal/perimenopausal women and men Primary: progression-free survival (imlunestrant vs standard therapy in ESR1-mutated patients; imlunestrant vs standard therapy in all patients; imlunestrant–abemaciclib vs imlunestrant in concurrently randomized patients). Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival by blinded independent central review, overall response, safety, CNS progression Imlunestrant significantly prolonged PFS vs standard endocrine therapy in ESR1-mutated disease but not in the overall population; imlunestrant–abemaciclib significantly improved PFS vs imlunestrant regardless of ESR1 status. ESR1-mutated (256 patients): median PFS 5.5 vs 3.8 mo; with nonproportional hazards, RMST at 19.4 mo 7.9 vs 5.4 mo (difference 2.6 mo; 95% CI 1.2-3.9). All patients: median PFS 5.6 vs 5.5 mo (HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.72-1.04; P=0.12). Interim OS (ESR1-mutated): HR 0.55, not significant; combination OS immature (HR 1.34; 95% CI 0.81-2.21). Grade ≥3 AEs 17.1% imlunestrant, 20.7% standard therapy, 48.6% combination (grade ≥3 neutropenia 19.7%, diarrhea 8.2%). One investigator-attributed treatment-related death each with imlunestrant (right ventricular failure) and the combination (unknown cause).

records.title: VERITAC-2 (vepdegestrant)
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · ESR1-mutant disease & next-generation oral SERDs · III · 2025
records.body: ER-positive, HER2-negative locoregional recurrent or metastatic breast cancer not amenable to resection or radiation; RECIST 1.1 measurable or nonmeasurable bone-only disease; one prior CDK4/6 inhibitor plus endocrine therapy line (adjuvant counts if progression during or within 12 months) and up to one more endocrine line, most recent for at least 6 months before progression; excluded prior chemotherapy for advanced disease, fulvestrant, elacestrant or PI3K/AKT/mTOR inhibitors Vepdegestrant 200 mg orally once daily in 28-day cycles vs fulvestrant 500 mg intramuscularly on days 1 and 15 of cycle 1, then day 1 of subsequent cycles Primary: progression-free survival in patients with ESR1 mutations and in all patients. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, safety, QTc interval Vepdegestrant was associated with significantly longer PFS than fulvestrant in patients with ESR1 mutations but not in the full population. ESR1-mutated (n=270): median PFS 5.0 vs 2.1 mo; HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.43–0.78; P<0.001). All 624 randomized: 3.8 vs 3.6 mo; HR 0.83 (95% CI 0.69–1.01; P=0.07). ORR in ESR1-mutated patients 18.6% vs 4.0%, not adjusted for multiplicity. OS immature (median not reached); short follow-up precluded OS and duration-of-response analyses. Grade ≥3 AEs 23.4% vs 17.6%; AE-related discontinuation 2.9% vs 0.7%; fatigue 26.6% vs 15.6%. QT prolongation 9.9% (grade 3, 1.6%) vs 1.3%, without clinical sequelae. Deaths from AEs 8 vs 2, none considered treatment-related.

records.title: SERENA-6
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · ESR1-mutant disease & next-generation oral SERDs · III · 2025
records.body: Adults with ER-positive, HER2-negative locoregionally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer and surveillance-detected emerging ctDNA ESR1 mutation, without progression after at least 6 months of first-line AI plus CDK4/6 inhibitor (palbociclib, ribociclib or abemaciclib); ECOG 0-1 Switch to camizestrant 75 mg orally once daily plus same CDK4/6 inhibitor at same dose with matched aromatase-inhibitor placebo vs continued anastrozole 1 mg or letrozole 2.5 mg orally once daily plus same CDK4/6 inhibitor with matched camizestrant placebo; palbociclib/ribociclib 21 days on, 7 days off in 28-day cycles, abemaciclib twice daily continuously; until RECIST 1.1 progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or death; one camizestrant reduction to 50 mg allowed Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Second progression-free survival, Overall survival, Chemotherapy-free or antibody-drug conjugate-free survival, Objective response rate, Clinical benefit, Time to first subsequent therapy or death, Time to second subsequent therapy or death, Time to deterioration in breast and arm symptoms, Time to deterioration in pain, Time to deterioration in physical functioning, Safety, Camizestrant plasma concentration, Time to deterioration in global health status/quality of life At the final second progression-free survival analysis (median follow-up 23.5 months; data cutoff Jan 2, 2026), switching to camizestrant at ctDNA ESR1 mutation emergence produced sustained progression-free survival benefit that translated into a statistically significant improvement in second progression-free survival versus continuing aromatase inhibitor, each with continued CDK4/6 inhibitor. Updated (descriptive) progression-free survival: median 16.8 vs 9.2 months, HR 0.45 (95% CI 0.34-0.59), nominal p<0.0001. Second progression-free survival: 25.7 vs 19.1 months, HR 0.63 (0.46-0.86), p=0.0037. Overall survival immature and not powered at this cutoff (95 deaths; 58% information fraction; median 41.2 vs 40.2 months, HR 0.87 [0.57-1.30]). records.body: Unresectable or metastatic breast cancer; one or two prior chemotherapy lines for metastatic disease, or recurrence during or within 6 months after adjuvant chemotherapy; HER2-low (IHC 1+ or IHC 2+ and ISH-negative, central testing), hormone receptor-positive (ER or PR ≥1% of tumour-cell nuclei) or -negative; hormone receptor-positive patients needed at least one endocrine therapy line; treated, stable brain metastases allowed; excluded glucocorticoid-treated noninfectious ILD or suspected ILD on screening imaging Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks vs physician's choice of capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel, given per local label or NCCN guidelines Primary: progression-free survival in the hormone receptor-positive cohort. Secondary: progression-free survival among all patients, overall survival in the hormone receptor-positive cohort, overall survival among all patients, investigator-assessed progression-free survival, confirmed objective response, duration of response, efficacy in the hormone receptor-negative cohort, disease control, clinical benefit, safety Trastuzumab deruxtecan resulted in significantly longer PFS and OS than physician's choice chemotherapy in HER2-low metastatic breast cancer. Hormone receptor-positive cohort (primary): median PFS 10.1 vs 5.4 mo (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.40–0.64; P<0.001); OS 23.9 vs 17.5 mo (HR 0.64; P=0.003). All patients: PFS 9.9 vs 5.1 mo (HR 0.50); OS 23.4 vs 16.8 mo (HR 0.64; P=0.001). OS P values crossed the interim stopping boundary; median survival follow-up 18.4 mo. Confirmed ORR 52.6% vs 16.3% in the hormone receptor-positive cohort. The hormone receptor-negative cohort was small: PFS 8.5 vs 2.9 mo (HR 0.46), OS 18.2 vs 8.3 mo (HR 0.48). records.title: TROPiCS-02
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · Antibody-drug conjugates & later-line therapy · III · 2022
records.body: Locally recurrent inoperable or metastatic breast cancer, endocrine-resistant; 2-4 prior systemic chemotherapy regimens for metastatic disease ((neo)adjuvant chemotherapy counted if relapse within 12 months); HR+/HER2−; measurable disease, with at least one prior taxane, anticancer hormonal treatment and CDK4/6 inhibitor required; excluded: prior topoisomerase 1 inhibitor therapy Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV on days 1 and 8 every 21 days vs physician's choice single-agent chemotherapy determined before randomization (eribulin 1.4 mg/m² [North America] or 1.23 mg/m² [Europe] IV days 1 and 8 every 21 days; vinorelbine 25 mg/m² IV weekly; gemcitabine 800-1,200 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days; capecitabine 1,000-1,250 mg/m² orally twice daily for 2 weeks then 1 week rest, every 21 days); until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or investigator decision Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, safety, time to response Sacituzumab govitecan significantly improved PFS over chemotherapy, with a manageable safety profile, in heavily pretreated endocrine-resistant HR+/HER2− advanced breast cancer. Median PFS by BICR 5.5 vs 4.0 mo (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.53-0.83); PFS at 6 and 12 mo 46% vs 30% and 21% vs 7%. At the planned final OS analysis (12.5-mo median follow-up), OS was significantly improved: median 14.4 vs 11.2 mo (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.65-0.96), consistent across exploratory Trop-2 expression subgroups. ORR (21% vs 14%) and time to deterioration of global health status/QoL (4.3 vs 3.0 mo) and fatigue were then formally tested and significantly improved; pain was similar. 22 (8%) patients assigned chemotherapy were never treated. Grade ≥3 treatment-related neutropenia 51% vs 38% and diarrhea 9% vs 1%; treatment-related febrile neutropenia 5% vs 4%; 6 fatal adverse events with sacituzumab govitecan (1 treatment-related: septic shock from neutropenic colitis), none with chemotherapy.

records.body: Inoperable/metastatic HR+/HER2- breast cancer (HER2- IHC 0, 1+ or 2+/ISH-); one or two prior chemotherapy lines in the inoperable/metastatic setting; progression on endocrine therapy, further endocrine therapy unsuitable (original protocol allowed endocrine-naive); prior CDK4/6 inhibitor not required (CDK4/6-naive capped); clinically stable brain metastases allowed; no prior topoisomerase I-targeting chemotherapy (including ADCs) or TROP2-directed therapy Dato-DXd 6 mg/kg IV once every 3 weeks vs investigator's choice single-agent chemotherapy (eribulin 1.4 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8; capecitabine 1,000 or 1,250 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1-14; vinorelbine 25 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8; or gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV days 1 and 8; each every 3 weeks); treatment until investigator-assessed radiologic progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent or other predefined discontinuation criterion Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate at 12 weeks, duration of response, time to first subsequent therapy or death, time to second subsequent therapy or death, PFS2, safety, tolerability Dato-DXd met the dual primary PFS endpoint, with a statistically significant and clinically meaningful PFS improvement vs ICC and a favorable, manageable safety profile. PFS by BICR: median 6.9 vs 4.9 mo; HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52 to 0.76); P < .0001; median follow-up 10.8 mo. The dual primary OS endpoint was immature at this interim analysis (maturity 23.4%): HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.62 to 1.14); final OS pending. ORR by BICR 36.4% vs 22.9%. Grade ≥3 TRAEs 20.8% vs 44.7%. With Dato-DXd, nausea (51.1%) and stomatitis (50%; grade ≥3 6.4%) were most common; ocular surface events occurred in 40%; adjudicated drug-related ILD in 3.3%, including one grade 5 event (characterized by the investigator as grade 3 pneumonitis, with death attributed to progression). records.title: DESTINY-Breast06
records.subtitle: HR+ HER2- MBC · Antibody-drug conjugates & later-line therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Hormone receptor–positive metastatic breast cancer; chemotherapy-naive for advanced/metastatic disease; HER2-low (IHC 1+ or 2+, ISH-negative) or HER2-ultralow (IHC 0 with membrane staining); progression after at least two endocrine-based lines for metastatic disease, or one line with recurrence within 24 months of starting adjuvant endocrine therapy or progression within 6 months of starting first-line endocrine therapy plus CDK4/6 inhibitor; clinically active CNS metastases excluded Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg IV once every 3 weeks vs physician's choice of single-agent chemotherapy (capecitabine 1250 or 1000 mg per square meter orally twice daily for 2 weeks then 1-week rest, 3-week cycles; nab-paclitaxel 100 mg per square meter IV weekly for 3 weeks then 1-week rest, 4-week cycles; or paclitaxel 80 mg per square meter IV weekly, 3-week cycles); both until disease progression (RECIST 1.1) or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety Trastuzumab deruxtecan prolonged PFS vs chemotherapy in HR-positive, HER2-low or HER2-ultralow metastatic breast cancer after one or more endocrine-based lines, with no new safety signals. Primary endpoint met: HER2-low median PFS 13.2 vs 8.1 mo (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.52–0.75; P<0.001); all randomized, 13.2 vs 8.1 mo (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.54–0.76; P<0.001). HER2-ultralow was exploratory and not formally tested: 13.2 vs 8.3 mo (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.50–1.21). Confirmed ORR (HER2-low) 56.5% vs 32.2%. records.title: NSABP B-31 / NCCTG N9831 (joint analysis)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2005
records.body: Operable HER2-positive breast adenocarcinoma; adjuvant after complete resection and axillary dissection (negative sentinel-node biopsy allowed in N9831); HER2 IHC 3+ or FISH-amplified; histologically node-positive, or (N9831 from May 2, 2003) high-risk node-negative: tumour >2 cm and ER/PR-positive or >1 cm and ER/PR-negative; excluded metastatic disease, LVEF below lower limit of normal, significant cardiac disease or history of MI, CHF or cardiomyopathy Doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² every 21 days × 4 → paclitaxel 175 mg/m² every 3 weeks × 4 (B-31; weekly 80 mg/m² × 12 permitted from May 16, 2003) or 80 mg/m² weekly × 12 (N9831) (control: B-31 group 1, N9831 group A) vs same chemotherapy + trastuzumab 4 mg/kg loading dose with first paclitaxel dose, then 2 mg/kg weekly for 51 weeks (52 weeks total; B-31 group 2, N9831 group C) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to distant recurrence, death from breast cancer, contralateral breast cancer, other second primary cancers, time to recurrence, NYHA class III or IV congestive heart failure or cardiac death, safety Adding trastuzumab to paclitaxel after doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide durably improved survival in resected HER2-positive breast cancer. First interim (394 events; median follow-up 2.0 yr): DFS HR 0.48 (95% CI 0.39–0.59), crossing the stopping boundary. Definitive joint analysis (median follow-up 8.4 yr; trastuzumab vs control): DFS HR 0.60 (95% CI 0.53–0.68), 10-yr DFS 73.7% vs 62.2%; OS HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.54–0.73), 10-yr OS 84% vs 75.2%, ITT despite 20% control crossover. Interim node-negative subgroup (191 patients, 3 events) too small to assess. Pooled RFS analysis: benefit persisted in years 5–10 (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.49–0.97; nominal), similar in HR+ and HR− disease (interaction P=.87); years 5–10 recurrence in trastuzumab-treated HR+ disease 3.23% N0, 6.39% N1. 3-yr NYHA III/IV CHF or cardiac death 4.1% vs 0.8% (B-31), 2.9% vs 0% (N9831); 8-yr known-cardiac death 0.2% vs 0.1%. 3 treatment-related deaths (1 cardiomyopathy, 2 pneumonitis) with paclitaxel plus trastuzumab.

records.title: HERA (BIG 1-01)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2005
records.body: HER2-positive, completely excised early invasive breast cancer; after locoregional therapy and at least four cycles of neoadjuvant or adjuvant chemotherapy; HER2 IHC 3+ or FISH-positive, centrally confirmed; node-positive, or node-negative with tumour >1 cm, and LVEF ≥55% after all chemotherapy and radiotherapy; excluded: distant metastases, clinical T4/inflammatory tumours or supraclavicular nodes, significant cardiac history, cumulative doxorubicin >360 or epirubicin >720 mg per square meter Trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV once → 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for 1 year vs the same dose and schedule for 2 years vs observation, all starting after completion of chemotherapy and locoregional therapy Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: cardiac safety, overall survival, site of first disease-free survival event, time to distant recurrence, safety, cumulative incidence of breast cancer and non-breast cancer disease-free survival events, efficacy by hormone receptor status 1 year of trastuzumab after chemotherapy significantly improved long-term DFS vs observation; 2 years added no benefit. Final analysis (median follow-up 11 yr): DFS HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.68–0.86); 10-yr DFS 63% observation, 69% 1 yr, 69% 2 yr; 2 vs 1 yr landmark HR 1.02 (0.89–1.17). Time to distant recurrence HR 0.49 (95% CI 0.38–0.63) at the first interim (median 1 yr). OS did not differ at the interim (29 vs 37 deaths; HR 0.76, 0.47–1.23) but improved at 11 yr (HR 0.74, 0.64–0.86). Selective crossover of 884 (52%) observation patients to trastuzumab likely underestimates benefit. Final cardiac endpoints (observation vs 1 yr vs 2 yr): primary 0.1% vs 1% vs 1%; secondary 0.9% vs 4.4% vs 7.3%, mostly during treatment. Final grade 3 or 4 AEs 18% (1 yr) and 22% (2 yr) vs 9%. At the interim: severe CHF 0.54% vs 0; symptomatic CHF 1.73% vs 0.06%; LVEF decrease 7.08% vs 2.21%; fatal AEs 6 vs 3; 8.5% stopped trastuzumab early for reasons other than relapse.

records.title: FinHer
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2006
records.body: Early invasive breast cancer, adjuvant setting, randomised within 12 weeks after surgery; at least one positive axillary node, or node-negative tumour more than 20 mm and progesterone-receptor-negative (usually <10 percent of cells stained); HER2 IHC 2+ or 3+ tested by CISH (HER2 positive if six or more gene copies), amplified tumours further randomised to trastuzumab; age <66 years, WHO PS 0 or 1; excluded distant metastases, pregnancy, severe hypertension, cardiac disease Docetaxel 100 mg/m² IV day 1 every 21 days for three cycles (starting dose reduced to 80 mg/m² after a February 2002 monitoring-committee recommendation) vs vinorelbine 25 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 every 21 days for three cycles (day-15 dose omitted from the third cycle), each → three cycles of FEC (fluorouracil 600 mg/m², epirubicin 60 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² IV day 1 every 21 days); chemotherapy duration 18 weeks; HER2-amplified subset additionally randomised: trastuzumab 4 mg/kg then 2 mg/kg IV weekly for nine infusions from day 1 of the first docetaxel or vinorelbine cycle, none during FEC, vs no trastuzumab Primary: recurrence-free survival, distant disease-free survival. Secondary: adverse effects, left ventricular ejection fraction, time to distant recurrence, overall survival At final analysis (median 62 mo), docetaxel improved DDFS vs vinorelbine (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.49-0.91; P=.010), but 9-week trastuzumab did not significantly improve DDFS in 232 HER2-positive women (HR 0.65; 95% CI 0.38-1.12; P=.12; node-adjusted HR 0.57, P=.047, above the P=.029 limit). At the 36-mo interim, three-year RFS was 91% vs 86% (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.40-0.85; P=0.005) and, with vs without trastuzumab, 89% vs 78% (HR 0.42; 95% CI 0.21-0.83; P=0.01). Final OS did not differ (docetaxel HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.46-1.05; trastuzumab HR 0.55, 95% CI 0.27-1.11). Exploratory: docetaxel+trastuzumab improved DDFS vs docetaxel alone (HR 0.32) and vinorelbine+trastuzumab (HR 0.31); the small HER2 subgroup limits power. Docetaxel was more toxic: neutropenic fever in 36.9% prompted a starting-dose reduction from 100 to 80 mg/m², after which it fell to 14.9%. Heart failure: 1 trastuzumab-treated vs 2 chemotherapy-only HER2-positive women; median LVEF stayed 65% with trastuzumab.
