records.title: BCIRG 006
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · III · 2011
records.body: HER2-positive invasive breast adenocarcinoma; early-stage disease, adjuvant setting; HER2 positivity confirmed by fluorescence in situ hybridization before randomization; women with stage T1, T2 or T3, high-risk node-negative or node-positive disease AC-T: doxorubicin 60 mg/m² + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m² every 3 weeks for four cycles → docetaxel 100 mg/m² every 3 weeks for four doses vs AC-T plus trastuzumab: same AC-T with trastuzumab from the first docetaxel dose for 1 year vs TCH: docetaxel 75 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 6 mg/mL/min every 3 weeks for six cycles with concurrent trastuzumab → trastuzumab for an additional 34 weeks; trastuzumab 4 mg/kg initial dose, then 2 mg/kg weekly during chemotherapy, then 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks to complete 1 year Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, global safety, cardiac safety, congestive heart failure, sustained subclinical LVEF loss, acute leukemia One year of adjuvant trastuzumab significantly improved DFS and OS; the authors judged the risk–benefit ratio to favour nonanthracycline TCH over AC-T plus trastuzumab, citing similar efficacy, fewer acute toxic effects and lower cardiotoxicity and leukemia risk. At the 656-event protocol-specified analysis (median follow-up 65 months), 5-yr DFS was 75% with AC-T, 84% with AC-T plus trastuzumab (HR 0.64; P<0.001) and 81% with TCH (HR 0.75; P=0.04); OS 87%, 92% (HR 0.63) and 91% (HR 0.77). The two trastuzumab regimens did not differ significantly, but the study was not powered to detect equivalence. In the TOP2A-coamplified subgroup, DFS with trastuzumab regimens was virtually indistinguishable from AC-T. NYHA grade 3/4 CHF 2.0% with AC-T plus trastuzumab vs 0.4% with TCH (P<0.001); >10% relative LVEF loss 18.6% vs 9.4%. Acute leukemia: seven cases with anthracycline regimens, one with TCH after outside-study anthracycline; five of eight died.
records.keywords: Slamon et al. N Engl J Med 2011;365:1273-1283

records.title: EBCTCG trastuzumab meta-analysis
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant trastuzumab — foundational trials · N/A · 2021
records.body: Early-stage, operable, HER2-positive breast cancer (node-negative or node-positive); adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy in randomised trials begun before Jan 1, 2010; HER2 by local IHC or FISH; most trials required node-positive or high-risk node-negative disease (generally grade 3, tumour >1 cm if ER-negative or >2 cm if ER-positive); trials adding trastuzumab to other biological therapies (lapatinib, pertuzumab, neratinib) excluded Chemotherapy (adjuvant or neoadjuvant; regimen varied by trial) plus trastuzumab, given concurrently with taxane (or vinorelbine) after any anthracycline or sequentially after all chemotherapy (HERA, PACS-04, one NCCTG N9831 group), for 12 months (9 weeks in FinHER; HERA also a 24-month group; mean scheduled duration 14·4 months) vs the same chemotherapy alone Primary: breast cancer recurrence, breast cancer mortality, death without recurrence, all-cause mortality. Secondary: distant recurrence, local recurrence, contralateral breast cancer, brain metastases as first site of distant recurrence, cardiovascular mortality, deaths from non-breast cancers, cardiac toxicity Adding trastuzumab to chemotherapy for early-stage, HER2-positive breast cancer reduced recurrence of, and mortality from, breast cancer by a third, with worthwhile proportional reductions irrespective of recorded patient and tumour characteristics. Recurrence RR 0·66 (95% CI 0·62–0·71) and breast cancer mortality RR 0·67 (0·61–0·73); 10-year absolute reductions: 9·0% recurrence, 6·4% breast cancer mortality, 6·5% all-cause mortality; no increase in death without recurrence (0·4%, –0·3 to 1·1). Recurrence reduction was largest in years 0–1 (RR 0·53) and smaller in years 5–9 (0·80, 99% CI 0·64–1·01). Substantial control crossover in two trials may have diluted benefit. First-year deaths without recurrence were higher with trastuzumab (0·37% vs 0·16%; RR 2·15), possibly by chance; cardiovascular mortality was not significantly increased. Patient-level cardiac data came from one trial; CHF and LVEF decline were more frequent with trastuzumab but uncommon, with no excess fatal toxicity.
records.keywords: Early Breast Cancer Trialists' Collaborative Group (EBCTCG). Lancet Oncol 2021;22:1139-1150

records.title: PHARE
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · III · 2013
records.body: Invasive HER2-positive early breast cancer (IHC or FISH, certified local laboratory); operable, node-positive or node-negative with tumour ≥10 mm; adjuvant trastuzumab after breast-axillary surgery and at least four cycles of adjuvant or neoadjuvant chemotherapy; women over 18 years who had received up to 6 months of trastuzumab, with LVEF assessed after at least 2 months, and were suitable to continue it; excluded if chemotherapy not completed or early recurrence before randomisation Trastuzumab IV every 3 weeks (8 mg/kg loading, 6 mg/kg thereafter) continued for another 6 months (12 months total) vs trastuzumab discontinued at 6 months (6 months total); protocol-defined cardiac-monitoring stopping rules; chemotherapy, hormone therapy and radiotherapy at investigator choice Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: cardiac safety, overall survival, metastasis-free survival, serious adverse events The final analysis again did not show 6 months of adjuvant trastuzumab to be non-inferior to 12 months; the authors concluded 12 months should remain the standard duration. At median follow-up 7·5 yr, DFS events were 345 (12 mo) vs 359 (6 mo); adjusted HR 1·08 (95% CI 0·93–1·25), with the 1·15 margin inside the CI; 7-yr DFS 82·3% vs 80·6%. Hazards were non-proportional: first-2-yr DFS HR 1·43 (95% CI 1·12–1·84) favoured 12 months, a difference that seemed to disappear later. Final OS: 170 vs 186 deaths, HR 1·13 (95% CI 0·92–1·39); MFS HR 1·15 (95% CI 0·96–1·37). The interim ER-negative/sequential subgroup heterogeneity disappeared. Cardiac events were more frequent with 12 months (96 [5·7%] vs 32 [1·9%] of 1690 each; p<0·0001), as was LVEF <50% (6·3% vs 4·7%); since then, no new heart failure and three further LVEF <50% cases (12 mo). Serious adverse events were 20 (1·2%) per group; no trastuzumab-related deaths were reported.

records.title: ShortHER
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · III · 2018
records.body: Surgically resected HER2-positive breast cancer in women aged 18–75; adjuvant setting, suitable for adjuvant chemotherapy; node-positive, or node-negative with at least one of pathological tumour size >2 cm, histological grade 3, lympho-vascular invasion, Ki-67 >20%, age ≤35 years or hormone receptor negativity (ER and PgR <10%); LVEF within institutional normal range; stage IIIB/IV excluded Arm A (long): AC (adriamycin 60 mg/sqm + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/sqm) or EC (epidoxorubicin 90 mg/sqm + cyclophosphamide 600 mg/sqm) every 3 weeks for four courses → paclitaxel 175 mg/sqm or docetaxel 100 mg/sqm every 3 weeks for four courses, with trastuzumab every 3 weeks for 18 doses from the first taxane dose (8 mg/kg loading, then 6 mg/kg) vs arm B (short): docetaxel 100 mg/sqm every 3 weeks for three courses with concomitant weekly trastuzumab for 9 weeks (4 mg/kg loading, then 2 mg/kg) → FEC (5-fluorouracil 600 mg/sqm, epidoxorubicin 60 mg/sqm, cyclophosphamide 600 mg/sqm) every 3 weeks for three courses; after protocol amendment, patients aged ≥65 years received docetaxel 80 mg/sqm in both arms Primary: disease-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: 2-year failure rate, cardiac safety, trastuzumab permanent discontinuation, non-cardiac adverse events Nine weeks of trastuzumab failed to show non-inferiority to 1 year, and 1-year trastuzumab remains the standard; 9 weeks decreased cardiac toxicity. Primary DFS analysis: HR 1.13 (90% CI 0.89–1.42), upper limit crossing the 1.29 margin. Final analysis (median follow-up 9 years): 10-year DFS 77% long vs 78% short (HR 1.06, 90% CI 0.86–1.31); co-primary 10-year OS 89% vs 88% (HR 1.15, 90% CI 0.85–1.56); 10-year Bayesian probability of non-inferiority 93.2 (no a priori positivity cut-off). The trial was underpowered (sample size reduced to 1252; power 0.56), and arms also differed in chemotherapy (planned epidoxorubicin 360 vs 180 mg/sqm long vs short). Exploratory nodal subgroups: N4+ favoured 1 year (10-year DFS 63% vs 53%, HR 1.84, 95% CI 1.14–2.97; OS 84% vs 64%); N0/N1-3 similar. Grade ≥2 cardiac events 13.1% long vs 4.3% short (risk-ratio 0.33, 95% CI 0.22–0.50); grade 3 cardiac events 2.4% vs 0.8%; permanent trastuzumab discontinuation 8.5% vs 3.4%.

records.title: PERSEPHONE
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Duration of adjuvant trastuzumab · III · 2019
records.body: Invasive early breast cancer; adjuvant or neoadjuvant setting with a clear indication for chemotherapy (any regimen, trastuzumab given concurrently or sequentially); HER2 positive per UK Royal College of Pathologists guidelines (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ with ISH amplification); randomisation before starting trastuzumab or, after a July 2009 amendment, at any time up to and including the ninth trastuzumab cycle Trastuzumab every 3 weeks for 6 months (9 cycles) vs 12 months (18 cycles), IV 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg maintenance or SC 600 mg fixed dose (SC permitted from a 2013 amendment), with chemotherapy given concurrently or sequentially Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, incremental cost-effectiveness, cardiac function (LVEF), predictive factors for cardiac damage, landmark disease-free survival, landmark overall survival, disease-free interval, distant disease-free interval, distant disease-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, breast-cancer specific survival, quality of life, adverse events, clinical cardiac dysfunction 6-month adjuvant trastuzumab was non-inferior to 12 months for disease-free survival in HER2-positive early breast cancer, with less cardiotoxicity and fewer severe adverse events. At 6.1 yr median follow-up, 4-year DFS was 89.5% (6 mo) vs 90.3% (12 mo); HR 1.10 (90% CI 0.96-1.26), below the non-inferiority HR limit of 1.33 (3% margin). 4-year OS 94.2% vs 94.9%; HR 1.14 (90% CI 0.96-1.34), also non-inferior. Underpowered subgroup analyses showed DFS heterogeneity favouring 12 months with concurrent trastuzumab-chemotherapy (HR 1.54, 95% CI 1.19-1.99; timing not randomised; authors judged it likely due to chance); no conclusion is possible for non-anthracycline regimens (403 patients, very few events). Lifetime modelling gave a high probability that 6 months is cost-effective. Severe adverse events 19% vs 24%; trastuzumab stopped for cardiotoxicity 3% vs 8%; clinical cardiac dysfunction 8% vs 11%. 11 cardiac deaths occurred, none during trastuzumab or considered trastuzumab-related.

records.title: NeoSphere
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2012
records.body: HER2-positive breast cancer; treatment-naive, neoadjuvant: operable (T2–3, N0–1, M0), locally advanced (T2–3, N2–3, M0 or T4a–c, any N, M0) or inflammatory (T4d, any N, M0); centrally confirmed HER2 IHC 3+ or 2+ with positive fluorescence or chromogenic in-situ hybridisation; women with primary tumours >2 cm and LVEF ≥55%; excluded stage IV, bilateral breast cancer, other malignancies, impaired cardiac function Four neoadjuvant intravenous cycles every 3 weeks of trastuzumab (8 mg/kg loading, then 6 mg/kg) + docetaxel (75 mg/m², escalating if tolerated to 100 mg/m²) (group A) vs pertuzumab (840 mg loading, then 420 mg) + trastuzumab + docetaxel (group B) vs pertuzumab + trastuzumab without chemotherapy (group C) vs pertuzumab + docetaxel (group D, added after 29 patients) → surgery → adjuvant FEC for three cycles (group C: four cycles of docetaxel → FEC); trastuzumab every 3 weeks for 1 year in all groups Primary: pathological complete response in the breast. Secondary: clinical response rate, time to clinical response, breast-conserving surgery rate, safety, pCR by hormone-receptor status, pCR by axillary nodal status at surgery, LVEF change, progression-free survival, disease-free survival Adding pertuzumab to trastuzumab plus docetaxel significantly improved breast pCR after four cycles with similar tolerability; pertuzumab plus trastuzumab without chemotherapy eradicated tumours in some women. ITT pCR: group B 45.8% (49/107) vs group A 29.0% (31/107), p=0.0141 (alpha 0.2); group D 24.0% (23/96); group C 16.8% (18/107). At 5 years (descriptive; wide, overlapping CIs), PFS 86% (B) vs 81% (A), HR 0·69 (0·34–1·40); C and D 73%; DFS consistent. Exploratory: tpCR linked to longer 5-year PFS (85% vs 76%; HR 0·54). pCR descriptively higher in hormone receptor-negative tumours (B 63.2% vs 26.0% positive). 25 of 417 patients did not undergo surgery. Grade ≥3 neoadjuvant neutropenia 61/107 (A), 48/107 (B), 52/94 (D), one of 108 (C); febrile neutropenia 7–8% with docetaxel, none in C. One neoadjuvant death (fulminant hepatitis, possibly treatment-related, B); a reported group D death was reclassified as withdrawal for progression. No new long-term safety concerns.

records.title: TRYPHAENA
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2013
records.body: HER2-positive early breast cancer in women; neoadjuvant, no prior systemic or local anticancer therapy, operable (T2-3, N0-1, M0), locally advanced (T2-3, N2 or N3, M0; T4a-c, any N, M0) or inflammatory (T4d, any N, M0) with primary tumour >2 cm; HER2 IHC 3+ or FISH-positive (FISH mandatory for IHC 2+), centrally confirmed; baseline LVEF ≥55%; excluded stage IV or bilateral disease, uncontrolled hypertension, myocardial infarction within 6 months Arm A: FEC (5-fluorouracil 500 mg/m², epirubicin 100 mg/m², cyclophosphamide 600 mg/m²) + trastuzumab + pertuzumab ×3 → docetaxel 75 mg/m² (escalating to 100 mg/m² if no dose-limiting toxicity in cycle 4) + trastuzumab + pertuzumab ×3 vs Arm B: same FEC ×3 → docetaxel + trastuzumab + pertuzumab ×3 vs Arm C: docetaxel 75 mg/m² (no escalation) + carboplatin AUC6 + trastuzumab + pertuzumab ×6; all IV q3w for six neoadjuvant cycles; trastuzumab 8 mg/kg then 6 mg/kg, pertuzumab 840 mg then 420 mg; then surgery and trastuzumab to complete 1 year Primary: symptomatic LVSD, LVEF decline ≥10% points from baseline to <50%. Secondary: pathological complete response (ypT0/is), clinical response rate, time to clinical response, rate of breast-conserving surgery, disease-free survival, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety Pertuzumab plus trastuzumab with standard neoadjuvant chemotherapy resulted in low rates of symptomatic LVSD. Neoadjuvant symptomatic LVSD occurred in 2 patients (2.7%) in Arm B and none in Arms A or C; only 1 of 223 (0.4%) occurred while receiving trastuzumab-pertuzumab with chemotherapy. LVEF decline ≥10% points to <50%: 5.6% (A), 5.3% (B), 3.9% (C), all improved to ≥50% at data cutoff. Full study: symptomatic LVSD 0/72, 2/75, 1/76; LVEF decline 11.1%, 16.0%, 11.8%; no new safety signals. pCR (ypT0/is) was 61.6% (A), 57.3% (B) and 66.2% (C). At 5-year follow-up, 3-yr DFS 87%, 88%, 90% and PFS 89%, 89%, 87%, similar across arms; tpCR vs no tpCR DFS HR 0.27 (95% CI 0.11-0.64), unpowered. All three arms were experimental with no control arm; efficacy is descriptive only. Grade ≥3 febrile neutropenia: 18.1% (A), 9.3% (B), 17.1% (C); SAEs 27.8%, 20.0%, 35.5%; Arm C grade ≥3 anemia 17.1% and thrombocytopenia 11.8%. No neoadjuvant deaths; 22 (9.9%) died over the full study, mostly PD.

records.title: TRAIN-2
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer Neoadjuvant trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) concurrent throughout, with FEC ×3 → paclitaxel–carboplatin ×6 (anthracycline) vs paclitaxel–carboplatin ×9 (anthracycline-free); trastuzumab continued to complete 1 year Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: event-free survival, recurrence-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, breast cancer-specific survival, overall survival, breast-conserving surgery rate, safety Adding anthracyclines to neoadjuvant paclitaxel–carboplatin plus trastuzumab–pertuzumab did not improve pCR (67% vs 68%) or show an EFS or OS advantage at 48.8 months; 3-year EFS was 92.7% vs 93.6% (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.50–1.63). Anthracyclines increased grade ≥3 febrile neutropenia (10% vs 1%), severe LVEF decline (7.7% vs 3.2%), and caused 2 acute leukaemias.

records.title: TRAIN-3
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2026
records.body: Stage II-III HER2-positive breast cancer (hormone receptor-negative and hormone receptor-positive cohorts); multicentre, Netherlands (single-arm) Paclitaxel + carboplatin + trastuzumab + pertuzumab for up to 9 cycles, with MRI-guided surgery at first complete radiological response; pCR: trastuzumab–pertuzumab to complete 1 year; residual disease: complete 9 neoadjuvant cycles then T-DM1 every 3 weeks ×14 cycles Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, pathological complete response rate, radiological response, quality of life, safety MRI-guided early surgery after neoadjuvant paclitaxel–carboplatin–trastuzumab–pertuzumab was feasible: pCR after 3 cycles occurred in about one-third of HR-negative and one-sixth of HR-positive patients; 3-year EFS was 92.2% and 92.0%, respectively. Patients stopping after 1–3 cycles were selected by early radiological response and had favourable outcomes, while toxicity rose with cycle count. This single-arm, response-selected study does not establish that shortening preserves efficacy vs a fixed course.
records.keywords: Louis FM et al. Lancet Oncol 2026;27:349-360

records.title: KRISTINE (TRIO-021)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2018
records.body: HER2-positive stage II-III operable breast cancer (neoadjuvant) Six neoadjuvant cycles Q3W: T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV Q3W + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) vs docetaxel–carboplatin + trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (TCHP); after surgery the assigned HER2 regimen continued for 12 more cycles (18 cycles total, ~1 year) Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: event-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, overall survival, breast-conserving surgery rate, quality of life, safety Neoadjuvant T-DM1–pertuzumab produced lower pCR than TCHP (44.4% vs 55.7%; difference −11.3%, 95% CI −20.5 to −2.0) and worse 3-year EFS (85.3% vs 94.2%; HR 2.61, 95% CI 1.36–4.98), driven by preoperative progression. Surgery-landmark iDFS was similar (93.0% vs 92.0%; HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.52–2.40) but excludes 15 preoperative progressions; OS had only 11 deaths. Grade 3–4 adverse events were lower with T-DM1–pertuzumab (13% vs 64%).

records.title: DESTINY-Breast11
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2026
records.body: High-risk HER2-positive early breast cancer (neoadjuvant) Neoadjuvant T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W ×8 cycles (alone), or T-DXd 5.4 mg/kg Q3W ×4 → paclitaxel + trastuzumab (6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) ×4 (T-DXd-THP), vs dose-dense AC (doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide Q2W) ×4 → THP ×4 (standard of care); post-neoadjuvant trastuzumab ± pertuzumab to 1 year, or T-DM1 ×14 cycles if residual disease Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: event-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, distant metastasis-free survival, overall survival, residual cancer burden, safety Neoadjuvant T-DXd→THP improved pCR vs dose-dense AC→THP (67.3% vs 56.3%; difference 11.2%, 95% CI 4.0–18.3), while T-DXd alone was inferior (43.0%) and closed early. Grade ≥3 adverse events were 37.5% vs 55.8%; drug-related ILD was about 4% in each comparison arm. EFS was only 4.5% mature (HR 0.56), so survival benefit is not established.

records.title: neoCARHP
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Stage II-III HER2-positive invasive breast cancer, previously untreated (neoadjuvant); multicentre China Six 3-weekly cycles of investigator-selected taxane (docetaxel, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel) + trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W), without carboplatin (THP; docetaxel 100 mg/m²) vs with carboplatin AUC 6 (TCbHP; docetaxel 75 mg/m²); adjuvant trastuzumab ± pertuzumab to complete 1 year, or T-DM1 ×14 cycles if residual disease Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: clinical response rate, breast-conserving surgery rate, event-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, overall survival, safety Omitting carboplatin from neoadjuvant taxane–trastuzumab–pertuzumab was non-inferior for pCR (64.1% vs 65.9%; difference −1.8%, 95% CI −8.5 to 5.0). Grade 3–4 adverse events were lower without carboplatin (20.7% vs 34.6%), as were serious adverse events (1.3% vs 4.7%); EFS and OS remain immature.

records.title: PHERGain-2
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2026
records.body: Treatment-naive, centrally confirmed HER2-positive (IHC 3+), node-negative early breast cancer, tumours 5-30 mm by MRI (single-arm) Fixed-dose SC trastuzumab–pertuzumab every 3 weeks ×8 neoadjuvant cycles (+ endocrine therapy if HR-positive), then surgery; pCR: HP ×10 adjuvant cycles; residual disease/ypN0(i+/mol+)/ypN1mi: T-DM1 ×10 cycles; ypN1–3: chemotherapy permitted then T-DM1 ×10 cycles; adjuvant endocrine therapy ≥5 years if HR-positive Primary: global health status, recurrence-free interval. Secondary: pathological complete response rate, objective response rate, breast-conserving surgery rate, event-free survival, relapse-free survival, disease-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, overall survival, safety Chemotherapy-free neoadjuvant HP achieved pCR in 59.6%; 1-year global health status declined ≥10% in 42.8% of questionnaire respondents. Treatment-related adverse events occurred in 86.6% (5.6% grade ≥3), with 1 T-DM1-attributed pneumonitis death. The report is noncomparative and 3-year recurrence-free interval is pending, so it supports feasibility and response-adapted escalation but does not establish efficacy preservation vs chemotherapy.
records.keywords: Garrigós L et al. Ann Oncol 2026;37:837-848

records.title: WSG-ADAPT-TP
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2023
records.body: Hormone receptor-positive/HER2-positive early breast cancer, clinical stage I-III 12 weeks of neoadjuvant T-DM1, or T-DM1 + endocrine therapy, or trastuzumab + endocrine therapy (1:1:1); adjuvant chemotherapy optional at investigator discretion after pCR (76 of 117 received it) and mandatory after non-pCR Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival, overall survival, biomarkers T-DM1-based chemotherapy-free neoadjuvant therapy produced higher pCR than trastuzumab + endocrine therapy; 5-year iDFS was 88.9%, 85.3% and 84.6% across the 3 arms, but the trial was not powered for survival and non-pCR patients received mandatory chemotherapy. pCR was associated with better iDFS, yet post-pCR chemotherapy use was nonrandomised. These data identify a favourable response-selected group; they do not prove that chemotherapy can safely be omitted.
records.keywords: Harbeck N et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:3796-3804

records.title: WSG-TP-II
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · II · 2026
records.body: Hormone receptor-positive/HER2-positive early breast cancer 12 weeks neoadjuvant trastuzumab + pertuzumab (HP) + endocrine therapy vs HP + weekly paclitaxel (1:1); all received adjuvant dual HER2 blockade; standard chemotherapy mandatory if non-pCR, optional after pCR Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: overall survival, event-free survival, invasive disease-free survival, safety Neoadjuvant HP + paclitaxel produced more pCR than chemotherapy-free HP + endocrine therapy (56.4% vs 23.7%). Five-year OS was 97.9% vs 100%, untested; prespecified EFS-DCIS was 94.8% vs 92.1%. A separate exploratory surgery-landmark iDFS analysis was based on 7 events and gave imprecise, directionally conflicting results. The study supports feasibility of response-guided de-escalation but does not establish survival equivalence or safe chemotherapy omission.

records.title: Neoadjuvant HER2+ therapy NMA (Villacampa)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Neoadjuvant therapy · N/A · 2023
records.body: Operable / local-regionally advanced HER2+ breast cancer (neoadjuvant; 46 RCTs, 32 regimens) Network meta-analysis of neoadjuvant anti-HER2 regimens (trastuzumab +/- pertuzumab or TKI; +/- anthracycline; +/- carboplatin) Primary: pathological complete response. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, safety, trial-level pathological-complete-response–survival association Across 46 neoadjuvant RCTs, dual HER2 blockade + chemotherapy improved pCR and network estimates of EFS and OS vs trastuzumab + chemotherapy, with more cardiotoxicity. Anthracycline-containing regimens were not superior to non-anthracycline regimens; carboplatin-containing anthracycline-free regimens ranked favourably. Indirect comparisons and trial heterogeneity do not establish a single preferred regimen.

records.title: APHINITY
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · Adjuvant dual blockade & post-neoadjuvant escalation · III · 2017
records.body: HER2-positive, node-positive or high-risk node-negative early breast cancer Standard adjuvant chemotherapy (anthracycline → taxane, or docetaxel–carboplatin ×6) + trastuzumab (8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W) + pertuzumab (840 mg IV loading then 420 mg Q3W) vs + placebo; anti-HER2 therapy from the first taxane cycle to complete 1 year (max 18 cycles) Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free survival, relapse-free interval, distant relapse-free interval, quality of life, cardiac safety, overall safety Adjuvant pertuzumab modestly improved iDFS vs placebo when added to chemotherapy–trastuzumab (8-year HR 0.77). Descriptive estimates favoured node-positive disease (HR 0.72) but not node-negative disease (HR 1.01); the nodal interaction did not reach statistical significance. OS remained immature and did not reach statistical significance (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.68–1.02; P=.078). Grade ≥3 diarrhoea was about 10% vs 4%.

records.title: APT (Adjuvant Paclitaxel + Trastuzumab)
records.subtitle: HER2+ EBC · De-escalation for low-risk / node-negative disease · II · 2015
records.body: HER2-positive invasive tumours <=3 cm, node-negative, or one nodal micrometastasis after axillary dissection with no further involvement (small, low-risk) (single-arm) Paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV weekly ×12 + trastuzumab (4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg weekly ×12), then trastuzumab monotherapy (6 mg/kg every 3 weeks or weekly) to complete 1 year Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: recurrence-free interval, breast cancer-specific survival, overall survival, biomarkers, safety Weekly paclitaxel–trastuzumab followed by trastuzumab to complete 1 year produced 10-year iDFS 91.3%, recurrence-free interval 96.3%, OS 94.3% and breast cancer-specific survival 98.8% in this single-arm, predominantly stage I cohort. Grade 3 neuropathy occurred in 3.2% and symptomatic heart failure in 0.5%. Without a comparator, the study provides a low-risk outcome benchmark rather than a comparative efficacy estimate.

records.title: H0648g (pivotal trastuzumab)
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2001
records.body: Untreated HER2-overexpressing metastatic breast cancer First-line trastuzumab 4 mg/kg IV loading then 2 mg/kg IV weekly (to progression) added to chemotherapy — doxorubicin (or epirubicin)–cyclophosphamide, or paclitaxel if prior adjuvant anthracycline, Q3W for 6 cycles — vs the same chemotherapy alone Primary: time to disease progression, incidence of adverse effects. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, time to treatment failure, overall survival Adding trastuzumab to first-line chemotherapy prolonged time to progression (7.4 vs 4.6 months), increased objective response (50% vs 32%), and improved OS (25.1 vs 20.3 months). Eight-year survival was 37% vs 23%, with no added cardiotoxicity.

records.title: PERUSE
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2019
records.body: HER2-positive (IHC 3+ or ISH-positive) unresectable locally recurrent or metastatic breast cancer, with no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease except <=2 endocrine lines; stable treated CNS metastases allowed; excluded progression during (neo)adjuvant trastuzumab/lapatinib or recurrence within 6 mo of adjuvant non-hormonal therapy (single-arm) Investigator-selected docetaxel, paclitaxel or nab-paclitaxel weekly or Q3W + pertuzumab 840 mg loading then 420 mg Q3W + trastuzumab 8 mg/kg loading then 6 mg/kg Q3W; to progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or death Primary: safety and tolerability. Secondary: progression-free survival, overall survival, objective response rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of response, time to response, patient-reported outcomes Mature single-arm PERUSE suggests paclitaxel is a practical taxane alternative with first-line pertuzumab-trastuzumab; at 5.7 years' median follow-up, PFS was 20.7 mo and OS 65.3 mo overall. Paclitaxel and docetaxel subgroups had descriptively similar PFS (23.2 vs 19.4 mo) and OS (64.0 vs 66.5 mo); taxane choice was not randomised and no formal comparisons were performed. ORR was 79%. Grade 3+ neutropenia was 5% with paclitaxel vs 15% with docetaxel and febrile neutropenia 1% vs 11%, while grade 3+ diarrhoea was 9% vs 8%; fatal AEs occurred in 2%.

records.title: JBCRG-M06/EMERALD
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2026
records.body: Histologically diagnosed locally advanced or metastatic breast cancer; first-line chemotherapy; HER2-positive; age 20-70 years and no prior cytotoxic chemotherapy for LABC/MBC other than T-DM1 (prior hormonal and/or anti-HER2 therapy for recurrent disease allowed) Eribulin 1.4 mg/m² days 1 and 8 + trastuzumab + pertuzumab, 21-day cycles vs physician-choice taxane (docetaxel 75 mg/m² day 1 or paclitaxel 80 mg/m² days 1, 8 and 15) + trastuzumab + pertuzumab, 21-day cycles; continued until progression, unmanageable toxicity or consent withdrawal (recommended minimum six cycles) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, PFS and OS by ctDNA PIK3CA mutation status, PFS and OS by ctDNA HER2 amplification status At final analysis, median OS exceeded 6 years with eribulin or taxane plus trastuzumab-pertuzumab, with no significant difference between arms; OS was a secondary endpoint the study was not powered to test. Median OS 78.5 mo (95% CI 64.3-NR) eribulin vs NR taxane; HR 1.25 (95% CI 0.92-1.71), log-rank P = 0.19; 60-month OS 59.7% vs 65.2%, numerically favouring taxane (median follow-up 48.6 mo). The primary PFS non-inferiority was reported previously (median 14.0 vs 12.9 mo, HR 0.95). In the ctDNA subset (313 of 446), PIK3CAm+ was poor prognostic (median OS 43.2 mo vs NR; 60-month 38.5% vs 67.4%) and HER2 amp+ was associated with longer OS (60-month 64.7% vs 54.9%), without treatment interaction; these analyses were unpowered and ctDNA testing incomplete. HER2 amp+ was less frequent with eribulin (53.5% vs 66.2%).

records.title: KL166-III-06
records.subtitle: HER2+ MBC · Second-line metastatic disease · III · 2026
records.body: HER2-positive unresectable/metastatic breast cancer; progression after ≥1 trastuzumab-based regimen and prior taxane; HER2 IHC 3+ (>10% of invasive tumor cells with strong, complete, uniform membrane staining) or IHC 2+ with FISH confirmation; age 18-75 years; excluded prior HER2-targeted ADC with microtubule inhibitor payload, prior trastuzumab discontinuation for AEs, severe corneal epithelial disease, active CNS metastases or spinal cord compression, clinically active ILD Trastuzumab botidotin 4.8 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks vs trastuzumab emtansine 3.6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks; both until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or other protocol-specified discontinuation Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, clinical benefit rate, duration of response, safety Trastuzumab botidotin significantly prolonged PFS vs trastuzumab emtansine in HER2-positive advanced BC previously treated with trastuzumab and a taxane, with a distinct safety profile. The superiority boundary was crossed at the interim analysis; in this descriptive final PFS analysis (median follow-up 14.9 mo), median PFS was 11.1 vs 4.4 mo (HR 0.39, 95% CI 0.30-0.51; nominal P<.0001). ORR 76.9% vs 53.0%; median DoR 12.2 vs 5.7 mo. OS immature (17.5% maturity; HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.38-1.03). Comparator was not trastuzumab deruxtecan; China-only enrollment. Grade ≥3 TEAEs 69.8% vs 63.7%. Botidotin caused frequent ocular toxicity: corneal disorder 92.9% (grade ≥3 37.9%), dry eye 61.5%, grade ≥3 blurred vision 20.9%; corneal disorder/dry eye caused no discontinuations. Grade ≥3 platelet decrease 45.6% with emtansine. No on-treatment deaths vs 3 with emtansine (all unrelated).

records.body: Previously untreated, operable, biopsy-confirmed stage II-III non-inflammatory invasive TNBC (ER/PR <=10%; HER2 IHC 0-1+ or non-amplified), with adequate marrow, renal, hepatic and cardiac function. Grade >=2 neuropathy or bevacizumab contraindications were excluded. The long-term analysis used the 443 patients who started protocol treatment Weekly paclitaxel → dose-dense doxorubicin–cyclophosphamide (ddAC) as neoadjuvant backbone; 2×2 factorial ± carboplatin AUC 6 IV Q3W ×4 and/or bevacizumab 10 mg/kg IV Q2W ×9 Primary: breast pathological complete response rate, breast-and-axillary pathological complete response rate. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival, distant recurrence-free interval, residual cancer burden, treatment delivery, safety Adding carboplatin increased pathological complete response in breast and axilla (54% vs 41%, P=.003), but no EFS or OS improvement was established at 7.9 years in this phase 2 trial, which was not powered for survival. Pathological complete response was strongly prognostic for patients, but the randomized treatment effect did not establish a survival benefit; correlative immune findings were exploratory.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2015;33:13-21   J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1323-1334 long-term outcomes 35044810

records.title: BrighTNess
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · III · 2018
records.body: Neoadjuvant stage II–III triple-negative breast cancer All arms: weekly paclitaxel ×12 then AC ×4. Randomization 2:1:1 to carboplatin AUC6 every 3 weeks ×4 + veliparib, carboplatin alone, or paclitaxel alone before AC Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: event-free survival, overall survival Carboplatin increased pCR and improved EFS versus paclitaxel alone, whereas veliparib added no pCR benefit beyond carboplatin. The EFS comparison was secondary, so the data support carboplatin's contribution without a confirmatory survival claim for veliparib.

records.title: TMC TNBC Platinum Trial (Gupta)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-based regimens) · III · 2026
records.body: Women aged 18-80 with previously untreated invasive TNBC, stage II or locally advanced stage III, ECOG 0-1 and adequate organ function; metastatic disease was excluded Weekly carboplatin AUC 2 + weekly paclitaxel ×8 weeks → anthracycline (doxorubicin or epirubicin)–cyclophosphamide Q3W ×4 (neoadjuvant) vs the same taxane–anthracycline backbone without carboplatin Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, pathological complete response rate Adding carboplatin missed the primary EFS endpoint (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.62–1.03, P=.081). OS and pathological complete response favoured carboplatin only in secondary analyses, and the menopausal-status interaction and premenopausal subgroup estimates are hypothesis-generating rather than proof that benefit is confined by menopausal status.

records.title: KEYNOTE-522
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2020
records.body: High-risk stage II–III triple-negative breast cancer (neoadjuvant/adjuvant) Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W + carboplatin–paclitaxel ×4 cycles → pembrolizumab + AC/EC ×4 cycles, then adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W ×9 cycles vs placebo + the same chemotherapy backbone → adjuvant placebo Primary: pathological complete response rate, event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, alternative pathological complete response rates, distant progression-free survival, distant recurrence-free survival, residual cancer burden, safety Adding pembrolizumab to neoadjuvant chemotherapy, then continuing it adjuvantly, increased pCR (64.8% vs 51.2%). At the fourth interim analysis, it improved EFS (36-month 84.5% vs 76.8%; HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.48–0.82, P<.001). At the final OS analysis, 5-year OS was 86.6% vs 81.7% (P=.002), and updated EFS had HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.51–0.83). Grade ≥3 immune-mediated events were 13.0% vs 1.5%, and treatment-related deaths 0.5% vs 0.3%.

records.title: NeoPACT
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · II · 2024
records.body: Stage I-III triple-negative breast cancer (neoadjuvant; single-arm) (single-arm) Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks + carboplatin–docetaxel ×6 cycles (anthracycline-free) Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: residual cancer burden, event-free survival, safety, biomarkers Anthracycline-free carboplatin–docetaxel plus pembrolizumab produced pCR in 58% and 3-year EFS of 86% in this single-arm phase 2 study. Outcomes differed strongly by pCR, but without a randomized comparator the regimen cannot be judged equivalent or superior to an anthracycline-containing standard.

records.title: GeparNuevo (durvalumab)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy · II · 2019
records.body: Early triple-negative breast cancer (cT1b-cT4a-d) Durvalumab 1.5 g IV Q4W (0.75 g window dose 2 weeks before chemotherapy) + nab-paclitaxel → dose-dense epirubicin–cyclophosphamide (neoadjuvant) vs placebo + the same chemotherapy backbone; no adjuvant checkpoint continuation Primary: pathological complete response rate. Secondary: invasive disease-free survival, distant disease-free survival, overall survival, alternative pathological complete response rates, clinical outcomes, surgical outcomes Adding neoadjuvant durvalumab did not improve pathological complete response (53.4% vs 44.2%; OR 1.45, P=.287). Long-term secondary iDFS, distant-DFS and OS estimates favoured durvalumab, but the small phase 2 study provides no confirmatory survival evidence; the apparent response–survival discordance remains hypothesis-generating.

records.title: CREATE-X (JBCRG-04)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — post-neoadjuvant therapy (residual disease) · III · 2017
records.body: HER2-negative (TNBC and HR+) residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant anthracycline/taxane Adjuvant capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily, days 1–14 Q3W ×8 cycles vs observation (standard postsurgical therapy without capecitabine) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety Adjuvant capecitabine improved DFS and OS vs observation in HER2-negative residual invasive disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy. TNBC subgroup estimates favoured capecitabine (DFS HR 0.58; OS HR 0.52) but were not a primary test; sequencing with other post-neoadjuvant agents was not evaluated.

records.title: RJBC-1501
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Early triple negative breast cancer — adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin) · III · 2026
records.body: Patients with completely resected early-stage TNBC eligible for adjuvant epirubicin-cyclophosphamide followed by a taxane, with no metastatic disease. The bound article does not provide a more granular harmonized stage/exclusion description beyond the protocol-defined postoperative population Adjuvant EC x4 → taxane + carboplatin (AUC-2 weekly or AUC-5–6 q3wk with docetaxel) vs EC x4 → taxane alone Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: distant disease-free survival, overall survival, toxicity Adding carboplatin to adjuvant epirubicin–cyclophosphamide then taxane improved the primary DFS endpoint (3-year 93.1% vs 89.8%; HR 0.66, P=.034). Distant DFS and OS also favoured carboplatin as secondary outcomes; grade 3–4 haematologic toxicity increased.

records.title: IMpassion130
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated metastatic/unresectable locally advanced TNBC (PD-L1 IC+ subgroup primary) Atezolizumab 840 mg IV days 1 & 15 of a 28-day cycle + nab-paclitaxel vs placebo + nab-paclitaxel; to progression Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, response duration, quality of life, safety Atezolizumab plus nab-paclitaxel improved ITT PFS (HR 0.80, P=.002), but statistical significance was not reached for final ITT OS (HR 0.87, P=.077). The PD-L1-positive OS estimate (25.4 vs 17.9 months; HR 0.67) remained descriptive and cannot support a confirmatory subgroup survival claim.

records.title: KEYNOTE-355
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2020
records.body: Untreated locally recurrent inoperable/metastatic TNBC (PD-L1 CPS ≥10 subgroup) Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) + chemotherapy (nab-paclitaxel, paclitaxel, or gemcitabine–carboplatin) vs placebo + the same chemotherapy Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, response duration, disease control, safety Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy improved PFS and OS in the PD-L1 CPS ≥10 population (OS 23.0 vs 16.1 months; HR 0.73, P=.0185). Benefit below CPS 10 was not established, and without a reported treatment-by-PD-L1 interaction the nested CPS populations do not prove benefit was confined to CPS ≥10.

records.title: IMpassion131
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated advanced TNBC (PD-L1 IC+ primary analysis) Atezolizumab 840 mg IV on days 1 and 15 of each 28-day cycle + paclitaxel 90 mg/m² IV on days 1, 8 and 15 versus placebo + the same paclitaxel; continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, quality of life, safety Atezolizumab plus solvent-based paclitaxel did not improve PFS in PD-L1-positive disease (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.60–1.12, P=.20), and OS numerically favoured placebo in both PD-L1-positive and ITT analyses. The trial does not establish corticosteroid or taxane formulation as the cause and does not itself support a regulatory or cross-trial inference.

records.title: ASCENT-04 (KEYNOTE-D19)
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line chemoimmunotherapy (PD-L1-positive) · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated PD-L1+ (CPS ≥10) locally advanced/metastatic TNBC Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 & 8 of a 21-day cycle + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) vs chemotherapy (physician's choice — taxane or gemcitabine–carboplatin) + pembrolizumab Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, response duration, time to response, quality of life, safety Sacituzumab govitecan plus pembrolizumab improved PFS versus chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab in first-line PD-L1 CPS ≥10 mTNBC (11.2 vs 7.8 months; HR 0.65, P<.001) and prolonged response duration. OS was immature and not formally tested, so the result is PFS-led pending survival maturity.

records.title: ASCENT-03
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line TROP2 ADCs (immunotherapy-ineligible) · III · 2025
records.body: Untreated advanced TNBC ineligible for PD-(L)1 inhibitors (PD-L1-negative or prior IO) Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 & 8 of a 21-day cycle vs chemotherapy (physician's choice — paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, or gemcitabine–carboplatin) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, response duration, time to response, safety First-line sacituzumab govitecan improved PFS versus single-agent chemotherapy in checkpoint-inhibitor-ineligible mTNBC (9.7 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.62, P<.001) and prolonged response duration. OS was descriptive without formal testing. Grade ≥3 neutropenia was frequent in both arms (43% vs 41%); adverse-event discontinuation was less frequent with sacituzumab govitecan (4% vs 12%).

records.title: TROPION-Breast02
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — first-line TROP2 ADCs (immunotherapy-ineligible) · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated advanced TNBC for whom immunotherapy was not an option Datopotamab deruxtecan (Dato-DXd) 6 mg/kg IV Q3W vs investigator's choice chemotherapy (paclitaxel, nab-paclitaxel, carboplatin, eribulin, or capecitabine) Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, response duration, disease control, quality of life, safety Datopotamab deruxtecan improved PFS (HR 0.57) and OS (HR 0.79) versus chemotherapy in checkpoint-inhibitor-ineligible mTNBC. ORR was higher, and adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis occurred in 3%, including one grade 5 event. No head-to-head comparison with another ADC was performed.

records.title: ASCENT
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — pretreated disease (antibody-drug conjugates) · III · 2021
records.body: Relapsed/refractory metastatic TNBC, ≥2 prior chemotherapy lines (no active brain metastases) Sacituzumab govitecan 10 mg/kg IV days 1 & 8 of a 21-day cycle vs single-agent chemotherapy (physician's choice — eribulin, vinorelbine, capecitabine, or gemcitabine) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, response duration, time to response, safety Sacituzumab govitecan improved PFS, OS and response versus chemotherapy in the brain-metastasis-negative primary population; the final ITT analysis including patients with brain metastases confirmed an OS benefit (11.8 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.42–0.63). Grade ≥3 neutropenia and diarrhoea were common; this trial did not compare first-line regimens.

records.title: DESTINY-Breast04
records.subtitle: Triple Negative BC · Advanced/metastatic TNBC — pretreated disease (antibody-drug conjugates) · III · 2022
records.body: Pretreated HER2-low metastatic breast cancer (exploratory HR-negative/TNBC cohort, n=58) Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) 5.4 mg/kg IV Q3W vs physician's choice chemotherapy (eribulin, capecitabine, gemcitabine, paclitaxel, or nab-paclitaxel) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, response duration, safety In the exploratory HR-negative cohort of 58 patients, T-DXd had median PFS of 8.5 vs 2.9 months (HR 0.46) and median OS of 18.2 vs 8.3 months (HR 0.48). This small subgroup does not independently establish efficacy for TNBC.

records.title: OlympiA
records.subtitle: BRCA · Adjuvant therapy · III · 2021
records.body: Germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic/likely pathogenic variant, high-risk HER2-negative early breast cancer after definitive local therapy and >=6 cycles of neoadjuvant or adjuvant anthracycline/taxane chemotherapy; TNBC required residual disease post-neoadjuvant or node-positive/T2+ post-adjuvant; HR-positive required >=4 positive nodes post-adjuvant or residual disease with CPS+EG score >=3 post-neoadjuvant Olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily for 1 year vs matching placebo orally twice daily for 1 year, after (neo)adjuvant chemotherapy, surgery and radiotherapy if indicated; concurrent endocrine therapy >=5 years in hormone receptor-positive disease Primary: invasive disease-free survival. Secondary: distant disease-free survival, overall survival, contralateral invasive breast cancer incidence, contralateral noninvasive breast cancer incidence, ovarian cancer incidence, fallopian tube cancer incidence, safety At the prespecified second interim analysis (median follow-up 3.5 years, ITT), 1 year of adjuvant olaparib significantly improved overall survival vs placebo: HR 0.68 (98.5% CI 0.47-0.97; P=0.009, boundary P<0.015); 4-year OS 89.8% vs 86.4%. Sustained benefit in IDFS (HR 0.63; 4-year 82.7% vs 75.4%) and DDFS (HR 0.61; 86.5% vs 79.1%). Grade >=3 AEs 24.5% vs 11.3%; grade >=3 anemia 8.7% (olaparib); AML/MDS 0.2% vs 0.3% with no new cases since primary analysis, though longer follow-up is needed

records.title: TNT (CRUK/07/012)
records.subtitle: BRCA · Advanced disease · III · 2018
records.body: Adults with measurable, confirmed advanced breast cancer unsuitable for local therapy; ER-, PgR- and HER2-negative (TNBC) primary invasive breast cancer, or any receptor status if known germline BRCA1/2 mutation carrier; metastatic or recurrent locally advanced disease Carboplatin AUC 6 IV day 1 of a 3-weekly cycle x 6 cycles vs docetaxel 100 mg/m2 IV day 1 of a 3-weekly cycle x 6 cycles; up to two further cycles if responding/tolerated; crossover to six cycles of the alternative drug at progression or toxicity discontinuation Primary: Objective response rate. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Overall survival, Response to crossover treatment, Tolerability, Safety Carboplatin was not superior to docetaxel in unselected advanced TNBC: ORR 31.4% vs 34.0% (P=0.66); median PFS 3.1 vs 4.4 months; median OS 12.8 vs 12.0 months (no difference). In prespecified subgroup analysis, germline BRCA1/2 carriers had higher carboplatin response (ORR 68% vs 33.3%; interaction P=0.01) and longer PFS (6.8 vs 4.4 months; interaction P=0.002), with OS interpretation confounded by crossover. BRCA1 methylation, BRCA1 mRNA-low and high Myriad HRD score did not predict platinum benefit. Docetaxel caused more grade 3/4 AEs (SAEs 174 vs 102); one death (pulmonary embolism) was possibly carboplatin-related

records.title: EMBRACA
records.subtitle: BRCA · Advanced disease · III · 2018
records.body: Germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative advanced breast cancer (≤3 prior chemotherapy lines) Talazoparib 1 mg orally once daily vs physician’s-choice single-agent capecitabine, eribulin, gemcitabine or vinorelbine, each until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, clinical benefit, response duration, quality of life, safety Talazoparib improved PFS vs physician-choice chemotherapy (8.6 vs 5.6 months; HR 0.54, 95% CI 0.41–0.71, P<.001). Statistical significance was not reached for final OS (19.3 vs 19.5 months; HR 0.848, 95% CI 0.670–1.073, P=.17). Time to definitive deterioration in global health status/quality of life was longer (26.3 vs 6.7 months; HR 0.385), while grade 3–4 haematologic adverse events were more frequent (56.6% vs 38.9%).

records.title: OlympiAD
records.subtitle: BRCA · Advanced disease · III · 2017
records.body: Germline BRCA-mutated HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer (≤2 prior chemotherapy lines) Olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily vs physician’s-choice single-agent capecitabine, eribulin or vinorelbine, each until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival 2, objective response rate, response duration, quality of life, safety Olaparib improved PFS (7.0 vs 4.2 months; HR 0.58, P<.001) and response vs physician-choice chemotherapy in germline BRCA-mutated, HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. Final OS improvement was not established overall (HR 0.90), and the first-line metastatic subgroup finding was exploratory; platinum was not a comparator.

records.title: PLUS trial (van Tinteren et al.)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2002
records.body: Suspected operable NSCLC undergoing preoperative staging Conventional workup vs conventional workup + whole-body FDG-PET Futile thoracotomy (surgery not resulting in cure) Adding PET to conventional staging reduced futile thoracotomies from 41% to 21% (relative reduction ~51%) by detecting unsuspected advanced/metastatic disease; established PET in preoperative NSCLC staging.

records.title: Fischer et al. (PET-CT staging)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2009
records.body: Newly diagnosed or highly suspected NSCLC; referred for preoperative staging and considered operable after conventional staging (history, examination, blood test, contrast-enhanced CT of chest and upper abdomen, bronchoscopy); age 18 to 80 years; excluded type 1 diabetes, another malignant condition, confirmed distant metastases, known claustrophobia, estimated FEV1 <30% after surgery Conventional staging + 18F-FDG PET–CT (400 MBq IV) → further invasive diagnostic procedures (mediastinoscopy, endoscopic or endobronchial ultrasonography) vs conventional staging + invasive diagnostic procedures alone; mediastinoscopy mandatory in both groups; after consensus staging, stage I–IIB offered surgery, stage IIIA (N2)–IV offered chemotherapy with or without radiotherapy Primary: number of futile thoracotomies. Secondary: total number of thoracotomies, justified thoracotomies, diagnostic accuracy, sensitivity, overall survival, relapse Adding PET–CT to preoperative staging of NSCLC reduced both total and futile thoracotomies but did not affect overall mortality. Thoracotomy was performed in 60 (61%) of 98 vs 73 (80%) of 91 patients (P=0.004). Futile thoracotomies were 21/60 (35%) vs 38/73 (52%) of thoracotomies (P=0.05), or 21/98 (21%) vs 38/91 (42%) of randomized patients. Justified thoracotomies were similar (39 [40%] vs 35 [38%]). After excluding PET–CT-arm patients who did not undergo PET–CT or who declined further procedures, futile thoracotomies were 13/52 (25%) vs 38/73 (52%) (P=0.002). Survival did not differ significantly (median 31 vs 49 mo; P=0.29). The trial closed early at 189 patients because of slow accrual (215 per group planned), and P values were unadjusted. Excluding thoracotomies deemed futile because of recurrence or death within 12 months, futile rates were virtually the same (28% vs 29%; P=1.00). One death per group was attributable to complications after primary surgery.
records.keywords: Fischer et al. N Engl J Med 2009;361:32-39

records.title: Maziak et al. (PET-CT staging)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · N/A · 2009
records.body: Clinical stage I-IIIA NSCLC considered resectable Conventional staging vs conventional + PET-CT Correct upstaging / disease stage PET-CT more often correctly upstaged disease and identified patients who would not benefit from surgery, refining selection for thoracotomy.

records.title: ASTER
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · III · 2010
records.body: Potentially resectable (suspected) NSCLC; preoperative mediastinal nodal staging; guideline indication for nodal sampling (mediastinal nodes short axis ≥10 mm, PET-positive mediastinal or hilar nodes, or centrally located tumour) and able to undergo resection; excluded proven distant metastasis, irresectable disease, small peripheral tumours without enlarged or PET-positive intrathoracic nodes, concurrent malignancy, or technical contraindication to EUS, EBUS or surgical staging Surgical staging alone (mediastinoscopy, plus left parasternal mediastinotomy or video-assisted thoracoscopy if deemed necessary) vs endosonography (EUS-FNA then EBUS-TBNA under moderate sedation) → surgical staging if no nodal metastases found; in both arms thoracotomy with complete lymph node dissection if no mediastinal metastases after surgical staging, N2/N3 or T4 disease referred for multimodality therapy Primary: sensitivity for mediastinal nodal (N2/N3) metastases. Secondary: unnecessary thoracotomy rate, complication rate of preoperative staging procedures, detection rate of locally advanced disease, rate of avoided mediastinoscopies, detection rate of nodal metastases by endosonography alone vs surgical staging, interobserver agreement of EUS/EBUS cytology, negative predictive value Among patients with (suspected) NSCLC, endosonography followed by surgical staging gave greater sensitivity for mediastinal nodal metastases and fewer unnecessary thoracotomies than surgical staging alone. Sensitivity (ITT, multiple imputation) 94% (62/66) vs 79% (41/52), P=.02; NPV 93% vs 86%, P=.18. Unnecessary thoracotomy 9 of 123 (7%) vs 21 of 118 (18%), P=.02; surgical staging was avoided in 58 of 123 (47%). Endosonography alone did not differ significantly from surgical staging in sensitivity (85% vs 79%, P=.47). Positive EUS/EBUS results were not surgically verified, and all procedures were done in tertiary referral centres. Overall complication rates did not differ (6 of 123 [5%] vs 7 of 118 [6%], P=.78); complications followed 1 of 123 endosonographies (1%) vs 7 of 118 surgical stagings (6%), P=.03. Persistent hoarseness from recurrent nerve palsy was the most common adverse event.

records.title: MEDIASTrial
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Staging · III · 2023
records.body: Proven or suspected resectable NSCLC without distant metastasis; mediastinal staging indicated by central, FDG-non-avid or peripheral >3 cm tumour or cN1-3 on CT/FDG-PET; tumour-negative N2-3 cytology on systematic endosonography of stations 4R-7-4L plus all CT-enlarged (>10 mm) and/or FDG-avid (SUV >2.5) stations; excluded neoadjuvant treatment, bulky cN2-3, and highly suspicious nodes (SUV >5 plus at least three endosonographic malignant criteria) beyond surgical reach Immediate anatomic lung tumour resection with mediastinal lymph node dissection (at least three stations incl. subcarinal) vs confirmatory cervical videomediastinoscopy (sampling 4R-7-4L, plus 2R for right-sided tumours; at least four surgical biopsies or entire node per station) → lung tumour resection with lymph node dissection if no nodal metastases Primary: unforeseen N2 rate. Secondary: major morbidity, 30-day mortality, quality of life, costs, minor morbidity, mediastinoscopy nodal metastasis detection rate, interval from endosonography to resection Based on the prespecified 8% noninferiority margin for unforeseen N2 (uN2), confirmatory mediastinoscopy after negative systematic endosonography can be omitted in resectable NSCLC with an indication for mediastinal staging. ITT uN2 8.8% (15/171) with immediate resection vs 7.7% (12/155) with mediastinoscopy first (difference 1.03%; upper 95% CI 7.2%; P noninferior = .0144); per-protocol 9.0% vs 8.2% (upper limit 7.3%). Mediastinoscopy detected N2-3 in 8.0% (14/175). In the exploratory cN1 subgroup uN2 was 13.6% vs 7.0%; the authors suggest cN1 may deserve special consideration. Major morbidity plus 30-day mortality 12.9% vs 15.4% (P = .4940); 30-day mortality 2 (1%) vs 5 (3%). Mediastinoscopy caused major complications in 3 patients (1.7%) and was followed by one sudden death 10 days later; mean endosonography-to-resection interval 28 vs 38 days.
records.keywords: Bousema et al. J Clin Oncol 2023;41:3805-3815

records.title: IALT (International Adjuvant Lung Cancer Trial)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · III · 2004
records.body: Pathologically documented non-small-cell lung cancer; completely resected pathological stage I, II or III (1986 AJCC), adjuvant setting, with each centre choosing which stages to include; randomized within 60 days after surgery, age 18–75 yr; excluded: previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy, contraindications to chemotherapy, previous cancer other than nonmelanoma skin cancer or carcinoma in situ of the cervix Cisplatin-based chemotherapy for 3 or 4 cycles, regimen chosen by each centre: cisplatin 80 mg/m² ×4 cycles (days 1, 22, 43, 64), 100 mg/m² ×3 (days 1, 29, 57) or ×4 cycles (days 1, 29, 57, 85), or 120 mg/m² ×3 cycles (days 1, 29, 71), plus etoposide 100 mg/m² per day on days 1 to 3 of each cisplatin cycle, vinorelbine 30 mg/m² weekly to last cisplatin dose, or vindesine 3 mg/m² or vinblastine 4 mg/m² weekly days 1 to 29 then every 2 weeks after day 43 to last cisplatin dose; started within 60 days after surgery and 14 days after randomization → postoperative radiotherapy (≤60 Gy to mediastinal nodes) per centre policy (never, pN2 only, or pN1 and pN2) vs observation, with the same centre-policy postoperative radiotherapy after randomization Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, second primary cancers, adverse effects, lung cancer mortality, non-lung cancer mortality, local recurrence, distant metastases Long-term follow-up confirmed significant efficacy of adjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy at 5 years, but results differed beyond 5 years. At 7.5-yr median follow-up, whole-period OS was not significantly improved (HR 0.91, 95% CI 0.81–1.02; P=.10): HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.76–0.97) in the first 5 yr vs 1.45 (95% CI 1.02–2.07) thereafter (interaction P=.006). At the primary analysis (median follow-up 56 mo), 5-yr OS was 44.5% vs 40.4% with observation and 5-yr DFS 39.4% vs 34.3%. At 7.5 yr, DFS HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.78–0.98; P=.02). Non-lung cancer death HR 1.34 (95% CI 0.99–1.81; P=.06); second malignancies not increased (HR 0.89). Interactions with predefined factors were not significant at the primary analysis. Accrual stopped early at 1867 randomized vs 3300 required. 7.8% of the chemotherapy group never received it. Among 851 treated, 7 (0.8%) died of chemotherapy toxicity, mainly bone marrow aplasia; grade 4 toxicity 22.6%, mainly neutropenia (17.5%).
records.keywords: Arriagada et al. N Engl J Med 2004;350:351-360   Arriagada et al. J Clin Oncol 2010;28:35-42  19933916

records.title: JBR.10 (NCIC CTG)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · III · 2005
records.body: Completely resected pathological stage IB (T2N0) or II (T1-2N1) NSCLC after lobectomy or pneumonectomy with specified nodal sampling. Excluded incomplete staging/resection, station 10 or central mediastinal nodal disease, mixed histology, T3 tumours, diffuse/multifocal bronchioloalveolar carcinoma, or recent other cancer Cisplatin 50 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8 every 4 weeks for 4 cycles plus vinorelbine 25 mg/m2 weekly for 16 weeks (initially 30 mg/m2 before August 1995 amendment) vs Observation Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Relapse-free survival; Safety; Quality of life Adjuvant cisplatin-vinorelbine improved OS versus observation: 5-year OS 69% vs 54%, median 94 vs 73 months, HR 0.69. Grade 3-4 neutropenia occurred in 73%, febrile neutropenia in 7%, and 2 treatment-related deaths (0.8%) occurred.

records.title: ANITA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · III · 2006
records.body: Histologically proven primary NSCLC other than bronchoalveolar carcinoma; pathological stage I (T2N0 only), II, or IIIA by 1986 TNM; age 18-75 years; complete R0 resection. Excluded concurrent malignancy except adequately treated nonmelanoma skin cancer or cervical carcinoma in situ, and other previous primary tumours Vinorelbine 30 mg/m² days 1,8,15,22 every 4 weeks up to 16 doses plus cisplatin 100 mg/m² days 1,29,57,85; optional postoperative RT by center policy vs Observation; optional postoperative RT by center policy Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Disease-free survival; Safety Adjuvant cisplatin-vinorelbine improved OS versus observation: median 65.7 vs 43.7 months, HR 0.80, with an 8.6-point absolute 5-year benefit; DFS also improved (HR 0.76). Among 368 treated patients, grade 3-4 neutropenia occurred in 85%, febrile neutropenia in 9%, and 7 treatment-related deaths occurred.

records.title: LACE (Lung Adjuvant Cisplatin Evaluation) meta-analysis
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · N/A · 2008
records.body: Completely resected NSCLC; postoperative adjuvant setting, trial entry stage I–IIIA or I–III (JBR10: pT2pN0 or pT1-2pN1); randomized trials of >300 patients after the 1995 NSCLC meta-analysis comparing cisplatin-based chemotherapy vs none (or sequential chemotherapy plus postoperative RT vs RT alone); excluded: non-cisplatin or preoperative chemotherapy, concurrent chemoradiotherapy, incomplete resection or neoadjuvant chemotherapy Postoperative cisplatin-based chemotherapy, three or four planned cycles, cisplatin with vinorelbine, vindesine, vinblastine or etoposide, or with mitomycin plus ifosfamide or vinblastine (doses per trial), with optional sequential postoperative RT per trial vs no chemotherapy (RT per trial policy) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: disease-free survival, lung cancer-related deaths, non-lung cancer-related deaths, treatment delivery, toxicity Postoperative cisplatin-based chemotherapy significantly improved survival in completely resected NSCLC. At median follow-up 5.2 years, OS HR 0.89 (95% CI, 0.82 to 0.96; P = .005), 5-year absolute benefit 5.4%; DFS HR 0.84 (95% CI, 0.78 to 0.91), 5-year benefit 5.8%; no significant heterogeneity among trials. In preplanned exploratory analyses, benefit varied with stage (trend P = .04; stage IA HR 1.40, 95% CI 0.95 to 2.06), no longer significant after excluding stage IA; effect increased with better PS and may be detrimental with PS 2. Cisplatin-vinorelbine was only marginally better than other combinations (P = .11 for OS), and its effect could not be separated from higher cisplatin dose. Grade 3–4 toxicity 66% (1,190 treated patients, four trials), grade 4 32%; 19 chemotherapy-related deaths (0.9%). Non-lung cancer deaths increased (HR 1.36; 95% CI, 1.10 to 1.69), mainly in the first 6 months.

records.title: CALGB 9633
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · III · 2008
records.body: Completely resected pathological T2N0 stage IB NSCLC after lobectomy or pneumonectomy; no planned adjuvant radiotherapy Paclitaxel 200 mg/m2 IV over 3 hours plus carboplatin AUC 6 IV over 45-60 minutes every 3 weeks for 4 cycles vs Observation Primary: Overall survival Secondary: Disease-free survival; Treatment delivery and toxicity Adjuvant paclitaxel-carboplatin did not improve OS in resected stage IB disease: median 95 vs 78 months, HR 0.83 (90% CI 0.64-1.08); DFS also did not improve. An unplanned tumour >=4 cm subgroup suggested benefit (OS HR 0.69) but is hypothesis-generating. Grade 3 and grade 4 maximum toxicity occurred in 41% and 28%; there were no treatment deaths.

records.title: NSCLC Meta-analysis Collaborative Group
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant chemotherapy - HISTORIC evidence · N/A · 2014
records.body: Resectable NSCLC, mainly clinical stage IB–IIIA (93%), predominantly squamous (50%) or adenocarcinoma (29%); trials of chemotherapy-naive patients suitable for surgery without previous malignancy; IPD pooled across 15 randomised trials accruing 1965–2013 Preoperative chemotherapy (2–3 cycles; platinum-based in all trials but one) then surgery vs surgery alone; eight trials planned postoperative radiotherapy in both arms, and five gave additional postoperative chemotherapy to responders Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Recurrence-free survival, Time to locoregional recurrence, Time to distant recurrence, Cause-specific survival, Complete resection rate, Overall resection rate, Postoperative mortality Preoperative chemotherapy significantly improves overall survival, time to distant recurrence and recurrence-free survival in resectable NSCLC (mainly stage IB–IIIA; 92% of all randomised patients) and is a valid treatment option for most of these patients. OS HR 0·87 (95% CI 0·78–0·96, p=0·007), a 13% reduction in relative risk of death and 5% absolute gain at 5 years (40%→45%); RFS HR 0·85 (0·76–0·94, p=0·002), 6% absolute gain; time to distant recurrence HR 0·69 (0·58–0·82, p<0·0001), 10% absolute gain; locoregional recurrence not significant (HR 0·88, 0·73–1·07, p=0·20). No clear effect difference by regimen, scheduling, radiotherapy or patient characteristics. Benefit on a similar scale to postoperative chemotherapy, though formal indirect comparison was difficult. No excess of early mortality from deferred surgery; toxic effects could not be assessed at patient level

records.title: IMpower010
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · III · 2021
records.body: Completely resected NSCLC, stage IB (tumours ≥4 cm) to IIIA (T2–3 N0, T1–3 N1, T1–3 N2, T4 N0–1; UICC/AJCC 7th edition); adjuvant setting after one to four cycles of cisplatin-based chemotherapy, without recurrence at randomisation; no biomarker selection at entry (EGFR/ALK-positive tumours allowed), with primary analyses in the stage II–IIIA and PD-L1 TC ≥1% (SP263) subsets; negative-margin resection with protocol-specified mediastinal lymph node dissection or sampling required Investigator-choice cisplatin-based adjuvant chemotherapy (cisplatin 75 mg/m² plus vinorelbine, docetaxel, gemcitabine or pemetrexed; up to four 21-day cycles) → atezolizumab 1200 mg IV day 1 of each 21-day cycle for up to 16 cycles (or 1 year) vs best supportive care (observation and regular scans for disease recurrence) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, disease-free survival in stage II–IIIA PD-L1 TC ≥50%, 3-year disease-free survival rate, 5-year disease-free survival rate, safety Adjuvant atezolizumab after chemotherapy improved DFS vs best supportive care in resected stage II–IIIA NSCLC, with pronounced benefit when PD-L1 TC ≥1%, and no new safety signals. DFS significance in stage II–IIIA PD-L1 TC ≥1% and all stage II–IIIA was established at the 32.2-mo interim; at the DFS final analysis (≥5-year follow-up), HRs were 0.70 (95% CI 0.55–0.91; 5-yr DFS 53.2% vs 42.7%) and 0.83 (0.69–1.00). ITT stage IB–IIIA DFS did not cross the significance boundary (HR 0.85, 0.71–1.01). At the second OS interim, OS remained immature and not formally tested (ITT HR 0.97, 0.78–1.22). PD-L1 TC ≥50%: DFS HR 0.48 (0.32–0.72), OS HR 0.47 (0.28–0.77); TC 1–49% DFS HR 0.91 (0.65–1.27); earlier post-hoc TC <1% HR 0.97 (0.72–1.31). Grade 3–4 AEs occurred in 22% vs 12%; atezolizumab-related grade 3–4 AEs in 11% and grade 5 in 1% (myocarditis, interstitial lung disease, multiple organ dysfunction syndrome, AML); 18% discontinued atezolizumab for AEs.

records.title: KEYNOTE-091 (PEARLS)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · III · 2022
records.body: Completely resected (R0) NSCLC of any histology; stage IB (tumours ≥4 cm), II or IIIA (AJCC 7th edition), adjuvant setting after optional adjuvant chemotherapy (considered for IB, strongly recommended for II–IIIA; ≤4 cycles); any PD-L1 TPS, central PD-L1 status required; disease-free on imaging before randomisation; excluded prior neoadjuvant/adjuvant radiotherapy, HIV, active hepatitis B/C, active autoimmune disease needing treatment within 2 years Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks vs saline placebo IV every 3 weeks, each for up to 18 administrations (approximately 1 year) or until recurrence, new malignancy or unacceptable toxicity; triple-blind, no crossover Primary: disease-free survival in the overall population, disease-free survival in the PD-L1 TPS ≥50% population. Secondary: disease-free survival in the PD-L1 TPS ≥1% population, overall survival in the overall population, overall survival in the PD-L1 TPS ≥50% population, overall survival in the PD-L1 TPS ≥1% population, lung cancer-specific survival, safety Adjuvant pembrolizumab significantly improved disease-free survival vs placebo in completely resected, PD-L1-unselected stage IB–IIIA NSCLC, without new safety signals (second interim analysis; median follow-up 35.6 mo). Overall population: median DFS 53.6 vs 42.0 mo; HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.63–0.91), p=0.0014. The co-primary DFS endpoint in PD-L1 TPS ≥50% did not cross its significance boundary: median not reached in either arm; HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.57–1.18), p=0.14. OS is immature: HR 0.87 (95% CI 0.67–1.15). Subgroup results carry wide CIs and are not definitive. Grade ≥3 AEs 34% vs 26%; serious AEs 24% vs 15%; AE-related discontinuation 20% vs 6%; four (1%) treatment-related deaths with pembrolizumab, two involving myocarditis, vs none with placebo.

records.title: ANVIL (ALCHEMIST)
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · III · 2026
records.body: Completely resected NSCLC with tumour >=4 cm and/or N1/N2 disease; nonsquamous tumours required no sensitising EGFR or ALK alteration, while squamous tumours were eligible. Enrolled after surgery and planned adjuvant therapy without recurrence; excluded contraindication to immune-checkpoint inhibition Nivolumab IV (initially 240 mg every 2 weeks, amended to 480 mg every 4 weeks) for up to 1 year vs Standard-care observation with protocol surveillance Primary: Disease-free survival; overall survival. Secondary: Safety; DFS by PD-L1, stage, tumour mutation burden and stratification factors 1 year of adjuvant nivolumab after standard postoperative therapy did not improve DFS: ITT median 71.3 vs 68.8 months, HR 0.97 (97% CI 0.79-1.20), and PD-L1>=50% median 89.8 vs 78.5 months, HR 0.86 (98% CI 0.55-1.34). OS was not improved (HR 1.02). Grade 3-5 treatment-related toxicity occurred in 25%, with 2 grade 5 respiratory deaths.

records.title: CheckMate 816
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · III · 2022
records.body: Resectable non-small-cell lung cancer; stage IB (≥4 cm) to IIIA (AJCC 7th edition), untreated, neoadjuvant setting; pretreatment tumour tissue for PD-L1 assessment required; ECOG 0 or 1, measurable disease per RECIST 1.1; known ALK translocations or EGFR mutations excluded Nivolumab 360 mg plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy every 3 weeks for three cycles → definitive surgery vs platinum-doublet chemotherapy alone every 3 weeks for three cycles → definitive surgery; surgery planned within 6 weeks of completing neoadjuvant treatment; optional adjuvant chemotherapy (up to four cycles), radiotherapy or both; exploratory concurrently randomized arm: nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks for three cycles plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg once at cycle 1 → definitive surgery (vs concurrently randomized chemotherapy) Primary: event-free survival, pathological complete response. Secondary: major pathological response, time to death or distant metastases, overall survival, event-free survival 2, objective response, radiographic downstaging, ctDNA clearance, surgical feasibility, safety Neoadjuvant nivolumab plus chemotherapy significantly prolonged EFS and increased pCR vs chemotherapy alone, without increasing adverse events or impeding surgery. Median EFS 31.6 vs 20.8 mo (HR 0.63; 97.38% CI 0.43-0.91; minimum follow-up 21 mo); pCR 24.0% vs 2.2% (OR 13.94). Final analysis (median follow-up 68.4 mo): 5-yr EFS 49.2% vs 34.4% (HR 0.68; 95% CI 0.51-0.91); OS significantly improved (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.523-0.998; 5-yr OS 65.4% vs 55.0%). Definitive surgery 83.2% vs 75.4%. Exploratory nivolumab plus ipilimumab vs concurrent chemotherapy (n=113 vs 108; median follow-up 49.2 mo): EFS HR 0.77 (95% CI 0.51-1.15) with more early events; pCR 20.4% vs 4.6%; OS immature (HR 0.73; 95% CI 0.47-1.14). Grade 3-4 TRAEs 33.5% vs 36.9% (nivolumab plus ipilimumab vs concurrent chemotherapy 14% vs 36%); three treatment-related deaths, all with chemotherapy alone; two grade 5 surgery-related events with nivolumab plus chemotherapy judged unrelated to trial drugs.

records.title: KEYNOTE-671
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · III · 2023
records.body: Pathologically confirmed non-small-cell lung cancer; previously untreated resectable stage II, IIIA or IIIB (N2: ≥1 ipsilateral mediastinal or subcarinal lymph node) per AJCC 8th edition, resectable after surgical consultation and investigator assessment; tumour sample required for central PD-L1 assessment, EGFR/ALK testing not mandated; ECOG 0 or 1 Neoadjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks + cisplatin-based chemotherapy (cisplatin–gemcitabine if squamous, cisplatin–pemetrexed if nonsquamous) for 4 cycles → surgery (within 20 weeks of first dose) → adjuvant pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks for up to 13 cycles vs placebo + the same chemotherapy for 4 cycles → surgery → adjuvant placebo IV every 3 weeks for up to 13 cycles (double-blind); treatment continued until maximum cycles, progression/recurrence, unacceptable toxicity, investigator decision or consent withdrawal Primary: event-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: major pathological response, pathological complete response, EORTC QLQ-C30 global health status/quality of life, safety Adding perioperative pembrolizumab to neoadjuvant cisplatin-based chemotherapy and surgery significantly improved EFS and OS at interim analyses; at 5-yr follow-up (median 60.4 mo; no alpha assigned) EFS and OS improvement continued. 5-yr EFS 49.9% vs 26.5% (HR 0.58; 95% CI 0.48-0.69), median 57.1 vs 18.4 mo; 5-yr OS 64.6% vs 53.6% (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.59-0.92), median not reached vs 70.7 mo. First interim: MPR 30.2% vs 11.0%; pCR 18.1% vs 4.0%. GHS/QoL change from baseline did not differ between groups; no long-term detriment with longer follow-up. The design cannot separate neoadjuvant from adjuvant contributions, and EFS benefit regardless of MPR/pCR status was exploratory. Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs 45% vs 38%, with treatment-related deaths in 1% vs 1%; grade ≥3 immune-mediated AEs/infusion reactions 7% vs 2%; treatment-related AEs led to discontinuation of all trial treatment in 14% vs 5%; no late-term toxicities observed.
