records.title: AEGEAN
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · III · 2023
records.body: Newly diagnosed, previously untreated resectable AJCC 8th-edition stage IIA-IIIB (N2) NSCLC, ECOG 0-1, planned for lobectomy, sleeve resection, or bilobectomy. An amendment excluded most T4 tumours, planned pneumonectomy, and documented EGFR mutation or ALK translocation; mITT excluded documented EGFR/ALK alterations Neoadjuvant durvalumab 1,500 mg IV Q3W × 4 cycles + platinum-based chemotherapy, then surgery, then adjuvant durvalumab IV Q4W up to 12 cycles vs placebo + chemotherapy on the same schedule; postoperative assigned treatment required R0/R1 resection and no evidence of disease on first postsurgical RECIST v1.1 scan Primary: Event-free survival; pathological complete response. Secondary: Major pathological response; disease-free survival; overall survival; pharmacokinetics; immunogenicity; quality of life; safety; lung cancer-specific survival Updated EFS remained favorable with perioperative durvalumab (second-interim HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.55-0.88; 24-month EFS 65.0% vs 54.4% in mITT 366 vs 374), a descriptive update after the previously established primary EFS result. pCR met its primary endpoint at the 2023 interim analysis (P<0.001; N=402); final rates were 17.2% vs 4.3% and were not formally tested at that cut. Interim DFS did not cross its protected boundary (HR 0.66; P=.0137 vs .0123). Interim OS was not formally tested (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.70-1.14). Original full-period grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs were 32.4% vs 32.9%, with treatment-related deaths 7/401 (1.7%) vs 2/398 (0.5%); the 2026 update reported only adjuvant all-cause grade 3/4 AEs, 15.4% vs 10.6%, with denominator unstated.

records.title: CheckMate 77T
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · III · 2024
records.body: Resectable non-small-cell lung cancer; stage IIA (>4 cm) to IIIB (N2 node stage, single- or multistation) per AJCC 8th edition, no previous systemic anticancer treatment; no EGFR mutations or known ALK translocations; ECOG performance status 0 or 1 Neoadjuvant nivolumab 360 mg + platinum-doublet chemotherapy every 3 weeks for 4 cycles → definitive surgery within 6 weeks → adjuvant nivolumab 480 mg every 4 weeks for 1 year (starting within 90 days after surgery) vs neoadjuvant placebo + platinum-doublet chemotherapy every 3 weeks for 4 cycles → surgery → adjuvant placebo every 4 weeks for 1 year (double-blind) Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: pathological complete response, major pathological response, overall survival, safety, objective response, event-free survival by pathological response, disease-related symptoms (NSCLC-SAQ), quality of life, surgical outcomes Perioperative nivolumab significantly prolonged event-free survival vs chemotherapy in resectable NSCLC, with no new safety signals. At the prespecified interim analysis (median follow-up 25.4 mo), 18-month EFS was 70.2% vs 50.0% (HR 0.58; 97.36% CI 0.42–0.81; P<0.001). pCR 25.3% vs 4.7% (OR 6.64) and MPR 35.4% vs 12.1% (OR 4.01) were not formally compared; their CIs are descriptive. Long-term benefit will be ascertained as data mature. In the PD-L1 <1% subgroup, EFS HR was 0.73 (95% CI 0.47–1.15; not multiplicity-adjusted). Grade 3–4 treatment-related AEs 32.5% vs 25.2%; treatment-related AEs led to discontinuation in 19.3% vs 7.4%; 2 treatment-related deaths (pneumonitis) with nivolumab vs none. Grade 5 surgery-related AEs 1.7% vs 0.6%, all deemed unrelated to trial treatment.

records.title: Neotorch
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · III · 2024
records.body: Age 18-70 years; resectable AJCC 8th-edition stage II-IIIB (N2) NSCLC; nonsquamous tumours required absence of sensitising EGFR mutations and ALK translocations. The publication reports the randomised stage III cohort; the stage II cohort remained blinded Toripalimab 240 mg IV Q3W plus platinum-doublet chemotherapy for 3 neoadjuvant cycles; surgery; 1 adjuvant combination cycle; then toripalimab 240 mg Q3W for up to 13 maintenance cycles vs Matched placebo Q3W plus the same platinum-doublet schedule, surgery, 1 adjuvant combination cycle, then placebo for up to 13 maintenance cycles Primary: Event-free survival; major pathological response. Secondary: Overall survival; pathological complete response; disease-free survival; surgical outcomes; safety Perioperative toripalimab improved interim EFS in stage III disease (2-year 64.7% vs 38.7%; HR 0.40) and MPR (48.5% vs 8.4%). Interim OS remained uncertain (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.38-1.00). Grade >=3 treatment-emergent AEs occurred in 63.4% vs 54.0%, and fatal treatment-emergent events in 3.0% vs 2.0%.

records.title: RATIONALE-315
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · III · 2025
records.body: Previously untreated, histologically confirmed stage II–IIIA squamous or non-squamous NSCLC (AJCC/UICC 8th edition) deemed eligible for R0 resection with curative intent; no known EGFR mutation or ALK translocation; stage IIIB disease excluded; conducted solely in China Neoadjuvant tislelizumab 200 mg IV q3w for 3–4 cycles plus platinum-based doublet chemotherapy (cisplatin or carboplatin with paclitaxel for squamous, pemetrexed for non-squamous) → curative-intent resection → adjuvant tislelizumab 400 mg IV q6w up to 8 cycles vs matched placebo arms; treatment continued until recurrence/progression, unacceptable adverse events, death, completion of maximum adjuvant cycles or discontinuation Primary: major pathological response rate, event-free survival. Secondary: pathological complete response rate, overall survival, objective response rate, disease-free survival, event-free survival (investigator-assessed), health-related quality of life, safety and tolerability Perioperative tislelizumab plus neoadjuvant chemotherapy showed sustained, clinically meaningful EFS improvement and, at final analysis, a statistically significant OS benefit versus placebo plus chemotherapy in resectable stage II–IIIA NSCLC. Final analysis (median follow-up 38.5 months): OS stratified HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.45–0.93), P=0.009, crossing the prespecified boundary; 36-month OS 79.3% vs 69.3%; median OS not reached in either arm; deaths 52/226 vs 70/227. Final EFS: median NR vs 30.6 months, HR 0.58 (0.43–0.79); 36-month EFS 64.7% vs 48.0%. Interim: MPR 56% (127/226) vs 15% (34/227); pCR 41% (92/226) vs 6% (13/227); 24-month EFS 68% vs 52%. Grade ≥3 TRAEs 73.0% vs 67.3%; fatal TRAEs 4 (1.8%) vs 2 (0.9%); immune-mediated AE deaths 2/226 vs 0.

records.title: LCMC3
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA negative) · II · 2022
records.body: Pathologically documented AJCC 8th-edition stage IB-IIIB NSCLC considered surgically resectable and functionally operable; biomarker status was not required. Excluded lung cancer within 3 years, prior PD-(L)1 therapy, autoimmune disease, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, organising pneumonia, or active pneumonitis (single-arm) Neoadjuvant atezolizumab 1200 mg IV Q3W x2 doses → surgery; optional adjuvant atezolizumab for up to 12 months Primary: Major pathological response. Secondary: Objective response; pathological complete response; disease-free survival; overall survival; safety; biomarker and correlative outcomes Single-arm neoadjuvant atezolizumab produced MPR in 20% (29/143) of the EGFR/ALK-negative-or-unknown primary efficacy population. Among 137 R0-resected patients, 3-year DFS and OS were 72% and 80%. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 11%; 3 patients died during the neoadjuvant phase, including 1 treatment-related pneumonitis death.

records.title: ALINA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA positive) · III · 2024
records.body: Completely resected, histologically confirmed NSCLC; adjuvant setting, stage IB (tumors ≥4 cm), II or IIIA (AJCC/UICC seventh edition), randomized 4 to 12 weeks after complete resection; ALK-positive by FDA-approved or CE-marked test (local or central); eligible for platinum-based chemotherapy, no previous systemic anticancer therapy Oral alectinib 600 mg twice daily for 24 months or until disease recurrence, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent vs IV platinum-based chemotherapy in four 21-day cycles: cisplatin 75 mg per square meter day 1 plus vinorelbine 25 mg per square meter days 1 and 8, gemcitabine 1250 mg per square meter days 1 and 8, or pemetrexed 500 mg per square meter day 1 (carboplatin AUC 5 or 6 if cisplatin intolerance) Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, safety, CNS disease-free survival, quality of life Adjuvant alectinib significantly improved disease-free survival vs platinum-based chemotherapy at a preplanned interim analysis (median follow-up 27.8 mo). Stage II–IIIA: 2-yr DFS 93.8% vs 63.0%; HR 0.24 (95% CI 0.13–0.45). ITT: 2-yr DFS 93.6% vs 63.7%; HR 0.24 (95% CI 0.13–0.43). Exploratory CNS DFS favoured alectinib (HR 0.22; 95% CI 0.08–0.58). OS data were immature (six deaths). In an exploratory, largely post-hoc AJCC 8th-edition reanalysis, DFS favoured alectinib across stages (II HR 0.28, 95% CI 0.11–0.70; IIIA HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.10–0.51) and nodal status (N0 HR 0.19, 95% CI 0.04–0.88); small subgroups may be underpowered. Post-hoc, untested SF-36v2 comparisons at week 12 favoured alectinib in MCS and all domains except physical functioning; alectinib week-96 MCS 49.9, PCS 48.8 (norm 50). No grade 5 AEs; grade 3 or 4 AEs 29.7% vs 30.8% (treatment-related 18.0% vs 27.5%); serious AEs 13.3% vs 8.3%; AE discontinuation 5.5% vs 12.5%, with median treatment 23.9 vs 2.1 mo.

records.title: NeoADAURA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA positive) · III · 2025
records.body: Resectable nonsquamous NSCLC, stage II–IIIB (AJCC 8th ed), deemed completely resectable by a multidisciplinary team; sensitizing EGFR mutations (exon 19 deletion or L858R) confirmed by preapproved local or central tissue testing; neoadjuvant setting before planned curative surgery; age ≥18 years, WHO performance status 0 or 1 Neoadjuvant osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily for ≥9 weeks plus IV pemetrexed 500 mg/m² with investigator's choice of carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² every 3 weeks for three cycles (double-blind) vs osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily for ≥9 weeks as monotherapy (open-label, sponsor-blinded) vs oral placebo once daily for ≥9 weeks plus the same platinum-pemetrexed doublet, each followed by surgical resection; adjuvant osimertinib offered to eligible patients after surgery Primary: major pathologic response. Secondary: event-free survival, pathologic complete response, nodal downstaging at surgery, safety Neoadjuvant osimertinib with or without chemotherapy significantly improved the MPR rate over chemotherapy alone in resectable, EGFR-mutated, stage II-IIIB NSCLC. MPR was 26% with osimertinib plus chemotherapy and 25% with monotherapy vs 2% with placebo plus chemotherapy (ORs 19.82, 95.002% CI 4.60 to 85.33 and 19.28, 99.9% CI 1.71 to 217.39; both P < .0001). Interim EFS at 15% maturity favored the osimertinib arms but did not reach the prespecified significance level (HR 0.50, 99.8% CI 0.17 to 1.41, P = .04, vs P < .002 required); 12-month EFS 93%, 95% and 83%. Among baseline N2 patients, downstaging was 53% and 53% vs 21%. Neoadjuvant grade ≥3 AEs of any cause: 36%, 13%, 33%; no fatal AEs and no deaths within 30 days after surgery.

records.title: LORIN
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA positive) · II · 2026
records.body: Stage III ALK-fusion NSCLC assessed as potentially resectable or unresectable Neoadjuvant lorlatinib x3 cycles → optional surgery/local therapy → consolidation lorlatinib up to 2 years Primary: Pathological complete response Secondary: Major pathological response; Event-free survival; Overall survival; Safety Single-arm neoadjuvant lorlatinib reached its pCR target among operated patients: 15/32 (46.9%); MPR was 26/32 (81.3%). Surgery occurred in 32/43, including 18/24 (75%) initially unresectable patients; R0 resection was 31/32. One-year EFS was 97.1% at 13-month median follow-up and no OS events had occurred, so survival remains immature. The abstract reports common treatment-related lipid abnormalities and oedema but no grades or counts.

records.title: LIBRETTO-432
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA positive) · III · 2026
records.body: Histologically confirmed RET fusion-positive NSCLC; stage IB, II or IIIA (8th edition staging) after definitive curative-intent surgery or radiotherapy, plus adjuvant systemic therapy if applicable (primary analysis population: stage II or IIIA); RET fusion by local PCR, comprehensive genomic profiling or sponsor-approved test; excluded additional oncogenic driver alterations or recurrence/progression after definitive therapy Selpercatinib 160 mg twice daily (120 mg twice daily if weight <50 kg) in continuous 28-day cycles until recurrence/progression or unacceptable toxicity, up to 3 years vs placebo on the same schedule (double-blind) Primary: event-free survival in the stage II–IIIA population. Secondary: overall survival, event-free survival in the stage IB–IIIA population, event-free survival by blinded independent central review, safety Among patients with stage II or IIIA RET fusion-positive NSCLC, adjuvant selpercatinib significantly prolonged event-free survival vs placebo. Stage II or IIIA (109 patients): 2-yr EFS 92% vs 61%; HR 0.17 (95% CI 0.06–0.51). Stage IB, II or IIIA (151 patients): 2-yr EFS 94% vs 70%; HR 0.16 (95% CI 0.06–0.48). Central-review EFS was consistent. Follow-up is short (median 24 vs 27 mo) and OS is immature; three deaths, all in the placebo group, from disease progression. Grade ≥3 AEs 67% vs 24%, including grade ≥3 ALT (17%) and AST (19%) increases with selpercatinib; dose reductions 55% vs 8%; discontinuation for AEs 17% vs 1%; no fatal events during treatment.

records.title: ELEVATE
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA positive) · III · 2026
records.body: Completely resected AJCC 8th-edition stage IB-IIIB ALK-positive NSCLC. Stage IIB-IIIB required adjuvant chemotherapy unless toxicity or refusal; stage IB-IIA chemotherapy was discretionary. Preoperative and postoperative radiotherapy were prohibited Ensartinib 225 mg orally once daily for up to 24 months after complete resection and any planned adjuvant chemotherapy vs Matched placebo orally once daily for up to 24 months after complete resection and any planned adjuvant chemotherapy Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; DFS landmarks; safety; CNS disease-free survival; biomarkers Adjuvant ensartinib improved interim DFS versus placebo: stage II-IIIB 24-month DFS 86.4% vs 53.5% (HR 0.20); overall stage IB-IIIB HR was 0.20. OS was immature (1 vs 2 deaths). Grade >=3 AEs were 35.8% vs 18.2%; grade >=3 rash occurred in 14.6% vs 0.

records.title: ADAURA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · (Neo)adjuvant & perioperative therapy (AGA positive) · III · 2020
records.body: Completely resected nonsquamous AJCC 7th-edition stage IB-IIIA NSCLC with centrally confirmed EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R. Adjuvant chemotherapy was allowed but not mandatory; preoperative, postoperative, or planned radiotherapy was prohibited Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily for 3 years or until recurrence/discontinuation, after optional adjuvant chemotherapy vs Matched placebo orally once daily for 3 years or until recurrence/discontinuation, after optional adjuvant chemotherapy Primary: disease-free survival (stage II-IIIA). Secondary: disease-free survival (stage IB-IIIA); Overall survival; health-related quality of life; safety; site of recurrence; CNS disease-free survival; time to first subsequent treatment or death Adjuvant osimertinib significantly prolonged DFS vs placebo after resection of stage IB-IIIA EGFR-mutated NSCLC. At the unplanned interim analysis, 24-month DFS in stage II-IIIA (primary) was 90% vs 44% (HR 0.17; 99.06% CI, 0.11-0.26) and in stage IB-IIIA 89% vs 52% (HR 0.20); exploratory 24-month CNS DFS was 98% vs 85% (HR 0.18). OS was immature at that cut. At the planned final OS analysis (cutoff January 27, 2023), osimertinib significantly improved OS: 5-year OS 85% vs 73% in stage II-IIIA (HR 0.49; 95.03% CI, 0.33-0.73) and 88% vs 78% in stage IB-IIIA (HR 0.49; 95.03% CI, 0.34-0.70). Subsequent anticancer therapy was given to 22% vs 54%; the effect of post-recurrence osimertinib on OS could not be determined. Grade >=3 AEs were 20% vs 13%, with no fatal AEs on osimertinib; interstitial lung disease occurred in 3% vs 0 and was mild/moderate. Safety at the final OS cut was consistent with the primary analysis.

records.title: Lung ART
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Adjuvant radiotherapy · III · 2022
records.body: Completely resected NSCLC with N2 disease proven at surgery or documented before downstaging, after lobectomy, bilobectomy, or pneumonectomy with mediastinal exploration. Excluded prior chest radiotherapy, synchronous contralateral lung cancer, another neoplasm, or recent severe cardiac/pulmonary disease PORT 54 Gy (27 x 2 Gy or 30 x 1.8 Gy), 5 days/week over about 5.5 weeks; 3D conformal mandatory, IMRT permitted; chemotherapy neoadjuvant or adjuvant but not concurrent vs No postoperative radiotherapy; chemotherapy could be neoadjuvant or adjuvant Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; recurrence pattern; second cancers; early and late toxicity Postoperative mediastinal radiotherapy did not improve DFS after complete resection of N2 NSCLC: median 30.5 vs 22.8 months, HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.68-1.08; P=.18), with 3-year DFS 47% vs 44%. It reduced mediastinal relapse but increased grade >=3 toxicity (25% vs 15%); 3-year OS was 67% vs 69% (HR 0.97, 0.73-1.28). Routine PORT is not supported by this modern conformal-radiotherapy trial.

records.title: RTOG 9410
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Unresectable stage III NSCLC — chemoradiation & consolidation · III · 2011
records.body: Unresectable stage II-III NSCLC Concurrent vs sequential chemoradiotherapy (cisplatin/vinblastine + RT) Overall survival Concurrent chemoradiation improved median OS (17.0 vs 14.6 months) versus sequential, at the cost of more acute oesophagitis; established concurrent CRT as the standard for unresectable stage III NSCLC.

records.title: RTOG 0617
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Unresectable stage III NSCLC — chemoradiation & consolidation · III · 2015
records.body: Unresectable stage IIIA-IIIB NSCLC 60 Gy vs 74 Gy RT, +/- cetuximab, with concurrent carboplatin/paclitaxel (2x2 factorial) Overall survival High-dose RT (74 Gy) did not improve and was worse for OS than 60 Gy (median 20.3 vs 28.7 months); cetuximab added no benefit. Cemented 60 Gy as the standard radiation dose.

records.title: PACIFIC
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Unresectable stage III NSCLC — chemoradiation & consolidation · III · 2017
records.body: Stage III locally advanced, unresectable NSCLC; no progression after ≥2 cycles of platinum-based chemotherapy concurrent with definitive radiotherapy (54 to 66 Gy; mean lung dose <20 Gy and/or V20 <35%), last radiation dose 1 to 42 days before randomization (1 to 14 days before amendment); no PD-L1 selection; excluded prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1 antibodies, autoimmune disease within 2 years, grade ≥2 pneumonitis from prior chemoradiotherapy Durvalumab 10 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks for up to 12 months vs matching placebo every 2 weeks for up to 12 months; started 1 to 42 days after chemoradiotherapy; stopped at confirmed progression, alternative anticancer therapy, unacceptable toxicity or consent withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: 12-month progression-free survival rate, 18-month progression-free survival rate, objective response rate, duration of response, time to death or distant metastasis, time to second progression, overall survival at 24 months, safety, health-related quality of life, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity Consolidation durvalumab significantly prolonged both coprimary endpoints vs placebo: BICR-assessed PFS at the planned interim analysis, and OS at the first OS interim analysis (HR 0.68; 99.73% CI 0.47-0.997; 24-mo OS 66.3% vs 55.6%). In exploratory 5-yr updates (median follow-up 34.2 mo), benefit was sustained: OS HR 0.72 (95% CI 0.59-0.89), median 47.5 vs 29.1 mo, 5-yr OS 42.9% vs 33.4%; PFS HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.45-0.68), median 16.9 vs 5.6 mo, 5-yr PFS 33.1% vs 19.0%. Primary PFS analysis: median 16.8 vs 5.6 mo (HR 0.52). At the 5-yr update, ORR 29.8% vs 18.3%; median time to death or distant metastasis 36.5 vs 17.7 mo (HR 0.59). Post hoc, OS did not favour durvalumab with PD-L1 <1% (HR 1.15; 95% CI 0.75-1.75). At the primary OS analysis (safety not updated at 5 yr), grade 3/4 AEs 30.5% vs 26.1%; discontinuation for AEs 15.4% vs 9.8%; deaths due to AEs 4.4% vs 6.4%. At the primary analysis, pneumonitis or radiation pneumonitis 33.9% vs 24.8% (grade 3/4 3.4% vs 2.6%).

records.title: PACIFIC-2
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Unresectable stage III NSCLC — chemoradiation & consolidation · III · 2025
records.body: Adults with newly diagnosed unresectable IASLC 8th-edition stage III NSCLC, ECOG/WHO performance status 0-1 and measurable RECIST v1.1 disease; archived tissue or recent biopsy required. EGFR/ALK testing was not required Durvalumab 1,500 mg IV Q4W from the start of concurrent platinum-based CRT, then durvalumab 1,500 mg IV Q4W after nonprogression vs matching placebo with the same CRT and antibody schedule; treatment until progression or discontinuation Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Objective response rate, overall survival, 24-month overall survival rate, complete response rate, duration of response, disease control rate at 24 weeks, safety and tolerability In PACIFIC-2, durvalumab begun with cCRT did not improve primary BICR PFS versus placebo plus cCRT (median 13.8 vs 9.4 months; HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.65-1.12; P=.247). OS was nominal after primary failure (36.4 vs 29.5 months; HR 1.03, 95% CI 0.78-1.39); OS24 was 58.4% vs 59.5%. Serious AEs were 47.0% vs 51.9%, assigned-treatment discontinuation 25.6% vs 12.0%, and all-cause grade-5 AEs 13.7% vs 10.2% in the 219-versus-108 safety set. Post hoc, 0-4-month fatal AEs were 6.8% vs 4.6%; six fatal infections and four fatal respiratory/hemorrhagic events occurred with durvalumab versus none with placebo.

records.title: PACIFIC-5
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Unresectable stage III NSCLC — chemoradiation & consolidation · III · 2025
records.body: Unresectable IASLC/AJCC 8th-edition stage III NSCLC without progression after definitive platinum concurrent or sequential chemoradiotherapy. An amendment excluded sensitising EGFR mutations and ALK translocations from primary/key-secondary analyses while retaining them in randomised ITT Durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal vs Placebo IV every 4 weeks until progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; PFS and OS in all randomised patients; OS landmarks; objective response rate; duration of response; PFS landmarks; PFS2; time to death or distant metastasis; safety Consolidation durvalumab improved PFS after concurrent or sequential CRT (14.0 vs 6.5 months; HR 0.75). Interim OS did not reach statistical significance (38.3 vs 32.5 months; HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.66-1.17). PFS estimates after cCRT and sCRT were exploratory, both CIs crossed 1 and no interaction test was reported, so benefit specifically after sCRT is unproven. Grade 3-4 AEs were 26.9% vs 23.9%; pneumonitis was 39.5% vs 40.3% (grade 3-4, 3.7% vs 2.2%); treatment-related deaths were 1.5% vs 0.

records.title: CheckMate 73L
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Unresectable stage III NSCLC — chemoradiation & consolidation · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated, unresectable locally advanced stage III NSCLC Nivolumab + cCRT then nivolumab + ipilimumab (arm A) or nivolumab (arm B) vs cCRT then durvalumab (arm C) Progression-free survival (arm A vs arm C) Nivolumab + cCRT then nivolumab + ipilimumab did not improve PFS versus the durvalumab standard (HR 0.95, non-significant; descriptive OS HR 1.12); nivolumab alone also did not (PFS HR 0.84), with more pneumonitis. Adding nivolumab during CRT, with or without ipilimumab consolidation, does not beat consolidation durvalumab (PACIFIC).

records.title: LAURA
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Unresectable stage III NSCLC — chemoradiation & consolidation · III · 2024
records.body: Locally advanced unresectable stage III NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R, alone or with other EGFR mutations, without progression during or after concurrent or sequential platinum chemoradiotherapy. Excluded pre-CRT interstitial lung disease, post-CRT symptomatic pneumonitis, or unresolved grade ≥2 adverse effects after CRT Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily until disease progression or discontinuation vs Placebo Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; CNS progression-free survival; objective response rate; duration of response; health-related quality of life; safety Consolidation osimertinib improved PFS after chemoradiotherapy for unresectable EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R stage III disease (39.1 vs 5.6 months; HR 0.16). Interim OS was immature and did not differ (HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.42-1.56), with crossover offered after progression. ORR was 57% vs 33% and median duration of response 36.9 vs 6.5 months; new brain lesions occurred in 8% vs 29%. Grade >=3 AEs were 35% vs 12%; grouped interstitial lung disease occurred in 8% vs 1%, and fatal AEs in 2% vs 3%. Radiation pneumonitis, mostly grade 1-2, occurred in 48% vs 38%.

records.title: PROCLAIM
records.subtitle: Early & Locally Adv NSCLC · Unresectable stage III NSCLC — chemoradiation & consolidation · III · 2016
records.body: Nonsquamous stage IIIA or IIIB NSCLC without malignant pleural/pericardial effusion; supraclavicular nodes permitted. Excluded lung V20 >35% or prior systemic chemotherapy for NSCLC Pemetrexed/cisplatin + concurrent thoracic RT 60-66 Gy, then consolidation pemetrexed vs etoposide/cisplatin + concurrent thoracic RT 60-66 Gy, then consolidation platinum doublet Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival; tumour response rate; survival landmarks; first site of disease failure Pemetrexed-cisplatin chemoradiotherapy followed by pemetrexed did not improve OS versus etoposide-cisplatin chemoradiotherapy followed by a platinum doublet: 26.8 vs 25.0 months, HR 0.98 (95% CI 0.79-1.20); enrolment stopped early for futility. PFS also did not improve (HR 0.86, 0.71-1.04). Grade 3-4 toxicity was 64.0% vs 76.8%, but any-grade pneumonitis was 17.0% vs 10.7%; possibly drug-related deaths were 1.8% vs 1.1%.

records.title: IPASS
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2009
records.body: Untreated stage IIIB or IV lung adenocarcinoma (including bronchoalveolar carcinoma); first line, no previous chemotherapy or biologic or immunologic therapy; clinically selected, EGFR mutation not required; East Asian nonsmokers (<100 cigarettes lifetime) or former light smokers (stopped ≥15 years previously, ≤10 pack-years) Gefitinib 250 mg orally once daily until progression or discontinuation vs carboplatin AUC 5-6 + paclitaxel 200 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, ORR, quality of life, symptom reduction, safety Gefitinib was superior to carboplatin-paclitaxel as initial treatment for pulmonary adenocarcinoma in East Asian never/former light smokers: PFS met noninferiority and superiority (ITT HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.65-0.85) with crossing curves; 12-month PFS 24.9% vs 6.7%. Gefitinib's PFS effect depended on EGFR mutation (interaction P<.001; planned exploratory): HR 0.48 in EGFR-mutant tumours vs 2.85 in wild type; ORR 71.2% vs 47.3% and 1.1% vs 23.5%, respectively. Overall ORR was 43.0% vs 32.2%. OS was immature (HR 0.91, 450 deaths). More patients had clinically relevant QoL improvement with gefitinib (FACT-L OR 1.34; TOI OR 1.78); symptom reduction was similar (LCS OR 1.13). Grade 3/4 AEs were 28.7% vs 61.0%; AEs leading to death 3.8% vs 2.7%; ILD occurred in 2.6% vs 1.4%, with 3 vs 1 deaths.

records.title: LUX-Lung 3
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2013
records.body: Untreated advanced EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma Afatinib 40 mg orally once daily until progression vs cisplatin 75 mg/m² + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV every 21 days for up to 6 cycles; no pemetrexed maintenance Primary: independent-review progression-free survival. Secondary: investigator-assessed PFS, ORR, duration of response, disease control, OS, patient-reported symptoms and quality of life, safety Afatinib improved PFS vs cisplatin-pemetrexed (11.1 vs 6.9 months; HR 0.58). Pooled post-hoc OS improved in exon 19 deletion disease (31.7 vs 20.7 months; HR 0.59), while the LUX-Lung 3 L858R estimate showed no benefit (27.6 vs 40.3 months; HR 1.30, 95% CI 0.80-2.11). Grade 3 treatment-related AEs were 49% vs 48%; 4 treatment-related deaths occurred with afatinib vs none with chemotherapy.

records.body: Untreated advanced EGFR-mutant (ex19del/L858R) NSCLC First-line osimertinib 80 mg once daily vs gefitinib 250 mg once daily or erlotinib 150 mg once daily; to progression Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. At final OS follow-up, grade >=3 AEs were 42% vs 47%, serious AEs 27% in each arm, fatal AEs 3% vs 4%, and treatment-related deaths 0 vs 2.

records.title: FLAURA2
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated advanced EGFR-mutant NSCLC Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² and cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 IV every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, then osimertinib + pemetrexed maintenance until progression/toxicity vs osimertinib 80 mg once daily until progression/toxicity Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. records.title: MARIPOSA
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated advanced EGFR-mutant (ex19del/L858R) NSCLC First-line amivantamab (1050 mg IV, 1400 mg if ≥80 kg; weekly ×4 then Q2W) + lazertinib 240 mg once daily vs osimertinib 80 mg once daily; to progression Primary: BICR progression-free survival for amivantamab-lazertinib vs osimertinib. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, symptomatic progression, subsequent-treatment outcomes, intracranial efficacy, safety Amivantamab-lazertinib improved OS vs osimertinib (HR 0.75; 3-year OS 60% vs 51%) after improving PFS (23.7 vs 16.6 months; HR 0.70). Grade >=3 AEs were 80% vs 52%; venous thromboembolism 40% vs 11%, and fatal AEs 9% vs 8%.

records.title: AURA3
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2017
records.body: Advanced EGFR T790M-positive NSCLC after progression on prior EGFR TKI Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles, then optional pemetrexed maintenance until progression/toxicity Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary: ORR, duration of response, disease control, tumour shrinkage, OS, patient-reported outcomes, safety Osimertinib improved PFS vs platinum-pemetrexed after T790M-positive progression (10.1 vs 4.4 months; HR 0.30), including baseline CNS metastases (8.5 vs 4.2 months; HR 0.32); ORR was 71% vs 31%. Grade >=3 AEs were 23% vs 47%; ILD-like events were 4% vs 1%, including one osimertinib-arm death.

records.title: WU-KONG28
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2026
records.body: Advanced nonsquamous NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations; locally advanced (stage IIIB or IIIC) or metastatic (stage IV), first line with no previous systemic anticancer therapy (chemotherapy or EGFR-TKIs); ECOG performance status 0–1; brain metastases allowed if stable after local therapy Oral sunvozertinib 300 mg once daily until disease progression or other protocol-defined discontinuation vs carboplatin (target AUC 5) plus pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for up to 4 or 6 cycles followed by pemetrexed maintenance until progression or other discontinuation criteria Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, investigator-assessed progression-free survival, objective response, change in tumor size, duration of response, health-related quality of life, safety Sunvozertinib was superior to platinum-based chemotherapy as first-line treatment for advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertions. Median PFS by blinded independent central review was 10.3 vs 7.5 months (HR for progression or death 0.65, 95% CI 0.50–0.85; P<0.001); PFS at 12 months 46.1% vs 26.7%. Objective response 58.9% vs 31.1%; median duration of response 11.2 vs 7.1 months. Overall survival data were immature (38.9% maturity), with HR 0.99 (95% CI 0.70–1.40), and interpretation was possibly confounded by crossover from chemotherapy to sunvozertinib after progression. Grade ≥3 adverse events occurred in 75.5% vs 56.7%; most common grade ≥3 events with sunvozertinib were increased serum creatine kinase (20.9%) and diarrhea (14.1%); no treatment-related fatal adverse events with sunvozertinib, while one fatal treatment-related pneumonia occurred with chemotherapy.

records.title: AENEAS2
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2026
records.body: Treatment-naive locally advanced/metastatic NSCLC with EGFR exon 19 deletion or L858R Aumolertinib 110 mg orally once daily + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² and cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 IV every 21 days for 4-6 cycles, then aumolertinib-pemetrexed maintenance until progression/toxicity vs aumolertinib 110 mg once daily until progression/toxicity Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, investigator-assessed PFS, BICR ORR, disease control, duration and depth of response, safety Aumolertinib-chemotherapy improved BICR PFS vs aumolertinib (28.9 vs 18.9 months; HR 0.47); OS was immature. Grade >=3 AEs were 80% vs 35%, including grade 3/4 neutrophil decrease 55% vs 1%; treatment-related deaths were 1 vs 2.

records.title: Sampath (osimertinib + consolidative RT)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · II · 2025
records.body: Advanced EGFR exon 19/21-mutant NSCLC, treatment-naive to EGFR or checkpoint inhibitors Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily; after 8-10 weeks, responders/stable disease received radiotherapy to residual disease at up to 6 sites, then continued osimertinib until progression/toxicity (single-arm) Primary: investigator-assessed PFS from osimertinib initiation. Secondary: OS, response, duration of osimertinib, radiotherapy delivery, progression patterns, safety including pneumonitis Response-adapted consolidative radiotherapy with osimertinib produced median PFS 32.3 months and OS 45.0 months; 76% received radiotherapy. The uncontrolled design precludes comparison with osimertinib alone. Pneumonitis occurred in 2/42 (5%), including one grade 4 event; no other grade >=3 radiation-related or late radiation events were reported.

records.title: ACHILLES/TORG1834
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2025
records.body: Treatment-naive nonsquamous NSCLC with sensitizing uncommon EGFR mutations (excluding exon 20 insertions and T790M) Afatinib 30 or 40 mg orally once daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 6 every 3 weeks for 4 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression/toxicity Primary: investigator-assessed PFS from randomisation. Secondary: ORR, disease control, time to treatment failure, OS, duration of response, safety PFS improved with afatinib vs platinum-pemetrexed (10.6 vs 5.7 months; HR 0.421; P=.0010). Mutation-specific ORRs (major uncommon 55.8%, compound 72.7%, other 60.0%) were exploratory without an interaction test. OS was immature (29 deaths). Grade >=3 AEs were 44% vs 37%; one afatinib-related death occurred.

records.title: Robichaux et al. (structure-based EGFR classification)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · N/A · 2021
records.body: EGFR-mutant NSCLC (all mutation subtypes, exons 18-21) N/A — retrospective structure-function analysis of drug sensitivity across EGFR-TKIs Structural EGFR classification, mutation prevalence, drug-response associations, time to treatment failure, duration of treatment, objective response, preclinical sensitivity Retrospective structure-function grouping classified EGFR mutations as classical-like, T790M-like, exon20ins-loop or PACC and predicted TKI sensitivity better than exon grouping. In PACC mutations, time to treatment failure was 21.7 months with second-generation vs 10.0 with first-generation and 4.1 with third-generation TKIs (second vs third HR 0.23). This retrospective/preclinical analysis did not assess comparative treatment safety.

records.title: LUX-Lung 2/3/6 pooled (Yang)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · N/A · 2015
records.body: EGFR mutation-positive advanced (stage IIIb-IV) NSCLC adenocarcinoma, TKI-naive, with uncommon EGFR mutations (75 of 600 afatinib-treated patients across LUX-Lung 2/3/6) Afatinib 40 or 50 mg orally once daily in LUX-Lung 2 and 40 mg once daily in LUX-Lung 3/6, until progression/toxicity/withdrawal (pooled treated cohort) Objective response rate, PFS and OS by uncommon EGFR mutation group Post-hoc pooled analysis of afatinib-treated uncommon EGFR mutations: point mutations/duplications (n=38) had ORR 71.1%, PFS 10.7 months and OS 19.4 months; de-novo T790M (n=14) and exon 20 insertions (n=23) had ORR 14.3%/8.7%, PFS 2.9/2.7 months and OS 14.9/9.2 months. No formal comparisons or interaction test were performed; this publication did not provide a comparative safety analysis.

records.title: KCSG-LU15-09 (Cho)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · II · 2020
records.body: Metastatic/recurrent NSCLC with uncommon EGFR mutations; exon 19 deletion, L858R, T790M and exon 20 insertion excluded Osimertinib 80 mg once daily (single-arm); to progression Primary: investigator-assessed objective response rate. Secondary: PFS, OS, duration of response, disease control, CNS response, safety Single-arm osimertinib produced ORR 50% and median PFS 8.2 months in uncommon EGFR-mutant NSCLC; exploratory ORRs were 78% for L861Q, 53% for G719X and 38% for S768I. OS was immature (7/36 deaths). Grade 3/4 AEs occurred in 2/36 (6%); no ILD, QT prolongation, AE discontinuation or treatment-related death was reported.

records.title: UNICORN (Okuma)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · II · 2024
records.body: Previously untreated metastatic NSCLC with uncommon EGFR mutations other than exon 20 insertions Osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily until progression or unacceptable toxicity (single-arm) Primary: BICR-confirmed objective response rate. Secondary: disease control, PFS, time to treatment failure, OS, duration of response, safety Single-arm first-line osimertinib produced ORR 55%, median PFS 9.4 months and response duration 22.7 months in uncommon EGFR-mutant NSCLC; OS was not reached. Grade 3/4 AEs occurred in 27.5%, ILD in 5/40 (12.5%), and no treatment-related deaths were reported.

records.title: CHRYSALIS-2 Cohort C (Tomasini)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · I · 2026
records.body: Advanced NSCLC harboring atypical EGFR mutations (G719X, S768I, L861Q; co-occurring exon 20 insertion, exon 19 deletion or L858R excluded), ≤2 prior lines (treatment-naïve or after a 1st/2nd-generation EGFR TKI) Amivantamab (1050 mg IV, 1400 mg if ≥80 kg) + lazertinib 240 mg once daily (single-arm); to progression Primary: investigator-assessed objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, clinical benefit rate, PFS, OS, time to treatment discontinuation, safety Single-arm amivantamab-lazertinib produced ORR 52%, median response duration 14.1 months and PFS 11.1 months; OS was not estimable. Grade >=3 AEs occurred in 70%, venous thromboembolism in 30% (grade 3, 10%), and treatment-related death in 1%.

records.title: Marcoux et al. (EGFR-mutant SCLC transformation)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · N/A · 2019
records.body: Retrospective 8-centre cohort of 67 EGFR-mutant SCLC/high-grade neuroendocrine lung cancers: 58 transformed after EGFR-mutant NSCLC (predominantly adenocarcinoma) and 9 were de novo SCLC or mixed histology N/A — retrospective multicentre cohort; treatment was clinician-selected before and after transformation or, for de novo/mixed cases, after SCLC diagnosis; platinum-etoposide was the most common post-SCLC regimen Clinical response, progression-free survival, overall survival, CNS progression, histologic characteristics, molecular characteristics Platinum-etoposide and taxanes showed activity after SCLC transformation/de novo SCLC, but this retrospective cohort was noncomparative: pooled platinum-etoposide response was 54% among 46 evaluable, with transformed-case PFS 3.4 months (48 at risk); taxane response was 50% among 20 evaluable, with transformed-case PFS 2.7 months (17 at risk). Checkpoint response was 0/17. Pooled median OS from transformation/SCLC diagnosis was 10.9 months (95% CI 8.0-13.7), and CNS progression occurred in 38/59 (64%) with radiographic follow-up. All 59 genotyped at first SCLC evidence retained founder EGFR; 15/19 previously T790M-positive cases lost T790M. Responses were investigator-estimated without formal measurement/confirmation; no safety table was reported.

records.title: Zhou et al; osimertinib with or without chemotherapy in EGFR/TP53 co-mutated advanced NSCLC
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · EGFR-mutant · III · 2026
records.body: Treatment-naive stage IV or recurrent nonsquamous NSCLC with concurrent EGFR-sensitizing (Ex19del or L858R) and TP53 mutations (NGS, central or local); first-line; ECOG 0-1; asymptomatic stable brain metastases allowed; no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease Osimertinib 80 mg once daily + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² and carboplatin AUC 5 IV every 3 weeks for 4 cycles → maintenance osimertinib + pemetrexed vs osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily continuously Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, safety, quality of life First-line osimertinib plus pemetrexed-carboplatin significantly improved investigator-assessed PFS vs osimertinib monotherapy in EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC with concurrent TP53 mutations: median PFS 34.0 vs 15.6 months (HR 0.44, 95% CI 0.32-0.60; P < .001; 67/146 vs 107/148 progression/death events), consistent across prespecified subgroups including brain metastases and L858R. ORR 82.9% vs 71.6%; median DoR 32.7 vs 15.3 months. OS immature (30.6% maturity; median 48.4 vs 36.5 months; HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.38-0.88; nominal P = .01, interim analysis without alpha adjustment). Grade ≥3 TRAEs 62.4% vs 14.9%, including neutrophil decrease 38.3% vs 4.1%; serious TRAEs 10.6% vs 1.4%; one treatment-related death from severe thrombocytopenia causing pulmonary hemorrhage. Global health status deteriorated faster with combination during induction (RMST difference -7.8)

records.title: PROFILE 1014
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ALK-positive · III · 2014
records.body: Untreated advanced ALK-positive non-squamous NSCLC Crizotinib 250 mg orally twice daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5-6 IV every 3 weeks for up to 6 cycles Primary: independent-review progression-free survival. Secondary: ORR, duration of response, OS, patient-reported outcomes, safety Crizotinib improved independent-review PFS vs platinum-pemetrexed (10.9 vs 7.0 months; HR 0.45) and ORR (74% vs 45%). OS was immature and inconclusive (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.54-1.26) with 70% crossover. Grade 3/4 aminotransferase elevation occurred in 14% vs 2%; one fatal treatment-related pneumonitis occurred after crossover to crizotinib.

records.title: ALEX
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ALK-positive · III · 2017
records.body: Untreated advanced ALK-positive NSCLC First-line alectinib 600 mg twice daily vs crizotinib 250 mg twice daily; to progression Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary: independent-review PFS, time to CNS progression, ORR, duration of response, CNS response and response duration, OS, safety Final OS was negative for alectinib vs crizotinib (81.1 vs 54.2 months; HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.56-1.08). Alectinib improved PFS at the primary analysis (IRC 25.7 vs 10.4 months; HR 0.47) and reduced CNS progression (12% vs 45%). Long-term grade 3-5 AEs were 57.9% vs 57.6%; fatal AEs 6.6% vs 4.6%.

records.title: ALTA-1L

Grade >=3 AEs were 61% vs 55%; early-onset ILD/pneumonitis occurred in 3% vs 0%.

records.title: CROWN
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ALK-positive · III · 2020
records.body: Untreated advanced ALK-positive NSCLC First-line lorlatinib 100 mg once daily vs crizotinib 250 mg twice daily; to progression Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: investigator-assessed PFS, OS, ORR, intracranial response and response duration, time to CNS progression, quality of life, safety At 7 years, lorlatinib maintained PFS benefit vs crizotinib (median not reached vs 9.1 months; HR 0.19; 7-year PFS 55% vs 3%); OS remained immature. records.title: PROFILE 1001 (ROS1 cohort)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ROS1-positive · I · 2014
records.body: Advanced ROS1-rearranged NSCLC Crizotinib 250 mg twice daily (single-arm); to progression Primary: objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, PFS, OS, safety Single-arm crizotinib produced ORR 72% and median PFS 19.2 months in ROS1-rearranged NSCLC; PFS was immature (23/50 events). Grade 3 treatment-related hypophosphataemia and neutropenia each occurred in 10%, ALT elevation in 4%, and no treatment-related grade 4/5 events occurred. Five deaths were due to progression and considered unrelated.

records.title: Entrectinib (integrated ALKA/STARTRK)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ROS1-positive · I/II · 2020
records.body: Adults with locally advanced/metastatic ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC, ROS1-inhibitor naive, RECIST 1.1 measurable disease, ECOG 0-2, treated with at least one 600 mg entrectinib dose and followed at least 12 months; prior non-ROS1 therapy and asymptomatic or controlled brain metastases were allowed (single-arm pooled efficacy n=53) (single-arm) Entrectinib orally in 4-week cycles until radiographic progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal; pooled efficacy eligibility required at least 1 600-mg oral dose. ALKA-372-001 and STARTRK-1 included other dose levels/schedules; STARTRK-2 used 600 mg orally once daily Primary: Objective response rate, duration of response. Secondary: Progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, intracranial response, intracranial duration of response, intracranial progression-free survival, time to CNS progression Entrectinib showed activity in the descriptive single-arm pooled efficacy population: BICR ORR was 77% (41/53; 95% CI 64-88), median DoR among 41 responders 24.6 months (95% CI 11.4-34.8), and median PFS 19.0 months (95% CI 12.2-36.6; 25 events). In the BICR baseline-CNS subgroup, intracranial ORR was 55% (11/20; 95% CI 32-77). Radiotherapy-timing subgroups were small, descriptive, and had no interaction test. In the safety set (n=134), grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs were 34%, serious treatment-related AEs 11%, discontinuation for treatment-related AEs 5%, and all 9 deaths were deemed unrelated to treatment.

records.title: TRIDENT-1
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ROS1-positive · I/II · 2024
records.body: Advanced ROS1-rearranged NSCLC (TKI-naive and pretreated) Repotrectinib 160 mg once daily for 14 days then 160 mg twice daily (single-arm); to progression Primary: BICR-confirmed objective response rate. Secondary: duration of response, PFS, OS, intracranial response, safety Single-arm repotrectinib produced ORR 79%, response duration 34.1 months and PFS 35.7 months in ROS1 TKI-naive disease; after one prior ROS1 TKI, ORR was 38% and PFS 9.0 months. ORR was 59% with G2032R and intracranial ORR 89%/38% in the two cohorts. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 122/426; fatal AEs in 19/426, with none treatment related.

records.title: TRUST-I and TRUST-II integrated analysis
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · ROS1-positive · N/A · 2025
records.body: Adults with advanced ROS1 fusion-positive NSCLC, ECOG PS 0 or 1 and at least one measurable lesion; TKI-naïve or previously treated with one ROS1 TKI (crizotinib or entrectinib), with no more than one prior systemic chemotherapy line; asymptomatic or previously treated, clinically stable brain metastases permitted (single-arm) Taletrectinib 600 mg orally once daily in 21-day cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or consent withdrawal Primary: confirmed objective response rate. Secondary: disease control rate, duration of response, time to response, progression-free survival, intracranial objective response rate, intracranial disease control rate, safety At the June 7, 2024 cutoff, single-arm pooled data showed taletrectinib activity in both TKI-naïve and TKI-pretreated ROS1-positive NSCLC; comparative benefit remains unestablished. IRC cORR was 88.8% among 160 TKI-naïve patients and 55.8% among 113 TKI-pretreated patients; median DOR was 44.2 and 16.6 months and median PFS was 45.6 and 9.7 months, respectively. In measurable baseline brain metastases, IC-ORR was 76.5% among 17 TKI-naïve and 65.6% among 32 TKI-pretreated patients. Three treatment-related fatal events occurred.
records.keywords: Pérol M, Li W, Pennell NA, et al. Taletrectinib in ROS1-positive non–small cell lung cancer: TRUST. J Clin Oncol. 2025;43:1920-1929. doi:10.1200/JCO-25-00275

records.title: DESTINY-Lung01
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · HER2-altered (ERBB2) · II · 2022
records.body: Pretreated advanced HER2 (ERBB2)-mutant NSCLC Trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg IV Q3W (single-arm); to progression or toxicity Primary: BICR-confirmed objective response rate. Secondary: disease control, duration of response, PFS, OS, CNS activity, safety Single-arm trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg produced ORR 55%, response duration 9.3 months, PFS 8.2 months and OS 17.8 months in HER2-mutant NSCLC. Grade >=3 drug-related AEs occurred in 46%; ILD in 26%, including 2% grade 5, and 2 deaths were considered drug related.

records.title: DESTINY-Lung02
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · HER2-altered (ERBB2) · II · 2023
records.body: Previously treated (platinum) HER2 (ERBB2)-mutant metastatic NSCLC Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 mg/kg vs 6.4 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks, each until progression or discontinuation Primary: BICR-confirmed objective response rate. Secondary: investigator-assessed ORR, disease control, duration and time to response, PFS, OS, safety Trastuzumab deruxtecan 5.4 vs 6.4 mg/kg produced ORR 49.0% vs 56.0%; the lower dose had fewer grade >=3 drug-related AEs (38.6% vs 58.0%), discontinuations (14.9% vs 26.0%) and ILD (12.9% vs 28.0%), including grade 5 ILD 1.0% vs 2.0%. This dose-ranging study was not powered for between-dose efficacy comparison.

records.title: Beamion LUNG-1 (zongertinib)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · HER2-altered (ERBB2) · I · 2025
records.body: Previously treated HER2 (ERBB2) TKD-mutant advanced NSCLC (cohort 1) Zongertinib 120 mg once daily (single-arm); to progression Primary: BICR-confirmed objective response rate in cohorts 1 and 5. Secondary: investigator-assessed ORR in cohort 3, duration of response, PFS, CNS activity, safety Single-arm zongertinib 120 mg produced updated ORR 71%, median response duration 14.1 months and PFS 12.4 months. Drug-related grade >=3 AEs occurred in 17%, discontinuation in 3%, and ILD in 0%; all-cause fatal AEs were 9%, with none drug related.

records.title: SOHO-01 (sevabertinib)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · HER2-altered (ERBB2) · I/II · 2025
records.body: Previously treated HER2 (ERBB2)-mutant NSCLC, naive to HER2-targeted therapy (cohort D) Sevabertinib (BAY 2927088) 20 mg twice daily (single-arm); to progression Primary: BICR-confirmed objective response rate in each expansion cohort. Secondary: disease control, duration of response, PFS, brain-metastasis activity, safety Single-arm sevabertinib produced ORR 64%, response duration 9.2 months and PFS 8.3 months in the post-treatment cohort. Drug-related grade >=3 AEs occurred in 38%, grade 3 diarrhoea in 23%, discontinuation in 5%, and no ILD or drug-related grade 5 events were reported.

records.title: CodeBreaK 200
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · III · 2023
records.body: Pretreated advanced KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC Sotorasib 960 mg orally once daily vs docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks, each until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: ORR, duration of response, OS, safety Sotorasib improved PFS vs docetaxel (5.6 vs 4.5 months; HR 0.66; P=.0017) and ORR was 28.1% vs 13.2%. Final OS was negative (10.6 vs 11.3 months; HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.77-1.33). Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 56/169 vs 61/151; related deaths 1 vs 2.

records.title: KRYSTAL-12 (adagrasib)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · III · 2025
records.body: Previously treated advanced KRAS G12C-mutated NSCLC (post platinum + anti-PD-(L)1) Adagrasib 600 mg orally twice daily vs docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks, each until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: BICR ORR, duration of response, OS, intracranial activity, safety Adagrasib improved PFS vs docetaxel (5.5 vs 3.8 months; HR 0.58) and ORR was 32% vs 9%. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 140/298 vs 64/140; related deaths 4 vs 1.

records.title: Dabrafenib + trametinib (BRF113928)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · II · 2017
records.body: Untreated advanced BRAF V600E-mutant NSCLC (first-line cohort) Dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily + trametinib 2 mg once daily (single-arm); to progression Primary: investigator-assessed objective response rate. Secondary: independent-review ORR, PFS, duration of response, OS, safety Single-arm dabrafenib-trametinib produced ORR 64% (23/36), median PFS 10.9 months and OS 24.6 months in untreated BRAF V600E NSCLC. Grade 3/4 AEs occurred in 25/36; one grade 5 cardiorespiratory-arrest event was considered unrelated.

records.title: INSIGHT 2
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · II · 2024
records.body: EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC with MET amplification after progression on first-line osimertinib Tepotinib 500 mg + osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily until progression/toxicity (single-arm combination cohort) Primary: independently confirmed objective response rate in the central-FISH population with at least 9 months' follow-up. Secondary: duration of response, PFS, OS, safety Single-arm tepotinib-osimertinib produced ORR 50% and median PFS 5.6 months after first-line osimertinib in MET-amplified EGFR-mutant NSCLC; the small internal tepotinib-only cohort had ORR 8.3%. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 34%; potentially treatment-related deaths 4/128 and permanent discontinuation 13/128. Comparisons were descriptive.

records.title: LIBRETTO-431
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated advanced RET fusion-positive non-squamous NSCLC Selpercatinib 160 mg orally twice daily until progression/toxicity vs carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² ± pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 21 days for 4 cycles, then pemetrexed ± pembrolizumab maintenance until progression/toxicity Primary: BICR PFS hierarchically in the ITT-pembrolizumab then overall ITT populations. Secondary: OS, investigator-assessed PFS, ORR, duration of response, pulmonary-symptom deterioration, intracranial response and time to progression, safety In the prespecified pembrolizumab-intent population, selpercatinib improved interim BICR PFS vs platinum-pemetrexed-pembrolizumab: 24.8 vs 11.2 months (HR 0.46; P<.001). Overall-ITT PFS also favoured selpercatinib (HR 0.48); OS was immature (HR 1.04, 95% CI 0.58-1.87). ORR was 84% vs 65%; intracranial ORR 82% vs 58% (exploratory). Grade >=3 AEs were 70% vs 57%; grade >=3 ALT elevation 22% vs 3% and hypertension 20% vs 3%; dose reductions 51% vs 29%.

records.title: AcceleRET Lung
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · III · 2026
records.body: Previously untreated RET fusion-positive advanced/metastatic NSCLC without another actionable oncogenic driver or prior selective RET inhibitor Pralsetinib 400 mg orally once daily vs histology-based platinum chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab (non-squamous: platinum–pemetrexed ± pembrolizumab → pemetrexed ± pembrolizumab maintenance; squamous: platinum–gemcitabine or carboplatin + paclitaxel/nab-paclitaxel + pembrolizumab, until progression or up to 2 years) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: ORR, OS, duration of response, safety Pralsetinib improved investigator-assessed PFS vs platinum chemotherapy ± pembrolizumab (18.7 vs 9.0 months; HR 0.59) and ORR was 65.5% vs 41.6%. OS was negative (not reached vs 39.8 months; HR 1.09, 95% CI 0.65-1.85). Infection occurred in 71.3% vs 51.9%, including 8 vs 0 infection-related deaths. Conference abstract; the trial ended early for sponsor organisational/commercial reasons.

records.title: PHAROS
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Other actionable drivers (KRAS G12C, BRAF, MET, RET, NTRK) · II · 2023
records.body: Histologically confirmed NSCLC; stage IV or recurrent, treatment-naive or previously treated with first-line platinum-based chemotherapy ± anti-PD-1/PD-L1 (more than one prior advanced-setting line excluded); BRAF V600 class I mutation by local NGS or PCR testing; excluded prior BRAF/MEK inhibitor, other drivers (EGFR, ALK, ROS1), untreated symptomatic brain metastases or leptomeningeal disease (untreated <5 mm or treated brain metastases allowed if asymptomatic and stable ≥28 days) (single-arm) encorafenib 450 mg orally once daily + binimetinib 45 mg orally twice daily in 28-day cycles until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal of consent, initiation of subsequent anticancer therapy or death; binimetinib could be stopped with encorafenib continued, but stopping encorafenib required stopping binimetinib Primary: confirmed objective response rate. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, progression-free survival, time to response, overall survival, safety, pharmacokinetics, biomarker analyses Encorafenib plus binimetinib showed meaningful clinical benefit in treatment-naive and previously treated BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic NSCLC, with safety consistent with the approved melanoma indication; as a single-arm study it does not establish comparative benefit. The primary endpoint was met in both cohorts: IRR-assessed ORR 75% (95% CI, 62 to 85) treatment-naive and 46% (95% CI, 30 to 63) previously treated; this updated report gives 49% (95% CI, 32 to 65) previously treated. At the March 14, 2025 cutoff, median OS was 47.6 mo (95% CI, 31.3 to NE) and 22.7 mo (95% CI, 14.1 to 32.6) at median OS follow-up of 52.3 and 48.2 mo; 4-year OS 49% and 31%. Updated median DOR 40.0 and 16.7 mo; median PFS by IRR 30.4 and 9.3 mo. Grade 3/4 TRAEs in 46% of 98 patients; commonest TRAEs nausea 52%, diarrhea 44%, fatigue 33%; TRAEs led to dose reduction of each drug in 33% and permanent discontinuation in 20%; one grade 5 treatment-related intracranial hemorrhage.

records.title: KEYNOTE-024
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2016
records.body: Untreated stage IV NSCLC, PD-L1 >=50%, no EGFR/ALK; ECOG 0-1; excluded untreated brain metastases, active autoimmune disease needing systemic therapy within 2 years, active ILD or glucocorticoid-treated pneumonitis, systemic glucocorticoids or immunosuppression First-line pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles / 2 years; second course up to 17 cycles allowed for progression after 35 cycles or after confirmed CR) vs platinum-doublet chemotherapy (4–6 cycles; investigator's choice of carboplatin or cisplatin plus pemetrexed or gemcitabine, or carboplatin plus paclitaxel; optional pemetrexed maintenance for nonsquamous; crossover to pembrolizumab allowed at BICR-verified progression before the second interim analysis, investigator-assessed progression thereafter) Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, PFS2, safety, tolerability Pembrolizumab improved PFS, the primary endpoint, vs platinum chemotherapy in untreated PD-L1 TPS >=50% NSCLC, with superiority established at the second interim analysis; at the 5-year cut, updated investigator-assessed PFS HR was 0.50 (median 7.7 vs 5.5 months). At 5 years, pembrolizumab improved OS (26.3 vs 13.4 months; HR 0.62; 5-year OS 31.9% vs 16.3%) despite a 66.0% effective crossover rate; no alpha was assigned to this analysis. ORR 46.1% vs 31.1%; median DoR 29.1 vs 6.3 months; exploratory PFS2 HR 0.51. Of 39 patients completing 35 cycles, 82.1% were alive at data cutoff. Treatment-related grade 3-5 AEs were 31.2% vs 53.3% and related deaths 1.3% vs 2.0%.
records.keywords: Reck et al. N Engl J Med 2016;375:1823-1833   Reck et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:2339-2349  33872070

records.title: KEYNOTE-042
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated advanced NSCLC, PD-L1 >=1%, no EGFR/ALK First-line pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W (to 35 cycles) vs platinum-doublet chemotherapy (4–6 cycles) Primary: OS in PD-L1 TPS >=50%, >=20% and >=1% populations. Secondary: BICR PFS, BICR ORR, duration of response, PFS2, safety At 5 years, pembrolizumab improved OS vs platinum chemotherapy across nested PD-L1 populations; in TPS >=1%, median OS was 16.4 vs 12.1 months (HR 0.79; 5-year OS 16.6% vs 8.5%). The exploratory TPS 1-49% estimate was inconclusive (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.75-1.04). Treatment-related AEs were 63.8% vs 90.2%; no new fatal treatment-related events occurred.

records.title: IMpower110
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2020
records.body: Untreated metastatic non-squamous or squamous NSCLC, EGFR/ALK wild-type, PD-L1 >=1% (SP142) Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV every 3 weeks until progression/loss of benefit/toxicity vs histology-based platinum chemotherapy every 3 weeks for 4 or 6 cycles Primary: OS in hierarchically nested SP142 PD-L1 populations; investigator-assessed PFS if all OS hypotheses passed. records.title: RATIONALE-304
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · No actionable driver — immunotherapy & chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Treatment-naive stage IIIB/IV nonsquamous NSCLC not amenable to curative surgery or radiotherapy; without known EGFR-sensitising variants or ALK fusions on tissue testing; aged 18–75 y; excluded uncontrolled or untreated brain metastases, interstitial lung disease or noninfectious pneumonitis, active or relapsed autoimmune disease Tislelizumab 200 mg + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 + pemetrexed 500 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for 4-6 cycles, then tislelizumab-pemetrexed maintenance until progression vs platinum-pemetrexed for 4-6 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression, with crossover to tislelizumab monotherapy permitted on IRC-confirmed progression Primary: IRC progression-free survival for arm A vs arm B in the ITT population. Secondary: investigator-assessed PFS, IRC PFS by PD-L1 expression, IRC ORR, IRC duration of response, time to response, OS, safety Adding tislelizumab to platinum-pemetrexed significantly prolonged IRC-assessed PFS, with higher response rates and longer response duration. At the interim analysis (median follow-up 9.8 mo), median PFS was 9.7 vs 7.6 mo (HR 0.645, 95% CI 0.462-0.902; p=0.0044); at the final analysis (median follow-up 16.1 mo; descriptive) PFS remained improved (9.8 vs 7.6 months; HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.47-0.86), with ORR 57.8% vs 36.0%. OS was not improved at the final analysis (21.4 vs 21.3 months; HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.63-1.28) or at an ad hoc update (median follow-up 19.3 mo; HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.63-1.14); the trial was not powered for OS and allowed crossover, and a post hoc crossover-adjusted HR was 0.68 (95% CI 0.48-0.96). The trial was open-label and conducted entirely in China. Grade >=3 pneumonitis was 4.1% vs 0.9%; treatment-related deaths 4/222 vs 1/110.

Grade 3-5 rash was 9% vs 0 and diarrhoea 6% vs <1%; toxicity discontinuation 5% vs 2%. One pneumonitis death occurred in each arm.

records.title: SACHI
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2026
records.body: EGFR-mutated, MET-amplified locally advanced/metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC after first-line EGFR-TKI failure Savolitinib 600 mg (>=50 kg) or 400 mg (<50 kg) + osimertinib 80 mg orally once daily until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 IV every 21 days for 4-6 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression Primary: investigator-assessed PFS hierarchically in third-generation EGFR-TKI-naive then ITT populations. Secondary: IRC PFS, ORR, disease control, duration of response, OS, safety Savolitinib-osimertinib improved PFS vs chemotherapy in the third-generation-TKI-naive population (9.8 vs 5.4 months; HR 0.34) and ITT population (8.2 vs 4.5 months; HR 0.34). OS was immature and inconclusive (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.55-1.29). Grade >=3 AEs were 57% in both arms; treatment-related deaths 2% vs 0%.

records.title: HERTHENA-Lung02
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Advanced EGFR-mutant (Ex19del or L858R) NSCLC after progression on a 3rd-generation EGFR TKI Patritumab deruxtecan (HER3-DXd) vs platinum-based chemotherapy; dose, component drugs, schedules and treatment duration were not stated in the filed conference abstract Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, intracranial PFS, safety Conference-abstract evidence: patritumab deruxtecan improved BICR PFS vs platinum chemotherapy (5.8 vs 5.4 months; HR 0.77) and ORR was 35.2% vs 25.3%; OS was immature. Grade >=3 AEs were 73% vs 57%; adjudicated ILD occurred in 5%, including two grade 5 cases. Full publication remains unfiled.

records.title: OptiTROP-Lung04
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2026
records.body: EGFR exon 19 deletion/L858R locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC after EGFR-TKI progression Sacituzumab tirumotecan 5 mg/kg IV days 1 and 15 every 28 days until progression/toxicity vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV every 21 days for up to 4 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression Primary: BICR progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, investigator-assessed PFS, ORR, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, safety Sacituzumab tirumotecan improved PFS vs platinum-pemetrexed (8.3 vs 4.3 months; HR 0.49) and interim OS (median not reached vs 17.4 months; HR 0.60; 18-month OS 65.8% vs 48.0%). Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs were 58.0% vs 53.8%; no drug-related ILD was reported.

records.title: ATTLAS (KCSG-LU19-04)
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Stage IV EGFR-mutated or ALK-translocated NSCLC after relevant TKI progression Atezolizumab 1200 mg + bevacizumab 15 mg/kg + paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5/5.5 IV every 21 days for 4 or 6 cycles, then atezolizumab-bevacizumab maintenance until progression vs pemetrexed 500 mg/m² + carboplatin AUC 5 or cisplatin 70 mg/m² for 4 or 6 cycles, then pemetrexed maintenance until progression Primary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival. Secondary: OS, ORR, duration of response, landmark PFS and OS, safety Atezolizumab-bevacizumab-carboplatin-paclitaxel improved PFS vs pemetrexed-platinum (8.48 vs 5.62 months; HR 0.62; P=.004); ORR was 69.5% vs 41.9%. OS was negative (20.63 vs 20.27 months; HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.69-1.46). PD-L1 subgroup estimates were exploratory without an interaction test. Grade >=3 treatment-related AEs were 35.1% vs 14.9%; related deaths 3/151 vs 0/74.

records.title: CURB
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · II · 2024
records.body: Adults with histologically confirmed metastatic NSCLC or breast cancer after at least one systemic-therapy line, with extracranial oligoprogression in up to five RECIST/PERCIST lesions all safely amenable to SBRT; prior brain metastases/radiotherapy were allowed, but same-site re-irradiation was not. Standard-of-care systemic therapy per physician discretion (no protocol SBRT) vs SBRT to all oligoprogressive sites plus standard-of-care systemic therapy per physician discretion; SBRT dose/fractionation selected by the treating radiation oncologist, usually 27-30 Gy in 3 fractions or 30-50 Gy in 5 fractions, with other schemes used infrequently for organ-at-risk constraints Primary: PFS to 12 months from randomisation to systemic disease progression. Secondary: OS, time to new systemic therapy and PFS by disease site, SBRT toxicity, quality of life, paired-blood biomarkers At the planned interim analysis, SBRT improved the alpha-protected pooled primary PFS endpoint vs standard of care (7.2 vs 3.2 months; HR 0.53, 95% CI 0.35-0.81; P=.0035, crossing the P<.006 boundary). In the prespecified NSCLC subgroup, median PFS was 10.0 vs 2.2 months (nominal HR 0.41, 95% CI 0.22-0.75; P=.0039); 86% had no actionable driver alteration. The breast-cancer subgroup was negative (4.4 vs 4.2 months; HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.43-1.43), with no treatment-by-disease interaction reported. Pooled OS was inconclusive (HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.55-1.81); grade >=2 adverse events occurred in 62% vs 41%, including SBRT-attributed grade >=2 toxicity in 16%.

records.title: SAVANNAH
records.subtitle: Advanced NSCLC · Second-line & post-progression therapy · II · 2025
records.body: EGFR-TKI-sensitizing-mutated locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC; radiologic progression on osimertinib (first-line only from protocol versions 6-7; versions 1-4 allowed no more than three prior lines); central MET overexpression and/or amplification on post-progression tissue, initially IHC3+/≥50% and/or FISH5+ (≥5 MET gene copies or MET/CEP7 ratio ≥2), from version 7 IHC3+/≥90% and/or FISH10+ (≥10 MET gene copies); measurable RECIST 1.1 disease, ECOG PS 0 or 1 Oral savolitinib 300 mg b.i.d. + osimertinib 80 mg o.d. vs savolitinib 300 mg o.d. + osimertinib 80 mg o.d. vs savolitinib 600 mg o.d. + osimertinib 80 mg o.d. (dose cohorts allocated by protocol version) vs savolitinib 300 mg b.i.d. + placebo (double-blind, randomized against the 300 mg b.i.d. combination under protocol version 7); 28-day cycles until objective progression, unacceptable toxicity or consent withdrawal Primary: confirmed objective response rate (savolitinib 300 mg b.i.d. cohort, MET IHC3+/≥90% and/or FISH10+, after first-line osimertinib), confirmed objective response rate (savolitinib 300 mg o.d. cohort, MET IHC3+/≥50% and/or FISH5+). Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, overall survival, safety, depth of response, time to onset of response Savolitinib 300 mg b.i.d. plus osimertinib showed high, durable responses in EGFR-mutated advanced NSCLC with MET IHC3+/≥90% and/or FISH10+ after first-line osimertinib; the primary cohort was single-arm, so comparative benefit is unestablished. In the primary efficacy population (n = 80), investigator-assessed confirmed ORR was 56.3% (95% CI 44.7-67.3%), with the lower bound above the ~30% historical chemotherapy reference; BICR ORR 55.0%; median DoR 7.1 mo; median PFS 7.4 mo (median follow-up 5.70 mo). In the small randomized CAS, BICR ORR was 58.3% with osimertinib vs 16.0% with placebo. The 300 mg o.d. co-primary cohort (IHC3+/≥50% and/or FISH5+) had ORR 31.6% (95% CI 25.2-38.6%) against a planned 30% null; no test result was reported. Among 341 combination-treated patients, grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 51.0%, serious AEs in 33.1% and AEs leading to death in 5.9%; peripheral edema 46.0%, grade ≥3 pulmonary embolism 4.4%.
records.keywords: de Marinis et al. Ann Oncol 2025;36:920-933

records.title: Pignon Meta-Analysis
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — chemoradiation · N/A · 1992
records.body: Individual-patient data from 13 randomised trials of chemotherapy plus or minus thoracic RT in limited-stage SCLC; extensive-disease patients were excluded; trial eligibility, chemotherapy, RT timing/dose/fractionation and PCI varied Trial-defined chemotherapy + thoracic RT (32–50 Gy in 8–25 fractions; start day 1–224; concurrent/alternating or sequential; some PCI) vs the same chemotherapy without thoracic RT Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: 3-year survival, sensitivity analyses, indirect RT timing/sequence comparisons, exploratory modifiers Adding thoracic RT reduced mortality (RR 0.86; p=.001) and improved 3-year OS 14.3% vs 8.9% (+5.4 points). Indirect comparisons did not show a clear early-vs-late or sequential-vs-nonsequential advantage. Nonfatal toxicity could not be pooled reliably

records.title: INT-0096 (Turrisi)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — chemoradiation · III · 1999
records.body: Previously untreated, histologically/cytologically confirmed LS-SCLC confined to one hemithorax, the ipsilateral supraclavicular fossa, or both; any pleural effusion, contralateral hilar/supraclavicular adenopathy, prior cancer, symptomatic cardiac disease, or MI within 6 months excluded Thoracic RT concurrent from chemotherapy cycle 1 with cisplatin 60 mg/m² day 1 + etoposide 120 mg/m² days 1–3 Q21D ×4: 45 Gy/30 BID fractions (1.5 Gy) over 3 weeks vs 45 Gy/25 QD fractions (1.8 Gy) over 5 weeks; complete responders offered PCI 25 Gy/10 Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Treatment failure/local failure, tumour response and toxicity Twice-daily RT improved primary OS in 417 ITT patients: median 23 vs 19 mo; HR for death with once-daily vs twice-daily 1.2 (95% CI 1.0–1.6; p=.04); 5-year OS 26% vs 16%. Secondary 2-year failure-free survival (29% vs 24%; nominal p=.10) and local failure (36% vs 52%; nominal p=.06) did not show nominally significant differences. Among 409 patients with toxicity data (including 28 ineligible), grade-3 oesophagitis was 27% vs 11%; nominal p<.001 applied to the ordinal incidence comparison, not grade 3 alone. Grade-4 oesophagitis was 5% in each arm, with no permanent stricture reported. There were 11 treatment-related deaths (6 twice-daily vs 5 once-daily).

records.title: CONVERT
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — chemoradiation · III · 2017
records.body: Adults with cytologically/histologically confirmed LS-SCLC encompassable in a radical RT portal, ECOG 0–1 or disease-related ECOG 2; no malignant pleural/pericardial effusion; acceptable RT volume, FEV1 >1 L or 40% predicted and DLCO >40%; no more than one adverse factor (ALP >1.5×ULN, sodium <LLN, LDH >ULN) Thoracic RT from day 22/cycle 2: 45 Gy/30 twice-daily 1.5-Gy fractions ≥6 h apart, 5 days/week over 19 days vs 66 Gy/33 once-daily 2-Gy fractions, 5 days/week over 45 days; both with cisplatin-etoposide Q3W for 4 or 6 cycles (etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1-3 plus cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1 or 25 mg/m² IV days 1-3), 3D conformal RT without elective nodal irradiation, and PCI within 6 weeks of final chemotherapy for eligible non-progressors Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Treatment compliance, acute toxicity, late toxicity, local progression-free survival, metastatic progression-free survival, response Once-daily RT did not improve modified-ITT primary OS versus twice-daily: median 25 vs 30 months; HR for death 1.18 (95% CI 0.95–1.45), p=.14. This negative superiority result does not establish equivalence. Grade 3–4 oesophagitis was 47/246 vs 47/254 (19% in each arm; nominal p=.85). Grade 3–4 pneumonitis was 4/246 vs 4/254 (nominal p=.70); grade 3–5 counts were 6 vs 5, including 2 vs 1 deaths, with no separate p value. The headline reported 11 treatment-related deaths (8 vs 3), but detailed causes enumerate 12 instances; the discrepancy remains unresolved.

records.title: PCI Overview Collaborative Group (Aupérin)
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI) · N/A · 1999
records.body: IPD from 7 randomised trials of histologically proven SCLC in complete remission after induction chemotherapy ± thoracic RT, with no brain metastases or prior cranial RT; trials included both limited- and extensive-stage disease PCI (n=526; trial-defined 8–40 Gy in 1–20 fractions, most commonly 24 Gy/8 fractions) vs no PCI (n=461); one cranial-irradiation course after complete response Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, brain and other metastases, local/regional recurrence PCI improved OS (RR death 0.84; p=.01) and 3-year OS 20.7% vs 15.3% (+5.4 points). Brain metastases were reduced (RR 0.46; p<.001; 3-year incidence 33.3% vs 58.6%). Only 140 patients had extensive-stage disease, limiting stage-specific certainty. Neurotoxicity evidence was limited and longer follow-up was needed

records.title: ADRIATIC
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — consolidation immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Adults with medically inoperable stage I–II or stage III LS-SCLC, WHO 0–1, no progression after definitive concurrent platinum–etoposide CRT, and no unresolved grade ≥2 CRT toxicity; prior PCI allowed After concurrent platinum–etoposide CRT ± PCI: durvalumab 1500 mg IV Q4W vs durvalumab 1500 mg + tremelimumab 75 mg IV Q4W ×4 then durvalumab Q4W vs placebo; continue to progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or 24 months Primary: Overall survival and progression-free survival for durvalumab. Secondary: Overall survival and progression-free survival for durvalumab+tremelimumab, objective response, response duration, survival landmarks, safety including pneumonitis Both primary endpoints were met with durvalumab vs placebo: interim median OS 55.9 vs 33.4 mo (HR 0.73; p=.01) and median PFS 16.6 vs 9.2 mo (HR 0.76; p=.02). The durvalumab+tremelimumab OS endpoint was not met and that arm remained blinded. Grade 3/4 all-cause AEs were 24.4% vs 24.2%, AE deaths 2.7% vs 1.9%, and pneumonitis/radiation pneumonitis 38.2% vs 30.2%, including one grade-5 event with durvalumab

records.title: ACHILES
records.subtitle: SCLC · Limited-stage SCLC (LS-SCLC) — consolidation immunotherapy · II · 2025
