records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2019
records.body: Locally advanced resectable gastric or Siewert I-III GEJ adenocarcinoma, cT2 or higher and/or cN+, without clinical distant metastases; perioperative treatment setting FLOT every 2 weeks ×4 preop → surgery → ×4 postop vs ECF/ECX every 3 weeks ×3 preop → surgery → ×3 postop Primary: Pathological complete tumour regression, overall survival. Secondary: R0 resection, disease-free survival, surgical morbidity and mortality, adverse events FLOT improved final ITT median OS (50 vs 35 months; HR 0.77), R0 resection and pathological complete regression versus ECF/ECX. Grade 3-4 neutropenia (51% vs 39%) and infection (18% vs 9%) were more frequent with FLOT, but treatment-related serious AEs were 27% in both arms and toxic deaths were 2 in each.

records.title: PRODIGY
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2021
records.body: Newly diagnosed resectable gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma, cT2-3N+M0 or cT4 any-N M0, suitable for D2 gastrectomy; excluded metastatic disease, prior gastric-cancer treatment or impaired oral-drug absorption DOS every 3 weeks ×3 preop → D2 gastrectomy → S-1 every 6 weeks ×8 vs D2 gastrectomy → S-1 every 6 weeks ×8 Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, postoperative pathologic stage, R0 resection, safety Neoadjuvant DOS improved final modified-ITT 3-year PFS (66.3% vs 60.2%; HR 0.70), R0 resection and downstaging versus surgery followed by S-1. At the preliminary truncated cut, OS (74.2% vs 73.4%; HR 0.84) did not reach statistical significance. Grade ≥3 neutropenia was 12.6%, febrile neutropenia 9.2%, with 2/238 grade 5 neoadjuvant events.

records.title: RESOLVE
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2021
records.body: Treatment-naive resectable cT4aN+M0 or cT4b any-N M0 gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma planned for D2 gastrectomy Perioperative SOX every 3 weeks ×3 preop → D2 gastrectomy → ×5 postop → S-1 ×3 vs D2 gastrectomy → SOX every 3 weeks ×8 vs D2 gastrectomy → CAPOX every 3 weeks ×8 Primary: 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: 5-year overall survival, R0 resection, safety Perioperative SOX improved 3-year DFS versus adjuvant CAPOX (59.4% vs 51.1%; HR 0.77), while adjuvant SOX met its independent noninferiority hypothesis. At longer follow-up, 5-year OS was 60.0% with perioperative SOX and 61.0% with adjuvant SOX versus 52.1% with adjuvant CAPOX (HR 0.79 and 0.77); no OS subgroup interaction supported treatment selection.
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2021;22:1081-1092   Lancet Oncol 2025;26:312-319 5-yr overall survival 39952264

records.title: RESONANCE
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2024
records.body: Resectable stage II/III gastric cancer assigned to perioperative versus postoperative SOX SOX ×2-4 preop → surgery → SOX ×4-6 postop vs surgery → SOX ×8 postop Disease-free survival, R0 resection, treatment completion, pathological complete response, surgical outcomes, postoperative complications, safety Perioperative SOX was associated with higher reported modified-ITT 3-year DFS (61.7% vs 53.8%; HR 0.76), R0 resection (94.9% vs 83.7%) and 8-cycle completion (41.1% vs 19.2%) than postoperative SOX. OS was not reported. Grade 3-4 neutropenia was 19.6% preoperatively and 14.8% postoperatively in the perioperative arm versus 18.9%; deaths were 2 vs 1 with attribution unstated.

records.title: TOPGEAR (AGITG)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative & neoadjuvant chemotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2024
records.body: Surgeon-assessed resectable T3/T4 gastric adenocarcinoma or Siewert II GEJ with ≤2 cm oesophageal involvement, or Siewert III adenocarcinoma; node-positive or node-negative, although the randomised population included cT1/T2 and cTX disease ECF/ECX ×2 or FLOT ×3 preop → 45 Gy/25 fractions over 5 weeks with continuous 5-FU or capecitabine → surgery → postop chemotherapy vs ECF/ECX ×3 or FLOT ×4 preop → surgery → the same postop chemotherapy Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, pathological complete response, toxic effects, quality of life Adding preoperative chemoradiotherapy increased pCR (17% vs 8%) but did not improve final OS (median 46 vs 49 months; HR 1.05) or PFS (median 31 vs 32 months; HR 0.98). Grade ≥3 toxicity was 66% vs 61%, and grade ≥3 surgical complications were 18% vs 16%.

records.title: INT-0116 (SWOG 9008)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · III · 2001
records.body: Completely resected gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma, 1988 AJCC stage IB-IV M0, after curative-intent negative-margin gastrectomy; D2 dissection was recommended but not required Gastrectomy → observation vs gastrectomy → 5-FU/leucovorin ×1 → 45 Gy/25 fractions over 5 weeks with concurrent 5-FU/leucovorin → 5-FU/leucovorin ×2 Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Relapse-free survival, toxic effects, first site of relapse Adjuvant chemoradiotherapy improved eligible-ITT median OS (36 vs 27 months; 3-year 50% vs 41%; HR for death with surgery alone 1.35) and relapse-free survival after R0 gastrectomy. Only 64% completed treatment as planned; grade 3 and 4 toxicities occurred in 41% and 32%, and 3/273 died from attributed toxic effects.

records.title: ACTS-GC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · III · 2007
records.body: Japanese stage II (excluding T1), IIIA or IIIB gastric cancer after R0 D2-or-greater gastrectomy, with negative peritoneal cytology and no hepatic, peritoneal or distant metastases; no prior cancer therapy apart from gastrectomy D2-or-greater R0 gastrectomy → observation vs D2-or-greater R0 gastrectomy → S-1 twice daily for 4 weeks on/2 weeks off every 6 weeks for 1 year Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Relapse-free survival, safety of S-1, first site of relapse After D2-or-greater R0 resection, 1 year of adjuvant S-1 improved updated-interim 3-year OS (80.1% vs 70.1%; HR 0.68) and relapse-free survival in the Japanese stage II/III population; the trial stopped early. Grade 3-4 anorexia, nausea and diarrhoea occurred in 6.0%, 3.7% and 3.1%.

records.title: CLASSIC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · III · 2012
records.body: AJCC/UICC stage II-IIIB gastric adenocarcinoma without metastases after R0 D2 gastrectomy with at least 15 examined nodes; no prior chemotherapy, immunotherapy or radiotherapy for gastric cancer D2 R0 gastrectomy → observation vs D2 R0 gastrectomy → CAPOX every 3 weeks ×8 over 6 months Primary: 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, safety At the planned interim analysis, adjuvant CAPOX improved 3-year DFS after R0 D2 gastrectomy (74% vs 59%; HR 0.56). OS remained immature (3-year 83% vs 78%; HR 0.72). Severe adverse events occurred in 56% vs 6%; 10% discontinued CAPOX for adverse events, with 1 possibly treatment-related death.

records.title: JACCRO GC-07 (START-2)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · III · 2019
records.body: Pathologic stage IIIA-IIIC gastric cancer after R0 D2-or-greater gastrectomy under Japanese 3rd-English/AJCC 7 staging S-1 every 6 weeks for 1 year vs S-1 lead-in → S-1 + docetaxel every 3 weeks ×6 → S-1 to complete 1 year Primary: 3-year relapse-free survival. Secondary: 3-year overall survival, 5-year overall survival, 5-year relapse-free survival, adverse events At the interim analysis, adding docetaxel improved projected 3-year RFS (66% vs 50%; HR 0.63), but median follow-up was 12.5 months and only 179 patients had reached 3 years. OS was immature (44 vs 60 deaths), and a mature OS benefit was not established. Severe adverse events occurred in 58% vs 42%; 1 S-1 patient died of respiratory failure considered drug related, although the Discussion states no treatment-related deaths.

records.title: ARTIST 2
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant therapy — resected gastric adenocarcinoma · III · 2021
records.body: Node-positive AJCC 2010 stage II or III gastric adenocarcinoma after R0 D2 gastrectomy S-1 days 1-28 every 6 weeks ×8 (1 year) vs SOX every 3 weeks ×8 (6 months) vs SOX ×2 → 45 Gy/25 fractions over 5 weeks with concurrent S-1 → SOX ×4 Primary: 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, pattern of recurrence, safety, quality of life At the interim analysis with 178/226 DFS events, SOX improved 3-year DFS versus S-1 (74.3% vs 64.8%; HR 0.693), while SOXRT versus S-1 did not reach statistical significance (72.8%; HR 0.724, 95% CI 0.507-1.032). The trial was not designed to compare SOX with SOXRT; OS was unreported. Grade 3-4 neuropathy was absent with S-1 and occurred in 12%/6% with SOX/SOXRT; 4 deaths occurred during or within 30 days of treatment.

records.title: KEYNOTE-585
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated locally advanced, non-metastatic resectable gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma, T3 or higher or any node-positive disease, including Siewert II/III tumours; planned surgery after preoperative chemotherapy Pembrolizumab every 3 weeks + cisplatin/fluoropyrimidine ×3 preop → surgery → ×3 postop → pembrolizumab ×11 vs placebo on the same schedule; FLOT cohort: pembrolizumab + FLOT every 2 weeks ×4 preop → surgery → ×4 postop → pembrolizumab ×11 vs placebo + FLOT on the same schedule Primary: Pathological complete response, event-free survival, overall survival, safety. Secondary: Disease-free survival, event-free survival, overall survival, safety Pembrolizumab increased pCR at the first interim cut (12.9% vs 2.0%), but did not meet the primary EFS endpoint at the third interim analysis (median 44.4 vs 25.3 months; HR 0.81). OS was immature and formal testing was not reached. Severe treatment-related adverse events were similar (65% vs 63%), but discontinuations (26% vs 20%), immune events and treatment-related deaths (4 vs 2) were more frequent; perioperative anti-PD-1 was not established.

records.title: MATTERHORN
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2025
records.body: Previously untreated resectable stage II-IVA gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma eligible for radical surgery, irrespective of PD-L1 or MSI; excluded peritoneal/distant disease, squamous/adenosquamous histology and GIST Durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks + FLOT every 2 weeks ×2 preop → surgery → ×2 postop → durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks for ten additional cycles vs matched placebo plus the same FLOT and maintenance schedule Primary: event-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, pathological complete response, disease-free survival, surgery, R0 resection, metastasis-free survival, disease-specific survival, health-related quality of life, 24-month and 36-month overall survival, 24-month and 36-month event-free survival, 24-month and 36-month disease-free survival, overall survival by PD-L1 expression, association of PD-L1 expression with event-free survival, disease-free survival and pathological complete response, pharmacokinetics, anti-drug antibodies, safety Durvalumab plus FLOT improved interim EFS (24-month 67.4% vs 58.5%; HR 0.71) and final pCR (19.2% vs 7.2%). At the final OS analysis (data cutoff Sept 1, 2025; 37% maturity), durvalumab plus FLOT significantly improved OS (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63-0.96; p=0.021); OS was 76% vs 70% at 24 months and 69% vs 62% at 36 months, median not reached, with no evidence of proportional-hazards violation. The OS benefit was not evident in clinically node-negative disease (HR 1.01, 95% CI 0.67-1.51; interaction p=0.19), and the PD-L1 TAP <1% estimate was imprecise (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.41-1.50). EFS analyses by pathological and nodal response were post-hoc, exploratory and restricted to patients who completed surgery. Severe adverse events were similar (71.6% vs 71.2%), while serious events, regimen discontinuation and immune-mediated events were numerically more frequent with durvalumab; deaths possibly related to treatment occurred in 6 of 475 vs 2 of 469.
records.keywords: Janjigian et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393:217-230   Janjigian et al. Lancet 2026;408:1114-1128  42716074

records.title: DRAGON IV (CAP 05)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2025
records.body: Untreated imaging-resectable cT3-4a N+ M0 gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma in a perioperative SOX setting Camrelizumab + rivoceranib 250 mg daily + SOX every 3 weeks ×3 preop → D2 gastrectomy → ×3 postop → camrelizumab/rivoceranib ×3 (optional continuation to 1 year/17 camrelizumab doses) vs SOX ×3 preop → D2 → ×3 postop (optional S-1 to 1 year); initial rivoceranib 500 mg + SOX 3+3-cycle arm → rivoceranib ×3 (optional to 1 year) was stopped before the 2-arm phase Primary: Pathological complete response, event-free survival. Secondary: Major pathological response, total pathological complete response, ypN stage, R0 resection, disease-free survival, overall survival, safety At the interim pathological-response analysis, adding camrelizumab + rivoceranib to perioperative SOX increased pCR (18.3% vs 5.0%; OR 4.5). EFS, DFS and OS remain pending. Severe treatment-related adverse events (34% vs 17%), treatment modification (41% vs 26%) and immune-related events were more frequent, with no treatment-related deaths. The trial tested the whole combination and cannot isolate either component's contribution.

records.title: ASTRUM-006
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Perioperative immunotherapy — gastric & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated locally advanced resectable gastric or GEJ adenocarcinoma with centrally confirmed PD-L1 CPS ≥5; age 18-70 years Serplulimab + SOX every 3 weeks ×3 preop → surgery → serplulimab every 3 weeks up to 17 cycles vs placebo + SOX ×3 preop → surgery → SOX every 3 weeks ×5 postop Primary: Event-free survival. Secondary: Event-free survival, overall survival, disease-free survival, pathological complete response, R0 resection, objective response, safety, quality of life Perioperative serplulimab + SOX improved EFS in PD-L1 CPS ≥5 resectable gastric/GEJ cancer (median not reached vs 35.9 months; HR 0.73) and in the higher-CPS sequential primary analysis (HR 0.65). OS and DFS were immature. At this interim safety cut, severe treatment-related adverse events were less frequent (47% vs 59%), but treatment-related deaths occurred in 2 vs 1 patients. The trial tested whole perioperative strategies and does not isolate the effects of adjuvant serplulimab or omitting postoperative chemotherapy.

records.title: CROSS
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Neoadjuvant chemoradiation & perioperative strategy — esophageal & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2012
records.body: Potentially curable non-metastatic cT1N1 or cT2-3N0-1 oesophageal or true GEJ carcinoma: adenocarcinoma, squamous-cell or large-cell undifferentiated histology; suitable for chemoradiotherapy and surgery; printed age 18-75 and stage criteria notwithstanding, the randomised population included cT4 disease and patients aged up to 79 CROSS chemoradiotherapy: weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel ×5 + 41.4 Gy/23 fractions → surgery vs surgery alone Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, R0 resection, pathological response and nodal status, postoperative complications and mortality, toxicity, recurrence Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy improved ITT median OS (49.4 vs 24.0 months; HR 0.657), R0 resection (92% vs 69%) and pCR (29%) versus surgery alone. pCR was 49% in squamous and 23% in adenocarcinoma among treated patients, but no OS treatment-by-histology interaction supported differential benefit. In-hospital mortality was 4% in both arms; a chemoradiotherapy recipient died awaiting surgery.

records.title: Neo-AEGIS
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Neoadjuvant chemoradiation & perioperative strategy — esophageal & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2023
records.body: Resectable cT2-3 N0-3 M0 oesophageal or Siewert I-III GEJ adenocarcinoma, eligible for either perioperative chemotherapy or CROSS-type chemoradiotherapy followed by surgery Perioperative modified MAGIC ×3 preop → surgery → ×3 postop (later FLOT ×4 preop/postop permitted) vs CROSS chemoradiotherapy: weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel ×5 + 41.4 Gy/23 fractions → surgery Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, site of treatment failure, 90-day operative complications, toxicity, pathological complete and major response, R0 resection, health-related quality of life, time to treatment failure Neo-AEGIS did not establish noninferiority of perioperative chemotherapy to CROSS; recruitment stopped after the second futility analysis at 377/540 patients and the trial was underpowered (3-year OS 55% vs 57%; HR 1.03). CROSS improved pathological response and R0 resection, but no comparative survival advantage was proven; only 15% of the perioperative arm received FLOT.

records.title: ESOPEC
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Neoadjuvant chemoradiation & perioperative strategy — esophageal & GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2025
records.body: Resectable non-metastatic locally advanced oesophageal adenocarcinoma, including Siewert I-III GEJ disease, eligible for either FLOT or CROSS-type chemoradiotherapy followed by surgery FLOT every 2 weeks ×4 preop → surgery → ×4 postop vs CROSS chemoradiotherapy: weekly carboplatin/paclitaxel ×5 + 41.4 Gy/23 fractions → surgery Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, disease progression and recurrence, surgical and pathological outcomes, surgery-related death, adverse events Perioperative FLOT improved final ITT median OS (66 vs 37 months; HR 0.70) and 3-year PFS (51.6% vs 35.0%; HR 0.66) versus CROSS chemoradiotherapy. Grade ≥3 AEs were 58.0% vs 50.0% and serious AEs 47.3% vs 41.8%; postoperative mortality was 3.1% vs 5.6%.

records.title: CheckMate 577
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Adjuvant immunotherapy — resected esophageal & GEJ cancer · III · 2021
records.body: Resected oesophageal or GEJ adenocarcinoma or squamous-cell carcinoma with residual pathological disease after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and R0 resection, irrespective of PD-L1 expression Nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks for 16 weeks → 480 mg every 4 weeks to 1 year vs matched placebo on the same schedule Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, survival at 1 year, survival at 2 years, survival at 3 years, recurrence, distant metastasis-free survival, quality of life, safety At the prespecified interim analysis, adjuvant nivolumab prolonged median DFS (22.4 vs 11.0 months; HR 0.69) after residual disease following neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy and R0 resection. OS was not reported at this cut. Severe treatment-related adverse events were 13% vs 6%, discontinuations 9% vs 3%, with 1 disputed treatment-related death.

records.title: JCOG9907
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · III · 2012
records.body: Resectable thoracic oesophageal squamous-cell carcinoma, clinical stage II or III excluding T4; age ≤75 years; no prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy for any malignancy Oesophagectomy → CF every 3 weeks ×2 postop (pN+ only) vs CF every 3 weeks ×2 preop → oesophagectomy Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, chemotherapy toxicities, operative morbidity and mortality, clinical response rate, complete resection rate Moving CF preoperatively did not improve the final primary 5-year PFS comparison versus postoperative CF (44% vs 39%; HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.63-1.11). Secondary 5-year OS was 55% vs 43% (HR 0.73). Grade 3-4 chemotherapy toxicities were generally ≤8%, with no chemotherapy-related deaths; 1 surgery-related death occurred in each arm.

records.title: NEOCRTEC5010
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated potentially resectable thoracic oesophageal squamous-cell carcinoma, AJCC6 stage IIB/III (cT1-4N1M0 or cT4N0M0); age 18-70 years Vinorelbine/cisplatin every 3 weeks ×2 with concurrent 40 Gy/20 fractions → oesophagectomy vs oesophagectomy alone Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, safety, R0 resection, pathological response Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy improved final ITT median OS (100.1 vs 66.5 months; HR 0.71), R0 resection among operated patients (98.4% vs 91.2%) and pCR (43.2%) versus surgery alone. During chemoradiotherapy, severe haematologic toxicity occurred in 54.3%; peritreatment deaths were 5/224 vs 1/227, and 90-day postoperative mortality was 0.5% vs 0.9%.

records.title: JCOG1109 (NExT)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated resectable thoracic oesophageal squamous-cell, adenosquamous or basal-cell carcinoma, UICC7 stage IB-III excluding T4; age 20-75 years; planned oesophagectomy after neoadjuvant therapy CF every 3 weeks ×2 → oesophagectomy vs DCF every 3 weeks ×3 → oesophagectomy vs CF every 4 weeks ×2 with concurrent 41.4 Gy/23 fractions over 5 weeks → oesophagectomy Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, R0 resection, objective response, pathological complete response, adverse events, recurrence Neoadjuvant DCF improved primary 3-year OS versus CF (72.1% vs 62.6%; HR 0.68), while CF-RT did not (68.3%; HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.63-1.12). Grade 3-4 neutropenia and febrile neutropenia with DCF were 85% and 16%; treatment-related deaths were 4/196 with DCF, 3/193 with CF and 2/191 with CF-RT.

records.title: ESCORT-NEO/NCCES01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma — neoadjuvant / perioperative therapy · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated resectable thoracic oesophageal squamous-cell carcinoma, cT1b-3N1-3M0 or cT3N0M0 (AJCC8), with expected R0 resection; excluded supraclavicular nodal metastases or obvious adjacent-organ invasion Camrelizumab + nab-paclitaxel/cisplatin every 3 weeks ×2 → oesophagectomy → camrelizumab every 3 weeks up to 15 cycles vs camrelizumab + paclitaxel/cisplatin on the same sequence vs paclitaxel/cisplatin ×2 → oesophagectomy Primary: Pathological complete response, event-free survival. Secondary: Major pathological response, R0 resection, ypTNM stage, overall survival, disease-free survival, adverse events, surgical complications Both camrelizumab regimens improved ITT pCR versus paclitaxel/cisplatin: 28.0% with camrelizumab/nab-paclitaxel/cisplatin and 15.4% with camrelizumab/paclitaxel/cisplatin versus 4.7%. EFS remained immature; DFS and OS were unreported. Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs were 34.1%/29.2%/28.8%; 1 fatal treatment-related event occurred with camrelizumab/paclitaxel/cisplatin. No direct comparison between the camrelizumab regimens was prespecified.

records.title: RTOG 85-01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Definitive chemoradiation — non-surgical curative therapy (especially esophageal SCC) · III · 1999
records.body: Nondisseminated thoracic oesophageal squamous-cell carcinoma or adenocarcinoma with a normal tracheobronchial tree; no prior chest radiotherapy or chemotherapy or prior/concurrent malignancy; adenocarcinoma became eligible after October 1986 Cisplatin/5-FU ×4 (weeks 1, 5, 8 and 11), first 2 concurrent with 50 Gy/25 fractions over 5 weeks vs radiotherapy alone 64 Gy/32 fractions over 6.4 weeks Primary: overall survival. Secondary: patterns of treatment failure, acute toxic effects, late toxic effects Concurrent chemoradiotherapy improved final 5-year OS versus radiotherapy alone (26% vs 0%; median 14.1 vs 9.3 months). Randomisation stopped after the interim comparison. Acute life-threatening toxicity occurred in 8%, with 2% treatment-related deaths.

records.title: INT 0123 (RTOG 94-05)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Definitive chemoradiation — non-surgical curative therapy (especially esophageal SCC) · III · 2002
records.body: Cervical, mid, or distal esophageal squamous cell carcinoma or adenocarcinoma, AJCC T1–4 N0/1 M0, selected for definitive nonsurgical treatment; tumors had to end >2 cm above the gastroesophageal junction; excluded M1 disease, tracheobronchial invasion/fistula, and prior chemotherapy, thoracic radiotherapy, or resection Cisplatin/5-FU every 4 weeks ×4, first 2 concurrent with 64.8 Gy vs the same chemotherapy with 50.4 Gy Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Local/regional control and time to first local/regional failure or persistence, patterns of first failure, acute and late radiation toxicity, treatment-related mortality The truncated trial analysis, stopped after an interim futility review, found no survival or local-control advantage from 64.8 Gy over 50.4 Gy (median OS 13.0 vs 18.1 months). Treatment-related deaths were 10% vs 2%, but 7 of 11 high-dose-arm deaths occurred before patients had received more than 50.4 Gy.

records.title: PRODIGE5/ACCORD17
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Definitive chemoradiation — non-surgical curative therapy (especially esophageal SCC) · II/III · 2014
records.body: Previously untreated oesophageal squamous-cell, adenocarcinoma or adenosquamous cancer, TNM6 stage I-IVA including metastatic coeliac/cervical nodes but no distant metastases; definitive nonsurgical treatment because potentially unresectable, comorbidity or patient/physician choice FOLFOX every 2 weeks ×6, first 3 concurrent with 50 Gy/25 fractions over 5 weeks vs cisplatin/5-FU ×4, first 2 every 4 weeks concurrent with 50 Gy and 2 every 3 weeks after radiotherapy Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, endoscopic complete response, time to treatment failure, grade 3 or 4 toxicities, quality of life FOLFOX-CRT was not superior to fluorouracil/cisplatin-CRT for final ITT median PFS (9.7 vs 9.4 months; HR 0.93, 95% CI 0.70-1.24) at median 25.3 months' follow-up. Toxic deaths were 1/131 vs 6/128; all-grade paraesthesia (47% vs 2%) and sensory neuropathy (18% vs 1%) were more frequent with FOLFOX, while serum creatinine increase was more frequent with fluorouracil/cisplatin (3% vs 12%).

records.title: Hulscher (Dutch THTC)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2002
records.body: Resectable mid-to-distal oesophageal or gastric-cardia adenocarcinoma involving the distal oesophagus, without distant metastases or unresectable local disease; fit for surgery; no prior gastric/oesophageal surgery or neoadjuvant therapy Limited transhiatal oesophagectomy without formal lymphadenectomy (single procedure) vs extended transthoracic oesophagectomy with en-bloc two-field lymphadenectomy (single procedure) Primary: Overall survival, disease-free survival. Secondary: Early postoperative morbidity, in-hospital mortality, quality-adjusted survival, cost-effectiveness, disease-free interval Extended transthoracic resection did not improve the primary ITT OS comparison versus limited transhiatal resection (median 2.0 vs 1.8 years; 5-year 39% vs 29%; absolute-difference 95% CI -3 to 23), and DFS also did not reach statistical significance. Pulmonary complications were 57% vs 27% and in-hospital mortality 4% vs 2%; any survival trend remained inconclusive at median 4.7 years' follow-up.

records.title: JCOG9501
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · III · 2008
records.body: Potentially curable gastric adenocarcinoma, intraoperatively confirmed T2b/T3/T4 with no gross para-aortic nodal metastases and negative peritoneal cytology; age <75 years; Borrmann type 4 excluded D2 gastrectomy (single procedure) vs D2 gastrectomy + para-aortic nodal dissection (single procedure); no adjuvant therapy before recurrence Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Recurrence-free survival, surgery-related complications, hospital death Adding PAND to D2 did not improve final modified-ITT OS (HR for death 1.03, 95% CI 0.77-1.37) or recurrence-free survival (HR 1.08, 95% CI 0.83-1.42). Overall surgery-related complications were 28.1% vs 20.9%, minor complications 20.0% vs 9.1%, and hospital death 0.8% in both arms. D2 was already the regional standard; the result supports not extending it with PAND in experienced centres.

records.title: Dutch D1D2 (Songun)
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2010
records.body: Histologically proven gastric adenocarcinoma without distant metastases and suitable for D1 or D2 lymphadenectomy; curative-intent analysis required a macroscopically removable tumour without peritoneal, hepatic or distant-nodal metastases at laparotomy D1 gastrectomy vs D2 gastrectomy (single procedure) Primary: Overall survival, recurrence. Secondary: Disease-free survival, cause-specific death, postoperative mortality, complications, reoperation D2 reduced local recurrence and gastric-cancer death (37% vs 48%) versus D1, but excess operative harm offset these gains: the final modified-ITT 15-year OS difference did not reach statistical significance (29% vs 21%; HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.78-1.09). Operative mortality was 10% vs 4%, complications 43% vs 25% and reoperation 18% vs 8%.

records.title: TIME
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2012
records.body: Resectable intrathoracic oesophageal or GEJ cancer, cT1-3 N0-1 M0, with adenocarcinoma, squamous or undifferentiated histology; age 18-75 years; cervical oesophageal cancer excluded Open transthoracic oesophagectomy with two-field resection (single procedure) vs minimally invasive thoracoscopic/laparoscopic oesophagectomy with two-field resection (single procedure) Primary: Postoperative pulmonary infection. Secondary: Hospital stay, quality of life, pathology, operative outcomes, non-pulmonary complications, ICU stay, mortality, pain Minimally invasive oesophagectomy reduced pulmonary infection within 2 weeks (9% vs 29%) and during admission (12% vs 34%), shortened median stay (11 vs 14 days), and improved several 6-week quality-of-life domains. R0 resection, retrieved nodes, reoperation and short-term mortality were not clearly different; the trial did not test long-term oncologic equivalence.

records.title: CLASS-01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2019
records.body: Resectable cT2-4aN0-3M0 gastric adenocarcinoma (AJCC7 stages IB-IIIC, excluding T1/T4b) in the middle or lower stomach, planned for curative distal gastrectomy with D2 dissection; bulky regional nodes >3 cm or distant metastases excluded Laparoscopic vs open distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy (single procedure) Primary: 3-year disease-free survival. Secondary: 3-year overall survival, recurrence patterns, intraoperative and postoperative morbidity and mortality Laparoscopic distal gastrectomy met the 3-year DFS noninferiority margin in the primary analysis set (76.5% vs 77.8%); 3-year OS was 83.1% vs 85.2%. In a post hoc sensitivity excluding pathologic stage I, the lower confidence bound crossed the noninferiority margin.

records.title: KLASS-01
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2019
records.body: Resectable clinical stage I gastric adenocarcinoma suitable for distal gastrectomy: cT1N0M0, cT1N1M0 or cT2aN0M0; excluded prior chemotherapy/radiotherapy, another malignancy or need for combined resection other than cholecystectomy Laparoscopic vs open radical distal gastrectomy with D1+beta or D2 lymphadenectomy and partial omentectomy (single procedure) Primary: 5-year overall survival. Secondary: Gastric cancer-specific survival, morbidity and mortality, quality of life, cost-effectiveness, recurrence Laparoscopic distal gastrectomy met the prespecified 5-year OS noninferiority criterion (94.2% vs 93.3%); gastric cancer-specific survival and recurrence were similar. In-hospital deaths were reported in 4 vs 2 patients.

records.title: KLASS-02
records.subtitle: Localized Gastroesophageal · Surgical management — extent of resection & operative approach · N/A · 2020
records.body: Resectable gastric adenocarcinoma planned for curative distal subtotal gastrectomy, clinical T2-4a with no or limited perigastric nodal metastasis; excluded possible distant metastasis, prior gastric resection, gastric-cancer complications or prior gastric chemo/radiotherapy Laparoscopic vs open radical distal gastrectomy with D2 lymphadenectomy and total omentectomy (single procedure) Primary: 3-year relapse-free survival. Secondary: Postoperative morbidity and mortality, postoperative recovery, quality of life, 3-year overall survival, recurrence Laparoscopic distal gastrectomy met the reported 3-year RFS noninferiority conclusion (80.3% vs 81.3%; HR 1.04), but event maturity was truncated at 165 of 330 planned events and longer follow-up was needed. Early (15.7% vs 23.4%) and late complications (4.7% vs 9.5%) were lower; no baseline subgroup interaction supported a treatment mandate.

records.title: V325
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2006
records.body: Histologically proven gastric or esophagogastric junction adenocarcinoma; untreated advanced disease, first-line, no prior palliative chemotherapy; measurable and/or assessable metastatic disease (WHO) or locally recurrent disease with one or more measurable lymph nodes, Karnofsky performance status higher than 70; excluded concurrent cancer, neuropathy, brain or leptomeningeal involvement, uncontrolled significant comorbidity, and patients who could potentially undergo resection after response Docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV + cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 1, then fluorouracil 750 mg/m²/d continuous IV infusion days 1 to 5, every 3 weeks (DCF) vs cisplatin 100 mg/m² day 1 + fluorouracil 1,000 mg/m²/d days 1 to 5, every 4 weeks (CF); until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or consent withdrawal Primary: time to progression. Secondary: overall survival, overall response rate, time to 5% definitive deterioration in global health status (EORTC QLQ-C30), time to definitive worsening of Karnofsky performance status, safety Adding docetaxel to CF significantly improved TTP, survival and response rate in untreated advanced gastric cancer, with some increase in toxicity. In the 445-patient full analysis population, median TTP 5.6 vs 3.7 mo (HR 1.47, HR >1 favouring DCF; 95% CI 1.19 to 1.82; P<.001). Median OS 9.2 vs 8.6 mo (HR 1.29; 95% CI 1.0 to 1.6; P=.02) at median follow-up 23.4 mo; curves came near each other at the median, with 2-year OS 18% vs 9%. Confirmed ORR 37% vs 25%. Time to deterioration of global health status and to definitive worsening of Karnofsky PS was longer with DCF. Related grade 3 to 4 AEs 69% vs 59%; grade 3 to 4 neutropenia 82% vs 57%, diarrhea 19% vs 8%; complicated neutropenia 29% vs 12%. Deaths within 30 days of last infusion 23 (10%) vs 19 (8%); infection was the main cause of toxic deaths (7 of 8 DCF, 8 of 12 CF), mainly in DCF cycle one.
records.keywords: Van Cutsem et al. J Clin Oncol 2006;24:4991-4997

records.title: REAL-2
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2008
records.body: Adenocarcinoma, squamous-cell or undifferentiated carcinoma of the esophagus, gastroesophageal junction or stomach; locally advanced (inoperable) or metastatic, previously untreated; measurable disease per RECIST, ECOG PS 0–2; positive resection margin after radical surgery (tumour within 1 mm) without measurable disease also eligible, survival only; excluded prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy (unless adjuvant with relapse outside the field), uncontrolled cardiac disease, previous or concurrent cancer ECF: epirubicin 50 mg/m² IV bolus + cisplatin 60 mg/m² IV day 1 + fluorouracil 200 mg/m² daily by continuous infusion vs ECX: epirubicin + cisplatin + capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily continuously vs EOF: epirubicin + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 + fluorouracil vs EOX: epirubicin + oxaliplatin + capecitabine; every 3 weeks for a maximum of eight cycles unless progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or death Primary: overall survival. Secondary: overall survival among the four regimens, progression-free survival, response rate, toxic effects, quality of life Capecitabine and oxaliplatin were noninferior to fluorouracil and cisplatin, respectively, for OS in previously untreated advanced esophagogastric cancer. Per-protocol HR for death was 0.86 (95% CI 0.80–0.99) for capecitabine vs fluorouracil and 0.92 (95% CI 0.80–1.10) for oxaliplatin vs cisplatin, both below the 1.23 margin. In a secondary ITT analysis with P values unadjusted for multiple testing, EOX prolonged OS vs ECF (median 11.2 vs 9.9 mo; HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.66–0.97; P=0.02). PFS and response rates did not differ significantly among regimens. Oxaliplatin had less grade 3/4 neutropenia and less alopecia, renal toxicity and thromboembolism (7.6% vs 15.1%) but more grade 3/4 diarrhea and neuropathy than cisplatin; ECX had more grade 3/4 neutropenia (51.1% vs 41.7%) and hand-foot syndrome (10.3% vs 4.3%) than ECF.
records.keywords: Cunningham et al. N Engl J Med 2008;358:36-46

records.title: GASTFOX (PRODIGE 51)
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2025
records.body: Histologically confirmed gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; locally advanced unresectable or metastatic, no previous treatment for advanced cancer (first line); HER2-negative; RECIST 1.1 measurable disease, ECOG 0-1, prior (neo)adjuvant chemoradiotherapy allowed if relapse occurred 12 months after end of treatment; excluded grade ≥2 peripheral neuropathy, cerebral or meningeal metastases, known DPD deficiency, prior docetaxel-based treatment TFOX: docetaxel 50 mg/m², folinic acid 400 mg/m² and oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², then 5-fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² continuous 46 h infusion, IV every 2 weeks vs FOLFOX: folinic acid 400 mg/m², oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², 5-fluorouracil bolus 400 mg/m², then 5-fluorouracil 2400 mg/m² continuous 46 h infusion, IV every 2 weeks; both until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, investigator decision or patient refusal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, safety, quality of life, therapeutic index ratio, disease control rate TFOX significantly improved PFS, OS and ORR vs FOLFOX in previously untreated advanced HER2-negative gastric/GOJ adenocarcinoma and might represent a new first-line option for patients eligible for docetaxel triplet chemotherapy. At median follow-up 42.8 mo, median PFS 7.59 vs 5.98 mo; proportional hazards were violated, so 12-month restricted mean PFS was used: 7.52 vs 6.62 mo (p=0.0072). Median OS 15.08 vs 12.65 mo (HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68–0.99; p=0.048); ORR 62.3% vs 53.4% (p=0.045). Greater OS benefit with ECOG 0 or age <70 years was a post-hoc exploratory finding. Open-label, single-country trial; results do not apply to patients who received prior FLOT for resectable disease. Grade 3–4 TEAEs: neuropathy 32% vs 20%, neutropenia 27% vs 18%, diarrhoea 15% vs 7%; febrile neutropenia 3% vs 2%; serious treatment-related AEs 27% vs 13%; 2 vs 1 treatment-related deaths.

records.title: GO2
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2021
records.body: Locally advanced and/or metastatic gastroesophageal cancer; not pretreated, palliative chemotherapy; no biomarker selection (ERBB2-positive could add trastuzumab); oncologist considered full-dose standard combination chemotherapy unsuitable because of advanced age and/or frailty, no chronological age limit or fixed PS threshold, fit for the treatments of the selected randomization; CHEMO-BSC entry when the indication for chemotherapy was uncertain CHEMO-INTENSITY: Level A oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1 + capecitabine 625 mg/m² twice daily days 1-21, 21-day cycles vs Level B (80% of Level A doses) vs Level C (60% of Level A doses); CHEMO-BSC: Level C vs best supportive care alone; chemotherapy until radiological or clinical progression, unacceptable toxic effects or patient choice; optional trastuzumab for ERBB2-positive disease Primary: progression-free survival (CHEMO-INTENSITY), overall survival (CHEMO-BSC). Secondary: overall treatment utility, toxic effects, symptoms (QLQ-C30/OG25), quality of life, RECIST response, overall survival, quality-adjusted survival, time to deterioration of fatigue (CHEMO-INTENSITY); patient-reported fatigue, quality of life (CHEMO-BSC) Reduced-intensity oxaliplatin/capecitabine (Levels B and C) was noninferior to Level A for PFS under a permissive margin (HR 1.34) with less toxicity; the authors conclude it should be considered for older and/or frail patients. PFS HR B vs A 1.09 (95% CI 0.89-1.32), C vs A 1.10 (95% CI 0.90-1.33); no evidence higher dose improved OS (C vs A HR 1.14, 95% CI 0.92-1.41). Level C had more good (43%) and fewer poor (29%) OTU outcomes than A or B, but differences were not statistically significant; no subgroup benefited from higher doses. Grade ≥3 nonhematological toxicity within 9 weeks: 38% (A), 36% (B), 23% (C); 32%, 44% and 58% completed 3 cycles without reduction or stoppage. Exploratory CHEMO-BSC (n=45): OS nonsignificantly longer with Level C than BSC (median 6.1 vs 3.0 mo; HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.32-1.48). Baseline frailty, quality of life and NLR were independently associated with OTU.
records.keywords: Hall et al. JAMA Oncol 2021 (online ahead of print)

records.title: RELIGHT
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · III · 2026
records.body: HER2-negative gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic; previously untreated, first-line; any PD-L1 expression (stratified by CPS ≥5 vs <5); prior neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapy allowed if recurrence or progression interval ≥6 months; conducted at 64 centers across China Retlirafusp alfa 30 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks + CAPOX (capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1, every 3 weeks) for up to six cycles; retlirafusp alfa for up to 2 years or until progression or unacceptable toxicity vs matching placebo IV every 3 weeks + CAPOX on the same schedule (double-blind) Primary: overall survival in PD-L1 CPS ≥5 and overall populations. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, safety Adding retlirafusp alfa to CAPOX significantly prolonged OS versus placebo plus CAPOX at the interim analysis, and the authors support it as a first-line option; key limitations are a chemotherapy-alone comparator (not PD-1 inhibitor plus chemotherapy) and enrolment of Chinese patients only. Median OS was 16.8 vs 10.4 mo in PD-L1 CPS ≥5 (HR 0.53) and 15.8 vs 11.2 mo in the ITT set (HR 0.66); median follow-up 13.6 mo. ITT median PFS per BICR was 7.0 vs 5.5 mo (HR 0.57); confirmed ORR 53.4% vs 32.8%. In the PD-L1 CPS <1 subgroup, OS was worse with retlirafusp alfa (8.1 vs 12.8 mo; HR 2.22). Grade ≥3 TRAEs occurred in 62.6% vs 59.0% and serious TRAEs in 34.9% vs 24.0%; TRAEs led to discontinuation in 10.4% vs 3.0%; treatment-related deaths were seven (1.9%) vs four (1.1%).
records.keywords: Peng et al. J Clin Oncol 2026 (online ahead of print)

records.title: Shitara et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line chemotherapy backbone — HER2-negative · N/A · 2026
records.body: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma, HER2-negative or unknown HER2 status; first-line; RCTs of zolbetuximab or ICI plus chemotherapy in global trials, analysed by PD-(L)1 CPS ≥1 to <5, ≥5 to <10 and ≥10 (TAP used for tislelizumab); CLDN18.2 status not evaluated in ICI trials; Asia-only trials excluded Zolbetuximab + CAPOX/FOLFOX vs pembrolizumab + CF/CAPOX (CF/CX/CAPOX for CPS ≥10) vs tislelizumab + CF/CAPOX vs nivolumab + CAPOX/FOLFOX vs chemotherapy alone (common comparator); chemotherapy backbones assumed interchangeable Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: treatment ranking (SUCRA) In this indirect Bayesian NMA, zolbetuximab + chemotherapy had similar or numerically favourable OS and PFS vs ICI + chemotherapy at PD-(L)1 CPS ≥1 to <10, whereas ICIs were numerically favourable at CPS ≥10; findings need prospective confirmation. The CPS ≥5 to <10 PFS HR for zolbetuximab vs pembrolizumab was 0.75 (95% CrI 0.53, 1.06), not significant; at CPS ≥1 to <5, PFS vs tislelizumab 0.73 (0.54, 0.97); at CPS ≥10, OS vs tislelizumab 1.36 (0.98, 1.87). With optimal zolbetuximab exposure (no nausea/vomiting causing inadequate exposure or discontinuation), CPS ≥10 OS HRs vs chemotherapy were 0.67 zolbetuximab, 0.67 pembrolizumab, 0.57 tislelizumab and 0.68 nivolumab; selection bias is possible. The zolbetuximab ITT HR was applied to every CPS stratum; CLDN18.2 was not evaluated in most trials; most network links rest on a single trial; safety was not compared.

records.title: ToGA
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · III · 2010
records.body: Histologically confirmed inoperable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic adenocarcinoma of the stomach or gastro-oesophageal junction; first-line; centrally tested HER2-positive: IHC 3+ or FISH positive (HER2:CEP17 ratio ≥2); ECOG 0–2, measurable or non-measurable disease; excluded previous chemotherapy for metastatic disease, congestive heart failure, LVEF <50% or other significant cardiac disease, active gastrointestinal bleeding, brain metastases Trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV day 1 of cycle 1, then 6 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent, plus investigator's choice of capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily for 14 days then 1-week rest, or fluorouracil 800 mg/m²/day continuous IV infusion days 1–5, with cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV day 1, every 3 weeks for six cycles vs the same chemotherapy alone Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, time to progression, overall tumour response rate, duration of response, safety Adding trastuzumab to cisplatin plus capecitabine or fluorouracil significantly improved overall survival in HER2-positive advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer; the authors consider it a new standard option. Median OS 13·8 vs 11·1 mo (HR 0·74, 95% CI 0·60–0·91; p=0·0046) in the 584-patient primary analysis set, at the 75%-of-events interim analysis deemed final. PFS 6·7 vs 5·5 mo (HR 0·71, 95% CI 0·59–0·85); ORR 47% vs 35%. In a post-hoc exploratory analysis, benefit was concentrated in IHC 2+/FISH-positive or IHC 3+ tumours (n=446; OS 16·0 vs 11·8 mo, HR 0·65, 95% CI 0·51–0·83), not IHC 0 or 1+/FISH-positive tumours (n=131; HR 1·07, 95% CI 0·70–1·62); interaction p=0·036. Open-label, without independent response review. Grade 3 or 4 AEs 68% vs 68%; grade 3 or 4 diarrhoea 9% vs 4%; treatment-related mortality 3% vs 1%; cardiac AEs 6% vs 6%.

records.title: KEYNOTE-811
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · III · 2023
records.body: Gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; previously untreated unresectable or metastatic disease (first-line); HER2-positive by central review (IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ with positive ISH/FISH), tumour sample adequate for PD-L1 and MSI testing; measurable disease per RECIST v1.1, life expectancy >6 months; excluded prior checkpoint inhibitor therapy, known active CNS metastases Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w vs placebo IV q3w, each with trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg IV q3w plus investigator's choice of fluorouracil 800 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV q3w or capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV q3w; up to 35 cycles (about 2 years) or until progression, unacceptable toxicity, investigator decision or withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, safety, health-related quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-STO22, EQ-5D-5L) Adding pembrolizumab to first-line trastuzumab and chemotherapy significantly improved PFS versus placebo; the authors locate the benefit in PD-L1 CPS ≥1 tumours, although subgroup analyses were not powered or α-controlled. OS follow-up continues to the final analysis. At the second interim analysis, median PFS was 10·0 vs 8·1 mo (HR 0·72, 95% CI 0·60–0·87; p=0·0002); at the third interim analysis, HR 0·73 (0·61–0·87). OS did not meet prespecified significance criteria at the third interim analysis: median 20·0 vs 16·8 mo (HR 0·84, 0·70–1·01). There was no PFS benefit with CPS <1 (52 per group; third interim HR 1·03, 0·65–1·64). ORR was 72·6% vs 60·1% at the third interim analysis (not formally tested). Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs occurred in 58% vs 51%, treatment-related deaths in four (1%) vs three (1%), and grade ≥3 immune-mediated AEs in 10% vs 3%.

records.title: DESTINY-Gastric04
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · III · 2025
records.body: HER2-positive gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; unresectable or metastatic, second line after progression on trastuzumab-based therapy; HER2 IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ and ISH-positive, locally or centrally confirmed on a tumour biopsy taken after that progression; excluded history of noninfectious ILD/pneumonitis needing glucocorticoids, or current or suspected ILD/pneumonitis at screening Trastuzumab deruxtecan 6.4 mg/kg IV day 1 of each 21-day cycle vs ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV days 1 and 15 plus paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 of each 28-day cycle; both continued until disease progression, consent withdrawal, physician decision or unacceptable adverse events Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, confirmed objective response, disease control, duration of response, safety, quality of life Trastuzumab deruxtecan significantly prolonged OS vs ramucirumab plus paclitaxel in HER2-positive metastatic gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma; adverse events were common in both groups. At the prespecified interim analysis (median OS follow-up 16.8 vs 14.4 mo), median OS was 14.7 vs 11.4 mo (HR 0.70; 95% CI 0.55–0.90). PFS was also significantly longer: median 6.7 vs 5.6 mo (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.59–0.92). Confirmed ORR was 44.3% vs 29.1% among response-eligible patients; median DoR was 7.4 vs 5.3 mo. The trial was open-label, subgroups were not powered, and 25.8% of controls later received trastuzumab deruxtecan or disitamab vedotin. Drug-related grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 50.0% vs 54.1%. Adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis occurred in 13.9% with trastuzumab deruxtecan (grade 1 or 2 in 33, grade 3 in 1) vs 1.3% (grade 3 in 2, grade 5 in 1). Drug-related deaths occurred in 1.6% vs 0.9%.
records.keywords: Shitara et al. N Engl J Med 2025;393:336-348

records.title: HERIZON-GEA-01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · HER2-positive disease · III · 2026
records.body: HER2-positive adenocarcinoma of the stomach, gastroesophageal junction or esophagus; unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic, previously untreated (first-line); centrally confirmed HER2 IHC 3+ or IHC 2+ with ISH-positive status, PD-L1 not required; excluded prior systemic therapy for advanced disease and any prior HER2-targeted agent or checkpoint inhibitor Zanidatamab 1800 mg (<70 kg) or 2400 mg (≥70 kg) IV + tislelizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks + investigator's-choice capecitabine–oxaliplatin or fluorouracil–cisplatin in 21-day cycles vs zanidatamab + the same chemotherapy vs trastuzumab 8 mg/kg IV loading then 6 mg/kg every 3 weeks + the same chemotherapy; chemotherapy could be stopped after six cycles at physician discretion Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: investigator-assessed progression-free survival, confirmed objective response rate, duration of response, safety, complete response rate Zanidatamab plus chemotherapy, with or without tislelizumab, prolonged PFS vs trastuzumab plus chemotherapy; at the first interim OS analysis, OS was longer with zanidatamab–tislelizumab–chemotherapy, whereas zanidatamab–chemotherapy did not meet significance criteria (further analyses planned). At median follow-up 25.9 mo, median PFS by blinded central review was 12.4 and 12.4 vs 8.1 mo (HR 0.63 [95% CI 0.51 to 0.78] and 0.65 [95% CI 0.52 to 0.81]; P<0.001 for both). Median OS 26.4 vs 19.2 mo (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.57 to 0.90; P=0.004); zanidatamab–chemotherapy 24.4 mo (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.64 to 1.01; P=0.06). The comparator did not include pembrolizumab; subgroup analyses were exploratory. Grade ≥3 AEs 83.3%, 73.8% and 74.5%; grade ≥3 diarrhoea 24.8%, 20.0% and 12.9%; drug-related grade 5 events 2.4%, 0.3% and 1.3%.
records.keywords: Shitara et al. N Engl J Med 2026;394:2002-2014

records.title: CheckMate 649
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · III · 2021
records.body: Gastric, gastro-oesophageal junction or oesophageal adenocarcinoma; previously untreated, unresectable advanced or metastatic (first-line); enrolled regardless of PD-L1 expression, primary population amended to PD-L1 CPS ≥5; prior adjuvant/neoadjuvant therapy allowed if given ≥6 months before randomisation, unknown HER2 status allowed; excluded known HER2-positive status, untreated CNS metastases, peripheral neuropathy >grade 1, autoimmune disease, hepatitis B/C or HIV Nivolumab 360 mg IV every 3 weeks or 240 mg IV every 2 weeks (maximum 2 years) plus investigator's choice of XELOX (capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14, oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1, every 3 weeks) or FOLFOX (leucovorin 400 mg/m² day 1, fluorouracil 400 mg/m² day 1 and 1200 mg/m² days 1–2, oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² day 1, every 2 weeks) vs XELOX or FOLFOX alone; treatment until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, consent withdrawal or study end Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival in PD-L1 CPS five or more. Secondary: overall survival in PD-L1 CPS one or more, overall survival in all randomised patients, progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, landmark survival rates, predictive biomarkers, health-related quality of life, time to symptom deterioration, safety and tolerability Adding nivolumab to first-line chemotherapy gave superior OS with PFS benefit and an acceptable safety profile vs chemotherapy alone; both primary endpoints were met in PD-L1 CPS ≥5. CPS ≥5 (interim OS, minimum follow-up 12·1 mo): median OS 14·4 vs 11·1 mo, HR 0·71 (98·4% CI 0·59–0·86); median PFS 7·7 vs 6·0 mo, HR 0·68 (98% CI 0·56–0·81). OS was also significantly improved in CPS ≥1 (HR 0·77) and all randomised patients (HR 0·80); PFS benefit in these populations was not formally tested. Exploratory unstratified OS HRs were 0·92 (95% CI 0·70–1·23) for CPS <1 and 0·94 (0·78–1·13) for CPS <5, with significant OS interaction at the CPS cutoff of five. ORR in CPS ≥5 was 60% vs 45%. Grade 3–4 treatment-related AEs 59% vs 44%; discontinuation for treatment-related AEs 36% vs 24%; treatment-related deaths 16 (2%) vs four (1%).

records.title: KEYNOTE-859
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · III · 2023
records.body: Gastric or gastro-esophageal junction adenocarcinoma; locally advanced unresectable or metastatic, previously untreated (first-line); HER2-negative (IHC 0 or 1+, or ISH HER2:CEP17 <2 with average HER2 copy number <4·0 signals/cell), any PD-L1 CPS with tissue adequate for PD-L1 assessment; excluded squamous cell or undifferentiated gastric cancer, active CNS metastases, active autoimmune disease requiring treatment, immunodeficiency, HBV, active HCV or HIV Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV day 1 every 3 weeks for up to 35 cycles (approximately 2 years) + investigator's-choice chemotherapy vs placebo IV every 3 weeks for up to 35 cycles + the same chemotherapy; chemotherapy in 3-week cycles: fluorouracil 800 mg/m² per day IV days 1–5 + cisplatin 80 mg/m² IV day 1, or capecitabine 1000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1 (platinum could be limited to six cycles per local guidelines); treatment until progression, unacceptable toxicity or completion of maximum cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, safety, quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30, EORTC QLQ-STO22), time to deterioration Adding pembrolizumab to first-line chemotherapy gave a significant and clinically meaningful OS improvement with manageable toxicity; with 4.5-year follow-up the authors conclude improved efficacy and manageable safety are maintained, supporting it as a first-line option. At this cut (median follow-up 54.8 mo), median OS was 12.9 vs 11.5 mo in ITT (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.70-0.86; 48-month OS 14% vs 8%), 13.0 vs 11.4 mo with CPS ≥1 (HR 0.74) and 15.8 vs 11.8 mo with CPS ≥10 (HR 0.64). PFS (6.9 vs 5.6 mo; HR 0.76) and ORR (51.1% vs 42.0%) remained improved. Benefit was greater with higher PD-L1 CPS; at interim the small CPS <1 subgroup had an unstratified OS HR of 0·92 (0·73–1·17), and CPS 1–9 analyses were post-hoc and not powered. Grade 3–5 treatment-related AEs 59.4% vs 51.3%; treatment-related deaths 1.0% vs 2.0%; grade 3–5 immune-mediated AEs/infusion reactions 10.1% vs 2.0%; serious treatment-related AEs 23% vs 19% at interim.
records.keywords: Rha et al. Lancet Oncol 2023;24:1181-1195   Rha et al. ESMO Open 2026;11:108536  42748509

records.title: RATIONALE-305
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · First-line immunotherapy — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma (HER2-negative) · III · 2024
records.body: HER2-negative locally advanced unresectable or metastatic gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; first line, no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease (prior neoadjuvant/adjuvant therapy allowed after a progression-free interval of at least six months); any PD-L1 expression; excluded active leptomeningeal disease or uncontrolled brain metastasis, active autoimmune disease, need for systemic corticosteroids/immunosuppressants, prior checkpoint inhibitor Tislelizumab 200 mg IV every three weeks + investigator's choice chemotherapy every three weeks (capecitabine 1000 mg/m² twice daily days 1-14 + oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² day 1, or 5-fluorouracil 800 mg/m² days 1-5 + cisplatin 80 mg/m² day 1) for up to six cycles → tislelizumab ± optional capecitabine maintenance (capecitabine/oxaliplatin patients only) until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity; may stop after two years with CR, PR or SD vs matching placebo + same chemotherapy and maintenance Primary: overall survival (PD-L1 TAP score ≥5% and all randomised patients). Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, clinical benefit rate, time to response, duration of response, safety and tolerability, health related quality of life Tislelizumab plus chemotherapy provided significant and clinically meaningful OS benefit vs placebo plus chemotherapy in PD-L1 TAP ≥5% and in all randomised patients, with a manageable safety profile. TAP ≥5% (interim analysis): median OS 17.2 vs 12.6 mo, HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.59-0.94); final-analysis update HR 0.71. All randomised (final analysis, minimum follow-up 24.6 mo): median OS 15.0 vs 12.9 mo, HR 0.80 (0.70-0.92); 24-month OS 33% vs 23%. Investigator-assessed PFS HR 0.67 (TAP ≥5%) and 0.78 (all randomised); the ORR gain in TAP ≥5% was non-significant. In the exploratory TAP <5% subgroup, which was not powered for testing, OS HR was 0.92 (0.75-1.13). There was no independent review of tumour response. Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs 54% vs 50%; serious treatment-related AEs 23% vs 15%; discontinuation for treatment-related AEs 16% vs 8%; treatment-related deaths six of 498 vs two of 494; grade ≥3 immune-mediated AEs 8% vs 2%.

records.title: SPOTLIGHT
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Claudin 18.2-positive disease · III · 2023
records.body: Gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; previously untreated, locally advanced unresectable or metastatic; CLDN18.2-positive (≥75% of tumour cells with moderate-to-strong membranous CLDN18 staining by central IHC, VENTANA CLDN18 [43-14A] assay) and HER2-negative; radiologically evaluable disease (measurable or non-measurable) per RECIST 1.1 Zolbetuximab IV 800 mg/m² cycle 1 day 1, then 600 mg/m² every 3 weeks + mFOLFOX6 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m², folinic acid 400 mg/m², fluorouracil 400 mg/m² bolus then 2400 mg/m² over 46–48 h; days 1, 15 and 29) for four 42-day cycles → zolbetuximab ± folinic acid and fluorouracil (investigator's discretion) until disease progression, toxic effects, start of another anticancer treatment or other protocol discontinuation criteria vs placebo + mFOLFOX6 on the same schedule Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to confirmed deterioration, objective response, duration of response, safety, tolerability, patient-reported outcomes, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity Adding zolbetuximab to first-line mFOLFOX6 significantly prolonged PFS and OS vs placebo plus mFOLFOX6 in CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative advanced gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma. Median PFS 10·61 vs 8·67 mo (HR 0·75, 95% CI 0·60–0·94; p=0·0066). At the interim OS analysis, median OS 18·23 vs 15·54 mo (HR 0·75, 95% CI 0·60–0·94; p=0·0053 vs prespecified boundary p=0·0135); final OS analysis planned after 396 deaths. ORR was similar (48% vs 48%). No conclusions could be drawn for the small GEJ subgroup; testing of time to confirmed deterioration is pending. Grade ≥3 TEAEs 87% vs 78%; nausea (82% vs 61%) and vomiting (67% vs 36%) were most common, mainly in the first cycle; treatment-related AEs led to zolbetuximab/placebo discontinuation in 14% vs 2%; treatment-related deaths 2% vs 1%.

records.title: GLOW
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Claudin 18.2-positive disease · III · 2023
records.body: Gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma; previously untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic (first-line); CLDN18.2-positive (≥75% of tumour cells with moderate-to-strong membranous CLDN18 staining, central IHC) and HER2-negative; RECIST 1.1-evaluable disease; prior (neo)adjuvant therapy allowed if completed ≥6 months before randomization; excluded CNS metastases and complete or partial gastric outlet syndrome with persistent vomiting Zolbetuximab 800 mg/m² IV cycle 1 day 1, then 600 mg/m² IV day 1 of subsequent cycles + CAPOX (capecitabine 1,000 mg/m² orally twice daily days 1–14; oxaliplatin 130 mg/m² IV day 1) for eight 21-day cycles → zolbetuximab ± capecitabine (investigator's discretion) until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or start of another anti-cancer treatment vs placebo + CAPOX on the same schedule → placebo ± capecitabine Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to confirmed deterioration in EORTC global health status/quality of life, physical functioning, abdominal pain and discomfort, objective response rate, duration of response, safety and tolerability, additional patient-reported outcomes, pharmacokinetics, immunogenicity Adding zolbetuximab to first-line CAPOX significantly prolonged PFS and OS in CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative locally advanced unresectable or metastatic G/GEJ adenocarcinoma. Median PFS 8.21 vs 6.80 mo; HR 0.687 (95% CI 0.544–0.866); 12-month PFS 35% vs 19%. At the interim OS analysis (318 of 507 deaths), median OS 14.39 vs 12.16 mo; HR 0.771 (95% CI 0.615–0.965). Response rates were similar: ORR 42.5% vs 40.3%, median DOR 6.14 vs 6.08 mo. Subgroup analyses were underpowered, and quality-of-life deterioration results were not reported. Grade ≥3 TEAEs 72.8% vs 69.9%. Nausea (68.5% vs 50.2%) and vomiting (66.1% vs 30.9%) were more frequent with zolbetuximab, mostly in the first cycle; grade ≥3 vomiting 12.2% vs 3.6%, nausea 8.7% vs 2.4%. Grade 5 TRAEs 2.4% vs 2.8%.

records.title: REGARD
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2014
records.body: Metastatic or unresectable, locally recurrent gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; second line, after progression within 4 months of last dose of first-line platinum- or fluoropyrimidine-containing chemotherapy for metastatic disease, or within 6 months of last dose of platinum- or fluoropyrimidine-containing adjuvant treatment; ECOG 0 or 1; excluded grade ≥3 GI bleeding within 3 months, arterial thromboembolic event within 6 months, or poorly controlled hypertension Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV once every 2 weeks + best supportive care vs placebo IV once every 2 weeks + best supportive care (double-blind); until radiographically confirmed disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or death Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, 12 week progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, quality of life, safety, ramucirumab immunogenicity, disease control rate, duration of disease control, time to deterioration in ECOG performance status Ramucirumab monotherapy significantly prolonged overall survival vs placebo in advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma progressing after first-line chemotherapy. Median OS 5.2 vs 3.8 mo; HR 0.776 (95% CI 0.603–0.998; p=0.047). Median PFS 2.1 vs 1.3 mo; HR 0.483 (95% CI 0.376–0.620); 12 week PFS 40.1% vs 15.8%. Objective response 3% vs 3% (p=0.76); disease control 49% vs 23%. Quality-of-life data were scarce (only 48% vs 25% provided 6 week data), and stable or improved global quality of life did not differ significantly (p=0.23). In the safety population, grade ≥3 adverse events 57% vs 58%; hypertension 16% vs 8% (grade ≥3 8% vs 3%). Five (2%) vs two (2%) deaths were considered related to study drug, with ramucirumab-group deaths from myocardial infarction, gastric haemorrhage, intestinal perforation and pneumonia.

records.title: RAINBOW
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2014
records.body: Metastatic or non-resectable locally advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; second line; progression during or within 4 months of last dose of first-line platinum plus fluoropyrimidine doublet with or without anthracycline; excluded squamous or undifferentiated histology, GI perforation, fistulae or arterial thromboembolism within 6 months, significant GI bleeding or venous thromboembolism within 3 months, or poorly controlled hypertension Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg IV days 1 and 15 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle vs placebo IV days 1 and 15 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle; until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal of consent Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, EORTC QLQ-C30, EQ-5D-3L, immunogenicity, safety, duration of response Ramucirumab plus paclitaxel significantly increased overall survival vs placebo plus paclitaxel after first-line chemotherapy; the authors suggest it could be regarded as a new standard second-line treatment. Median OS 9·6 vs 7·4 mo (stratified HR 0·807, 95% CI 0·678–0·962; p=0·017); 12-mo OS 40% vs 30%. Median PFS 4·4 vs 2·9 mo (HR 0·635); objective response 28% vs 16%. In a preplanned regional subgroup analysis, OS HR was 0·986 (95% CI 0·727–1·337) in Asian region 3 vs 0·732 (0·591–0·907) in regions 1 and 2. Global QoL and EQ-5D index scores were similar between groups (descriptive). Grade ≥3 neutropenia 41% vs 19%, with febrile neutropenia 3% vs 2%; grade ≥3 hypertension 14% vs 2% and fatigue 12% vs 5%. Fatal adverse events attributed to study drug occurred in six (2%) vs five (2%) patients; grade ≥3 GI perforation occurred only with ramucirumab (four patients, one death).

records.title: TAGS
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2018
records.body: Histologically confirmed non-resectable metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (AJCC 7th edition); two or more prior regimens for advanced disease including a fluoropyrimidine, a platinum agent, and a taxane and/or irinotecan, plus anti-HER2 therapy if HER2 positive and available; radiological progression within 3 months of the last dose of the last therapy or intolerance of it; ECOG 0–1; excluded CNS metastasis, other active malignancy Oral trifluridine/tipiracil 35 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–5 and 8–12 of each 28-day cycle plus best supportive care vs identical-appearing placebo twice daily on the same schedule plus best supportive care (double-blind); until disease progression, intolerable toxicity or patient withdrawal Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, safety, tolerability, objective response rate, disease control rate, time to deterioration of ECOG performance status, health-related quality of life Trifluridine/tipiracil significantly improved OS vs placebo and was well tolerated in heavily pretreated advanced gastric cancer. Median OS 5.7 vs 3.6 mo (HR 0.69, 95% CI 0.56–0.85); 31 (21%) vs 10 (13%) patients alive at 12 months. PFS also improved (median 2.0 vs 1.8 mo; HR 0.57), but the medians were confounded by the first tumour assessment at about 8 weeks. Median time to ECOG deterioration to ≥2 was 4.3 vs 2.3 mo (HR 0.69). Objective response 4% vs 2% did not differ significantly (p=0.28); disease control 44% vs 14% among assessable patients. Grade ≥3 AEs of any cause 80% vs 58%, mainly neutropenia 34% and anaemia 19%; grade ≥3 febrile neutropenia 2%; serious AEs 43% vs 42%. One treatment-related death in each arm (cardiopulmonary arrest vs toxic hepatitis).

records.title: ATTRACTION-2
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2017
records.body: Unresectable advanced or recurrent gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction adenocarcinoma; refractory to or intolerant of standard therapy, with two or more previous chemotherapy regimens in the advanced/recurrent setting; unselected for PD-L1 expression; ECOG 0–1, life expectancy ≥3 months; excluded prior anti-PD-1, anti-PD-L1/PD-L2, anti-CD137 or anti-CTLA-4 antibodies, autoimmune or interstitial lung disease, and symptomatic or treated brain metastases Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks vs placebo (saline) IV every 2 weeks, double-blind; until investigator-assessed progression or toxicity requiring permanent discontinuation; continuation beyond first progression allowed with investigator-assessed clinical benefit, tolerance and stable performance status Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, time to response, best overall response, maximum percentage change from baseline in sum of target lesion diameters, overall survival by PD-L1 expression, adverse events, treatment-related adverse events Nivolumab significantly prolonged overall survival vs placebo in heavily pretreated advanced gastric or gastro-oesophageal junction cancer; the authors conclude it might be a new treatment option. Median OS 5·26 vs 4·14 mo (HR 0·63, 95% CI 0·51–0·78; p<0·0001); 12-mo OS 26·2% vs 10·9% (cutoff Aug 13, 2016; median follow-up 8·87 vs 8·59 mo). PFS HR 0·60 (median 1·61 vs 1·45 mo). Objective response in 30 (11·2%) of 268 vs none of 131 patients with baseline target lesions; median DoR 9·53 mo. Exploratory post-hoc PD-L1 analysis (n=192): HR 0·51 (95% CI 0·21–1·25) for PD-L1 ≥1% and 0·72 (0·49–1·05) for <1%; small PD-L1-positive subgroup. Enrolment was limited to Japan, South Korea and Taiwan; no quality-of-life data were collected. Grade 3–4 TRAEs 34 (10%) of 330 vs 7 (4%) of 161; treatment-related deaths five (2%) of 330 vs two (1%) of 161.

records.title: Li et al.
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Second-line & later — gastric/GEJ adenocarcinoma · III · 2026
records.body: Histologically or cytologically confirmed unresectable, recurrent or metastatic gastric cancer; second line after progression on fluoropyrimidine- or fluoropyrimidine plus platinum-based first-line therapy; ECOG PS ≤2 and ≥1 RECIST 1.1 measurable lesion; excluded squamous cell or undifferentiated gastric cancer and taxane use within 12 months before first dosing Paclitaxel oral solution 200 mg/m² orally twice daily on days 1, 8 and 15 of a 28-day cycle vs paclitaxel injection (Taxol) 175 mg/m² IV on day 1 of a 21-day cycle Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, disease control rate, safety, pharmacokinetics Paclitaxel oral solution was noninferior to three-weekly IV paclitaxel for PFS and improved OS; the authors conclude it is an effective alternative second-line option for gastric cancer. Final OS (15 February 2023 cut): median 9.13 vs 6.54 mo; HR 0.770 (95.5% CI 0.635-0.934), P = 0.006. BIRC PFS (31 January 2022 cut): 3.02 vs 2.89 mo; HR 0.894 (95% CI 0.719-1.112), upper bound below the 1.18 noninferiority margin. Confirmed ORR 13.6% vs 9.8%. Open-label; the three-weekly control is no longer standard in many regions, where weekly paclitaxel with ramucirumab is the reference; conducted only in Chinese patients. Grade ≥3 TRAEs 66.8% vs 71.8%; treatment-related deaths 4 (1.5%) vs 3 (1.1%). The oral arm had more dose interruptions (46.8% vs 9.8%), diarrhea (32.5% vs 8.3%) and febrile neutropenia (7.2% vs 4.1%), but less peripheral sensory neuropathy (22.3% vs 38.7%) and hypersensitivity (0.0% vs 3.4%).

records.title: KEYNOTE-590
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal & GEJ — first-line immunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Previously untreated locally advanced unresectable or metastatic oesophageal adenocarcinoma or squamous-cell carcinoma, or Siewert type 1 GEJ adenocarcinoma; known HER2-positive disease excluded; excluded active CNS disease, treatment-requiring autoimmune disease, immunodeficiency/chronic immunosuppression and noninfectious/current pneumonitis Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w + cisplatin 80 mg/m2 d1 + fluorouracil 800 mg/m2/d d1–5 q3w vs placebo + the same chemotherapy; cisplatin ≤6 cycles, pembrolizumab/placebo ± chemotherapy ≤35 cycles; no crossover Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, health-related quality of life, safety At the first interim OS and final PFS analysis, pembrolizumab-chemotherapy improved OS (12.4 vs 9.8 mo; HR 0.73), PFS and response; benefit estimates were largest in ESCC CPS ≥10, without a reported predictive interaction. Severe treatment-related events were 72% vs 68%, treatment-related deaths 2% vs 1%, and pneumonitis 6% vs 1%.

records.title: CheckMate 648
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal & GEJ — first-line immunotherapy · III · 2022
records.body: Unresectable advanced, recurrent or metastatic oesophageal squamous-cell or adenosquamous carcinoma not amenable to curative treatment; no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease; enrolled regardless of PD-L1 Nivolumab 240 mg IV q2w + cisplatin/fluorouracil vs nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q6w vs cisplatin/fluorouracil; immunotherapy ≤2 y, treatment otherwise until progression/toxicity/withdrawal/trial end Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, safety, PFS2 Both first-line nivolumab plus chemotherapy and nivolumab plus ipilimumab significantly prolonged OS vs chemotherapy, and at 5-year minimum follow-up continued to show clinically meaningful OS benefit, with no new safety signals. At 5-year follow-up, in tumour-cell PD-L1 ≥1%, median OS was 15.0 and 13.1 vs 9.1 mo (HR 0.62 for both), 5-year OS 12% and 18% vs 7%; in all randomised patients, 13.2 and 12.7 vs 10.7 mo (HR 0.77 for both). Nivolumab-chemotherapy improved PFS in PD-L1 ≥1% (5-year follow-up: 6.8 vs 4.4 mo; HR 0.67). Nivolumab-chemotherapy overall-population PFS did not meet its criterion; nivolumab-ipilimumab PFS failed in PD-L1 ≥1% (5-year follow-up HR 1.03), stopping overall PFS testing. Exploratory PFS2 favoured both nivolumab regimens. At 5-year follow-up, grade 3-4 treatment-related events were 49%, 33% and 37%; treatment-related deaths were 2% in each arm.
records.keywords: Doki et al. N Engl J Med 2022;386:449-462   Kato et al. Ann Oncol 2026 (online ahead of print)  42575473

records.title: ESCORT-1st
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic ESCC not amenable to oesophagectomy or definitive chemoradiation; age ≤75; prior perioperative therapy or definitive chemoradiation allowed only if progression occurred ≥6 mo later; excluded active or historical autoimmune disease and CNS metastases Camrelizumab 200 mg IV q3w + paclitaxel 175 mg/m2 + cisplatin 75 mg/m2 d1 q3w vs placebo + the same chemotherapy; chemotherapy ≤6 cycles, camrelizumab/placebo until confirmed progression/toxicity/withdrawal/death/new therapy Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, disease control, duration of response, landmark overall survival, health-related quality of life, safety At the first interim OS and final PFS analysis, camrelizumab-chemotherapy improved OS (15.3 vs 12.0 mo; HR 0.70) and PFS (6.9 vs 5.6 mo; HR 0.56). Severe treatment-related events were 63% vs 68%; serious events 30% vs 23%; reactive capillary endothelial proliferation 80% vs 11%; treatment-related deaths 3.0% vs 3.7%.

records.title: ORIENT-15
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2022
records.body: Untreated unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic ESCC unsuitable for curative surgery or definitive chemoradiotherapy; prior perioperative chemotherapy or definitive chemoradiotherapy allowed only if progression occurred >6 mo later; excluded aortic/tracheal invasion, hepatic metastases occupying >50% of liver and active autoimmune disease or steroid-requiring ILD Sintilimab 3 mg/kg (<60 kg) or 200 mg (≥60 kg) IV q3w + cisplatin/paclitaxel or cisplatin/fluorouracil vs placebo + the same chemotherapy; chemotherapy ≤6 cycles, sintilimab/placebo ≤24 mo Primary: overall survival.
