Secondary: objective response rate, progression-free survival, disease control, duration of response, health-related quality of life, safety At interim analysis (351/500 planned all-patient OS deaths), sintilimab-chemotherapy improved OS in all patients (16.7 vs 12.5 mo; HR 0.63) and CPS ≥10, plus PFS and response; no formal PD-L1 interaction supported subgroup selection. Severe treatment-related events were 60% vs 55%, serious events 28% vs 20%, discontinuation 21% vs 12%, and treatment-related deaths 3% vs 2%.

records.title: RATIONALE-306
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma — first-line chemoimmunotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated unresectable locally advanced, recurrent or metastatic ESCC not amenable to definitive surgery or radiotherapy; prior perioperative platinum allowed only after a ≥6-mo treatment-free interval; enrolled regardless of PD-L1; excluded CNS disease, untreatable obstruction/fistula, active autoimmune disease and prior checkpoint therapy Tislelizumab 200 mg IV q3w + investigator-choice platinum/fluoropyrimidine or platinum/paclitaxel vs placebo + the same chemotherapy; platinum could stop after 6 cycles, remaining therapy until progression/toxicity/withdrawal with conditional stop at 2 y; no crossover Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, health-related quality of life, safety At the primary interim analysis, which crossed its prespecified boundary and replaced the planned final analysis, tislelizumab-chemotherapy improved OS (17.2 vs 10.6 mo; HR 0.66), PFS and response; TAP subgroup findings did not establish predictive selection. Severe treatment-related events were 67% vs 64%, serious events 29% vs 19%, discontinuation 29% vs 19%, and investigator-attributed treatment-related deaths 6 vs 4 after excluding progression.

records.title: ATTRACTION-3
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal squamous — second-line immunotherapy · III · 2019
records.body: Unresectable advanced or recurrent cervical/thoracic oesophageal or GEJ squamous/adenosquamous carcinoma, refractory or intolerant to one prior fluoropyrimidine-platinum regimen and not indicated for radical resection; enrolled irrespective of PD-L1; excluded major malnutrition, adjacent-organ invasion, ILD, autoimmune disease and CNS metastases Nivolumab 240 mg IV q2w vs investigator-choice paclitaxel 100 mg/m2 weekly 6 of 7 wk or docetaxel 75 mg/m2 q3w; until progression or unacceptable toxicity, with protocol-permitted treatment beyond progression Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, progression-free survival, disease control, quality of life, safety Nivolumab improved OS (10.9 vs 8.4 mo; HR 0.77) vs taxane chemotherapy, but ORR did not favour nivolumab (19% vs 22%), stopping protected PFS testing; median PFS was 1.7 vs 3.4 mo. Severe treatment-related events were 18% vs 63%, with treatment-related deaths 2 vs 3.

records.title: DRAGON-01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Peritoneal metastasis — intraperitoneal (bidirectional) therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Untreated gastric adenocarcinoma with laparoscopically confirmed peritoneal metastasis, aged 18-75, ECOG 0-1; all ERBB2-negative (IHC 0/1+ or 2+ with FISH-negative); extraperitoneal distant metastasis excluded (ovarian involvement alone permitted), as were prior anticancer therapy and gastric outlet or bowel obstruction Paclitaxel 50 mg/m2 IV plus 20 mg/m2 intraperitoneally on days 1 and 8 of each 21-day cycle plus oral S-1 80 mg/m2/day days 1-14, until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal vs paclitaxel 70 mg/m2 IV days 1 and 8 plus S-1 80 mg/m2/day days 1-14, same stopping rule; no crossover permitted Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Conversion surgery rate, Major pathological response rate, Safety Adding IP paclitaxel to IV paclitaxel plus S-1 significantly improved overall survival in gastric cancer with peritoneal metastasis without increasing severe toxic effects. In the mITT population (IP 148 vs PS 74; median follow-up 72.2 months; cutoff March 11, 2025), median OS was 19.4 vs 13.9 months (HR 0.67; 95% CI 0.50-0.90; P=.01); median PFS 11.2 vs 7.2 months (HR 0.72; 0.54-0.96; P=.02). Conversion surgery was more frequent with IP (75 [50.7%] vs 26 [35.1%]; P=.04); surgery-stratified survival comparisons were exploratory and hypothesis-generating. Grade 3-4 adverse events occurred in 57 (38.5%) vs 31 (41.9%); no treatment-related deaths. Port-related complications occurred in 40 (27.0%) of the IP group, 16 (10.8%) requiring surgery. The authors note the chemotherapy backbone does not reflect current first-line standards and call for trials with immunotherapy/targeted agents

records.title: PERISCOPE II
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Peritoneal metastasis — intraperitoneal (bidirectional) therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Resectable cT3 or cT4a gastric adenocarcinoma with limited peritoneal metastases (PCI <7) or tumour-positive peritoneal cytology or both; metastatic setting after three or more cycles of systemic therapy without RECIST disease progression; complete criteria in appendix (pp 5–6) Continuation of palliative systemic therapy (standard group) vs (partial) gastrectomy with cytoreductive surgery plus HIPEC: intraperitoneal oxaliplatin 460 mg/m² at 41°C for 30 min then docetaxel 50 mg/m² at 37°C for 90 min, surgery within 12 weeks of last systemic course; PCI ≥7 or unresectable disease found intraoperatively did not proceed to HIPEC Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Treatment-related toxicity, Health-related quality of life Gastrectomy with cytoreductive surgery and HIPEC provided no overall survival benefit versus systemic therapy alone in gastric cancer with limited peritoneal metastases; the trial was closed early after an unplanned futility interim analysis. ITT median OS 16.6 vs 15.7 months (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.69–1.74; p=0.70); median PFS 7.6 vs 9.3 months (HR 0.93, p=0.73); post-hoc per-protocol PFS favoured experimental (13.2 vs 7.2 months, HR 0.51, p=0.0092) but is exploratory with unbalanced groups. Grade ≥3 adverse events 21 (42%) of 50 experimental vs 10 (20%) of 51 standard; serious adverse events 22 (44%) vs 3 (6%); three treatment-related deaths, all experimental (ARDS, anastomotic leakage, bleeding)

records.title: RENAISSANCE (AIO-FLOT5)
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oligometastatic disease — role of surgery · III · 2024
records.body: Previously untreated patients with limited-metastatic gastric or gastroesophageal-junction adenocarcinoma, defined by retroperitoneal lymph-node metastases only or at most one potentially resectable or locally controllable incurable organ site, with or without retroperitoneal nodes, after four induction FLOT cycles Arm A: 4 induction FLOT cycles, with trastuzumab if HER2-positive or nivolumab if PD-L1-positive, then radical complete resection of primary and metastases followed by the same systemic treatment vs Arm B: after the same induction and no progression, additional FLOT; exact doses, antibody continuation after randomisation, and post-randomisation duration were not reported in the abstract Primary: overall survival. Secondary: quality of life, surgery, R0 resection, perioperative mortality, treatment delivery Adding radical surgery after induction FLOT did not meet the OS primary endpoint; early postoperative mortality offset later separation in crossing survival curves. Surgery occurred in 91%, with 30-day and 90-day mortality of 3% and 8%. The apparent retroperitoneal-node subgroup difference was exploratory and does not support subgroup selection.

records.title: TROG 03.01
records.subtitle: Advanced Gastroesophageal · Oesophageal — palliative radiotherapy · III · 2018
records.body: Incurable advanced or metastatic oesophageal cancer with symptomatic dysphagia (Mellow 1–4), excluding Seifert type 2–3 lesions; no prior chemotherapy or chest radiotherapy; no tracheo-oesophageal fistula or stent in situ Palliative chemoradiotherapy: radiotherapy 35 Gy/15 fractions over 3 wk (Australia, NZ) or 30 Gy/10 fractions over 2 wk (Canada, UK) + cisplatin (80 mg/m2 d1 or 20 mg/m2/d d1-4) + fluorouracil 800 mg/m2/d continuous infusion d1-4 vs Radiotherapy alone: same radiotherapy dose schedule (35 Gy/15# or 30 Gy/10#) Primary: dysphagia relief. Secondary: dysphagia progression-free survival, overall survival, dysphagia response, complete dysphagia relief, secondary treatment, quality of life, acute toxicity, late toxicity Adding chemotherapy to palliative radiotherapy did not improve dysphagia relief (45% vs 35%; statistical significance not reached), dysphagia-PFS or OS, and increased severe acute toxicity (36% vs 16%). Radiotherapy alone provided similar palliation with less acute toxicity.

records.title: ESPAC-1
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2004
records.body: The target population was patients after complete macroscopic resection of histologically proven pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, with positive or negative margins eligible and stratified. Three ineligible patients were retained in the intention-to-treat analysis: one had not undergone resection and two had previously had breast cancer Observation vs Chemoradiotherapy: 40 Gy in two 20-Gy courses 2 weeks apart with IV bolus fluorouracil 500 mg/m2 on days 1-3 of each course vs Chemotherapy: leucovorin 20 mg/m2 IV then fluorouracil 425 mg/m2 IV on days 1-5 every 28 days for 6 cycles vs Chemoradiotherapy followed by the same chemotherapy Primary: Two-year survival rate. Secondary: Adverse effects, Recurrence, Quality of life Adjuvant chemotherapy improved OS (median 20.1 vs 15.5 months; HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.55-0.92, P=.009), whereas chemoradiotherapy showed no benefit and possible harm (15.9 vs 17.9 months; HR 1.28, 0.99-1.66, P=.05). The 2x2 factorial trial was not powered for direct four-arm comparisons and interaction tests were nonsignificant. Grade 3/4 events occurred in 29 patients and two treatment-related deaths occurred

records.title: ESPAC-3
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2010
records.body: The target population had complete macroscopic R0/R1 resection of histologically confirmed pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, no malignant ascites or distant spread, WHO performance status 0-2 and life expectancy >3 months. ESPAC-3 version 2 randomised 1088 patients; four ineligible patients were retained in the intention-to-treat analysis Fluorouracil plus folinic acid: Folinic acid 20 mg/m2 IV bolus followed by fluorouracil 425 mg/m2 IV bolus on 5 consecutive days every 28 days for 6 cycles (24 weeks). vs Gemcitabine: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV infusion over 30 minutes once weekly for 3 of every 4 weeks, for 6 cycles (24 weeks) Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Toxicity, Quality of life Gemcitabine did not improve OS versus fluorouracil/folinic acid (23.6 vs 23.0 months; HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.81-1.08, P=.39), so equivalence was not established. PFS was also similar (14.3 vs 14.1 months; HR 0.96, P=.53). Gemcitabine caused fewer treatment-related serious adverse events (7.5% vs 14%) but more grade 3/4 thrombocytopenia (1.5% vs 0%)

records.title: CONKO-001
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2007
records.body: Histologically proven T1-4 N0-1 M0 pancreatic cancer after macroscopically complete R0/R1 resection; no neoadjuvant therapy Adjuvant gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV on days 1, 8, and 15 every 4 weeks for 6 cycles, starting 10-42 days after surgery and wound healing vs Observation Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Toxicity, Quality of life Adjuvant gemcitabine prolonged DFS. The 2007 analysis found median DFS 13.4 vs 6.9 months (P<.001) but no significant OS difference (22.1 vs 20.2 months, P=.06) at 53 months; the 2013 update found DFS HR 0.55 and OS HR 0.76 (P=.01), with 5-year OS 20.7% vs 10.4%. Severe toxicity was uncommon; five gemcitabine serious events were treatment-related and neither study death was treatment-related. The update reported no new safety results

records.title: ESPAC-4
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2017
records.body: Adults after complete macroscopic R0/R1 resection of histologically confirmed pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, including 8 protocol-exception patients with stage IV tumours but complete surgical clearance; 732 were randomised and 730 remained in the paper's full analysis set after 2 pre-treatment consent withdrawals Gemcitabine: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV once weekly for 3 of every 4 weeks for six 28-day cycles (24 weeks). vs Gemcitabine plus capecitabine: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV once weekly for 3 of every 4 weeks plus capecitabine 1660 mg/m2 orally daily for 21 days followed by 7 days rest, for six 28-day cycles (24 weeks) Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Survival at 24 months and 5 years, Relapse-free survival, Toxicity, Quality of life Gemcitabine-capecitabine improved OS (28.0 vs 25.5 months; HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.68-0.98, P=.032) at an early publication requested after 458/480 target deaths. Relapse-free survival was not significantly improved (13.9 vs 13.1 months; HR 0.86, P=.082). Grade 3/4 neutropenia, hand-foot syndrome and diarrhoea were more frequent with the combination; treatment-related serious adverse events were similar (24% vs 26%)

records.title: PRODIGE 24/CCTG PA.6
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2018
records.body: 493 patients were randomised after complete macroscopic R0/R1 resection of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and retained in the intention-to-treat analysis. Target eligibility required age 18-79 years, randomisation 3-12 weeks postoperatively, no metastatic disease, WHO performance status 0-1 and postoperative CA 19-9 <=180 U/mL; 9 modified-FOLFIRINOX and 6 gemcitabine patients had major eligibility violations, primarily metastatic disease in 8 and 5, respectively Modified FOLFIRINOX: Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2 IV over 2 h, leucovorin 400 mg/m2 IV over 2 h, irinotecan 180 mg/m2 IV over 90 min then 2400 mg/m2 fluorouracil continuous IV over 46 h every 14 days for 24 weeks (12 cycles); irinotecan reduced to 150 mg/m2 after 162 patients following the prespecified safety analysis. vs Gemcitabine: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV over 30 min on days 1, 8, and 15 every 28 days for 24 weeks (6 cycles) Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Metastasis-free survival, Cancer-specific survival, Safety mFOLFIRINOX improved DFS (21.6 vs 12.8 months; HR 0.58, P<.001) and OS (54.4 vs 35.0 months; HR 0.64, P=.003). Reporting was requested at 91.8% of target DFS events, while OS remained immature with 61% alive. Grade 3/4 adverse events were more frequent (75.9% vs 52.9%), including more diarrhoea, neuropathy and fatigue; one gemcitabine patient died from treatment-related pneumonitis

records.title: APACT
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemotherapy · III · 2023
records.body: Adults with histologically confirmed PDAC after complete macroscopic resection, ECOG performance status <=1, CA19-9 <100 U/mL and no metastatic, locally recurrent, or screening-detected recurrent disease; no prior neoadjuvant, radiation, or systemic therapy; adjuvant treatment started <=12 weeks after surgery nab-Paclitaxel plus gemcitabine: nab-Paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 followed by gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV over 30-40 min on days 1, 8, and 15 of every 28-day cycle for 6 cycles, unless recurrence, unacceptable toxicity, or patient/physician decision. vs Gemcitabine: Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV over 30-40 min on days 1, 8, and 15 of every 28-day cycle for 6 cycles, unless recurrence, unacceptable toxicity, or patient/physician decision Primary: disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Safety Adding nab-paclitaxel did not improve independently assessed DFS (19.4 vs 18.8 months; HR 0.88, P=.1824), so the primary endpoint failed. Investigator-assessed DFS and OS estimates were descriptive; at 5 years OS was 38% vs 31% (HR 0.80, P=.0091) with 88% of target deaths. Grade 3 or worse events were 86% vs 68%, serious events 41% vs 23%, and two patients in each arm died from treatment-emergent adverse events

records.title: GITSG
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · N/A · 1985
records.body: Patients 4–10 weeks after apparently curative resection of histologically confirmed ductal, acinar, or undifferentiated pancreatic adenocarcinoma, with margin-negative specimens and no peritoneal metastases; periampullary, islet-cell, and cystadenocarcinoma excluded; adequate nutrition, stable weight, specified blood/renal/hepatic tests, and no prohibitive comorbidity required Control: no adjuvant treatment vs Chemoradiotherapy: 4,000 rad external-beam radiation in two 2,000-rad courses separated by 2 weeks; fluorouracil 500 mg/m² IV bolus on 3 consecutive days at the start of each radiation course, then once weekly for 2 years or until recurrence, with protocol-defined haematological interruption rules Primary: Overall survival, Disease-free survival. Secondary: Toxicity, Treatment compliance, Radiotherapy quality assurance Adjuvant 5-FU chemoradiation improved median OS (20 vs 11 months) and 2-year OS (42% vs 15%; one-sided P=.035) among 43 analyzed patients, but the trial randomised only 49, stopped early below target, designated no primary endpoint or hierarchy, and reported nominal one-sided tests. Severe haematologic toxicity occurred in 3/21 treated patients; no treatment-attributable death was reported

records.title: EORTC 40891
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · III · 1999
records.body: Post-resection patients with histologically proven adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head (T1–2N0–1aM0) or periampullary region (T1–3N0–1aM0; distal common bile duct, papilla of Vater, or duodenum), randomized after recovery and definitive pathology; pancreatic-head T3 and periampullary T4 disease, N1b disease, and patients unable to start treatment within 8 weeks were excluded Observation alone after curative resection vs Chemoradiotherapy: external-beam radiotherapy 40 Gy total (2 Gy per fraction, 5 fractions/week in two 2-week courses separated by 2 weeks) plus continuous-infusion 5-fluorouracil 25 mg/kg/24 h (maximum 1,500 mg/day) starting the same day before radiotherapy; second-course 5-fluorouracil was 0, 3, or 5 days according to toxicity, with no post-radiotherapy maintenance chemotherapy Primary: Duration of overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Treatment toxicity Adjuvant 5-FU chemoradiation did not significantly improve OS in the combined eligible pancreatic-head/periampullary cohort (24.5 vs 19.0 months; relative risk 0.8, 95% CI 0.6-1.1, P=.208) or PFS (17.4 vs 16.0 months, P=.643). The pancreatic-head analysis was exploratory (17.1 vs 12.6 months, P=.099), with no treatment-by-location interaction. Toxicity was generally limited, but no systematic late-toxicity window or treatment-related-death count was reported

records.title: RTOG 9704
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Adjuvant chemoradiation · III · 2008
records.body: Patients with histologically confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma after central-confirmed gross total resection, T1–4N0–1M0, postoperative CT without persistent/recurrent or metastatic disease, and adequate performance status, organ function and caloric intake; no prior chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or other malignancy (except nonmelanoma skin or in-situ cervical cancer); protocol therapy began 3–8 weeks after resection Fluorouracil: continuous infusion 250 mg/m2/day for 3 weeks; 1-2 weeks later, 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with continuous-infusion fluorouracil 250 mg/m2/day; 3-5 weeks later, fluorouracil for 4 weeks on/2 weeks off x2 vs Gemcitabine: 1000 mg/m2 IV weekly x3; the same chemoradiotherapy; then gemcitabine weekly for 3 weeks on/1 week off x3 Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, Toxicity Gemcitabine sequencing did not improve OS in all 451 eligible patients (P=.34); the pancreatic-head analysis was also nonsignificant (20.5 vs 16.9 months; HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.65-1.03, P=.09), with an adjusted HR 0.80 (0.63-1.00, P=.05) but no multiplicity allocation or location interaction. DFS was qualitatively null. Grade 3 or worse haematologic toxicity was 58% vs 9% and overall toxicity 79% vs 62%; one grade-5 infection occurred with gemcitabine

records.title: Prep-02/JSAP-05
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · III · 2026
records.body: Japanese patients aged 20–79 years with treatment-naive, histologically or cytologically confirmed localized PDAC, no distant metastases, ECOG 0–1, and anticipated R0/R1 curative resection without hepatic, celiac or superior mesenteric arterial involvement; blinded central review classified evaluable tumors as resectable or borderline resectable-PV without arterial contact Upfront surgery within 8 weeks, then postoperative S-1 within 10 weeks for 6 months vs Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 IV on days 1 and 8 plus S-1 orally twice daily on days 1-14 every 21 days for 2 cycles, then surgery 2-4 weeks after S-1 and postoperative S-1 within 10 weeks for 6 months Primary: Phase II resection rate, Phase III overall survival. Secondary: Adverse events, Recurrence-free survival, Resection and pathology, Tumour-marker kinetics, Dose intensity, Radiologic response, Histologic response Neoadjuvant gemcitabine-S-1 improved OS versus upfront surgery in the 361-patient full analysis set after three randomised exclusions (37.0 vs 26.6 months; HR 0.73, 95% CI 0.56-0.95, P=.018); relapse-free survival also favoured treatment nominally (14.3 vs 11.3 months; HR 0.77, P=.030). Among neoadjuvant recipients, grade 3 and 4 adverse events occurred in 48.8% and 23.8%; no operative deaths occurred. This full report supersedes the 2019 abstract and prints no median follow-up

records.title: SWOG S1505
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · II · 2021
records.body: Adults aged 18–75 years with tissue-confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma, Zubrod performance status 0–1, measurable Intergroup-criteria resectable disease, no prior therapy, and adequate marrow, hepatic, and renal function Perioperative mFOLFIRINOX: Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 180 mg/m2, then fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 hours every 2 weeks for 6 preoperative and 6 postoperative doses. vs Perioperative gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel: Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 followed by gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 weekly, 3 weeks on and 1 week off, for 9 preoperative and 9 postoperative doses Primary: Two-year overall survival. Secondary: Toxicity and overall resection rate; R0 resection rate, pathologic response, and disease-free survival Neither perioperative regimen met its own 40% null primary benchmark: 2-year OS was 47% (P=.15) with mFOLFIRINOX and 48% (P=.14) with gemcitabine-nab-paclitaxel, so no head-to-head comparison or equivalence claim was licensed. Median OS was 23.2 and 23.6 months. Only 102/147 enrolled patients were eligible/evaluable after central imaging. R0 resection was 85% in each resected cohort. Grade 3/4 profiles differed, but phase-specific denominators were confined to the unfiled supplement

records.title: NORPACT-1
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant & perioperative therapy — resectable disease · II · 2024
records.body: Adults with WHO performance status 0-1 and a radiologically strongly suspected, NCCN-resectable tumour of the pancreatic head: no arterial contact, SMV/PV contact no more than 180 degrees without contour irregularity, and no distant metastasis; fit for pancreatoduodenectomy. Histological confirmation was not required before randomisation after the December 2017 amendment Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX every 14 days x4, restaging, surgery, then gemcitabine-capecitabine x4 (or gemcitabine); after amendment, mFOLFIRINOX x8 was permitted vs Upfront surgery then gemcitabine-capecitabine x6 (or gemcitabine); after amendment, mFOLFIRINOX x12 was permitted Primary: Overall survival at 18 months. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Overall survival, Resection, R0 resection, Nodal status, Pathologic response, Surgical complications, Treatment feasibility, Safety Neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX did not improve survival in resectable pancreatic head cancer and may have worsened it: 18-month OS 60% vs 73% and median OS 25.1 vs 38.5 months (HR 1.52, 95% CI 1.00-2.33) favouring upfront surgery. Resection rate unchanged (82% vs 89%). R0 (56% vs 39%) and node-negative (29% vs 14%) status improved with neoadjuvant therapy, but severe toxicity rose (58% vs 40%, including 2 deaths after the first neoadjuvant cycle). Argues against routine neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX for clearly resectable disease

records.title: PREOPANC
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · III · 2020
records.body: Pathologically confirmed resectable or borderline-resectable pancreatic cancer without distant metastases; WHO PS 0-1 and adequate haematologic, hepatic and renal function. DPCG CT: resectable = SMV/PV contact <=90 degrees without arterial contact; borderline = SMV/PV contact <=270 degrees without occlusion or celiac/hepatic/SMA contact <=90 degrees. T1 tumours <2 cm without vascular contact were excluded; DPCG criteria are narrower than NCCN Neoadjuvant gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 on days 1 and 8 in cycles 1 and 3 and days 1, 8 and 15 with 36 Gy in 15 fractions in cycle 2, then surgery and adjuvant gemcitabine x4 vs Upfront surgery then adjuvant gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days x6 Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Disease-free survival, Locoregional failure-free interval, Distant metastasis-free interval, Resection, R0 resection, Serious adverse events, Postoperative complications PREOPANC did not meet its protocol primary OS endpoint in 2020 (16.0 vs 14.3 months; HR 0.78, P=.096). At the 2022 repeat look without repeated-testing alpha control, median OS was 15.7 vs 14.3 months and 5-year OS 20.5% vs 6.5% (HR 0.73, nominal P=.025). R0 resection by ITT was 41% vs 28% (nominal P=.025), without evidence of effect modification by resectability (interaction P=.56). Serious adverse events were 52% vs 41% (P=.096); Dutch criteria were narrower than NCCN
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2020;38:1763-1773   J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1220-1230 long-term results 35084987

records.title: Alliance A021501
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · II · 2022
records.body: Patients with centrally radiographically confirmed borderline resectable pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma enrolled through a 2-step registration process, with final stage confirmation by central review; evaluable patients provided consent, were centrally eligible, and received protocol-defined treatment. ECOG performance status 0–1 was required for surgery after preoperative treatment mFOLFIRINOX every 2 weeks x8 (oxaliplatin 85, irinotecan 180, leucovorin 400 and infusional fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46-48 h), surgery, then FOLFOX6 x4 vs the same mFOLFIRINOX x7, SBRT 33-40 Gy in 5 fractions or HIGRT 25 Gy in 5 fractions, surgery, then FOLFOX6 x4 Primary: Overall survival at 18 months. Secondary: Event-free survival, R0 resection, Pathologic complete response, Adverse events mFOLFIRINOX alone met its arm-specific historical benchmark (18-month OS 66.7%; median 29.8 months), while the radiotherapy arm closed after interim R0 futility (10/30) and was truncated. No formal between-arm efficacy comparison was licensed, so the trial does not show that radiotherapy harmed outcomes or that mFOLFIRINOX was superior. Grade 3 or worse related events occurred in 57% and 64%; arm 1 had a probable treatment-related sepsis death. Complete eligibility and historical-benchmark sources were confined to unfiled supplements

records.title: ESPAC-5 (ESPAC-5F)
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · II · 2023
records.body: Adults with centrally reviewed NCCN-defined borderline-resectable pancreatic-head ductal adenocarcinoma, including pathological variants, WHO performance status 0-1, no distant metastases, adequate organ function, biliary drainage by an allowed metal stent when needed, and fitness for surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy Immediate surgery vs Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 days 1, 8 and 15 plus capecitabine 830 mg/m2 twice daily days 1-21 every 28 days x2 vs FOLFIRINOX every 2 weeks x4 vs 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions with capecitabine 830 mg/m2 twice daily on weekdays; neoadjuvant arms were restaged before surgery and postoperative chemotherapy was discretionary Primary: Recruitment rate, Surgical resection. Secondary: R0 resection, Toxicity, Postoperative complications, Mortality, Response, Disease-free survival, Local disease-free survival, Overall survival, Quality of life ESPAC-5 did not improve the co-primary resection outcome (55% pooled neoadjuvant vs 68% immediate surgery, P=.33) and enrolled 90 rather than the 100-patient target. Pooled 1-year OS was 76% vs 39% (HR 0.29, nominal P=.0052), but survival was secondary, unadjusted and underpowered at 12.2 months with low event counts. Grade 3 or worse events were 34% vs 7% and serious events 22% vs 11%; no 30-day deaths occurred, while five patients died within 90 days

records.title: PREOPANC-2
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · III · 2025
records.body: Adults with histologically or cytologically confirmed, non-metastatic resectable or borderline-resectable PDAC by Dutch Pancreatic Cancer Group CT criteria, WHO performance status 0-1, and no prior PDAC treatment; both anatomical cohorts were eligible and the source's borderline definition was narrower than NCCN criteria FOLFIRINOX (oxaliplatin 85, irinotecan 180, leucovorin 400, fluorouracil bolus 400 then 2400 mg/m2 over 46 h) every 14 days x8 before surgery, with no adjuvant therapy planned vs Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days x3, cycles 1 and 3 shortened to days 1 and 8, with 36 Gy in 15 fractions in cycle 2, surgery, then gemcitabine x4 Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Locoregional failure-free interval, Distant metastasis-free interval, Disease-free survival, Resection and pathology, Treatment delivery, Safety, Quality of life, Cost-effectiveness, Biomarkers Total neoadjuvant FOLFIRINOX did not improve OS versus gemcitabine-based chemoradiotherapy (21.9 vs 21.3 months; HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.69-1.13, P=.32) and did not establish equivalence; PFS was also similar (12.1 vs 11.9 months; HR 0.84, P=.14). These were inseparable whole strategies, including no planned adjuvant therapy versus postoperative gemcitabine, so no radiotherapy effect can be isolated. Grade 3 or worse events were 67% vs 60%, with two versus one treatment-related deaths; no predictive subgroup interaction was found

records.title: CASSANDRA (PACT-21)
records.subtitle: Resectable & BR Pancreatic · Neoadjuvant therapy — borderline resectable disease · III · 2025
records.body: Adults aged 18-75 years with Karnofsky performance status at least 70, pathologically confirmed AJCC stage I-III PDAC considered anatomically resectable or borderline resectable by local NCCN criteria, or biologically borderline resectable by international consensus criteria including CA19-9 at least 500 IU/mL PAXG every 14 days for 4 months: capecitabine 625 mg/m2 twice daily, nab-paclitaxel 150, gemcitabine 800 and cisplatin 30 mg/m2 vs mFOLFIRINOX every 14 days for 4 months: oxaliplatin 85, leucovorin 400, irinotecan 150 and fluorouracil 2400 mg/m2 over 46 h; event-free eligible patients entered an unreported timing randomisation for 2 further months before vs after surgery Primary: Event-free survival. Secondary: Response, resection and pathology; Safety, quality of life and overall survival PAXG improved EFS over mFOLFIRINOX (16.0 vs 10.2 months; HR 0.63, 95% CI 0.47-0.84, P=.0018). Overall survival remained immature and was not formally tested (32.1 vs 26.4 months); the second timing randomisation was not reported, and no resectability interaction was available to support predictive selection. Grade 3 or worse adverse events were 66% vs 61%; toxicity profiles differed and one treatment-related sepsis death occurred with mFOLFIRINOX

records.title: Burris (gemcitabine)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 1997
records.body: Symptomatic, pathologically diagnosed unresectable locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer; no prior chemotherapy; Karnofsky performance status >=50 and protocol-specified organ function; symptom burden required before randomisation. Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV weekly (7 weeks on/1 off, then 3 weeks on/1 off; escalation to 1,250 mg/m2 allowed) versus 5-fluorouracil 600 mg/m2 IV weekly (escalation allowed but never used); until progression or clinically significant tumour-related deterioration Primary: clinical benefit response. Secondary: objective response, overall survival, time to progressive disease, safety Gemcitabine improved the principal clinical-benefit composite (23.8% versus 4.8%) and median OS (5.65 versus 4.41 months) versus weekly 5-fluorouracil. It also increased neutropenia and nausea/vomiting, without serious infections. This small 1992-1994 symptomatic population used an unvalidated clinical-benefit construct and a historical comparator; no printed alpha hierarchy, follow-up, or modern-combination comparison limits current applicability

records.title: NCIC PA.3
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2007
records.body: Locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with measurable or assessable disease, ECOG 0-2 and adequate organ function; no prior chemotherapy except radiosensitising fluorouracil or gemcitabine; prior local radiotherapy allowed only after documented progression. Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 weekly for 7 of 8 weeks then days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days plus erlotinib 100 or 150 mg orally daily versus matched placebo; until progression or unmanageable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response and duration, safety, quality of life, baseline EGFR correlation Adding erlotinib to gemcitabine produced a small OS difference (6.24 versus 5.91 months; HR 0.82) and PFS difference, with more grade 3-4 diarrhoea and rash and six protocol-related deaths in the erlotinib group. No global endpoint hierarchy was printed. EGFR and on-treatment rash analyses lack treatment-interaction tests, so neither supports predictive selection; the gemcitabine-era backbone and source-internal reporting conflicts further limit inference

records.title: GEM-CAP (Cunningham)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2009
records.body: Previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic ductal adenocarcinoma or undifferentiated pancreatic carcinoma not amenable to curative resection; WHO performance status 0-2 with protocol-specified organ function; no previous cancer-directed chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 IV weekly plus oral capecitabine 830 mg/m2 twice daily for 3 weeks of each 4-week cycle versus gemcitabine alone; until progression or intolerable toxicity. Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response, toxicity, quality of life and pain GEM-CAP did not meet its primary OS comparison (7.1 versus 6.2 months; HR 0.86; P=.08), although PFS and response were higher as nominal secondary outcomes. Grade 3-4 neutropenia, thrombocytopenia and hand-foot syndrome were more frequent with the combination. A publication-level meta-analysis cannot convert the within-trial OS result; the historical open-label backbone and unfiled appendix leave post-treatment, subgroup and detailed quality-of-life results unresolved

records.title: PRODIGE 4/ACCORD 11 (FOLFIRINOX)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2011
records.body: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma, measurable disease, age 18-75 years, ECOG 0-1, bilirubin <=1.5 times ULN, adequate marrow and renal function, and no previous chemotherapy; selected fit first-line population. FOLFIRINOX every 2 weeks: oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, irinotecan 180 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, fluorouracil 400 mg/m2 bolus then 2,400 mg/m2 over 46 hours; versus gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 weekly. Six months was recommended, with stop-and-go reintroduction allowed after 12 cycles Primary: phase 2 tumour response; phase 3 overall survival. Secondary: phase 2 safety; phase 3 progression-free survival, tumour response, safety and quality of life FOLFIRINOX improved OS (11.1 versus 6.8 months; HR 0.57) and PFS versus gemcitabine in fit metastatic patients. It increased neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, diarrhoea and neuropathy; one treatment-related death occurred in each arm, while deterioration in several quality-of-life domains was delayed. Eligibility was restricted to ECOG 0-1 and age <=75 years; phase-2 patients rolled into phase 3, secondary findings were nominal and supplement details are unfiled

records.title: MPACT
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2013
records.body: Previously untreated measurable metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma diagnosed within 6 weeks, Karnofsky performance status >=70 and adequate organ function; locally advanced disease and prior cytotoxic adjuvant therapy excluded. nab-Paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 then gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days versus gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 weekly for 7 of 8 weeks then days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days; until progression or unacceptable adverse events Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival and objective response nab-Paclitaxel plus gemcitabine improved OS (8.5 versus 6.7 months; HR 0.72), independent-review PFS and response versus gemcitabine. Peripheral neuropathy, myelosuppression and fatigue were more frequent; serious adverse events were 50% versus 43% and adverse events leading to death occurred in 4% of each arm without event-specific causality, while severe neuropathy generally improved after interruption. This first-line metastatic KPS >=70 population used a historical single-agent comparator; no protected secondary hierarchy, quality-of-life assessment or subgroup interaction testing was printed

records.title: NAPOLI-3 (NALIRIFOX)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2023
records.body: Treatment-naive metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with measurable disease, ECOG 0-1 and metastatic diagnosis within 6 weeks; prior adjuvant therapy permitted only when completed >12 months earlier without persistent toxicity. NALIRIFOX every 2 weeks: liposomal irinotecan 50 mg/m2, oxaliplatin 60 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2 and fluorouracil 2,400 mg/m2 over 46 hours; versus nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 plus gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days; until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival and objective response NALIRIFOX improved OS (11.1 versus 9.2 months; HR 0.83) and PFS versus nab-paclitaxel-gemcitabine under the prespecified sequence, but objective response was not significantly different. Gastrointestinal adverse events, hypokalaemia and treatment-related serious events were more frequent; neutropenia and neuropathy were less frequent, and treatment-related deaths occurred in 6 versus 8 patients. It applies to ECOG 0-1 measurable metastatic disease; the open-label source has unfiled protocol/SAP/appendix details and no predictive subgroup interaction results

records.title: GEST (Gemcitabine and S-1 Trial)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · First-line metastatic disease · III · 2013
records.body: Chemotherapy-naive patients with locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma or adenosquamous carcinoma in Japan and Taiwan; ECOG PS 0–1; no prior chemotherapy or radiotherapy; age >20 years, amended to <80 after serious adverse events in patients ≥80 Gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² IV d1, 8, 15 of 28-day cycle vs S-1 orally twice daily 80/100/120 mg/d by BSA d1–28 of 42-day cycle vs gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m² d1, 8 plus S-1 60/80/100 mg/d by BSA d1–14 of 21-day cycle; all cycles repeated until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or patient refusal Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, safety, quality of life First-line S-1 monotherapy was noninferior to gemcitabine for OS in locally advanced/metastatic pancreatic cancer (HR 0.96; 97.5% CI, 0.78 to 1.18; P < .001 for noninferiority), while gemcitabine plus S-1 (GS) did not significantly improve OS (HR 0.88; 97.5% CI, 0.71 to 1.08; P = .15). Median OS 8.8 months gemcitabine, 9.7 months S-1, 10.1 months GS; GS significantly improved PFS (HR 0.66; 97.5% CI, 0.54 to 0.81; P < .001). Grade ≥3 neutropenia 41.0% gemcitabine vs 8.8% S-1 vs 62.2% GS; GS had more grade ≥3 GI toxicities than gemcitabine. Noninferiority margin 1.33 may be large.
records.keywords: Ueno et al. J Clin Oncol 31:1640-1648, 2013

records.title: PANOPTIMOX (PRODIGE 35)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Maintenance therapy · II · 2021
records.body: Previously untreated measurable metastatic pancreatic cancer, age <=75 years, ECOG 0-1 and adequate organ function; prior perioperative chemotherapy allowed if completed >6 months earlier. Three baseline-assigned strategies: 12 cycles FOLFIRINOX; 8 cycles FOLFIRINOX then LV5FU2 maintenance with FOLFIRINOX reintroduction at progression; or alternating FOLFIRI.3 and gemcitabine. Primary: 6-month progression-free survival rate. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival, best response, duration of disease control, safety, oxaliplatin dose intensity, quality of life and second-line therapy This noncomparative phase II strategy trial found that the induction-to-LV5FU2-maintenance arm met its arm-specific 6-month PFS decision rule; it was not a direct three-arm efficacy comparison. Maintenance involved later FOLFIRINOX reintroduction and greater cumulative oxaliplatin exposure, with more late grade 3-4 neuropathy; treatment-related deaths were sepsis in arm A and hypertonic coma in arm C. Median OS was descriptive across arms. Results apply to the baseline-assigned strategy in fit patients, not maintenance-only randomisation among responders; several source-internal denominator inconsistencies remain

records.title: POLO
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Maintenance therapy · III · 2019
records.body: Metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma with deleterious or suspected deleterious germline BRCA1/2 mutation and no progression during >=16 weeks of continuous first-line platinum chemotherapy; protocol-specified organ and toxicity recovery criteria required. Maintenance olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily versus matching placebo, started 4-8 weeks after platinum chemotherapy and continued until investigator-assessed progression or unacceptable toxicity. Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, second progression-free survival, objective response, global quality of life and safety In the dual-selected germline BRCA/platinum-controlled population, maintenance olaparib improved blinded-central-review PFS (7.4 versus 3.8 months; HR 0.53) without a demonstrated benefit at the immature interim OS analysis. Grade >=3 adverse events, interruptions and reductions were more common with olaparib, while global quality of life did not show a clinically meaningful between-group difference. This source does not establish benefit beyond patients without progression after at least 16 weeks of platinum or final OS

records.title: CONKO-003
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Second-line therapy · III · 2014
records.body: Advanced pancreatic cancer progressing during first-line gemcitabine monotherapy, measurable disease, Karnofsky performance status >=70 and protocol-specified organ function; treatment planned within 4 weeks of progression. OFF: oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2 on days 8 and 22 plus folinic acid 200 mg/m2 and 24-hour fluorouracil 2,000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8, 15 and 22; versus the same fluorouracil/folinic-acid regimen without oxaliplatin, both with best supportive care, every 6 weeks until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: time to progression and tolerability After gemcitabine monotherapy, OFF improved median OS (5.9 versus 3.3 months; HR 0.66) and time to progression versus fluorouracil/folinic acid, crossing the interim-adjusted primary boundary. Neurotoxicity was substantially more common with OFF. The analysis excluded eight randomised patients and contains treated-population discrepancies; recruitment predated current first-line multiagent therapy, so it does not directly establish benefit after modern sequences or with a standard FOLFOX schedule

records.title: NAPOLI-1
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Second-line therapy · III · 2016
records.body: Metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma progressing after gemcitabine-based therapy; neoadjuvant or adjuvant exposure qualified only if distant metastases developed within 6 months. KPS >=70, normal bilirubin, albumin >=30 g/L and adequate marrow and renal function; prior irinotecan or fluorouracil permitted Liposomal irinotecan 80 mg/m2 plus folinic acid 400 mg/m2 and 46-hour fluorouracil 2,400 mg/m2 every 2 weeks versus version-2 fluorouracil/folinic-acid control; separate liposomal-irinotecan 120 mg/m2 every 3 weeks versus pooled control; until progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, time to treatment failure, objective response, CA19-9 response, clinical benefit response, quality of life and safety Liposomal irinotecan plus fluorouracil/folinic acid improved OS (6.1 versus 4.2 months; HR 0.67) and PFS after gemcitabine; liposomal-irinotecan monotherapy did not improve OS. The combination increased grade 3-4 neutropenia, diarrhoea, vomiting and fatigue, with one investigator-attributed treatment-related death. Combination and monotherapy used distinct amended/pool-control contexts and should not be merged; applicability immediately after FOLFIRINOX or in lower-performance patients remains unestablished

records.title: CodeBreaK 100 (sotorasib)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Biomarker-directed therapy · II · 2023
records.body: Previously treated locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer with locally identified KRAS p.G12C mutation; phase 1 allowed ECOG <=2 and phase 2 ECOG 0-1. All analysed patients had metastatic disease and prior chemotherapy. Single-arm oral sotorasib 960 mg once daily until progression, unacceptable adverse effects or withdrawal; pooled pancreatic cohort from phase 1 and phase 2. Primary: phase 1 safety and recommended phase 2 dose; phase 2 objective response. Secondary: duration and time to response, disease control, progression-free survival, overall survival and safety In phase 2, sotorasib produced centrally confirmed responses in 5/26 patients (19%); pooled phase 1-2 response was 8/38 (21%), with median PFS 4.0 months and OS 6.9 months. Treatment-related adverse events were generally manageable; no treatment-related grade 4-5 event occurred, while all-cause fatal events must not be attributed to sotorasib. This small pooled, nonrandomised KRAS G12C cohort has no comparator, no response benchmark and unfiled protocol/SAP/appendix details, so it supports no comparative or predictive claim beyond the enrolled subset

records.title: RASolute 302 (daraxonrasib)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Biomarker-directed therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Previously treated measurable metastatic pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with ECOG 0-1, adequate organ function and documented RAS G12/G13/Q61 mutation or no RAS mutation identified; required progression after one fluoropyrimidine- or gemcitabine-based metastatic regimen, or metastatic relapse <6 months after perioperative therapy. Prior RAS-targeted therapy was excluded; patients without identified RAS but another actionable driver required approved targeted therapy first Daraxonrasib 300 mg orally once daily versus investigator-choice gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel, modified FOLFIRINOX, FOLFOX, or liposomal irinotecan plus fluorouracil/folinic acid; until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal. Primary: overall survival and progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, progression-free survival, objective response, pain deterioration, global-health deterioration, time to response and safety At the first interim OS analysis, daraxonrasib improved RAS G12 OS (13.2 versus 6.6 months; HR 0.40) and final PFS (7.3 versus 3.5 months; HR 0.45) under the graphical testing plan. Treatment-related severe events, dose modifications and discontinuations were less frequent, but one related pneumonitis death occurred. Interpretation is limited by interim OS maturity, open-label differential treatment noninitiation and a multi-regimen investigator-choice control; non-G12 data are small and lack interaction evidence
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2026 (online ahead of print)

records.title: FOLFIRINOX in LAPC (Suker meta-analysis)
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · N/A · 2016
records.body: Treatment-naive locally advanced pancreatic cancer treated with first-line FOLFIRINOX in 13 nonrandomised studies; locally advanced definitions and subsequent treatment varied across studies. Systematic review and individual-patient meta-analysis of first-line FOLFIRINOX; subsequent chemotherapy, radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy, and surgery were not randomised and varied by study. Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, grade 3-4 adverse events, subsequent radiotherapy or chemoradiotherapy, resection and R0 resection This individual-patient meta-analysis reported median OS 24.2 months and PFS 15.0 months after first-line FOLFIRINOX in locally advanced disease. It is observational, not a regimen comparison: local therapy and resection were selected after treatment and cannot be credited causally. Severe-event reporting was heterogeneous and likely underestimates patient incidence. Variable definitions, retrospective cohorts, differing dose/supportive care and unfiled appendix analyses preclude a validated selection rule for radiotherapy or surgery

records.title: LAP07
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · III · 2016
records.body: Stage III locally advanced pancreatic cancer, WHO performance status <=2 and no previous chemotherapy or radiotherapy; second randomisation required disease control after 4 months of induction and retained WHO performance status <=2. Four months of induction gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 weekly for 3 of 4 weeks with or without erlotinib 100 mg daily; controlled patients then continued allocated chemotherapy for 2 months versus 54 Gy in 30 fractions with capecitabine 800 mg/m2 twice daily, with selected erlotinib maintenance at 150 mg daily Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, erlotinib-maintenance survival and tolerability, radiotherapy quality assurance and safety Among 269 patients controlled after induction, chemoradiotherapy did not improve OS versus continued chemotherapy (15.2 versus 16.5 months; HR 1.03), and the planned interim became the final primary analysis after a futility stop. PFS was not significantly improved; locoregional progression was lower, but quality of life was not assessed and grade 3-4 nausea was higher. Results are conditional on surviving and remaining progression-free after gemcitabine-era induction, not all locally advanced disease; contemporary multiagent induction, protocol supplements and central progression assessment were absent

records.title: PANOVA-3
records.subtitle: Advanced Pancreatic · Locally advanced disease · III · 2025
records.body: Previously untreated unresectable locally advanced, biopsy-confirmed pancreatic adenocarcinoma, ECOG performance status 0-2 and life expectancy >=3 months; implantable torso electronic devices and severe adhesive/hydrogel/chemotherapy hypersensitivity excluded. TTFields 150 kHz recommended >=18 hours/day with arrays replaced 2-3 times weekly plus nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m2 then gemcitabine 1,000 mg/m2 on days 1, 8 and 15 every 28 days, versus identical chemotherapy alone; until local progression or intolerance Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, local progression-free survival, 1-year survival, pain-free survival, puncture-free survival, objective response, resectability and safety Adding TTFields to gemcitabine/nab-paclitaxel met the OS boundary (16.2 versus 14.2 months; HR 0.82), but PFS, the only downstream hierarchical endpoint, was not improved, so all later endpoint P values are nominal. Objective response was not significantly different and resectability was numerically lower. Device-related adverse events were common, mainly skin reactions; no TTFields-related death occurred, but four patients died of chemotherapy-related adverse events. Open-label no-sham design, investigator assessment, safety-denominator conflicts and continuous device burden are material limits

records.title: SURF Trial
records.subtitle: HCC · Curative-intent locoregional therapy — ablation · N/A · 2022
records.body: Initial HCC, ≤3 nodules and largest lesion ≤3 cm, amenable to both resection and percutaneous RFA after multidisciplinary review; excludes lesions near vasculature, biliary tree or adjacent organs, or not clearly visualised by ultrasound, when RFA is infeasible Surgical resection (open or laparoscopic, local technique) vs percutaneous ultrasound-guided RFA with CT margin confirmation; repeat RFA within 2 weeks for incomplete treatment. Single local-treatment course; no fixed postoperative course reported. Primary: recurrence-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: local recurrence, serious adverse effects, treatment for recurrence Resection did not improve OS or RFS over RFA for small initial HCC; early closure means the results do not establish equivalence. At median follow-up 6.4/6.6 years, 5-year OS was 74.6% versus 70.4% (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.64-1.43) and 5-year RFS 42.9% versus 42.7% (HR 0.90, 0.67-1.22). Local recurrence was 8.0% versus 15.8%; serious adverse effects 3.3% versus none. Accrual stopped at 308 of 600 target.
records.keywords: Liver Cancer 2022;11:209-218   J Clin Oncol 2025;43:2628-2638 final OS and updated RFS analysis 40554738

records.title: Llovet (BCLC)
records.subtitle: HCC · Transarterial chemoembolization (TACE) · N/A · 2002
records.body: Unresectable HCC, Child-Pugh A/B, Okuda I/II, not for curative therapy Arterial embolisation or chemoembolisation (doxorubicin) vs symptomatic care Overall survival Chemoembolisation improved survival (1- and 2-year 82% and 63% vs 63% and 27% for control; HR of death 0.47); established TACE as standard of care for unresectable intermediate-stage HCC.

records.title: SARAH
records.subtitle: HCC · Transarterial radioembolization (Y-90 / SIRT) · III · 2017
records.body: Locally advanced or inoperable HCC, including portal vein invasion Y-90 resin microsphere radioembolisation (SIRT) vs sorafenib Overall survival SIRT did not improve OS over sorafenib (median 8.0 vs 9.9 months, HR 1.15) despite higher tumour response (19% vs 12%) and better tolerability/quality of life; Y-90 is not a substitute for systemic therapy in advanced HCC.

records.title: DOSISPHERE-01
records.subtitle: HCC · Transarterial radioembolization (Y-90 / SIRT) · II · 2021
records.body: Locally advanced HCC ≥7 cm, eligible for Y-90 glass microspheres Personalised dosimetry (≥205 Gy to index lesion) vs standard dosimetry (120 Gy) Objective response rate (EASL) Personalised dosimetry doubled response (71% vs 36%) and markedly improved OS (median 26.6 vs 10.7 months); established tumour-dose–guided Y-90 radioembolisation.

records.title: TACTICS
records.subtitle: HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · II · 2020
records.body: Adults with liver-confined unresectable HCC amenable to TACE but unsuitable for resection/ablation; no vascular invasion or extrahepatic spread, ≤10 tumours each ≤10 cm, ECOG 0-1, Child-Pugh ≤7. Prior systemic therapy excluded. On-demand conventional TACE plus sorafenib 400 mg/day for 2-3 weeks before first TACE, held around TACE then restarted 400 mg/day with optional escalation to 800 mg/day vs on-demand conventional TACE alone; continue until unTACEable progression, refractoriness, intolerable toxicity or withdrawal. Primary: TACE-specific progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, safety TACE plus sorafenib improved the trial-specific PFS endpoint but did not improve final OS. In 156 ITT patients, TACE-specific PFS, which did not count new intrahepatic lesions as progression, was 22.8 versus 13.5 months (HR 0.661, 95% CI 0.466-0.938); OS was 36.2 versus 30.8 months (HR 0.861, 0.607-1.223). In 77/71 treated, grade-3 hypertension within 8 weeks after first TACE was 10.4% versus 4.2%.

records.title: EMERALD-1
records.subtitle: HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Adults with HCC not amenable to resection, ablation or transplant but amenable to up to four TACE procedures within 16 weeks; no extrahepatic disease, Child-Pugh A-B7, ECOG 0-1 and measurable intrahepatic disease. Endoscopy assessed variceal bleeding risk. TACE 1-4 procedures within 16 weeks plus durvalumab 1500 mg IV every 4 weeks starting ≥7 days after first TACE → durvalumab 1120 mg IV plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks starting ≥14 days after last TACE vs the same durvalumab schedule plus bevacizumab placebo vs double placebo; continue to mRECIST progression, toxicity, withdrawal or other discontinuation, with treatment beyond progression allowed for clinical benefit Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life, objective response rate, disease control rate, duration of response, time to progression, safety Adding bevacizumab to durvalumab-TACE improved PFS; durvalumab-TACE alone did not. BICR RECIST PFS was 15.0 versus 8.2 months with durvalumab-bevacizumab versus placebo (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.61-0.98) and 10.0 versus 8.2 months with durvalumab alone (HR 0.94, 0.75-1.19). In the 154/232/200 treatment-received safety sets, grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs were 27%/6%/6%; haemorrhagic AEs 28%/10%/14%, with fatal haemorrhage 0%/3%/1%.

records.title: LEAP-012
records.subtitle: HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Adults with unresectable, non-metastatic liver-only HCC amenable to TACE, no portal-vein invasion or extrahepatic spread, measurable disease, ECOG 0-1 and Child-Pugh A; excluded tumour ≥10 cm, >10 tumours or ≥50% liver involvement. TACE plus lenvatinib 12 mg orally daily (≥60 kg) or 8 mg daily (<60 kg) plus pembrolizumab 400 mg IV every 6 weeks for up to 2 years vs matched oral/IV placebos plus TACE; oral therapy held around TACE and otherwise continued to progression, toxicity, physician discontinuation or withdrawal. Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, time to progression, safety Lenvatinib-pembrolizumab-TACE improved PFS, but first-interim OS did not reach statistical significance. In 480 randomised patients, BICR RECIST PFS was 14.6 versus 10.0 months (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.51-0.84); interim OS HR was 0.80 (0.57-1.11), with 29% versus 34% deaths. In 237/241 treated, grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs were 71%/32% and treatment-related deaths 2%/<1%.

records.title: EMERALD-3
records.subtitle: HCC · Locoregional + systemic combination therapy · III · 2026
records.body: Confirmed HCC (imaging or histopathology) not amenable to curative surgery, ablation or transplantation but amenable to TACE; embolisation-eligible setting; Child–Pugh class A, ECOG 0–1, at least one measurable intrahepatic target lesion per mRECIST; excluded previous HCC systemic therapy, more than one previous palliative embolisation, major portal vein thrombosis (Vp3/Vp4) and investigator-assessed upper gastrointestinal bleeding risk TACE plus STRIDE (tremelimumab 300 mg plus durvalumab 1500 mg on day 1, then durvalumab 1500 mg every 4 weeks) plus lenvatinib 8 mg (<60 kg) or 12 mg (≥60 kg) once daily vs TACE plus STRIDE vs TACE; durvalumab and lenvatinib continued for ≤36 months, progression, toxicity or consent withdrawal; TACE technique and number at investigator discretion, first procedure ≥7 days after first durvalumab dose or ≤7 days after randomisation (TACE arm) Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response rate, disease control rate at 20 weeks, duration of response, time to progression, time to second progression or death, EORTC QLQ-HCC18, EORTC QLQ-C30, α-fetoprotein associations with outcomes, pharmacokinetics, antidrug antibodies, time to first subsequent therapy or death, safety STRIDE plus lenvatinib plus TACE significantly improved primary PFS versus TACE, but interim OS did not meet significance; STRIDE-TACE had favourable PFS and OS estimates versus the first 175 TACE controls, in descriptive analyses not formally tested. Triplet versus TACE had PFS 13.0 versus 9.8 months (HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.57-0.86) and interim OS 39.5 versus 34.7 months (HR 0.84, 0.65-1.09; 40% maturity). STRIDE-TACE versus TACE had PFS 12.9 versus 8.1 months (HR 0.71, 0.56-0.91) and median OS not reached versus 32.9 months (HR 0.70, 0.51-0.95; 45% maturity). Grade 3 or 4 treatment-related AEs occurred in 63% (180 of 287), 49% (85 of 175) and 19% (54 of 290) with triplet, STRIDE-TACE and TACE; treatment-related deaths occurred in seven of 287 (2%; two myocarditis), none of 175 and two of 290 (1%).

records.title: STORM
records.subtitle: HCC · Adjuvant therapy after resection / ablation · III · 2015
records.body: HCC at high recurrence risk after curative resection or ablation Adjuvant sorafenib vs placebo Recurrence-free survival Sorafenib did not improve RFS (median 33.4 vs 33.8 months, HR 0.94) or OS; showed adjuvant TKI therapy has no role after curative HCC treatment.

records.title: IMbrave050
records.subtitle: HCC · Adjuvant therapy after resection / ablation · III · 2023
records.body: Resected or ablated HCC at high risk of recurrence Adjuvant atezolizumab + bevacizumab (1 year) vs active surveillance Recurrence-free survival Improved RFS at the interim analysis (HR 0.72), but the benefit was not maintained on updated analysis; adjuvant atezolizumab/bevacizumab is not established as standard.

records.title: SHARP
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2008
records.body: Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma (pathology-confirmed) not eligible for or progressed after surgical or locoregional therapy; no prior systemic treatment; Child-Pugh class A, ECOG performance status 2 or less, at least one untreated measurable RECIST lesion; prior molecularly targeted or other systemic therapy excluded Sorafenib 400 mg (two 200-mg tablets) orally twice daily continuously vs matching placebo; treatment continued until both radiologic (RECIST) and symptomatic (FHSI8) progression, unacceptable adverse events, or death; no placebo crossover before the definitive survival analysis Primary: Overall survival, Time to symptomatic progression. Secondary: Time to radiologic progression, Disease-control rate, Response rate, Safety Sorafenib improved median OS (10.7 vs 7.9 months, HR 0.69; 95% CI 0.55–0.87) and time to radiologic progression (5.5 vs 2.8 months, HR 0.58); established the first systemic standard for advanced HCC. Final results at second planned interim analysis (321 deaths); 1-yr survival 44% vs 33%. Co-primary time to symptomatic progression did not differ (4.1 vs 4.9 months, HR 1.08, P=0.77). Disease-control 43% vs 32%, no complete responses. Grade 3 drug-related diarrhea and hand-foot skin reaction each 8%, grade 3 hypophosphatemia 11%; serious AEs similar (52% vs 54%)
records.keywords: Llovet et al. N Engl J Med 2008;359:378-90

records.title: Cheng et al. (Asia-Pacific sorafenib in advanced HCC)
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2009
records.body: Advanced (unresectable or metastatic) hepatocellular carcinoma, histologically or cytologically proven; first-line systemic therapy (no previous systemic therapy); Child-Pugh class A and ECOG PS 0–2 with at least one measurable RECIST lesion not previously treated locally; prior local therapy allowed if target lesion grew ≥25% or was untreated; enrolled in China, South Korea and Taiwan; excluded previous or concomitant systemic therapy, HIV, CNS tumour, cardiac disease, GI bleeding within 30 days Oral sorafenib 400 mg twice daily continuously vs matching placebo, in 6-week cycles, stratified by macroscopic vascular invasion/extrahepatic spread, ECOG PS and region, randomised 2:1; dose reductions to 200 mg twice daily then 200 mg once daily allowed for drug-related toxicity (removal if further reduction needed); continued until death or stopping criterion (toxicity requiring termination, progression, ECOG PS 4, second cancer, withdrawal) Overall survival Sorafenib is effective for advanced hepatocellular carcinoma in Asia-Pacific patients and well tolerated; with SHARP data it seems an appropriate treatment option (no predefined primary endpoint; ITT n=226). Median OS 6.5 vs 4.2 months (HR 0.68, p=0.014); median TTP 2.8 vs 1.4 months (HR 0.57, p=0.0005); DCR 35.3% vs 15.8% (p=0.0019); no meaningful TTSP difference (3.5 vs 3.4 months, HR 0.90, p=0.50). Population 73.0% HBV; benefit suggested in all preplanned exploratory subgroups (HRs <1, mostly non-significant). Grade 3/4 drug-related HFSR 10.7%, diarrhoea 6.0%, fatigue 3.4%; AE discontinuation 19.5% vs 13.3%; no drug-related deaths

records.title: REFLECT
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated unresectable HCC, BCLC B/C, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0-1 with measurable disease; excluded ≥50% liver occupation, main portal-vein invasion, bile-duct invasion and prior systemic HCC therapy. Lenvatinib 12 mg orally daily (≥60 kg) or 8 mg daily (<60 kg) in 28-day cycles vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily in 28-day cycles; no protocol stopping rule was reported, with median treatment duration 5.7 versus 3.7 months Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, time to progression, objective response rate, quality of life, pharmacokinetics, safety Lenvatinib was non-inferior but not superior to sorafenib for OS; it improved PFS and ORR without a validated treatment-selecting subgroup. In 954 ITT patients, OS was 13.6 versus 12.3 months (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.79-1.06); independent RECIST PFS 7.3 versus 3.6 months (HR 0.65, 0.56-0.77) and mRECIST ORR 40.6% versus 12.4%. In 476/475 treated, grade ≥3 AEs were 75%/67%; treatment-related deaths 11/4.

records.title: IMbrave150
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2020
records.body: Adults with locally advanced, metastatic or unresectable HCC, no prior systemic liver-cancer therapy, measurable disease, ECOG 0-1 and Child-Pugh A; untreated/incompletely treated high-risk oesophageal/gastric varices excluded after endoscopic assessment. Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily; continue to loss of clinical benefit or unacceptable toxicity. Primary: overall survival, progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, quality of life, safety Atezolizumab-bevacizumab retained longer OS and PFS than sorafenib at the descriptive update. In 501 ITT patients at 15.6-month median follow-up, OS was 19.2 versus 13.4 months (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.52-0.85), PFS 6.9 versus 4.3 months (HR 0.65, 0.53-0.81), and ORR 30% versus 11% in 326/159 measurable-disease patients. In 329/156 treated, grade 3/4 treatment-related AEs were 43%/46% and treatment-related deaths 6/1; hypertension/proteinuria increased with longer exposure.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2020;382:1894-1905   J Hepatol 2022;76:862-873 updated OS analysis 34902530

records.title: HIMALAYA
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2022
records.body: Adults aged ≥18 years with unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma and no prior systemic therapy, randomised first-line; participants with thrombosis in the main trunk of the portal vein were excluded STRIDE: tremelimumab 300 mg (1 dose) plus durvalumab 1,500 mg every 4 weeks vs durvalumab monotherapy 1,500 mg every 4 weeks vs sorafenib 400 mg twice daily; treatment beyond disease progression allowed if predefined protocol criteria met Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Depth of response, Serious adverse events At 5 years' follow-up (cut-off 01 March 2024), STRIDE sustained an OS benefit vs sorafenib with a manageable safety profile: in ITT 393/389, OS HR 0.76 (95% CI 0.65-0.89), median OS 16.43 vs 13.77 months, 60-month OS 19.6% vs 9.4% (exploratory updated analysis). Durvalumab remained noninferior, not superior (OS HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.73-1.00). OS with STRIDE was improved with disease control (60-month OS 28.7% vs 12.7%) and >25% tumour shrinkage (50.7% vs 26.3%). Extended long-term survivors (≥48 months): 83/393 (21.1%) vs 45/389 (11.6%). Serious treatment-related AEs in 388/388/374 treated: 17.5%, 8.5%, 9.9%; no additional STRIDE events after primary analysis
records.keywords: Abou-Alfa et al. NEJM Evid 2022;1:EVIDoa2100070   Sangro et al. Ann Oncol 2024;35:448-457  38382875 Rimassa et al. J Hepatol 2025;83:899-908  40222621

records.title: CheckMate 9DW
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2025
records.body: Adults with advanced HCC not eligible for curative/locoregional therapy or progressing after it, no prior systemic therapy, measurable disease, Child-Pugh 5-6 and ECOG 0-1; Vp4 invasion and clinically significant ascites excluded. Nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for ≤4 doses then nivolumab 480 mg IV every 4 weeks (maximum 2 years) vs investigator-choice lenvatinib 8/12 mg daily or sorafenib 400 mg twice daily; continue to progression, toxicity or withdrawal. Primary: overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, time to symptom deterioration, progression-free survival, quality of life, safety At the preplanned interim, nivolumab-ipilimumab improved OS and ORR but not median PFS versus a comparator that was 85% lenvatinib; crossed OS curves showed early harm before later benefit. In 668 ITT patients, OS was 23.7 versus 20.6 months (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.65-0.96); exploratory piecewise HR was 1.65 in the first 6 months and 0.61 thereafter. ORR was 36% versus 13% and PFS 9.1 versus 9.2 months (HR 0.87, 0.72-1.06). In 332/325 treated, grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs were 41%/42%, serious grade 3-4 treatment-related AEs 25%/13%, and treatment-related deaths 12/3, including 11/1 within 6 months.

records.title: CARES-310
records.subtitle: HCC · First-line advanced — systemic therapy · III · 2023
records.body: Adults with BCLC B/C HCC not amenable to or progressed after surgery/locoregional therapy, no prior systemic therapy, measurable disease, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0-1. Recent/high-risk gastrointestinal bleeding and uncontrolled hypertension were excluded. Camrelizumab 200 mg IV every 2 weeks plus rivoceranib 250 mg orally daily vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily; continue to BIRC progression, toxicity, consent withdrawal or investigator decision, with treatment beyond progression allowed for clinical benefit; rivoceranib reductions to 5-days-on/2-days-off then alternate days, no camrelizumab reduction Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: objective response rate, duration of response, disease control rate, time to progression, quality of life, safety Camrelizumab-rivoceranib retained longer OS and PFS than sorafenib at final follow-up, with substantial toxicity. In 543 ITT patients at 351 deaths, OS was 23.8 versus 15.2 months (HR 0.64, 95% CI 0.52-0.79) and updated PFS 5.6 versus 3.7 months (HR 0.54, 0.44-0.67). In 272/269 treated, grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs were 81%/54%, grade 3-4 hypertension 38%/15%, rivoceranib/sorafenib dose reduction 48%/33%, and treatment-related deaths 1/1.
records.keywords: Lancet 2023;402:1133-1146   Lancet Oncol 2025;26:1598-1611 final OS analysis 41308676

records.title: RESORCE
records.subtitle: HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2017
records.body: Hepatocellular carcinoma with documented radiological progression during sorafenib, BCLC stage B or C, not eligible for resection, ablation or chemoembolisation; sorafenib-tolerant (≥400 mg/day for ≥20 of last 28 days) with last dose within 10 weeks of randomisation; Child-Pugh A liver function; measurable lesion by mRECIST and RECIST 1.1; excluded prior other systemic HCC treatment or sorafenib stopped for toxicity Best supportive care plus oral regorafenib 160 mg once daily during weeks 1–3 of each 4-week cycle vs matching placebo plus BSC (2:1 randomisation); treatment continued until mRECIST or clinical progression, death, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or physician decision; dose reductions to 120 mg then 80 mg allowed, re-escalation to 160 mg permitted after toxicity resolution Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Time to progression, Objective response rate, Disease control rate, Quality of life, Safety This study met its primary endpoint: regorafenib improved overall survival after sorafenib progression in HCC (final analysis, cutoff Feb 29, 2016; 573 randomised, ITT). Median OS 10·6 vs 7·8 months (HR 0·63, 95% CI 0·50–0·79; one-sided p<0·0001); benefit maintained in all preplanned subgroups. Median PFS 3·1 vs 1·5 months; objective response 11% vs 4%; disease control 65% vs 36%. Grade 3/4 events: hypertension 15% vs 5%, hand-foot skin reaction 13% vs 1%; 7 (2%) drug-related deaths with regorafenib vs 2 (1%) with placebo. No firm conclusions possible for sorafenib-intolerant patients

records.title: CELESTIAL
records.subtitle: HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2018
records.body: Adults with pathological advanced HCC not amenable to curative treatment, previously treated with sorafenib and progressed after ≥1 systemic regimen; up to 2 prior systemic regimens, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0-1 Cabozantinib 60 mg orally once daily versus placebo; reductions to 40 then 20 mg permitted. Treatment continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal or protocol discontinuation. Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, objective response rate, safety Cabozantinib improved OS and PFS after sorafenib, but most patients required dose reduction. In the 707-patient ITT second interim, OS was 10.2 versus 8.0 months (HR 0.76, 95% CI 0.63-0.92) and PFS 5.2 versus 1.9 months (HR 0.44, 0.36-0.52). In 467/237 treated, grade 3/4 AEs were 68%/36%; 62% reduced dose to median 35.8 mg from 60 mg. Treatment-related deaths were 6/1.

records.title: REACH-2
records.subtitle: HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · III · 2019
records.body: Advanced hepatocellular carcinoma, BCLC stage B or C refractory or not amenable to locoregional therapy; second-line after first-line sorafenib discontinued for intolerance or progression; AFP ≥400 ng/mL; Child-Pugh class A, ECOG 0–1; excluded prior liver transplantation, hepatic encephalopathy, varices requiring endoscopic treatment, uncontrolled hypertension, clinically meaningful ascites (>grade 1 CTCAE v4.0) Ramucirumab 8 mg/kg intravenously over 1 h every 14 days plus best supportive care vs placebo intravenously every 14 days plus best supportive care, until disease progression, unacceptable toxicity, or withdrawal of consent Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Objective response rate, Time to radiographic progression, Safety, Time to deterioration in FHSI-8 score, Time to deterioration in ECOG performance status REACH-2 met its primary endpoint, showing improved OS for ramucirumab vs placebo in HCC with AFP ≥400 ng/mL after sorafenib (8.5 vs 7.3 months; HR 0.710 [0.531–0.949]; p=0.0199; ITT, cutoff 15 Mar 2018, median follow-up 7.6 mo); per authors, the first positive phase 3 trial in a biomarker-selected HCC population. PFS 2.8 vs 1.6 months (HR 0.452; p<0.0001); time to radiographic progression 3.0 vs 1.6 months (HR 0.427); disease control 59.9% vs 38.9%; objective response did not differ (5% vs 1%). FHSI-8 and ECOG deterioration did not differ. Pooled with REACH (AFP ≥400, n=542): OS 8.1 vs 5.0 months, HR 0.694 (p=0.0002). Grade ≥3 TEAEs ≥5%: hypertension 13% vs 5%, hyponatraemia 6% vs 0; 3 ramucirumab deaths judged treatment-related (AKI, hepatorenal syndrome, renal failure). Placebo-arm OS notably long; small placebo group (n=95).

records.title: CheckMate 040 / 459
records.subtitle: HCC · Second-line & subsequent therapy · I/II–III · 2022
records.body: CheckMate 459: untreated first-line advanced HCC, Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0-1 (743 randomised). CheckMate 040 reports: sorafenib-experienced nivolumab monotherapy (154 treated) and nivolumab-ipilimumab after progression on or intolerance of sorafenib (148 randomised; 146 previously received sorafenib), Child-Pugh A and ECOG 0-1 CheckMate 459: nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily until progression, toxicity, consent withdrawal or study closure. CheckMate 040 monotherapy: nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV every 2 weeks until progression, toxicity or discontinuation, with the escalation phase capped at 2 years. CheckMate 040 combination: arm A nivolumab 1 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks ×4 → nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks; arm B nivolumab 3 mg/kg plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg on the same induction/maintenance schedule; arm C nivolumab 3 mg/kg every 2 weeks plus ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks; combination-cohort treatment duration and stopping rules were not reported Primary: overall survival, safety, tolerability, objective response rate. Secondary: progression-free survival, duration of response, disease control, time to progression, quality of life Nivolumab monotherapy activity did not translate into confirmed first-line OS benefit, whereas nivolumab-ipilimumab remained active and was later confirmed first-line in CheckMate 9DW. CheckMate 459 missed its OS primary endpoint: 16.4 versus 14.7 months (HR 0.85, 95% CI 0.72-1.02); grade-3 treatment-related AEs were 18% versus 47% in 367/363 treated. At 5 years, sorafenib-experienced nivolumab monotherapy ORR was 14% by BICR (22/154). In the 148-patient combination cohort, arm A ORR was 32% and median OS 22.8 months (95% CI 9.4-not reached); the study was not powered for arm comparisons, and 1 treatment-related death occurred in 146 treated. At its preplanned interim, CheckMate 9DW showed OS 23.7 versus 20.6 months (HR 0.79), but OS curves crossed (first-6-month HR 1.65) and 11 of 12 versus 1 of 3 treatment-related deaths occurred within 6 months.
