records.title: RTOG 9408
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy with androgen deprivation — intermediate & high risk · III · 2011
records.body: Localized prostate cancer, PSA ≤20 (mostly intermediate-risk) RT + 4-month ADT vs RT alone Overall survival Adding 4 months of ADT to RT improved 10-yr OS (62% vs 57%) and reduced prostate-cancer death (4% vs 8%), with benefit concentrated in intermediate-risk men; defined short-course ADT with RT.

records.title: RTOG 9202
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy with androgen deprivation — intermediate & high risk · III · 2003
records.body: Locally advanced (T2c-T4) prostate cancer RT + long-term (28-mo) vs short-term (4-mo) ADT Disease-free survival Long-term ADT improved disease-free and disease-specific survival vs 4 months, with an overall-survival benefit in Gleason 8-10 disease; supported prolonged ADT for high-risk disease.

records.title: EORTC 22961
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy with androgen deprivation — intermediate & high risk · III · 2009
records.body: Locally advanced prostate cancer treated with RT 6 months vs 3 years of androgen suppression Overall survival (non-inferiority) Six months of ADT was not non-inferior to 3 years (5-yr mortality 19.0% vs 15.2%, HR 1.42); confirmed long-course ADT as standard with RT for locally advanced disease.

records.title: CAN-2409 (aglatimagene besadenovec)
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiotherapy combination — novel agents · III · 2026
records.body: Intermediate- or high-risk localised prostate cancer planned for EBRT, ECOG 0–2 (USA/Puerto Rico); ADT optional Intraprostatic aglatimagene besadenovec + valacyclovir + EBRT vs placebo + valacyclovir + EBRT (2:1) Disease-free survival (intention-to-treat) Adding intratumoral aglatimagene besadenovec (gene-mediated immunotherapy) + valacyclovir to standard EBRT improved the primary endpoint, disease-free survival, in intermediate/high-risk localised prostate cancer (median not reached vs 86.1 months, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52-0.94; p=0.016, ITT, alpha-protected). Grade >=3 TEAEs were 8% (40/479) vs 7% (17/232) in the safety population; no safety comparison is tested, so tolerability is similar on descriptive counts rather than demonstrated equivalent. Overall survival was immature and numerically favoured placebo (HR 1.18, 95% CI 0.64-2.15, nominal p=0.59, 51 deaths). ADT use was optional and stratified, not mandated - so this is an RT-combination, not an RT+ADT, trial.

records.title: CHHiP
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · III · 2016
records.body: Localized T1b-T3a prostate cancer Moderate hypofractionation (60 Gy/20) vs conventional (74 Gy/37) Biochemical/clinical failure (non-inferiority) 60 Gy in 20 fractions was non-inferior to 74 Gy in 37 (5-yr biochemical/clinical control 90.6% vs 88.3%, HR 0.84) with similar toxicity; established moderate hypofractionation as standard.

records.title: HYPO-RT-PC
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · III · 2019
records.body: Intermediate-to-high-risk localized prostate cancer Ultra-hypofractionation (42.7 Gy/7) vs conventional (78 Gy/39) Failure-free survival (non-inferiority) Ultra-hypofractionation was non-inferior to conventional RT for failure-free survival (per-protocol; prespecified margin 4% absolute at 5 years, critical HR 1.338): 5-yr FFS 84% in both arms (Widmark 2019; restated as 85% in the 10-yr report), and at 10 years 72% vs 65% with adjusted HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.69-1.03 (Nilsson 2026). Late grade >=2 cumulative incidence was similar - genitourinary 28% vs 30%, gastrointestinal 14% vs 14% (1 minus Kaplan-Meier from start of RT). Non-inferiority licenses no superiority claim, and the two post-hoc analyses point differently: a log-rank test gave p=0.12 (superiority not reached) while a separate fixed-timepoint analysis at 10 years was significant (p=0.025), favouring ultra-hypofractionation; both are post hoc with nominal p, so neither establishes superiority. Only 11% of patients were high-risk and no ADT was permitted, so both reports draw their conclusion for intermediate-risk disease.

records.title: PACE-B
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · III · 2024
records.body: Low/favorable-intermediate-risk localized prostate cancer (no ADT) 5-fraction SBRT (36.25 Gy) vs conventional/moderate hypofractionated RT Freedom from biochemical/clinical failure (non-inferiority) Five-fraction SBRT was non-inferior to conventional RT (5-yr freedom from failure 95.8% vs 94.6%) with similar late toxicity; established SBRT as a standard option for lower-risk disease.

records.title: ASCENDE-RT
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Radiation dose & fractionation · III · 2017
records.body: Intermediate- and high-risk localized prostate cancer LDR brachytherapy boost vs dose-escalated EBRT boost (both + 12-mo ADT + pelvic RT) Biochemical progression-free survival An LDR brachytherapy boost roughly halved biochemical failure vs dose-escalated EBRT (b-PFS HR 2.04 favoring brachytherapy; 9-yr ~83% vs 62%) at the cost of more genitourinary toxicity; established brachytherapy boost for higher-risk disease.
records.keywords: Int J Radiat Oncol Biol Phys 2017;98:275-285

records.title: STAMPEDE (abiraterone, M0)
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Intensification in high-risk non-metastatic disease · III · 2022
records.body: High-risk non-metastatic (M0) prostate cancer starting ADT + RT ADT + abiraterone (± enzalutamide) vs ADT alone Metastasis-free survival Adding abiraterone to ADT improved 6-yr metastasis-free survival (82% vs 69%, HR 0.53) and overall survival (HR 0.60); enzalutamide added no benefit over abiraterone. A new option for high-risk M0 disease.

records.title: PROTEUS
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Intensification in high-risk non-metastatic disease · III · 2026
records.body: Newly diagnosed, nonmetastatic high-risk localized or locally advanced prostate adenocarcinoma in candidates for radical prostatectomy; conventional imaging centrally negative (clinical N1 allowed), ECOG 0-1, and fit for at least 13 months of ADT; full PROTEUS biopsy-core risk criteria are in an unfiled supplement. Perioperative ADT + apalutamide (6 cycles before and 6 cycles after radical prostatectomy) vs Perioperative ADT + placebo (6 cycles before and 6 cycles after radical prostatectomy) Pathological complete response/minimal residual disease and metastasis-free survival (dual) After 6 neoadjuvant cycles, ITT pCR/MRD at surgery was 94/1057 (8.9%) with perioperative ADT plus apalutamide vs 10/1052 (1.0%) with ADT plus placebo (OR 10.17, 95% CI 5.27-19.64; P<0.001). At 61.7 months' median follow-up, final ITT central-review MFS analysis after 472 of 477 planned events showed 5-year MFS of 78.2% vs 73.5% (HR 0.80, 95% CI 0.67-0.96; P=0.02). Hierarchical EFS, time to subsequent treatment, distant metastasis and 4-year freedom from disease also favoured apalutamide. The hierarchy stopped at conventional-imaging-only MFS (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.67-1.07; no protected P), so the final PSA-free-survival endpoint was not formally tested. Treatment-period grade 3/4 AEs in the safety population were 416/1050 (39.6%) vs 325/1050 (31.0%); the between-group difference was driven primarily by rash. Control was perioperative ADT plus placebo with radical prostatectomy, not radical prostatectomy alone.

records.title: RTOG 9601
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy — adjuvant vs salvage · III · 2017
records.body: Biochemical recurrence after prostatectomy (pT2-3 N0) Salvage RT + 24-mo bicalutamide 150 mg vs salvage RT + placebo Overall survival Adding 2 years of bicalutamide to salvage RT improved 12-yr OS (76.3% vs 71.3%, HR 0.77) and halved prostate-cancer death, with benefit greatest at higher PSA; supported hormone-intensified salvage.

records.title: GETUG-AFU 16
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy — adjuvant vs salvage · III · 2016
records.body: Rising PSA after prostatectomy (0.2-2.0 ng/mL) Salvage RT + 6-mo goserelin vs salvage RT alone Progression-free survival Adding 6 months of goserelin to salvage RT improved 5-yr biochemical/clinical PFS (80% vs 62%, HR 0.50), sustained at 10 years (64% vs 49%); validated short-course ADT with salvage RT.

records.title: RADICALS-RT
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy — adjuvant vs salvage · III · 2020
records.body: Post-prostatectomy with ≥1 risk factor (pT3-4, Gleason 7-10, margin+, PSA≥10) Adjuvant RT vs observation with early salvage RT Freedom from distant metastasis (biochemical PFS reported) Adjuvant RT did not improve 5-yr biochemical PFS vs early salvage (85% vs 88%, HR 1.10) but doubled urinary/bowel toxicity; established observation with early salvage RT as standard.

records.title: SPPORT (RTOG 0534)
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy — adjuvant vs salvage · III · 2022
records.body: Biochemical recurrence after prostatectomy Prostate-bed RT alone vs +short-term ADT vs +ADT + pelvic-node RT Freedom from progression Escalating salvage RT improved 5-yr freedom from progression stepwise (70.9% prostate-bed RT, 81.3% +ADT, 87.4% +ADT + pelvic-node RT); supported adding ADT and pelvic-node coverage in salvage.

records.title: RADICALS-HD
records.subtitle: Localized Prostate · Postoperative radiotherapy — adjuvant vs salvage · III · 2024
records.body: Postoperative radiotherapy after radical prostatectomy (PSA <5, M0) 24 months vs 6 months of ADT added to postoperative RT (companion randomisation: 6 months vs none) Metastasis-free survival Adding 24 months of ADT improved MFS over 6 months (10-yr MFS 78.1% vs 71.9%, HR 0.77, p=0.029) at the cost of more toxicity; in the companion randomisation, adding 6 months versus no ADT did not significantly improve MFS. Defines ADT duration with postoperative RT - long-course for those who can tolerate it.

records.title: CHAARTED (E3805)
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - docetaxel intensification · III · 2015
records.body: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer (pathological diagnosis, or clinical scenario with elevated PSA) with radiologic metastases; starting ADT, or on ADT for metastatic disease begun within 120 days before randomization without progression; prior adjuvant ADT allowed if ≤24 months with progression >12 months after completion; high-volume disease only (visceral metastases or ≥4 bone lesions with ≥1 beyond vertebral bodies and pelvis) until a July 2008 amendment added low-volume disease ADT (intermittent hormonal therapy not allowed; nonsteroidal antiandrogen at investigator discretion) plus docetaxel 75 mg per square meter of body-surface area every 3 weeks for six cycles, started at the beginning of ADT, daily prednisone not required vs ADT alone Primary: overall survival. Secondary: PSA level <0.2 ng/ml at 6 months, PSA level <0.2 ng/ml at 12 months, time to castration-resistant prostate cancer, time to clinical progression, prostate-cancer deaths, adverse events Six cycles of docetaxel at the beginning of ADT significantly prolonged OS vs ADT alone in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer; with longer follow-up, benefit was confirmed in high-volume disease, but no OS benefit was discerned in low-volume disease. At median follow-up 53.7 mo, median OS was 57.6 vs 47.2 mo (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.59–0.89). High volume: 51.2 vs 34.4 mo (HR 0.63; 95% CI 0.50–0.79); low volume: HR 1.04 (95% CI 0.70–1.55; P=.86); interaction P=.033, but subgroups were not powered for separate analysis. Time to CRPC 19.4 vs 11.7 mo (HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.52–0.73); PSA <0.2 ng/ml at 12 mo 27.7% vs 16.8%. With docetaxel, grade 3–4 febrile neutropenia occurred in 6.2% and grade 3–4 infection with neutropenia in 2.3%; grade 4 neutropenia occurred in 9.0% of 390 treated patients, and 1 sudden death was possibly docetaxel-related; no additional long-term adverse effects were observed. Adverse events were not routinely documented with ADT alone.

records.title: STAMPEDE (docetaxel)
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - docetaxel intensification · III · 2016
records.body: Prostate cancer; newly diagnosed metastatic, node-positive or high-risk locally advanced (at least two of T3/4, Gleason score 8–10, PSA ≥40 ng/mL), or relapsing with high-risk features after radical surgery and/or radiotherapy; starting first-line long-term hormone therapy begun no longer than 12 weeks before randomisation; fit for chemotherapy, no age restriction; excluding clinically significant cardiovascular history Standard of care (SOC): hormone therapy for at least 2 years (GnRH agonist/antagonist or orchidectomy), radiotherapy encouraged for N0M0 until November 2011 then mandated, optional for N+M0 vs SOC + zoledronic acid 4 mg six 3-weekly cycles then 4-weekly until 2 years vs SOC + docetaxel 75 mg/m² six 3-weekly cycles with prednisolone 10 mg daily vs SOC + zoledronic acid + docetaxel (same schedules); trial therapy stopped at disease progression or intolerable adverse events Primary: overall survival. Secondary: failure-free survival, prostate-cancer-specific survival, adverse events, treatment after relapse, time to first skeletal-related event, osteonecrosis of the jaw, time to first fracture-related hospitalisation Docetaxel started with long-term hormone therapy improved overall survival at the cost of more adverse events; zoledronic acid showed no survival improvement. Median OS 71 mo SOC-only vs 81 mo SOC+Doc (HR 0·78, 95% CI 0·66–0·93) and 76 mo SOC+ZA+Doc (HR 0·82, 0·69–0·97); SOC+ZA HR 0·94 (0·79–1·11); median follow-up 43 mo. FFS improved with SOC+Doc (HR 0·61) and SOC+ZA+Doc (HR 0·62), not SOC+ZA (HR 0·92). Adding ZA to docetaxel gave no advantage (HR 1·06, 0·86–1·30). OS benefit was clear in M1 (SOC+Doc HR 0·76, 0·62–0·92); M0 OS immature. Post hoc linked-data analysis: ZA reduced fracture-related hospitalisation in M1 (SDHR 0.73, 0.55–0.97; not significant excluding pathological fractures), not M0 (0.88, 0.59–1.32); docetaxel no clear fracture effect. Docetaxel arms: grade 3–5 AEs 52% vs 32% without, febrile neutropenia 15% and 14%; eight deaths probably or possibly treatment-related (one SOC+Doc, seven SOC+ZA+Doc, mostly neutropenic sepsis); ONJ 2% SOC+ZA, 4% SOC+ZA+Doc.

records.title: LATITUDE
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2017
records.body: Prostate cancer without neuroendocrine or small-cell features; newly diagnosed (≤3 months before randomization) high-risk metastatic castration-sensitive disease; at least two of Gleason score ≥8, ≥3 bone lesions, measurable visceral metastasis; ECOG 0 to 2; excluded prior chemotherapy, radiotherapy or surgery for metastatic disease, except 3 months or less of ADT and one course of palliative radiation or surgery ADT plus abiraterone acetate 1000 mg orally once daily (four 250-mg tablets) plus prednisone 5 mg orally daily vs ADT plus dual placebos (double-blind); ongoing ADT to maintain testosterone <50 ng/dL unless surgically castrated; treatment until disease progression, withdrawal of consent, unacceptable toxicity or death Primary: overall survival, radiographic progression-free survival. Secondary: time to next symptomatic skeletal event, time to PSA progression, time to next therapy for prostate cancer, time to initiation of chemotherapy, time to pain progression, PSA response, safety, secondary progression-free survival Adding abiraterone plus prednisone to ADT significantly increased OS and rPFS in newly diagnosed metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer. At the final analysis (618 deaths; median follow-up 51.8 mo), median OS was 53.3 vs 36.5 mo (HR 0.66; 95% CI 0.56–0.78), despite unblinding after the first interim analysis and crossover of 72 placebo patients. Median rPFS was 33.0 vs 14.8 mo (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.39–0.55); rPFS was not re-analysed at the final analysis. All secondary endpoints favoured abiraterone at the final analysis, e.g. time to PSA progression HR 0.31 and time to chemotherapy HR 0.51; exploratory secondary PFS HR 0.58. In a post-hoc analysis, the OS benefit in low-volume disease was not significant (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.47–1.10). Final-analysis safety: grade 3–4 AEs 68% vs 50%; grade 3 hypertension 21% vs 10% and grade 3 hypokalaemia 11% vs 1%; AEs leading to death 6% vs 4%; treatment-related deaths three per arm.

records.title: STAMPEDE (abiraterone)
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2017
records.body: Prostate cancer starting long-term ADT for the first time; newly diagnosed metastatic, node-positive or high-risk locally advanced (at least two of T3/T4, Gleason 8–10, PSA ≥40 ng/ml), or relapsing after radical surgery/radiotherapy with high-risk features (PSA >4 ng/ml doubling <6 months, PSA >20 ng/ml, nodal/metastatic relapse, or <12 months total ADT with >12 months off treatment); ADT started ≤12 weeks before randomization; excluded clinically significant cardiovascular disease ADT alone vs ADT + abiraterone acetate 1000 mg + prednisolone 5 mg once daily; ADT given ≥2 years; abiraterone continued until PSA, radiologic or clinical progression (metastatic, or nonmetastatic without planned radiotherapy) or for 2 years or until any progression, whichever first (nonmetastatic with planned radiotherapy); radiotherapy at 6–9 months mandatory for node-negative, optional for node-positive nonmetastatic disease Primary: overall survival, failure-free survival (intermediate primary). Secondary: adverse events, symptomatic skeletal events, progression-free survival, prostate cancer-specific survival, quality of life Adding abiraterone and prednisolone to ADT significantly improved overall and failure-free survival vs ADT alone in men with locally advanced or metastatic prostate cancer, with fewer symptomatic skeletal events. At median follow-up 40 months: 184 vs 262 deaths (HR 0.63; 95% CI 0.52–0.76); 3-yr OS 83% vs 76%. Treatment failure 248 vs 535 events (HR 0.29; 95% CI 0.25–0.34); 3-yr FFS 75% vs 45%. 3-yr PFS 80% vs 62% (HR 0.40); symptomatic skeletal events HR 0.46. OS HR 0.61 in metastatic and 0.75 in nonmetastatic disease; nonmetastatic comparisons are immature (78 deaths). Open-label. Grade 3–5 AEs 47% vs 33% (safety population), with 9 vs 3 grade 5 events; grade 3–5 hypertension 5% vs 1% and ALT increase 6% vs <1%.
records.keywords: James et al. N Engl J Med 2017;377:338-351

records.title: TITAN
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2019
records.body: Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma with ≥1 bone-scan lesion, with or without visceral or nodal disease; newly diagnosed or relapsed after localized disease, not receiving ADT at progression; prior docetaxel ≤6 cycles without progression, ADT ≤6 mo for mCSPC or ≤3 yr for localized disease, and localized therapy ≥1 yr before randomization allowed; excluded severe angina, MI, CHF, thromboembolic events, seizure history/predisposition, recent ventricular arrhythmias Apalutamide 240 mg orally once daily + continuous ADT vs matched placebo orally once daily + continuous ADT (double-blind), until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: radiographic progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: time to cytotoxic chemotherapy, time to pain progression, time to chronic opioid use, time to skeletal-related event, time to PSA progression, second progression-free survival, time to symptomatic local progression, undetectable PSA rate, time to castration resistance, FACT-P quality of life, safety Adding apalutamide to ADT significantly lengthened OS and rPFS vs placebo plus ADT; the final analysis confirmed the OS benefit despite crossover. rPFS (final at interim; median follow-up 22.7 mo): 24-mo 68.2% vs 47.5% (HR 0.48; 95% CI 0.39–0.60). Final OS (median follow-up 44.0 mo; 39.5% crossover; no formal inference): median NR vs 52.2 mo; HR 0.65 (95% CI 0.53–0.79); crossover-adjusted HR 0.52. Time to pain progression was not significant at first interim, so further secondary endpoints were not formally tested (final HR 0.87; 95% CI 0.70–1.08). Final nominal HRs: cytotoxic chemotherapy 0.47, PFS2 0.62, castration resistance (ad hoc) 0.34. FACT-P quality of life was maintained, with no substantial between-group difference. Interim safety: grade 3–4 AEs 42.2% vs 40.8%; AEs leading to death 1.9% vs 3.0%; rash 27.1% vs 8.5% (grade ≥3 6.3%); ischemic heart disease 4.4% vs 1.5%, with fatal ischemic events in two patients per group. No treatment-related deaths at final analysis.
records.keywords: Chi et al. N Engl J Med 2019;381:13-24   Chi et al. J Clin Oncol 2021;39:2294-2303  33914595

records.title: ENZAMET
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2019
records.body: Metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostatic adenocarcinoma with metastases on CT and/or technetium-99 bone scan; first-line testosterone suppression initiated up to 12 weeks before randomization, with or without early docetaxel (up to two cycles allowed before randomization); ECOG ≤2; prior adjuvant testosterone suppression for up to 24 months allowed if completed at least 12 months earlier; history of seizure or seizure-predisposing condition excluded Open-label enzalutamide 160 mg orally daily vs standard nonsteroidal antiandrogen (bicalutamide, nilutamide or flutamide), each with continuous testosterone suppression, until clinical progression or prohibitive toxicity; optional early docetaxel 75 mg per square meter every 3 weeks for a maximum of six cycles without prednisone/prednisolone (patient/physician choice; stratified; permitted after the first 88 patients) Primary: overall survival. Secondary: PSA progression-free survival, clinical progression-free survival, adverse events, health-related quality of life, resource use, incremental cost-effectiveness Adding enzalutamide to testosterone suppression gave sustained longer OS, PSA PFS and clinical PFS than a standard nonsteroidal antiandrogen in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, with added toxicity including fatigue and a small seizure risk. At the planned primary analysis (median follow-up 68 mo; 476 deaths): deaths 208 vs 268, HR 0.70 (95% CI 0.58-0.84); 5-yr OS 67% vs 57%; median OS not reached. 5-yr PSA PFS 54% vs 25% (HR 0.44); 5-yr clinical PFS 56% vs 28% (HR 0.45). Interaction tests showed no evidence the effect differed across prespecified subgroups; with planned docetaxel, OS HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.63-1.06); among docetaxel recipients, HR 0.73 in synchronous vs 1.10 in metachronous disease; subgroups small, docetaxel not randomised. Grade 3-4 fatigue 6% vs 1%, hypertension 10% vs 6%; grade 1-3 memory impairment 13% vs 4%; seizures (6 grade 1-2, 1 grade 3) vs none; serious grade 3-4 AEs 47% vs 33%; grade 5 AEs 13 vs 10, none attributed to treatment.
records.keywords: Davis et al. N Engl J Med 2019;381:121-131   Sweeney et al. Lancet Oncol 2023;24:323-334

records.title: ARCHES
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2019
records.body: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma; de novo or recurrent after prior local therapy, metastases on bone scan or CT/MRI; prior ADT and up to six cycles of prior docetaxel permitted; excluded neuroendocrine, signet-cell or small-cell features and disease progression on ADT and/or docetaxel before randomization Enzalutamide 160 mg/day + ADT vs placebo + ADT (double-blind); continued until unacceptable toxicity, radiographic progression confirmed by independent central review, or start of an investigational agent or new prostate cancer therapy; after the primary analysis, unblinded with progression-free placebo patients allowed to cross over to open-label enzalutamide + ADT Primary: radiographic progression-free survival. Secondary: time to PSA progression, time to initiation of new antineoplastic therapy, PSA undetectable rate, objective response rate, time to deterioration in urinary symptoms, overall survival, time to first symptomatic skeletal event, time to castration resistance, patient-reported outcomes, time to deterioration of quality of life, time to pain progression, quality of life over time, safety Enzalutamide + ADT significantly reduced the risk of radiographic progression or death vs placebo + ADT in mHSPC: rPFS HR 0.39 (95% CI 0.30-0.50) at median follow-up 14.4 mo; final investigator-assessed rPFS HR 0.63 (95% CI 0.52-0.76). Final prespecified OS analysis (median follow-up 44.6 mo): OS significantly prolonged despite 180 (31.3%) placebo patients crossing over; 154/574 vs 202/576 deaths; HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.53-0.81); generally consistent across prespecified subgroups except soft-tissue-only disease (n = 96). Time to new antineoplastic therapy HR 0.38. Primary analysis: PSA progression HR 0.19, undetectable PSA 68.1% vs 17.6%, ORR 83.1% vs 63.7%; no significant difference in time to deterioration of urinary symptoms or QoL; pain progression (30% threshold) not delayed. Final analysis: grade 3-4 TEAEs 39.2% vs 27.9%; TEAEs leading to death 5.2% vs 2.1%, none drug-related with enzalutamide; earlier, two grade 5 cardiovascular AEs of special interest with enzalutamide.
records.keywords: Armstrong et al. J Clin Oncol 2019;37:2974-2986   Armstrong et al. J Clin Oncol 2022;40:1616-1622  35420921

records.title: ARANOTE
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2024
records.body: Metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma; ADT started not earlier than 12 weeks before random assignment; metastases centrally confirmed on conventional imaging (nonregional nodes M1a, bone M1b and/or other sites M1c); excluded regional lymph node metastases only (N1, below the aortic bifurcation), baseline superscan, prior androgen receptor pathway inhibitors or chemotherapy, small cell/ductal/neuroendocrine histology, known brain or leptomeningeal metastases Darolutamide 600 mg twice daily + ADT (investigator's choice of LHRH agonist/antagonist or orchiectomy) vs matched placebo + ADT; study drug continued until radiological progression, unacceptable toxicity, new anticancer therapy, patient/physician decision or interruption >28 consecutive days Primary: radiological progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to initiation of subsequent systemic anticancer therapy, time to mCRPC, time to PSA progression, rate of PSA <0.2 ng/mL, time to pain progression, safety Darolutamide plus ADT significantly improved rPFS vs placebo plus ADT in mHSPC, with a favorable safety profile consistent with prior darolutamide phase III trials. rPFS HR 0.54 (95% CI 0.41–0.71; P<.0001); median NR vs 25.0 mo; 24-mo rPFS 70.3% vs 52.1%; benefit consistent across subgroups including high- and low-volume disease. Interim OS was immature and only suggestive of benefit (HR 0.81; 95% CI 0.59–1.12); the trial was not powered for OS, and final OS is planned at approximately 180 events. Time to mCRPC (HR 0.40; 95% CI 0.32–0.51), time to PSA progression (HR 0.31; 95% CI 0.23–0.41) and time to pain progression (HR 0.72; 95% CI 0.54–0.96) were delayed. The placebo plus ADT comparator is no longer standard of care. Grade 3–4 AEs 30.8% vs 30.3%; grade 5 AEs 4.7% vs 5.4%; discontinuation for AEs 6.1% vs 9.0%; fatigue 5.6% vs 8.1%.

records.title: ARASENS
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - triplet therapy (ADT + docetaxel + ARPI) · III · 2022
records.body: Metastatic, hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, histologically or cytologically confirmed, with metastases on bone scan, contrast-enhanced CT or MRI; candidates for ADT and docetaxel; ECOG 0 or 1; excluded: regional lymph-node involvement only (N1, below the aortic bifurcation), ADT >12 weeks before randomization, prior second-generation androgen-receptor pathway inhibitor, chemotherapy or immunotherapy for prostate cancer, or radiotherapy within 2 weeks before randomization Darolutamide 600 mg (two 300-mg tablets) twice daily with food vs matched placebo, both with ADT (LHRH agonist or antagonist, or orchiectomy) plus six cycles of docetaxel 75 mg per square meter on day 1 every 21 days initiated within 6 weeks after randomization; darolutamide/placebo continued until symptomatic disease progression, change in antineoplastic therapy, unacceptable toxic effects, patient or physician decision, death or nonadherence Primary: overall survival. Secondary: time to castration-resistant prostate cancer, time to pain progression, symptomatic skeletal event-free survival, time to a first symptomatic skeletal event, time to initiation of subsequent systemic antineoplastic therapy, time to worsening of disease-related physical symptoms, time to initiation of opioid treatment for 7 or more consecutive days, safety Adding darolutamide to ADT and docetaxel significantly prolonged overall survival in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer and improved key secondary end points, with similar adverse-event frequency. At the primary analysis (533 deaths), OS HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.57–0.80; P<0.001); 4-year OS 62.7% vs 50.4%. Benefit persisted despite subsequent life-prolonging therapy in 75.6% of placebo patients entering follow-up. The first five hierarchically tested secondary end points were significant (time to CRPC HR 0.36), but time to worsening of disease-related physical symptoms was not (HR 1.04; 95% CI 0.89–1.22), so later analyses were exploratory. 86.1% had metastatic disease at initial diagnosis, limiting data for recurrent or node-only disease; only ECOG 0 or 1 patients were included. Grade 3/4 AEs 66.1% vs 63.5% (neutropenia 33.7% vs 34.2%; hypertension 6.4% vs 3.2%); deaths due to AEs 4.1% vs 4.0%.
records.keywords: Smith et al. N Engl J Med 2022;386:1132-1142

records.title: PEACE-1
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - triplet therapy (ADT + docetaxel + ARPI) · III · 2022
records.body: Histologically or cytologically confirmed prostate adenocarcinoma; de novo metastatic castration-sensitive disease documented by bone scan, CT or MRI; ECOG 0–1 (or 2 due to bone pain), ADT for no more than 3 months before randomisation, at least 6 weeks from ADT initiation to first docetaxel dose, docetaxel mandatory in SOC from the Aug 10, 2017 amendment; excluded pure small-cell carcinoma or previous prostate cancer treated by definitive local treatment SOC (continuous ADT alone or with docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV every 3 weeks for six cycles) vs SOC + radiotherapy (74 Gy in 37 fractions over 7–8 weeks) vs SOC + abiraterone 1000 mg orally once daily plus prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily until progression to castration resistance, withdrawal of consent, unacceptable toxicity or death vs SOC + radiotherapy + abiraterone Primary: radiographic progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: CRPC-free survival, serious genitourinary event-free survival, prostate-cancer-specific survival, time to next skeletal-related event, PSA response rate, prognostic study of serum PSA measured 6–8 months after initiation of systemic therapy, time to pain progression, time to chemotherapy for CRPC, quality of life, changes in bone mineral density, correlation of biomarkers with outcome, event rate per 100 person-years of treatment, toxicity Adding abiraterone to ADT plus docetaxel in de novo mCSPC improved rPFS and OS, with a modest toxicity increase, mostly hypertension. ADT+docetaxel population (355 vs 355): median rPFS 4.46 vs 2.03 yr, HR 0.50 (99.9% CI 0.34–0.71); median OS not reached vs 4.43 yr, HR 0.75 (95.1% CI 0.59–0.95). Overall population (583 vs 589): rPFS HR 0.54 (99.9% CI 0.41–0.71); OS HR 0.82 (95.1% CI 0.69–0.98). In the high-volume subgroup, OS HR 0.72 (95.1% CI 0.55–0.95); low-volume OS data immature (HR 0.83, 95.1% CI 0.50–1.39). Open-label; radiotherapy efficacy not yet analysed; triplet not compared with ADT plus abiraterone. Grade 3 or worse AEs 63% vs 52%; hypertension 22% vs 13%, hepatotoxicity 6% vs 1%, fatal AEs 2% vs 1%; neutropenia and febrile neutropenia not increased.

records.title: AMPLITUDE
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - PARP inhibitor + ARPI (HRR/BRCA-altered) · III · 2025
records.body: Metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer, metastases on conventional imaging; at least one deleterious HRR alteration (BRCA1, BRCA2, BRIP1, PALB2, RAD51B, RAD54L, CDK12, CHEK2 or FANCA) on central tissue, plasma or germline testing or approved local test; ADT started at least 14 days and no longer than 6 months before randomization; prior docetaxel (up to six cycles, completed within 3 months of randomization) and up to 45 days of abiraterone plus prednisone allowed Niraparib 200 mg plus abiraterone acetate 1,000 mg (dual-action tablet) plus prednisone 5 mg orally once daily vs matched placebo plus abiraterone acetate plus prednisone, continuously in 28-day cycles until progression; ADT continued in both arms Primary: radiographic progression-free survival. Secondary: time to symptomatic progression, overall survival, time to subsequent therapy, safety, second progression-free survival, objective response rate, duration of response, time to PSA progression, PSA response rate, quality of life (FACT-P) Adding niraparib to abiraterone plus prednisone significantly prolonged investigator-assessed rPFS in HRR-altered mCSPC, meeting the primary endpoint in all three hierarchically tested populations. rPFS HR 0.52 (95% CI 0.37–0.72) in the BRCA subgroup (median not reached vs 26.0 mo), 0.57 (0.42–0.77) in the HRR effector subgroup and 0.63 (0.49–0.80) in ITT (not reached vs 29.5 mo); median follow-up 30.8 mo. Time to symptomatic progression improved (ITT HR 0.50, 0.36–0.69). OS was immature at the first interim analysis (193/389 events): BRCA HR 0.75 (0.51–1.11), not significant; ITT HR 0.79 (0.59–1.04). In a post hoc analysis of non-BRCA HRR alterations, rPFS HR was 0.81 (0.56–1.18). Grade 3–4 AEs 75.2% vs 58.9%; grade 3–4 anemia 29.1% vs 4.6% (25.1% transfused) and hypertension 26.5% vs 18.4%; TEAE deaths 14 vs 7; one MDS case. FACT-P scores declined at cycles 2–4 with niraparib, with no difference from cycle 5.

records.title: TALAPRO-3
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - PARP inhibitor + ARPI (HRR/BRCA-altered) · III · 2026
records.body: Histologically or cytologically confirmed metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma; metastatic androgen pathway modulation-sensitive (castration-sensitive) disease, up to 3 months of prior ADT ± approved ARPI allowed; alteration in one or more HRR genes (12-gene panel) in blood, tumour or both; ongoing GnRH agonist/antagonist ADT unless bilateral orchiectomy; prior docetaxel excluded after September 2021 protocol amendment Talazoparib 0.5 mg (0.35 mg with moderate renal impairment) + enzalutamide 160 mg, both orally once daily vs placebo + enzalutamide 160 mg orally once daily (double-blind), with ongoing ADT; until investigator-assessed imaging-based progression (continuation allowed if benefit still derived), unacceptable toxicity or AE leading to permanent discontinuation, patient decision or death Primary: imaging-based progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, duration of response, PSA decrease of at least 50%, time to PSA progression, time to initiation of antineoplastic therapy, safety, patient-reported outcomes, time to disease progression during subsequent anticancer systemic therapy Adding talazoparib to enzalutamide significantly improved imaging-based PFS vs placebo plus enzalutamide in HRR-altered metastatic APMS prostate cancer, but serious adverse events were more common. 3-yr imaging-based PFS was 77% vs 56% (HR 0.48; 95% CI 0.36-0.65; P<0.001), with median follow-up 37.6 vs 37.7 mo. In subgroups not adjusted for multiplicity, the HR was 0.37 (95% CI 0.22-0.61) with BRCA alterations and 0.57 (95% CI 0.39-0.82) without. Overall survival at this interim analysis did not cross the efficacy boundary: 3-yr OS 78% vs 72% (HR 0.77; 95% CI 0.56-1.04); follow-up continues. Grade ≥3 AEs occurred in 81% vs 44% and serious AEs in 42% vs 32%. Grade ≥3 anemia occurred in 51% with talazoparib, and red-cell transfusions were given to 40% vs 2%. Myelodysplastic syndrome occurred in three vs one patient and AML in two vs none. There were two treatment-related deaths with talazoparib (pancytopenia, worsening idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis).
records.keywords: Agarwal et al. N Engl J Med 2026 (online ahead of print)

records.title: CAPItello-281
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - PIK3CA · III · 2026
records.body: PTEN-deficient metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer; PTEN selection used SP218 IHC by qualified pathologist: at least 90% of viable malignant cells with no specific cytoplasmic PTEN staining (no more than 10% with staining). Full criteria are in unfiled Supplementary Table S1 and are not inferred. Capivasertib 400 mg twice daily four days on/three days off plus abiraterone 1000 mg daily, prednisone/prednisolone, and ADT vs Matched placebo plus abiraterone 1000 mg daily, prednisone/prednisolone, and ADT Primary: Radiographic progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Time to first subsequent therapy, Symptomatic skeletal event-free survival, Time to pain progression, Time to PSA progression, Time to castration resistance, Safety In PTEN-deficient mCSPC (25.3% of tested patients), adding capivasertib to abiraterone improved rPFS (33.2 vs 25.7 months, HR 0.81); OS was immature (HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.71-1.15). Common adverse events with capivasertib were diarrhoea (51.9%), hyperglycaemia (38.0%) and rash (35.4%). Diabetic ketoacidosis occurred only with capivasertib; discontinuations and deaths attributed to adverse events were also more frequent descriptively.

records.title: PSMAddition
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - radioligand therapy (PSMA) · III · 2026
records.body: Men with PSMA-positive metastatic castration-sensitive prostate adenocarcinoma and at least one distant soft-tissue, visceral or bone metastasis on CT, MRI or ⁹⁹mTc bone scintigraphy. Central [⁶⁸Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 PET required at least one distant lesion with uptake greater than liver, including a PSMA-positive liver lesion when liver metastases were present. [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 7.4 GBq intravenously every 6 weeks for up to six cycles plus ADT and investigator-chosen ARPI vs ADT plus investigator-chosen ARPI; crossover to [¹⁷⁷Lu]Lu-PSMA-617 permitted after BIRC-confirmed radiographic progression Primary: Radiographic progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, PSA response, Time to PSA progression, Time to metastatic androgen pathway modulator-resistant prostate cancer, Progression-free survival, Second progression-free survival, Objective response rate, Disease control rate, Time to response, Duration of response, Time to soft-tissue progression, Safety and tolerability, Time to first symptomatic skeletal event, Quality of life, Pain Adding ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 to ADT plus ARPI improved rPFS (HR 0.72; medians not reached). At the first interim analysis, OS did not differ between groups (HR 0.84); it remained too immature for subgroup interpretation, and crossover after centrally confirmed progression may affect later survival results. Grade 3 or worse and cytopenia adverse events were more frequent with radioligand therapy; fatal events were 3% vs 2%, with none treatment-related.

records.title: STAMPEDE (prostate RT)
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CSPC - radiotherapy to the primary tumour · III · 2018
records.body: Newly diagnosed metastatic castration-sensitive prostate cancer; Newly diagnosed prostate cancer with metastatic disease confirmed by bone scintigraphy and soft-tissue imaging performed within 12 weeks of starting androgen-deprivation therapy; no previous radical treatment; intended for long-term ADT, started no earlier than 12 weeks before randomisation. There were no age restrictions; patients needed no contraindication to radiotherapy and no clinically significant cardiovascular history. Standard of care: lifelong ADT; docetaxel permitted after Dec 17, 2015 vs Standard of care plus prostate radiotherapy: 55 Gy in 20 daily fractions over 4 weeks or 36 Gy in 6 weekly fractions over 6 weeks, nominated before randomisation Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Failure-free survival, Progression-free survival, Metastatic progression-free survival, Prostate-cancer-specific survival, Symptomatic local event-free survival, Adverse effects, Treatment after failure-free survival Prostate RT did not improve OS overall but improved 3-yr OS in low-metastatic-burden disease (81% vs 73%, HR 0.68); Safety: Acute grade 3–4 RTOG bladder and bowel toxicity during prostate radiotherapy was uncommon; no grade 5 acute event was reported.

records.title: EMBARK
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M0 CSPC- high-risk biochemical recurrence · III · 2023
records.body: High-risk biochemical recurrence after prostatectomy and/or radiotherapy, with PSA doubling time no more than 9 months, PSA at least 1 ng/mL after prostatectomy or 2 ng/mL above nadir after radiotherapy, and no metastases on conventional imaging. Enzalutamide 160 mg once daily plus leuprolide, leuprolide alone, or enzalutamide monotherapy; 36 weeks of treatment followed by protocol-specified PSA-guided suspension and restart. Primary: Metastasis-free survival for enzalutamide plus leuprolide vs leuprolide. Secondary: Metastasis-free survival for enzalutamide monotherapy vs leuprolide, PSA progression, First use of new antineoplastic therapy, Overall survival, Progression-free survival with the first subsequent therapy Enzalutamide plus leuprolide improved metastasis-free survival versus leuprolide alone (5-year 87.3% vs 71.4%, HR 0.42) and improved final OS (8-year 78.9% vs 69.5%, HR 0.60). Enzalutamide monotherapy improved metastasis-free survival (5-year 80.0%, HR 0.63) but did not improve OS (8-year 73.1% vs 69.5%, HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.63–1.10); the two enzalutamide arms were not formally compared. Grade 3 or higher adverse events were 52.4%, 49.4% and 57.3%; fractures 22.4%, 15.0% and 14.1% for combination, leuprolide and monotherapy.

records.title: SPARTAN
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M0 CRPC · III · 2018
records.body: High-risk nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer on ongoing ADT, with no metastases on conventional imaging, PSA at least 2 ng/mL and PSA doubling time no more than 10 months. ECOG performance status 0–1 was required; prior cytotoxic chemotherapy and treatments affecting androgen signalling were excluded under protocol timing rules. Ongoing androgen deprivation therapy + apalutamide 240 mg/day vs Ongoing androgen deprivation therapy + placebo Primary: Metastasis-free survival. Secondary: Time to metastasis, Progression-free survival, Time to symptomatic progression, Overall survival, Time to initiation of cytotoxic chemotherapy Apalutamide improved metastasis-free survival (40.5 vs 16.2 months, HR 0.28). OS was immature in 2018 but improved at the event-driven final analysis (73.9 vs 59.9 months, HR 0.78), with 76 crossover patients retained in the placebo ITT group. Safety: grade 3–4 adverse events occurred in 56% vs 36% during blinded treatment and serious events in 36% vs 25%; the crossover group was reported separately.

records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M0 CRPC · III · 2018
records.body: Nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer; Nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate adenocarcinoma on conventional CT/MRI and bone scan, rising PSA despite ongoing ADT, baseline PSA at least 2 ng/mL and PSA doubling time no more than 10 months; prior cytotoxic chemotherapy, investigational therapy and enzalutamide were excluded. OS was immature in 2018 but improved at the prespecified analysis that became final (67.0 vs 56.3 months, HR 0.73). Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 48% vs 27%, although exposure-adjusted rates were 17 vs 20 events per 100 patient-years.

records.title: ARAMIS
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M0 CRPC · III · 2019
records.body: Nonmetastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer; previous seizure disorder or a condition predisposing to seizure was permitted. Continuing androgen-deprivation therapy + darolutamide 600 mg orally twice daily with food vs Continuing androgen-deprivation therapy + matched placebo; all 170 patients still receiving placebo at unblinding crossed over to open-label darolutamide; continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, or protocol discontinuation Primary: Metastasis-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Time to pain progression, Time to first use of cytotoxic chemotherapy, Time to first symptomatic skeletal event Darolutamide improved metastasis-free survival (40.4 vs 18.4 months, HR 0.41). records.title: TAX327
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - taxane chemotherapy · III · 2004
records.body: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate adenocarcinoma progressing during hormonal therapy with ongoing androgen-ablation maintenance; Karnofsky score at least 60% and stable baseline pain. Prior cytotoxic therapy other than estramustine and prior radioisotopes were excluded; adequate cardiac, marrow, hepatic and renal function was required. Docetaxel 75 mg/m² IV day 1 every 21 days + prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily; up to 10 cycles vs Docetaxel 30 mg/m² IV days 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 every 6 weeks + prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily; up to 5 cycles vs Mitoxantrone 12 mg/m² IV day 1 every 21 days + prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily; up to 10 cycles Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: pain response, quality-of-life response, PSA response, Objective tumour response, Adverse events Every-3-week docetaxel improved median OS (18.9 vs 16.5 months, HR 0.76) with better pain and PSA response; Safety: Three-weekly docetaxel caused more grade 3–4 neutropenia than weekly docetaxel or mitoxantrone; febrile neutropenia was uncommon.

records.title: TROPIC
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - taxane chemotherapy · III · 2010
records.body: Post-docetaxel metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer; mCRPC progressing during or after docetaxel, with ongoing castration and no prior mitoxantrone; measurable disease required RECIST progression, otherwise rising PSA or a new radiographic lesion; major marrow irradiation, active neuropathy or serious uncontrolled illness were excluded. Cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² IV over 1 h day 1 every 21 days + prednisone 10 mg orally daily; maximum 10 cycles; 1 permitted reduction to 20 mg/m² vs Mitoxantrone 12 mg/m² IV over 15–30 min day 1 every 21 days + prednisone 10 mg orally daily; maximum 10 cycles; 1 permitted reduction to 10 mg/m² Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Composite progression-free survival, PSA response and progression, Objective tumour response, Pain response and progression, Time to tumour progression, Safety Cabazitaxel improved median OS post-docetaxel (15.1 vs 12.7 months, HR 0.70); Safety: Cabazitaxel caused substantial grade ≥3 neutropenia, leukopenia and febrile neutropenia versus mitoxantrone.

records.title: CARD
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - taxane chemotherapy · III · 2019
records.body: Post-docetaxel metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer; prior ARPI could precede or follow docetaxel, including use in hormone-sensitive disease. Prior abiraterone or docetaxel for metastatic hormone-sensitive disease was permitted. Cabazitaxel 25 mg/m² IV over 1 hour every 3 weeks plus prednisone 10 mg orally daily; primary G-CSF prophylaxis at every cabazitaxel cycle vs After prior enzalutamide: abiraterone 1000 mg orally daily plus prednisone 5 mg twice daily; after prior abiraterone: enzalutamide 160 mg orally daily. Primary: Imaging-based progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Progression-free survival, PSA response, Tumour response, Pain response, Time to first symptomatic skeletal event, Safety Cabazitaxel beat switching ARPI for rPFS (8.0 vs 3.7 months, HR 0.54) and OS (13.6 vs 11.0 months, HR 0.64); favored chemotherapy over a second ARPI. Safety: Grade ≥3 AEs: 56.3% vs 52.4%; AEs leading to death: 5.6% vs 11.3%.

records.title: COU-AA-301
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2011
records.body: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing after one or two chemotherapy regimens, including docetaxel, with ongoing androgen deprivation and ECOG 0–2. Prior ketoconazole was excluded; adequate hepatic function and controlled cardiovascular status were required. Abiraterone acetate 1000 mg orally once daily fasting (four 250-mg tablets, ≥1 hour before or ≥2 hours after meal) plus prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily; 28-day cycles vs Four placebo tablets orally once daily fasting plus prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily; 28-day cycles. Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: PSA response rate, Time to PSA progression, Radiographic progression-free survival Abiraterone improved median OS after docetaxel (14.8 vs 10.9 months, HR 0.65). Fluid retention or oedema occurred in 31% vs 22% (grade 3–4 about 2% vs 1%), hypokalaemia in 17% vs 8% (grade 3–4 about 4% vs 1%), and hypertension in 10% vs 8%. Fatal adverse-event incidence and crossover were not reported in the filed interim publication.

records.title: AFFIRM
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2012
records.body: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing after one or two chemotherapy regimens, including at least one docetaxel-containing regimen, with testosterone at castrate levels and ECOG performance status 0–2. Patients with a history of seizure, seizure predisposition or clinically significant cardiovascular disease were excluded. Enzalutamide 160 mg orally once daily as four 40-mg capsules; administered without regard to food; prednisone or other glucocorticoids permitted but not required vs Matched placebo capsules; prednisone or other glucocorticoids permitted but not required; continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, or protocol discontinuation Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: PSA response, Objective soft-tissue response, Quality-of-life response, Time to PSA progression, Radiographic progression-free survival, Time to first skeletal-related event Enzalutamide improved median OS after docetaxel (18.4 vs 13.6 months, HR 0.63), with improvements in radiographic PFS and PSA, soft-tissue and quality-of-life responses. Safety: grade 3 or higher adverse events 45% vs 53%, serious events 34% vs 39%, and fatal events 3% vs 4%. Seizures occurred in 5/800 (0.6%; all grade 3 or higher) vs none.

records.title: COU-AA-302
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2013
records.body: Chemotherapy-naive, asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic metastatic castration-resistant prostate adenocarcinoma progressing on ongoing ADT, without visceral metastases. Previous ketoconazole exposure exceeding 7 days was excluded. Abiraterone acetate 1000 mg orally once daily (four 250-mg tablets) + prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily vs Matched placebo four tablets orally once daily + prednisone 5 mg orally twice daily; continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, or protocol discontinuation Primary: Radiographic progression-free survival, Overall survival. Secondary: Time to opiate use for cancer-related pain Abiraterone improved rPFS (16.5 vs 8.3 months, HR 0.53); coprimary OS was not established at the initial analysis but improved at the prespecified final analysis (34.7 vs 30.3 months, HR 0.81). Of placebo patients, 238 (44%) received abiraterone; crossover-adjusted OS was exploratory (HR 0.74). Safety: grade 3–4 adverse events occurred in 54% vs 44%, serious events in 38% vs 27%, and discontinuation for adverse events in 13% vs 10%.

records.title: PREVAIL
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - androgen-receptor pathway inhibitors · III · 2014
records.body: Chemotherapy-naive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer; Visceral (lung/liver) disease and NYHA I–II heart failure were allowed. Prior antiandrogens and concurrent glucocorticoids were allowed but not required. Excluded history of seizure or a seizure-predisposing condition; medications lowering seizure threshold allowed. records.title: PROfound
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - PARP inhibitors (HRR / BRCA alterations) · III · 2020
records.body: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing during enzalutamide, abiraterone or both, with prior taxane permitted. Central FoundationOne CDx tumour testing required a deleterious or suspected deleterious alteration in at least one of 15 prespecified HRR genes; cohort A comprised BRCA1, BRCA2 or ATM. Olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily vs Physician's choice enzalutamide 160 mg daily or abiraterone 1000 mg daily plus prednisone 5 mg twice daily; continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, or protocol discontinuation Primary: Imaging-based progression-free survival. Cohort B, overall-population and gene-level OS results were exploratory; 66% of controls crossed to olaparib. Safety: grade 3 or higher adverse events 52% vs 40%; anaemia 50% (grade 3 or higher 23%) vs 15% (5%); fatal adverse events 4% vs 5%.

records.title: TRITON3
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - PARP inhibitors (HRR / BRCA alterations) · III · 2023
records.body: BRCA1/2- or ATM-altered metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer progressing after one ARPI, with no chemotherapy for mCRPC. Prior taxane for hormone-sensitive disease was permitted. Secondary: Overall survival, Objective response, PSA response, Safety In BRCA-altered disease rucaparib improved rPFS (11.2 vs 6.4 months, HR 0.50); the ATM estimate was inconclusive (8.1 vs 6.8 months, HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.59–1.52). Interim BRCA-subgroup OS did not reach statistical significance (24.3 vs 20.8 months, HR 0.81), leaving later hierarchical endpoints exploratory at this cut. Physician's-choice controls mixed docetaxel and a second ARPI. Grade 3 or higher adverse events were 60% vs 53%; fatal adverse events were 2% vs 2%.

records.title: PROpel
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - PARP inhibitors (HRR / BRCA alterations) · III · 2022
records.body: First-line metastatic castration-resistant prostate adenocarcinoma with no previous systemic therapy for CRPC other than ADT or first-generation antiandrogens. Remote neoadjuvant/adjuvant or mHSPC docetaxel and selected remote non-abiraterone ARPI exposure were permitted without progression. Olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily approximately 12 hours apart + abiraterone acetate 1000 mg orally once daily fasting + prednisone/prednisolone 5 mg twice daily vs Matched placebo orally twice daily + abiraterone acetate 1000 mg orally once daily fasting + prednisone/prednisolone 5 mg twice daily; crossover to olaparib was not allowed; continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, or protocol discontinuation Primary: Radiographic progression-free survival. Final OS did not meet its prespecified criterion (42.1 vs 34.7 months, HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.67–1.00). The apparent BRCA benefit was post-hoc exploratory; the primary publication reported BRCA prevalence but no BRCA efficacy result. Safety: grade 3, 4 and 5 adverse events occurred in 41%, 8% and 7% vs 34%, 4% and 5%.

records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - PARP inhibitors (HRR / BRCA alterations) · III · 2023
records.body: Initial-treatment metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with asymptomatic or mildly symptomatic progressive disease on ongoing ADT and no previous life-prolonging systemic therapy for CRPC other than ADT or first-generation antiandrogens. records.title: MAGNITUDE
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - PARP inhibitors (HRR / BRCA alterations) · III · 2023
records.body: First-line metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer prospectively assigned as HRR-positive or HRR-negative, with no prior PARP inhibitor or systemic mCRPC therapy. HRR-positive disease required a pathogenic alteration in a prespecified HRR gene; prior mCSPC or nmCRPC therapy and limited abiraterone bridging were allowed. Niraparib 200 mg daily + abiraterone 1000 mg daily + prednisone 5 mg twice daily vs Placebo + abiraterone 1000 mg daily + prednisone 5 mg twice daily; continued until progression, unacceptable toxicity, withdrawal, or protocol discontinuation Primary: Radiographic progression-free survival. Secondary: Time to cytotoxic chemotherapy, Time to symptomatic progression, Overall survival, Safety Niraparib plus abiraterone improved rPFS in BRCA1/2-altered disease (16.6 vs 10.9 months, HR 0.53) and the overall HRR-positive population (16.5 vs 13.7 months, HR 0.73); benefit was not proven to differ between biomarker subsets, and non-BRCA gene-level estimates were limited. The HRR-negative cohort stopped for futility. Grade 3 or higher adverse events were 67.0% vs 46.4%; grade 3–4 anaemia 29.7% vs 7.6%; serious adverse events 35.8% vs 24.6%.

records.title: ALSYMPCA
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - radioligand therapy · III · 2013
records.body: Symptomatic metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with at least two bone metastases and no known visceral metastases, receiving best standard care. Previous docetaxel was required unless ineligible, unavailable or declined; recent chemotherapy, radiotherapy/radioisotope, bulky nodes and cord compression were excluded. Radium-223 50 kBq/kg IV every 4 weeks ×6 plus best standard care vs Matching placebo every 4 weeks ×6 plus best standard care Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Time to first symptomatic skeletal event, ALP response/progression, PSA progression, Safety Radium-223 improved overall survival (14.9 versus 11.3 months; HR 0.70) and delayed symptomatic skeletal events in symptomatic bone-predominant mCRPC. Grade 3–4 anaemia and thrombocytopenia were uncommon but occurred, with one possibly treatment-related fatal thrombocytopenia; no visceral disease was permitted.

records.title: VISION
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - radioligand therapy · III · 2021
records.body: PSMA-positive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after ARPI and taxane; centrally read 68Ga-PSMA-11 PET/CT required ≥1 PSMA-positive lesion (uptake greater than liver) and no exclusionary PSMA-negative lesion (uptake ≤ liver in node ≥2.5 cm, solid-organ lesion ≥1.0 cm, or bone lesion soft-tissue component ≥1.0 cm). ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 7.4 GBq IV every 6 weeks for 4–6 cycles plus protocol-permitted standard care vs protocol-permitted standard care alone; standard care continued per protocol. Primary: Imaging-based progression-free survival, Overall survival. Secondary: Objective response and disease control, Time to first symptomatic skeletal event, Safety, Health-related quality of life, pain and PSA biomarker outcomes ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 improved OS (15.3 vs 11.3 months, HR 0.62) and rPFS (8.7 vs 3.4 months, HR 0.40); Safety: Grade ≥3 adverse events 279/529 (52.7%) vs 78/205 (38.0%); fatal adverse events 19/529 (3.6%) vs 6/205 (2.9%).

records.title: PSMAfore
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - radioligand therapy · III · 2024
records.body: PSMA-positive taxane-naive metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer after ARPI; treating physician had to judge the patient a candidate for ARPI change. PSMA PET required ≥1 lesion with uptake greater than liver and no PSMA-negative node ≥25 mm short axis, bone soft-tissue component ≥10 mm longest diameter, solid-organ lesion ≥10 mm longest diameter, or intraprostatic lesion. ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 7.4 GBq IV every 6 weeks for six cycles vs abiraterone or enzalutamide; treatment continued until progression, toxicity, withdrawal, or protocol discontinuation. Primary: Radiographic progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Progression-free survival, PSA response, Time to symptomatic skeletal event, Second progression-free survival, Health-related quality of life and pain, Safety and tolerability At the updated analysis, ¹⁷⁷Lu-PSMA-617 improved radiographic PFS versus ARPI change (11.6 vs 5.6 months; HR 0.49). Third-interim OS was similar (HR 0.98) and may be confounded by 57% crossover. Grade 3 or higher events occurred in 36% vs 48%; grade 5 events were 2% in both groups, with no treatment-related death in the radioligand arm. Results do not compare against taxane or establish reverse sequencing.

records.title: IMPACT
records.subtitle: Advanced Prostate · M1 CRPC - immunotherapy · III · 2010
records.body: Asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer with PSA at least 5 ng/mL, expected survival at least 6 months and no visceral metastases, cord compression or pathologic long-bone fracture. Eligibility was amended from Gleason score 7 or lower to any Gleason score. Sipuleucel-T or placebo as three infusions approximately 2 weeks apart over 4 weeks. Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Time to objective disease progression, Safety Sipuleucel-T improved median overall survival (25.8 versus 21.7 months; HR 0.78) without improving PSA or radiographic progression endpoints. Infusion-related reactions were more frequent, including grade 3 or higher events within one day (6.8% versus 1.8%); applicability is limited to asymptomatic or minimally symptomatic mCRPC without visceral disease.

records.title: ASSURE (ECOG-ACRIN E2805)
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · III · 2016
records.body: Resected high-risk locoregional clear-cell or non-clear-cell RCC Adjuvant sunitinib vs sorafenib vs placebo (1 year) Disease-free survival Neither sunitinib nor sorafenib improved median DFS vs placebo (5.8 and 6.1 vs 6.6 years; HR 1.02 and 0.97) and both added substantial toxicity; a definitively negative trial that argued against adjuvant VEGFR-TKI therapy.

records.title: S-TRAC
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · III · 2016
records.body: Resected high-risk locoregional clear-cell RCC (UISS high risk) Adjuvant sunitinib vs placebo (1 year) Disease-free survival Sunitinib prolonged median DFS (6.8 vs 5.6 years, HR 0.76); the first adjuvant trial positive for DFS and the basis for FDA approval, though no OS benefit and notable toxicity limited uptake.

records.title: KEYNOTE-564
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · III · 2021
records.body: Adults ≥18 with intermediate-high/high-risk or M1 NED clear-cell RCC after nephrectomy, or nephrectomy plus metastasectomy; surgery ≤12 weeks before randomization; no prior systemic therapy for RCC Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W for up to 17 cycles (~1 year) vs placebo Primary: disease-free survival per investigator assessment. Secondary: overall survival, safety; post-hoc exploratory: distant metastasis-free survival, time to recurrence Adjuvant pembrolizumab sustained DFS and OS benefit versus placebo at a median 69.5 months from randomization (fourth interim analysis, cutoff September 25, 2024). DFS HR 0.71 (95% CI 0.59–0.86); median DFS NR vs 68.3 months; 5-year DFS 60.9% vs 52.2%. OS HR 0.66 (95% CI 0.48–0.90); median OS NR both arms; 5-year OS 87.7% vs 82.3%. Benefit consistent across key subgroups; no formal statistical testing at this analysis since prior endpoints met significance. Safety unchanged since prior analyses; most common grade ≥3 AEs with pembrolizumab were hypertension (2.9%), increased ALT (2.3%), diarrhea (1.8%)

records.title: IMmotion010
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · III · 2022
records.body: Resected high-risk clear-cell / sarcomatoid RCC Adjuvant atezolizumab vs placebo (1 year) Disease-free survival Atezolizumab did not improve median DFS (57.2 vs 49.5 months, HR 0.93); a negative adjuvant PD-L1 trial.

records.title: CheckMate 914 (Part A)
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · III · 2023
records.body: Predominantly clear-cell RCC at high risk of relapse after partial or radical nephrectomy, negative margins and no macroscopic residual or distant disease; pT2a grade 3–4, pT2b or pT3–4 N0M0, or any pT N1M0; randomised >4 to ≤12 weeks post-surgery; no prior systemic RCC therapy or active autoimmune disease/immunosuppression Nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks ×12 + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 6 weeks ×4 vs matching placebos; stop at completion, week 36 for delays, recurrence, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; safety and tolerability Adjuvant nivolumab plus ipilimumab did not improve BICR DFS: median not reached vs 50.7 mo; HR 0.92 (95% CI 0.71–1.19). OS was immature and not formally tested after negative DFS. Treatment-related grade 3–4 AEs occurred in 28% vs 2%, treatment-related discontinuation in 29% vs 1%, and 4 treatment-attributed deaths vs none

records.title: PROSPER (ECOG-ACRIN EA8143)
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated RCC of any histology planned for radical or partial nephrectomy: clinical ≥T2 or any T node-positive and initially nonmetastatic; amendment permitted ≤3 oligometastases outside brain, bone or liver if resectable to no evidence of disease within 12 weeks; ECOG 0–1; no prior therapy for current RCC, autoimmune disease or active hepatitis B/C Nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks ×2, 1–4 weeks before nephrectomy → 240 mg IV every 2 weeks for 9 months from 4–10 weeks postoperatively (amendment 4: one 480 mg IV preoperative dose → up to 9 adjuvant 480 mg IV doses every 4 weeks) vs surgery alone; omissions permitted, no reductions Primary: Recurrence-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; recurrence-free survival in clear-cell RCC; safety and tolerability; quality of life; correlative PD-L1 analysis Perioperative nivolumab did not improve RFS and the trial stopped for futility: HR 0.95 (95% CI 0.74–1.22; one-sided P=.34). Reported 5-year OS was post hoc and immature (HR 1.28, 95% CI 0.84–1.95). At least 9 cycles were completed by 55%; treatment-related grade 3–5 elevated lipase occurred in 5% vs 0.3%, and treatment-related deaths in 2% vs 1%

records.title: RAMPART (Arm C)
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · III · 2025
records.body: Resected intermediate/high-risk clear-cell or non-clear-cell RCC (Leibovich 3-11) Adjuvant durvalumab + tremelimumab vs active monitoring Disease-free survival Durvalumab plus tremelimumab improved 2-yr DFS (84% vs 78%, HR 0.65; high-risk subgroup HR 0.52) but with grade ≥3 toxicity in 40%; a second positive adjuvant immunotherapy signal (durvalumab-monotherapy arm pending).

records.title: LITESPARK-022
records.subtitle: RCC · Adjuvant therapy — resected localized / locoregional RCC · III · 2026
records.body: Resected clear-cell RCC at protocol-defined intermediate-to-high/high recurrence risk or M1 NED after nephrectomy and complete metastasectomy; last surgery ≤12 weeks. Microscopic positive soft-tissue or vascular margins without gross residual disease were allowed Pembrolizumab 400 mg IV every 6 weeks for ≤9 doses plus belzutifan 120 mg orally once daily vs the same pembrolizumab schedule plus oral placebo daily; belzutifan/placebo concurrent with pembrolizumab, or continued for ≤54 weeks if pembrolizumab stopped Primary: Disease-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, safety At the first interim analysis, pembrolizumab-belzutifan improved primary investigator-assessed DFS (HR 0.72, 95% CI 0.59-0.87; P<0.001; 24-month DFS 80.7% vs 73.7%). OS was immature and not significant at the first interim analysis (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.51-1.19; P=0.24; 87 deaths, 29% of planned final deaths). Among treated participants (n=915 vs 913), grade ≥3 any-cause AEs were 52.1% vs 30.2%; serious AEs 29.5% vs 19.9%; any-grade/grade ≥3 anemia was 84.0%/12.1% vs 11.4%/0.4%, and any-grade/grade ≥3 hypoxia was 7.0%/4.6% vs 0.1%/0%.

records.title: Motzer (sunitinib vs IFN)
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — VEGF-targeted therapy (historical standards) · III · 2007
records.body: Adults with previously untreated metastatic RCC containing a clear-cell component; ECOG 0–1; excluded brain metastases, uncontrolled hypertension, or clinically significant cardiovascular disease/events in the preceding 12 months Sunitinib 50 mg orally daily, 4 weeks on/2 weeks off in 6-week cycles vs interferon alfa-2a subcutaneously on nonconsecutive days 3 times weekly (3 MU week 1, 6 MU week 2, then 9 MU); until progression, unacceptable toxicity or withdrawal Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Objective response rate; overall survival; quality of life; safety In the 2007 primary report, sunitinib improved independent central-review PFS vs interferon alfa (11 vs 5 mo; HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.32–0.54) and central-review ORR (31% [103/335] vs 6% [20/327]). At this interim cut, OS was not reached; HR for death was 0.65 (95% CI 0.45–0.94; P=.02) but did not meet the prespecified interim level. Among treated patients (375 vs 360), treatment-related grade 3 hypertension (8% vs 1%) and hand-foot syndrome (5% vs 0%) were more frequent with sunitinib; grade 3 thrombocytopenia was 8% vs 0%, and dose interruption/reduction occurred in 38%/32% vs 32%/21%

records.title: AVOREN
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — VEGF-targeted therapy (historical standards) · III · 2007
records.body: Untreated metastatic clear-cell RCC Bevacizumab + interferon alfa-2a vs placebo + interferon Overall survival (PFS co-reported) Adding bevacizumab to interferon improved median PFS (10.2 vs 5.4 months, HR 0.63); validated VEGF-ligand blockade, though the OS gain was not statistically significant.

records.title: COMPARZ
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — VEGF-targeted therapy (historical standards) · III · 2013
records.body: Adults (≥18) with advanced or metastatic renal-cell carcinoma with a clear-cell histologic component and no prior systemic treatment, first-line; KPS ≥70, measurable RECIST disease; excluded brain metastases, poorly controlled hypertension, and cardiac/vascular conditions within 6 months Pazopanib 800 mg orally once daily, continuous vs sunitinib 50 mg orally once daily for 4 weeks followed by 2 weeks off, in 6-week cycles; both treated until progression, unacceptable toxic effects, or consent withdrawal; dose reductions for adverse events Primary: Progression free survival by independent review, powered for non-inferiority. Secondary: Overall survival, safety, QoL Pazopanib was noninferior to sunitinib for independently reviewed PFS (HR 1.05; 95% CI 0.90–1.22, upper bound <1.25 margin); median PFS 8.4 mo pazopanib (557) vs 9.5 mo sunitinib (553). OS was similar (HR 0.91; 95% CI 0.76–1.08; medians 28.4 vs 29.3 mo; 502 deaths). ORR was higher with pazopanib (31% vs 25%, P=0.03). HRQoL during first 6 months favored pazopanib in 11 of 14 domains. Sunitinib caused more fatigue (63% vs 55%), hand-foot syndrome (50% vs 29%) and thrombocytopenia (78% vs 41%); pazopanib more ALT elevation (60% vs 43%), with more discontinuations for liver-test abnormalities (6% vs 1%). Fatal AEs: 13 pazopanib vs 19 sunitinib (drug-related 3 vs 8). Noninferiority does not establish superiority or equivalence; day-28 HRQoL timing could bias toward pazopanib.
records.keywords: Motzer et al. N Engl J Med 2013;369:722-31.

records.title: CheckMate 214
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · III · 2018
records.body: Untreated advanced clear-cell RCC; IMDC intermediate/poor risk for primary endpoint Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W for 4 doses, then nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W vs sunitinib 50 mg once daily 4 weeks on/2 weeks off (6-week cycle); to progression or toxicity Primary: Overall survival, progression-free survival and objective response rate (IMDC intermediate/poor risk). Secondary: Overall survival, progression-free survival and objective response rate (ITT); duration of response; safety; quality of life Nivolumab-ipilimumab retained a long-term OS advantage, but this 2026 final analysis is descriptive. In ITT, median OS was 52.7 vs 37.8 months (HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.62-0.82; 108-month OS 31.4% vs 19.5%); IRRC PFS was HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.76-1.04), with 96-month PFS 22.7% vs 9.0%. In primary intermediate/poor risk, OS remained favorable (median 46.7 vs 26.0 months; HR 0.69) and PFS favored the combination (HR 0.73). Favorable-risk findings were exploratory: OS HR 0.80 (95% CI 0.59-1.09), but IRRC PFS favored sunitinib (HR 1.78) and ORR was lower (29.6% vs 51.6%), although complete response was higher (12.8% vs 6.5%). Among 547 vs 535 treated patients, grade 3-4 TRAEs were 48.6% vs 64.1%; toxicity discontinuation was 23.8% vs 13.3%, with eight vs five toxicity deaths.

records.title: KEYNOTE-426
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated advanced clear-cell RCC (all IMDC risk) Pembrolizumab + axitinib vs sunitinib Overall survival and progression-free survival Pembrolizumab plus axitinib improved OS (HR 0.53) and PFS (15.1 vs 11.1 months, HR 0.69) across risk groups; established IO + TKI as a first-line standard.

records.title: JAVELIN Renal 101
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · III · 2019
records.body: Untreated advanced clear-cell RCC Avelumab + axitinib vs sunitinib PFS and OS in PD-L1-positive tumors Avelumab plus axitinib improved median PFS in the overall population (13.8 vs 8.4 months, HR 0.69); a PFS benefit without a demonstrated OS advantage, providing an IO + TKI option.

records.title: CheckMate 9ER
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated advanced clear-cell RCC Nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W (max 2 years) + cabozantinib 40 mg once daily vs sunitinib 50 mg once daily 4 weeks on/2 weeks off (6-week cycle); to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival Nivolumab plus cabozantinib doubled median PFS (16.6 vs 8.3 months, HR 0.51) and improved OS (HR 0.60); another first-line IO + TKI standard.

records.title: CLEAR
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · III · 2021
records.body: Untreated advanced clear-cell RCC Lenvatinib 20 mg once daily + pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W vs lenvatinib 18 mg once daily + everolimus 5 mg once daily vs sunitinib 50 mg once daily 4 weeks on/2 weeks off; to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival Lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab markedly improved median PFS (23.9 vs 9.2 months, HR 0.39) and OS (HR 0.66) with a 71% ORR; among the most active first-line IO + TKI regimens.

records.title: COSMIC-313
records.subtitle: RCC · First-line metastatic — immunotherapy-based combinations · III · 2023
records.body: Untreated advanced clear-cell RCC, IMDC intermediate/poor risk Cabozantinib 40 mg once daily + nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W for 4 cycles, then nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W (up to 2 years) vs placebo + nivolumab + ipilimumab (same schedule) Primary: Progression-free survival (first 550 randomised patients). Secondary: Overall survival (ITT); objective response rate; duration of response; safety; biomarker analyses At 45.0 months, descriptive updated ITT PFS favored cabozantinib-nivolumab-ipilimumab (median 16.6 vs 11.2 months; HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.69-0.98), but mature OS was negative (median 41.9 vs 42.0 months; HR 1.02, 95% CI 0.85-1.23; nominal P=0.84). ORR was 46% vs 37%, while DOR numerically favored the doublet (median 31.1 months vs not estimable; HR 1.33, nominal P=0.103). Among 426 vs 423 treated patients, grade 3-4 TRAEs were 75% vs 43%, grade 5 TRAEs were three vs five, and TRAE discontinuation was 49% vs 26%. Biomarker results are exploratory and unvalidated.
records.keywords: N Engl J Med 2023;388:1767-1778   Ann Oncol 2026;37:861-871 final OS and updated PFS 41720427

records.title: SWOG 1500 (PAPMET)
records.subtitle: RCC · Non-clear-cell RCC · II · 2021
records.body: Metastatic papillary RCC (treatment-naïve or prior non-VEGF therapy) Cabozantinib vs sunitinib (crizotinib/savolitinib arms closed for futility) Progression-free survival Cabozantinib improved median PFS over sunitinib (9.0 vs 5.6 months, HR 0.60) with higher ORR (23% vs 4%); established cabozantinib as a standard for metastatic papillary RCC.

records.title: SUNNIFORECAST
records.subtitle: RCC · Non-clear-cell RCC · II · 2025
records.body: Adults with previously untreated advanced or metastatic RCC with ≥50% non-clear-cell component, measurable disease, KPS ≥70%, tissue available and any IMDC risk; randomisation used papillary versus non-papillary classification, with local diagnosis allowed pending mandatory central review Nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV then ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV every 3 weeks for four doses, then nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks or 480 mg IV every 4 weeks vs heterogeneous investigator-choice SOC, mostly sunitinib Primary: 12-month overall survival rate. Secondary: 6- and 18-month overall survival rates; median overall survival; progression-free survival; objective response rate; safety; quality of life Ipilimumab-nivolumab improved the primary 12-month OS rate (78% vs 68%; one-sided P=0.026). Exploratory median OS numerically favored the combination (33.2 vs 25.2 months; HR 0.81, 95% CI 0.61-1.09; nominal P=0.163), and PFS estimates were 5.4 vs 5.7 months (HR 0.99). ORR among patients with valid response assessment was 33% vs 20%. Among treated participants (n=156 vs 143), serious AEs occurred in 48% vs 39%; toxicity discontinuation was 17% vs 9%, and five vs three fatal AEs were reported, none treatment-related. FKSI-DRS showed no significant between-arm difference among questionnaire respondents, with participation declining at later timepoints.

records.title: RECORD-1
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · III · 2008
records.body: Adults with metastatic RCC containing a clear-cell component, progressing during or within 6 months after stopping sunitinib and/or sorafenib; Karnofsky score ≥70%; excluded prior mTOR inhibitor, untreated CNS metastases or uncontrolled medical conditions Everolimus 10 mg orally once daily + best supportive care vs matching placebo + best supportive care during double-blind treatment; continue until progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or withdrawal Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Safety; objective response rate; overall survival; quality of life Final RECORD-1 analysis confirmed longer independent central-review PFS with everolimus in all 416 randomised patients (4.9 vs 1.9 mo; HR 0.33, 95% CI 0.25–0.43). Final conventional ITT OS was 14.8 vs 14.4 mo (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.65–1.15; nominal one-sided P=.162); 111/139 placebo-assigned patients crossed over, limiting attribution. In the safety population (274 everolimus vs 137 placebo), noninfectious pneumonitis occurred in 14% vs 0% (grade 3, 4% vs 0%); adverse-event discontinuation occurred in 36/274 vs 2/137. During double-blind treatment, 4 patients died from causes other than disease progression alone (3 infection-related; 1 acute respiratory failure with progression and ongoing everolimus-related grade 3 interstitial lung disease); arm assignment was not stated
records.keywords: Lancet 2008;372:449-456   Cancer 2010;116:4256-4265 final analysis and mature OS 20549832

records.title: AXIS
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · III · 2011
