records.body: Metastatic RCC with a clear-cell component and RECIST progression after 1 first-line regimen containing sunitinib, bevacizumab plus interferon-alfa, temsirolimus or cytokines; ECOG 0–1; CNS metastases excluded; no myocardial infarction, uncontrolled angina, heart failure or cerebrovascular accident within 12 months, or DVT/PE within 6 months Axitinib 5 mg orally twice daily (eligible escalation to 7 then 10 mg twice daily) vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily; continue until RECIST progression, unacceptable toxicity, death or withdrawal Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; objective response rate; duration of response; composite time to deterioration; safety Axitinib improved independently reviewed PFS after 1 prior therapy: 6.7 vs 4.7 mo; HR 0.665 (95% CI 0.544–0.812). OS was immature and not reported. Treatment-related AE discontinuation occurred in 4% vs 8%; grade ≥3 hypertension in 16% vs 11% and palmar-plantar erythrodysaesthesia in 5% vs 16%; treatment-toxicity deaths were 0 vs 2

records.title: METEOR
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · III · 2015
records.body: Advanced or metastatic RCC with a clear-cell component and measurable disease progressing during or within 6 months after ≥1 VEGFR-targeting TKI; Karnofsky ≥70; stable treated brain metastases allowed; prior mTOR inhibitor, cabozantinib or uncontrolled clinically significant illness excluded Cabozantinib 60 mg orally daily vs everolimus 10 mg orally daily; dose reduce (40→20 mg vs 5→2.5 mg) or interrupt for AEs; continue while investigator-assessed clinical benefit or until unacceptable toxicity Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; objective response rate; safety Cabozantinib improved independently reviewed PFS in the first 375 patients: 7.4 vs 3.8 mo; HR 0.58 (95% CI 0.45–0.75). Interim OS in all 658 patients favoured cabozantinib (HR 0.67, 95% CI 0.51–0.89) but did not cross its prespecified boundary. Grade 3–4 AEs occurred in 68% vs 58%, dose reductions in 60% vs 25%, and treatment-related deaths in 1 vs 2 patients

records.title: CheckMate 025
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · III · 2015
records.body: Advanced clear-cell RCC after 1-2 antiangiogenic therapies Nivolumab vs everolimus Overall survival Nivolumab improved median OS (25.0 vs 19.6 months, HR 0.73) with higher ORR (25% vs 5%) despite similar PFS; the first checkpoint inhibitor to beat everolimus and a post-TKI standard.

records.title: TIVO-3
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · III · 2020
records.body: Metastatic RCC with a clear-cell component after 2–3 prior systemic regimens including a VEGFR TKI other than tivozanib or sorafenib; ECOG 0–1; CNS metastases allowed only if stable off steroids for ≥3 months; substantial cardiovascular disease or myocardial infarction, angina, thromboembolic or vascular events within 6 months excluded Tivozanib 1.5 mg orally daily, 21 days on/7 days off every 28 days vs sorafenib 400 mg orally twice daily continuously; continue until IRC-confirmed progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: Progression-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival; confirmed objective response; duration of response; safety Tivozanib improved IRC PFS after 2–3 prior regimens: 5.6 vs 3.9 mo; HR 0.73 (95% CI 0.56–0.94). At the prespecified second-interim OS analysis, HR was 0.99 (95% CI 0.76–1.29; nominal P=.95). Treatment-related AEs occurred in 84% vs 94%, with interruptions in 48% vs 63% and reductions in 24% vs 38%; grade 3–4 hypertension occurred in 20% vs 14%, with no treatment-related deaths

records.title: CONTACT-03
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · III · 2023
records.body: Advanced RCC progressing on/after immune checkpoint inhibitor Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV Q3W + cabozantinib 60 mg once daily vs cabozantinib 60 mg once daily Progression-free survival Adding atezolizumab to cabozantinib did not improve PFS (10.6 vs 10.8 months, HR 1.03) and added toxicity; the first randomized evidence against immune-checkpoint rechallenge by simple addition.

records.title: LITESPARK-005
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · III · 2024
records.body: Advanced clear-cell RCC after PD-(L)1 and VEGFR-TKI (1-3 prior regimens) Belzutifan 120 mg once daily vs everolimus 10 mg once daily; to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival and overall survival (co-primary) Belzutifan improved centrally reviewed PFS at the first interim analysis despite equal medians of 5.6 months: 18-month PFS was 24.0% vs 8.3% (P=0.002), meeting the prespecified significance criterion; confirmed ORR was 21.9% vs 3.5% (P<0.001). At the second interim analysis, OS did not meet its prespecified significance criterion (21.4 vs 18.1 months, HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.73-1.07; P=0.20).

records.title: TiNivo-2
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · III · 2024
records.body: Advanced RCC, progression during/after 1–2 prior lines including one ICI Tivozanib 0.89 mg once daily + nivolumab 480 mg IV Q4W; to progression vs tivozanib 1.34 mg once daily; to progression PFS by independent radiology review (RECIST 1.1) Median PFS 5.7 vs 7.4 mo (HR 1.10, 95% CI 0.84–1.43; p=0.49) — NEGATIVE; adding nivolumab (ICI rechallenge) to tivozanib post-ICI provided no PFS benefit. In ICI-immediate-prior subgroup (n=244): PFS 7.4 vs 9.2 mo. SAEs 32% vs 37%; 1 treatment-related death (tivozanib arm). Supports discouraging ICI rechallenge post-progression.

records.title: LenCabo
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · II · 2026
records.body: Metastatic ccRCC progressed on prior PD-(L)1 ICI (1–2 prior lines) Lenvatinib 18 mg once daily + everolimus 5 mg once daily vs cabozantinib 60 mg once daily; all to progression PFS (Bayesian optimal phase II design) Median PFS 15.7 vs 10.2 mo (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.29–0.89; p=0.02). ORR 52.6% vs 38.6%. OS immature (n=24/86 events; 1-yr OS 87.0% vs 84.6%). Tox-driven discontinuation 20% vs 10.9%. First head-to-head comparison of post-ICI targeted therapies in ccRCC; informs sequencing.

records.title: LITESPARK-011
records.subtitle: RCC · Subsequent-line / refractory metastatic disease · III · 2026
records.body: Unresectable locally advanced or metastatic stage IV clear-cell RCC progressing on or after one prior anti-PD-1/PD-L1 as first- or second-line treatment, or ≤6 months after last dose as adjuvant or neoadjuvant-adjuvant therapy; KPS ≥70%, resting pulse oximetry ≥92%, ≤2 prior systemic regimens with anti-PD-1/PD-L1 immediately preceding enrolment; no previous belzutifan or other HIF-2α inhibitor, cabozantinib or lenvatinib Belzutifan 120 mg orally once daily plus lenvatinib 20 mg orally once daily vs cabozantinib 60 mg orally once daily, both until radiographic progression, unacceptable adverse events, pregnancy, prohibited medication, or participant discontinuation Primary: Progression-free survival, Overall survival. Secondary: Objective response rate, Duration of response, Safety, Patient-reported outcomes Belzutifan–lenvatinib improved central-review PFS (final PFS analysis at second interim; median follow-up 29 months; median 14·8 vs 10·7 months; HR 0·70, 95% CI 0·59-0·84; one-sided p<0·0001) and the authors conclude it might be a new standard of care after anti-PD-1/PD-L1 therapy. Overall survival was not significantly different at this second interim (median 34·9 vs 27·6 months; HR 0·85, 95% CI 0·68-1·05; one-sided p=0·061) and will be tested at final analysis. ORR crossed its first-interim boundary (53% vs 40%; CR 5% vs 1%); median duration of response 23·0 vs 12·3 months. Among treated participants (n=370 vs 371), grade 3-5 TEAEs 84% vs 83%; serious TEAEs 52% vs 44%; treatment-related deaths two vs one; treatment-related discontinuation 19% vs 5%; anaemia 69% vs 26% and hypoxia 15% vs 0% with belzutifan-lenvatinib

records.title: Adjuvant Mitotane (Terzolo)
records.subtitle: Adrenocortical Carcinoma · Adrenocortical carcinoma · N/A · 2007
records.body: Adults with radically resected adrenocortical carcinoma at Italian tertiary centres or German registry centres, without distant metastases, incomplete staging/resection, major comorbidity, recent other cancer or non-mitotane adjuvant therapy Adjuvant mitotane after radical surgery: 3–5 g/day (n=20) or 1–3 g/day (n=27) vs Italian contemporaneous no-adjuvant control (n=55) vs German registry no-adjuvant control (n=75) Primary: Recurrence-free survival. Secondary: Overall survival, Mitotane-associated adverse events Adjuvant mitotane was associated with longer RFS than untreated Italian and German controls (median 42 vs 10 and 25 months; recurrence in 23/47 vs 50/55 and 55/75), with directionally favourable adjusted analyses. Median OS was 110 vs 52 and 67 months, but secondary comparisons were nominal. Toxicity was mainly grade 1–2; 6/47 (13%) required temporary interruption or dose reduction. Nonrandomised centre-policy allocation, baseline imbalance and retrospective safety ascertainment preclude definitive causal benefit

records.title: FIRM-ACT (Fassnacht)
records.subtitle: Adrenocortical Carcinoma · Adrenocortical carcinoma · III · 2012
records.body: Adults with histologically confirmed, radiologically measurable, unresectable locally advanced or metastatic adrenocortical carcinoma; no prior cytotoxic therapy other than mitotane; ECOG 0-2 and adequate organ function EDP-M: etoposide 100 mg/m2 IV days 2–4, doxorubicin 40 mg/m2 IV day 1 and cisplatin 40 mg/m2 IV days 3–4 every 4 weeks plus continuous oral mitotane; vs Sz-M: streptozocin 1 g IV days 1–5 in cycle 1 then 2 g IV day 1 every 3 weeks plus mitotane; mitotane began at least 1 week before chemotherapy, targeting 14–20 mg/L Primary: Overall survival. Secondary: Progression-free survival, Tumour response, Quality of life, Mitotane-level association, Second-line regimen response EDP-M did not meet the alpha-controlled primary OS endpoint (median 14.8 vs 12.0 months; HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.61–1.02; P=0.07) but improved nominal secondary PFS (5.0 vs 2.1 months; HR 0.55, 0.43–0.69; P<0.001) and response (23.2% vs 9.2%; P<0.001) versus Sz-M. Serious events per treatment-month (0.092 vs 0.099; P=0.64) and QoL were similar, with low questionnaire completion; mandated crossover may attenuate OS and second-line comparisons are selection-biased

records.title: IGCCCG
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Risk classification & prognosis · N/A · 1997
records.body: Metastatic germ-cell tumours (5,202 NSGCT + 660 seminoma), first-line cisplatin era Prognostic-factor analysis (primary site, marker levels, non-pulmonary visceral mets) Progression-free & overall survival Defined good / intermediate / poor prognosis groups; 5-yr OS 91% / 79% / 48% (poor risk all NSGCT, including mediastinal primaries). Became the universal risk-stratification framework guiding first-line therapy.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 1997;15:594-603   J Clin Oncol 2001;19:2534-2541 HCG-AFP decline analysis 11331333

records.title: IGCCCG Update
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Risk classification & prognosis · N/A · 2021
records.body: Metastatic NSGCT treated 1990-2013 with cisplatin/etoposide first-line chemo Contemporary re-analysis & refined prognostic model Progression-free & overall survival 5-yr OS improved to 96% (good), 89% (intermediate) and 67% (poor, from 48%); PFS 89% / 75% / 54%. Added age, lung metastases and an LDH 2.5x ULN cut-off for finer prognostication.

records.title: IGCCCG Update — Seminoma (Beyer 2021)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Risk classification & prognosis · N/A · 2021
records.body: Men with pure metastatic seminoma, or retroperitoneal/mediastinal seminoma even without metastases, treated with first-line conventional-dose cisplatin–etoposide chemotherapy; at least 3 cycles received or intended; AFP >30 ng/mL and prior chemotherapy for metastatic disease excluded First-line conventional-dose cisplatin/etoposide-based chemotherapy, with at least 3 cycles received or intended; retrospective prognostic cohorts with no randomized treatment comparison Primary: PFS; OS. Secondary: prognostic discrimination Metastatic seminoma remained highly curable. In the main cohort, 5-year PFS was 89% (95% CI 87–90; n=2281) versus 79% (70–85; n=121), and 5-year OS was 95% (94–96; n=2329) versus 88% (80–93; n=122), for original IGCCCG good versus intermediate prognosis. Within original good prognosis, LDH >2.5×ULN was prognostic: training 3-year PFS was 80% (75–84; n=260) versus 92% (90–94; n=916) and OS was 92% (88–95; n=267) versus 97% (96–98; n=930); independent-validation PFS was 75% (65–82; n=114) versus 93% (90–95; n=600). This retrospective, nonrandomized analysis cannot establish benefit from treatment intensification; formal between-era comparisons were unavailable, and no treatment-related toxicity results were reported.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 2021;39:1553-1562 IGCCCG Update — Seminoma 33729863

records.title: MRC TE19 / EORTC 30982
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · III · 2005
records.body: Stage I seminomatous germ-cell tumour with normal tumour markers after orchidectomy One intravenous carboplatin AUC 7 vs para-aortic or dog-leg radiotherapy (20 Gy/10 fractions or 30 Gy/15 fractions) Primary: relapse-free rate. Secondary: death from any cause; second cancer incidence; morbidity; quality of life; gonadal function Single-dose carboplatin was noninferior to radiotherapy for relapse-free rate in TE19. At 5 years, relapse-free rate was 94.7% with carboplatin versus 96.0% with radiotherapy (HR 1.25, 90% CI 0.83-1.89; upper bound excluded the prespecified noninferiority margin). Mature follow-up found fewer contralateral germ-cell tumours with carboplatin (2 vs 15; HR 0.22, 95% CI 0.05-0.95). This supports carboplatin as an adjuvant alternative, not superiority; long-term non-germ-cell second-cancer outcomes were immature.
records.keywords: Lancet 2005;366:293-300   J Clin Oncol 2011;29:957-962 mature results 21282539 J Natl Cancer Inst 2011;103:241-249 pooled relapse-pattern analysis (TE10/TE18/TE19) 21212385

records.title: MRC TE18 / EORTC 30942
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · III · 2005
records.body: Clinical stage I seminoma, adjuvant radiotherapy Para-aortic RT 20 Gy/10 fractions vs 30 Gy/15 fractions Relapse rate (non-inferiority) 20 Gy non-inferior to 30 Gy: 11 vs 10 relapses (HR 1.11), 2-yr relapse-rate difference 0.7%, with less acute lethargy and faster return to work. Established 20 Gy as the standard adjuvant RT dose when RT is used.

records.title: Carboplatin de-escalation (van de Wetering)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · N/A · 2018
records.body: Clinical stage I seminoma after orchidectomy N/A — opinion (surveillance vs adjuvant carboplatin / radiotherapy) N/A Argues surveillance should be the default for most compliant CS I seminoma patients, and that adjuvant carboplatin and radiotherapy — validated only in unselected populations — are now overused. Notes ~15% relapse on surveillance with near-100% salvage success, questioning routine adjuvant treatment. Influential de-escalation viewpoint from Erasmus MC / MSKCC germ-cell authorities.

records.title: SGCCG nomogram (Aparicio)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · N/A · 2014
records.body: Stage I seminoma after orchidectomy in three prospective SGCCG risk-adapted studies; surveillance or two-course adjuvant carboplatin selected by pathological risk criteria Observational pooled risk-adapted cohorts: surveillance vs two courses of adjuvant carboplatin (study I 400 mg/m² every 28 days; studies II/III AUC 7 every 21 days); surveillance-only relapse-nomogram derivation Disease-free survival; relapse; recurrence pattern and detection; outcome after salvage; 3-year disease-free survival nomogram; second malignancies and late complications The surveillance-derived nomogram identified rete testis invasion and continuous tumour size as relapse predictors; it requires prospective validation. In 744 risk-adapted patients, relapse was reported as Kaplan-Meier 14.8% with surveillance and 3.2% after carboplatin, but allocation was nonrandomized and the time horizon is inferred. The model was developed only in surveillance patients; it does not establish predictive treatment benefit.

records.title: SWENOTECA seminoma (Tandstad)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I seminoma · N/A · 2011
records.body: Testicular seminoma of any clinical stage after orchidectomy in the Sweden/Norway SWENOTECA V population-based cohort (2000-2006); 86.1% had clinical stage I; spermatocytic and extragonadal tumours excluded CS I: surveillance vs L-field radiotherapy 25.2 Gy/14 fractions vs one course carboplatin AUC 7 (nonrandomized); CS IIA radiotherapy 27 Gy/15 fractions; CS IIB+: EP ×4, BEP ×4 for large-volume disease, with BEP-if intensification for poor response after two courses Relapse-free interval; overall survival; cause-specific survival; relapse prognostic factors; site and timing of relapse; salvage treatment and treatment-related toxicity and mortality In this population-based, nonrandomized cohort, clinical stage I relapse-free interval was 85.7% with surveillance, 96.1% after one-course carboplatin and 99.2% after radiotherapy; 5-year cause-specific survival was 99.6% across 1,384 men. Carboplatin follow-up was shorter (median 3.4 years), and chosen-treatment comparisons were confounded by imbalanced risk factors; rete testis invasion was unrecorded. No clinical stage I patient died from progressive cancer, but one treatment-related death followed relapse after surveillance; five patients stopped salvage EP early for toxicity, including two myocardial infarctions and one cerebral infarction.

records.title: AUO AH 01/94 (GTCSG)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I non-seminoma · III · 2008
records.body: Histologically confirmed clinical stage I nonseminomatous germ-cell tumour after orchidectomy; CT chest/abdomen/pelvis and AFP, beta-hCG and LDH confirmed stage I; ipsilateral-template nodes >10 mm were excluded; treatment began <4 weeks after orchidectomy One course BEP — cisplatin 20 mg/m² and etoposide 100 mg/m² by 60-minute infusion on days 1–5 + bleomycin 30,000 IU (30 mg) by bolus infusion on days 1, 8 and 15 — vs open nerve-sparing or modified ipsilateral-template RPLND; pathological stage II after RPLND received two 21-day BEP cycles Primary: recurrence rate and time to recurrence. Secondary: overall survival; cancer-specific survival; toxicity One adjuvant BEP course reduced recurrence versus community-standard RPLND in this randomized trial. In the ITT population (382; 191 per arm), recurrences were 2 versus 15 and 2-year recurrence-free survival was 99.46% versus 91.87% (difference 7.59 percentage points, 95% CI 3.13–12.05; nominal two-sided P=.0011). The recurrence HR of 7.937 for RPLND versus BEP derives from the per-protocol population (n=347; 2 vs 13 recurrences), not ITT. RPLND included post-surgical two-course BEP for 32 patients with pathological stage II; surgical experience and quality limit applicability. Grade 3 toxicity events were 37.4% relative to the BEP denominator versus 8.7% relative to the RPLND-arm denominator, whose events included post-RPLND BEP; grade 4 toxicity-event rates were 2.3% in each arm. Six deaths were unrelated to disease, with no cancer-specific death or fatal bleomycin-related pulmonary toxicity reported.

records.title: SWENOTECA
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage I non-seminoma · N/A · 2014
records.body: Swedish and Norwegian men with clinical stage I nonseminomatous germ-cell tumour confirmed 6–8 weeks after orchidectomy by examination, CT chest/abdomen/pelvis and normalized tumour markers; lymphovascular invasion was the sole risk classifier Risk-adapted, nonrandomized choice: LVI-positive patients were advised one or two 21-day BEP courses; LVI-negative patients chose surveillance or one BEP course. BEP: cisplatin 20 mg/m² + etoposide 100 mg/m² daily days 1–5 + bleomycin 30 mg days 1, 5 and 15; the 2014 one-BEP cohort was treated 6–10 weeks after orchidectomy without prophylactic G-CSF or antibiotics Relapse rate; relapse-free survival; overall survival; cause-specific survival; time to relapse; relapse detection and treatment; short-term toxicity; follow-up; chemotherapy burden One-BEP cohorts showed low relapse; nonrandomized LVI selection precludes causal comparison. In 2009, relapse was 5/12 (41.7%) with LVI-positive surveillance versus 5/157 (3.2%) after one BEP, and 39/338 (11.5%; KM 13.2%) with LVI-negative surveillance versus 2/155 (1.3%) after one BEP; the narrative conflicts with the table. The 2014 report expanded the earlier one-BEP subset to 517 and did not update surveillance: relapse was 8/258 (KM 3.2%, 95% CI 1.6–6.4) with LVI and 4/255 (1.6%, 95% CI 0.6–4.2) without; median follow-up was 7.9 years and 10-year cancer-specific survival 99.6%. Results said 76% had >5-year follow-up versus 75% in Discussion; schedules changed and late relapse remained possible. In 2009, toxicity was reported for only 75%–80% by category, with grade 3/4 leukopenia 33% after one BEP. The 2014 report had no acute-toxicity table; late secondary-cancer/cardiovascular data were lacking, and AML diagnosed 2.5 months after BEP was not attributed to treatment.
records.keywords: Ann Oncol 2014;25:2167-2172   J Clin Oncol 2009;27:2122-2128 SWENOTECA NSGCT management program 19307506

records.title: Spanish GCCG (Garcia-del-Muro)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Clinical stage II seminoma · N/A · 2008
records.body: Stage IIA (nodes <2 cm) or IIB (2-5 cm) pure testicular seminoma after orchidectomy, at diagnosis (82%) or relapsing on stage I surveillance (18%) Cisplatin-based chemotherapy: E400P (etoposide-cisplatin) x4 in 83% or BE500P x3 in 17% (single-arm) Progression-free and overall survival Chemotherapy alone controlled most stage IIA/IIB seminoma without irradiating the retroperitoneum: 5-yr progression-free survival 90% (95% CI 82-98) and overall survival 95% (89-100) at a median 71.5 mo, with complete response in 60 of 72 and no failure of first-line treatment. All 6 relapses followed E400P, the reduced-etoposide schedule 83% received and which the authors recommend against, advising 3 cycles of BE500P or 4 of E500P instead. All 6 were stage IIB and no stage IIA patient relapsed. Two men who had never received radiotherapy developed oesophageal carcinoma at 2 and 4 yr and died of it, and 3 of the 4 deaths were not from seminoma. Observational and single-arm - no comparison against radiotherapy was made despite the title, and no late toxicity was reported at this follow-up with no systematic late-effects assessment performed.

records.title: Williams (Intergroup)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · III · 1987
records.body: Disseminated germ-cell tumours, first-line Cisplatin/bleomycin + etoposide (BEP) vs + vinblastine (PVB) Disease-free response & survival Substituting etoposide for vinblastine gave equal-to-higher disease-free rates (83% vs 74% in advanced disease) with markedly less neuromuscular toxicity. Established BEP as the standard first-line regimen.

records.title: Loehrer (ECOG)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · III · 1995
records.body: Good-risk (minimal/moderate) disseminated germ-cell tumours 3 cycles EP vs 3 cycles BEP (testing bleomycin) Failure-free survival Omitting bleomycin worsened outcomes: failure-free survival 69% vs 86% and OS 86% vs 95% (both P=.01). Confirmed bleomycin is essential when only three cycles are given for good-risk disease.

records.title: EORTC/MRC (de Wit)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · III · 2001
records.body: Good-prognosis metastatic germ-cell cancer (IGCCCG) 2×2 factorial: 3 vs 4 cycles of BEP, and 5-day vs 3-day schedule. Per cycle — etoposide 500 mg/m² (100 mg/m² days 1–5 [5-day] or 165 mg/m² days 1–3 [3-day]) + cisplatin 100 mg/m² (20 mg/m² days 1–5 or 50 mg/m² days 1–2) + bleomycin 30 mg weekly (days 1, 8, 15, cycles 1–3) Progression-free survival (equivalence) Three cycles of BEP equivalent to four (2-yr PFS 90.4% vs 89.4%) and a 3-day schedule equalled 5-day. Established 3xBEP as the good-risk standard, reducing cumulative toxicity.

records.title: Horwich (MRC/EORTC)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · III · 1997
records.body: Previously untreated, testicular-primary nonseminomatous GCT or seminoma with unequivocally raised AFP; MRC/EORTC good prognosis with low markers, limited nodal/lung burden, no liver, bone or brain metastases, and GFR >50 mL/min; protocol-criterion deviations occurred, and extragonadal-primary inclusion was not established BEP: four 21-day cycles of etoposide 120 mg/m² days 1–3, bleomycin 30 U day 2 and cisplatin 100 mg/m²/cycle on days 1–5 or 1–2 vs CEB: the same etoposide and bleomycin, with carboplatin AUC 5 mg/mL-min replacing cisplatin, dosed as 5 × (GFR + 25) mg using EDTA clearance or 10% lower with creatinine clearance Primary: failure-free survival. Secondary: response; overall survival; toxicity; renal function In the 598 randomized patients, substituting carboplatin for cisplatin in CEB was inferior to BEP. By allocated treatment, 1-year failure-free survival was 77% with CEB versus 91% with BEP (79/298 vs 30/300 failures; HR for CEB vs BEP 2.75, 95% CI 1.88–4.03); 3-year overall survival was 90% versus 97% (27 vs 10 deaths; HR 2.65, 95% CI 1.39–5.05). CEB caused more thrombocytopenia, whereas BEP caused more mainly mild sensory deficit and greater GFR decline. One patient in each arm died after cycle 1, without source attribution to treatment. Toxicity results were limited to the MRC subset, and the narrative/Table 6 CEB audiometry denominators conflict.

records.title: GETUG T93BP (Culine)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — good prognosis · III · 2007
records.body: Previously untreated metastatic NSGCT with a testicular or retroperitoneal primary, good risk by the Institut Gustave Roussy AFP/hCG model, and adequate hematologic, renal and hepatic function; retrospective IGCCCG reassignment identified 6 poor-risk patients and does not redefine the entry population 3BE500P: three 21-day cycles of etoposide 100 mg/m² and cisplatin 20 mg/m² days 1–5, plus bleomycin 30 IU on days 1, 8 and 15 vs 4E500P: four 21-day cycles of etoposide 100 mg/m² and cisplatin 20 mg/m² days 1–5, without bleomycin; the source prints bleomycin as IU in the treatment plan/Table 2 and mg elsewhere, so no conversion is made Primary: favorable response. Secondary: event-free survival; overall survival; toxicity; pulmonary toxicity; ototoxicity Three-cycle 3BE500P met the prespecified favorable-response equivalence criterion versus four-cycle 4E500P in eligible/evaluable patients. Favorable response was 94.7% (124/131) versus 96.8% (122/126); the 3BE500P-minus-4E500P difference was -2.2 percentage points (90% CI -5.15 to +0.07), within the ±10-point equivalence region. In the authors' defined 262-patient ITT cohort, 4-year event-free survival was 91% versus 86% (HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.29–1.19) and overall survival 96% versus 92% (HR 0.42, 95% CI 0.15–1.20); the trial was underpowered for survival and did not establish EFS/OS equivalence. Grade 3–4 neutropenia was reported more often with 4E500P, whereas grades 1–3 neurologic and dermatologic toxicity were more frequent with 3BE500P; no toxic deaths occurred, and the Table 3 4E500P neutropenia count/percentage conflicts with its header denominator.

records.title: Nichols (Intergroup)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — intermediate & poor prognosis · III · 1998
records.body: Previously untreated Indiana advanced-stage disseminated germ-cell cancer; all primary sites and histologies were eligible, including advanced pulmonary disease, mediastinal NSGCT, or nonpulmonary visceral/CNS metastases. Retrospective IGCCCG classification included good-risk patients and was not entry eligibility 4 courses of BEP vs VIP at 3-week intervals. BEP — cisplatin 20 mg/m² + etoposide 100 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + bleomycin 30 U IV weekly ×12 weeks. VIP — cisplatin 20 mg/m² + etoposide 75 mg/m² + ifosfamide 1.2 g/m² IV days 1–5 (mesna uroprotection) Complete response; favorable response; time to treatment failure; progression-free survival; overall survival; toxicity The randomized comparison did not show a statistically significant efficacy difference between BEP and VIP, but it was not designed to establish equivalence. At the final update (median follow-up 7.3 years), reported PFS was 58% with BEP versus 64% with VIP and OS 67% versus 69%. VIP caused more grade 3–5 toxicity in the retrospective IGCCCG-poor subgroup (93% vs 79%); 11 on-treatment deaths were reported across risk groups, with uncertain attribution for some. In the original treated safety cohort, grade 4 hematologic toxicity was 60% with VIP versus 34% with BEP. Toxicity predates routine G-CSF.
records.keywords: J Clin Oncol 1998;16:1287-1293   Cancer 2003;97:1869-1875 final analysis 12673712

records.title: GETUG-13
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · First-line metastatic — intermediate & poor prognosis · III · 2014
records.body: Previously untreated patients aged >16 years with testicular, retroperitoneal or mediastinal NSGCT and IGCCCG poor prognosis; 263 were registered, 254 had marker decline assessed after one BEP cycle, 203 with centrally classified unfavourable AFP and/or hCG decline were randomized, while 51 with favourable decline formed a nonrandomized BEP cohort After cycle 1 BEP: Unfav-BEP, three further BEP cycles; or Unfav-dose-dense, two T-BEP–oxaliplatin cycles followed by two cisplatin–bleomycin–ifosfamide cycles, with G-CSF and a 2005 neuropathy amendment removing later oxaliplatin. Fav-BEP was nonrandomized and received three further BEP cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival; response; adverse events Marker-guided switch to dose-dense therapy showed a clinically favourable PFS signal: among 203 randomized patients with unfavourable marker decline, 3-year PFS was 59% versus 48% (HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.44–1.00; reported P=.05; prespecified final nominal α=.048). The filed manuscript gives no unrounded P value or explicit boundary-crossing statement, so formal threshold status cannot be determined from the reported rounded value. Three-year OS was 73% versus 65% (HR 0.78, 95% CI 0.46–1.31; P=.34). Salvage HDCT was used in 6/105 (6%) versus 16/98 (16%; nominal P=.015). Dose-dense therapy increased haematotoxicity and grade 3/4 neuropathy (7% versus 1%); febrile neutropenia was 18/105 (17%) versus 18/98 (18%), and one toxic death occurred per arm. This accepted source is an author manuscript; the version of record and web supplements were not filed.

records.title: Kondagunta (MSKCC) TIP
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Relapsed / salvage therapy · II · 2005
records.body: First relapse, favourable-risk (testis primary + prior CR to first-line) Paclitaxel + ifosfamide + cisplatin (TIP) x4 cycles Complete response & PFS Four cycles of TIP achieved 70% complete response, 63% durable CR and 65% 2-yr PFS. Established TIP as a standard conventional-dose first-salvage regimen for favourable-risk relapse.

records.title: Einhorn (Indiana) HDCT
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Relapsed / salvage therapy · N/A · 2007
records.body: Relapsed/refractory metastatic germ-cell tumours (mostly second-line) Two sequential cycles high-dose carboplatin + etoposide with PBSC rescue Durable complete remission Tandem high-dose carboplatin/etoposide gave durable disease-free status in 116/184 (63%), including 18/40 platinum-refractory patients. Established high-dose chemotherapy with stem-cell rescue as a curative salvage option.

records.title: TI-CE (Feldman, MSKCC)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Relapsed / salvage therapy · II · 2010
records.body: Relapsed germ-cell tumours with unfavourable salvage-risk features TI-CE: paclitaxel/ifosfamide then high-dose carboplatin/etoposide x3 + PBSC Disease-free survival TI-CE produced 5-yr DFS 47% and OS 52% in poor-risk relapse; mediastinal primary and >=2 prior lines predicted worse outcome. Validated TI-CE high-dose chemotherapy for unfavourable-risk salvage.

records.title: CLIMATE (ANZUP 1906)
records.subtitle: Germ Cell Tumors · Post-chemotherapy management & biomarkers · N/A · 2026
records.body: Clinical stage I testicular germ-cell tumour, post-orchidectomy MRD assessment Plasma miR-371a-3p detectable vs undetectable (observational cohort) Recurrence-free survival Detectable post-orchidectomy plasma miR-371a-3p strongly predicted relapse (HR 10.3, 95% CI 5.3-19.8; 20% of the cohort relapsed), outperforming conventional markers. Positions miR-371 as an MRD tool to refine adjuvant decisions (not yet standard of care).

records.title: RTOG 90-01 (Morris)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · III · 1999
records.body: High-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (FIGO IIB-IVA, or IB-IIA ≥5 cm/node+) Pelvic RT + concurrent cisplatin/5-FU vs extended-field (pelvic + para-aortic) RT Overall survival Concurrent chemoradiation improved 5-year OS (73% vs 58%, HR for death 0.52) and reduced local failure and distant metastases; helped establish cisplatin-based chemoradiation as standard.

records.title: GOG 120 (Rose)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · III · 1999
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer, FIGO IIB-IVA Cisplatin-based chemoradiation (cisplatin or cisplatin/5-FU/hydroxyurea) vs hydroxyurea + RT Progression-free survival Cisplatin-containing chemoradiation improved PFS and OS vs hydroxyurea (relative risk of progression 0.57 and 0.55 for the cisplatin arms); weekly cisplatin became the standard radiosensitizer.

records.title: GOG 123 (Keys)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · III · 1999
records.body: Bulky stage IB2 cervical carcinoma (tumor ≥4 cm), pre-hysterectomy Weekly cisplatin + RT vs RT alone, both followed by adjuvant hysterectomy Progression-free survival Adding weekly cisplatin to RT reduced risk of progression (RR 0.51) and death (RR 0.54), with significantly higher 4-year PFS and OS; cemented concurrent cisplatin for bulky early-stage disease.

records.title: CCCMAC (IPD meta-analysis)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — concurrent chemoradiation (foundation) · N/A · 2008
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer across 18 randomized chemoradiation trials (individual patient data) Concurrent chemoradiation vs radiotherapy alone Overall survival Chemoradiation improved 5-year OS by 6% (66% vs 60%, HR 0.81) and DFS by 8%, with benefit greatest for platinum-based regimens; confirmed chemoradiation as the standard of care.

records.title: OUTBACK (GOG-0274)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — treatment intensification · III · 2023
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer after primary cisplatin-based chemoradiation Adjuvant carboplatin + paclitaxel after chemoradiation vs chemoradiation alone Overall survival Adjuvant chemotherapy did not improve 5-year OS (72% vs 71%, HR 0.90) and added toxicity; sequential adjuvant chemotherapy should not be given after chemoradiation.

records.title: INTERLACE (GCIG)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — treatment intensification · III · 2024
records.body: Locally advanced cervical cancer (FIGO 2008 IB1 node+ to IVA) Induction weekly IV carboplatin AUC 2 + paclitaxel 80 mg/m² for 6 weeks, then standard cisplatin-based chemoradiation (weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² for 5 weeks concurrent with external-beam RT plus brachytherapy) vs the same chemoradiation alone Progression-free survival Short induction chemotherapy improved 5-year PFS (72% vs 64%, HR 0.65) and OS (80% vs 72%, HR 0.60); a feasible intensification using existing drugs.

records.title: KEYNOTE-A18 (ENGOT-cx11/GOG-3047)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Locally advanced — treatment intensification · III · 2024
records.body: Newly diagnosed high-risk locally advanced cervical cancer (FIGO 2014 III-IVA, or IB2-IIB node+) Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W ×5 cycles concurrent with cisplatin-based chemoradiation (weekly cisplatin 40 mg/m² + external-beam RT plus brachytherapy), then pembrolizumab 400 mg IV Q6W ×15 cycles vs placebo plus the same chemoradiation Progression-free survival Pembrolizumab added to chemoradiation met both dual primary endpoints, at two different interim analyses. At the first interim analysis progression-free survival improved (2-year PFS 68% vs 57%, HR 0.70, 95% CI 0.55-0.89, p=0.0020). All alpha then passed to overall survival, tested at the second interim analysis: HR 0.67 (95% CI 0.50-0.90; one-sided p=0.0040) against a prespecified boundary of 0.01026, on 75 deaths (14%) vs 109 (21%) at a 76.7% information fraction, median overall survival not reached in either group, 36-month OS 82.6% vs 74.8%; the paper calls this the final, formally tested overall survival result. Progression-free survival was not formally tested again there, so the more mature HR 0.68 (95% CI 0.56-0.84) reported alongside it carries no alpha and does not supersede the 0.70. Potentially immune-mediated adverse events 39% vs 17% (grade >=3 5% vs 1%); grade >=3 treatment-emergent events 78% vs 70%; two treatment-related deaths in each group. The authors conclude that the two analyses together support pembrolizumab plus chemoradiotherapy as a new standard of care.
records.keywords: Lancet 2024;403:1341-1350   Lancet 2024;404:1321-1332 overall survival results, second interim analysis 39288779

records.title: GOG 204 (Monk)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemotherapy & antiangiogenics · III · 2009
records.body: Stage IVB, recurrent, or persistent cervical carcinoma, first-line Cisplatin + paclitaxel vs cisplatin + vinorelbine, gemcitabine, or topotecan Overall survival No doublet was superior to cisplatin/paclitaxel (median OS ~12.9 months), with trends favoring it; established cisplatin/paclitaxel as the chemotherapy backbone.

records.title: GOG 240 (Tewari)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemotherapy & antiangiogenics · III · 2014
records.body: Recurrent, persistent, or metastatic cervical cancer, first-line Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W + chemotherapy vs chemotherapy alone (2×2 factorial), chemo being cisplatin 50 mg/m² + paclitaxel 135–175 mg/m² or topotecan 0.75 mg/m² days 1–3 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m²; 21-day cycles to progression Overall survival Adding bevacizumab improved OS (17.0 vs 13.3 months, HR 0.71) and PFS (8.2 vs 5.9 months); the first antiangiogenic and first survival gain in this setting.

records.title: JCOG0505 (Kitagawa)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemotherapy & antiangiogenics · III · 2015
records.body: Metastatic or recurrent cervical cancer, first-line (Japan; JCOG) Paclitaxel + carboplatin (TC) vs paclitaxel + cisplatin (TP) Overall survival (non-inferiority) Non-inferiority met: median OS 17.5 (TC) vs 18.3 (TP) months (HR 0.994, 90% CI 0.789-1.253). In cisplatin-naive patients OS favoured TP (23.2 vs 13.0 months). Established carboplatin-paclitaxel as a convenient standard except in cisplatin-naive disease.

records.title: KEYNOTE-826 (Colombo)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2021
records.body: Persistent, recurrent, or metastatic cervical cancer, first-line Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV Q3W to 35 cycles + platinum doublet (paclitaxel 175 mg/m² + cisplatin 50 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5, capped at 6 cycles) ± bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV Q3W (investigator's discretion) vs placebo + the same chemotherapy ± bevacizumab Progression-free and overall survival Pembrolizumab improved PFS (10.4 vs 8.2 months, HR 0.65) and OS (HR 0.67; final median 26.4 vs 16.8 months); established first-line chemo-immunotherapy.

records.title: BEATcc (Oaknin)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Metastatic, persistent, or recurrent cervical cancer, first-line Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV Q3W added to bevacizumab 15 mg/kg + platinum–paclitaxel (cisplatin 50 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 + paclitaxel 175 mg/m², day 1 Q3W) vs the same bevacizumab + platinum–paclitaxel alone; treatment to progression or toxicity Progression-free survival Atezolizumab improved PFS (13.7 vs 10.4 months, HR 0.62) and OS (32.1 vs 22.8 months, HR 0.68); a bevacizumab-containing chemo-immunotherapy option regardless of PD-L1.

records.title: COMPASSION-16
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — first-line chemo-immunotherapy · III · 2024
records.body: Untreated persistent, recurrent, or metastatic cervical cancer (China; regardless of PD-L1) Cadonilimab (PD-1/CTLA-4 bispecific) + platinum chemotherapy +/- bevacizumab vs placebo + chemotherapy +/- bevacizumab Progression-free and overall survival (dual) At prespecified interim analyses, cadonilimab improved PFS (12.7 vs 8.1 months, stratified HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.49–0.80, p<0.0001 against a boundary of 0.0005) and OS (not reached vs 22.8 months, HR 0.64, 0.48–0.86, p=0.0011 against 0.006), the OS interim firing at 193 of the 290 deaths required for the final analysis. Bevacizumab was optional and used by 60%; the trial reports both strata with no interaction test — without bevacizumab PFS HR 0.46 (0.32–0.66) and OS 0.50 (0.33–0.75), with bevacizumab 0.81 (0.58–1.13) and 0.84 (0.56–1.26) — and the authors conclude benefit “regardless of the use of bevacizumab”, speculating only that it might suit those not eligible for it. No treatment-by-PD-L1 interaction test is reported either, so PD-L1 consistency is directional only. Conducted wholly in China; adverse events led to discontinuation in 28% vs 11%. At publication the NMPA approval covered cadonilimab monotherapy at second line or later, not this first-line combination.

records.title: KEYNOTE-158 (Chung)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · II · 2019
records.body: Previously treated advanced cervical cancer (cervical cohort) Single-arm pembrolizumab monotherapy Objective response rate ORR 14.3% overall and 14.6% in PD-L1+ (CPS ≥1) tumors with durable responses; led to accelerated approval for PD-L1+ pretreated disease.

records.title: EMPOWER-Cervical 1 (GOG-3016)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · III · 2022
records.body: Recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer after first-line platinum Cemiplimab vs investigator's-choice single-agent chemotherapy Overall survival Cemiplimab improved OS (12.0 vs 8.5 months, HR 0.69) regardless of PD-L1 or histology; validated checkpoint blockade as a second-line standard.

records.title: innovaTV 204 (GOG-3023/ENGOT-cx6)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · II · 2021
records.body: Previously treated recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer Single-arm tisotumab vedotin (tissue factor-directed ADC) Objective response rate Confirmed ORR 24% (7% complete) with median DOR 8.3 months; supported accelerated approval of the first ADC in cervical cancer.

records.title: innovaTV 301 (ENGOT-cx12)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · III · 2024
records.body: Recurrent/metastatic cervical cancer after 1-2 prior lines Tisotumab vedotin (tissue factor-directed ADC) 2.0 mg/kg IV Q3W vs investigator's-choice single-agent chemotherapy (topotecan, vinorelbine, gemcitabine, irinotecan, or pemetrexed); to progression Overall survival Tisotumab vedotin improved OS (11.5 vs 9.5 months, HR 0.70) and PFS (4.2 vs 2.9 months); confirmatory phase 3 converting accelerated to full approval.

records.title: CheckMate 358 (Oaknin)
records.subtitle: Cervical Cancer · Recurrent/metastatic — second-line immunotherapy & ADCs · I-II · 2024
records.body: Recurrent or metastatic squamous cell cervical carcinoma, ≤2 prior systemic therapies (first- and later-line) Nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W (monotherapy); or nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV Q2W + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg IV Q6W; or nivolumab 1 mg/kg IV Q3W + ipilimumab 3 mg/kg IV Q3W ×4 → nivolumab 240 mg IV Q2W; treatment to progression, toxicity, or 24 months Investigator-assessed objective response rate Multicohort phase 1–2 trial (176 treated of 193 enrolled; 90 randomised between the two combination regimens): objective response rate 26% (5/19) with nivolumab monotherapy, 31% (14/45) with NIVO3+IPI1, and 38% (43/112) with pooled NIVO1+IPI3 (40% in the randomised NIVO1+IPI3 group), with durable responses seen regardless of PD-L1 status. Serious treatment-related AEs were 16%, 27%, and 42% respectively, with one treatment-related death (immune-mediated colitis). Signal-generating support for chemotherapy-free dual immunotherapy; no randomised comparator arm, so hypothesis-generating rather than practice-defining.

records.title: EORTC 55971 (Vergote)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · III · 2010
records.body: FIGO IIIC–IV invasive epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube carcinoma confirmed by biopsy or qualified FNA with another primary excluded; WHO PS 0–2; no disabling disease precluding cytoreduction or platinum chemotherapy Primary debulking surgery → at least 6 courses of platinum chemotherapy, with interval debulking permitted after incomplete cytoreduction for response/stable disease vs 3 courses of neoadjuvant platinum chemotherapy → interval debulking for response/stable disease → at least 3 further courses Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, quality of life, adverse effects Neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by interval debulking was noninferior to primary surgery for OS in the ITT population (30 vs 29 mo; HR 0.98, 90% CI 0.84–1.13); PFS was 12 mo in both groups. Postoperative mortality was descriptively lower after neoadjuvant treatment (0.7% vs 2.5%), but surgical groups were unequal

records.title: CHORUS (Kehoe)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · III · 2015
records.body: FIGO 1988 stage III–IV ovarian, fallopian-tube, or primary peritoneal cancer with a pelvic mass and extrapelvic disease; fit for surgery and chemotherapy; CA125:CEA >25 or gastrointestinal primary excluded Primary debulking surgery → 6 cycles of q3w carboplatin-based chemotherapy vs 3 cycles of q3w carboplatin-based chemotherapy → delayed surgery → 3 further cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, quality of life, adverse events Primary chemotherapy was noninferior to primary surgery for OS (24.1 vs 22.6 mo; HR 0.87, upper one-sided 90% CI 0.98 below the 1.18 boundary). PFS was similar. Postoperative grade 3–4 events (14% vs 24%) and 28-day mortality (<1% vs 6%) were lower after primary chemotherapy

records.title: SCORPION (Fagotti)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · III · 2020
records.body: FIGO IIIC–IV epithelial ovarian cancer, age 18–75 years, chemotherapy-naive and fit for surgery/chemotherapy; high tumour load at laparoscopy (Predictive Index 8–12), resectable metastases and no mesenteric retraction Primary debulking surgery → 6 cycles of carboplatin/paclitaxel (q3w option: carboplatin AUC5 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m²; weekly option also permitted) vs 3–4 cycles of the same regimen → interval debulking for stable/responding disease → chemotherapy to 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival, major perioperative morbidity. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life In high-tumour-load disease, neoadjuvant chemotherapy did not improve PFS (14 vs 15 mo; HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.77–1.44) or OS. It increased R0 resection (67.0% vs 47.6%) and reduced early major postoperative complications (9.5% vs 46.4%) and postoperative deaths (0 vs 7/84)

records.title: LION (Harter)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · III · 2019
records.body: FIGO IIB–IV epithelial ovarian cancer, age 18–75 years, ECOG 0–1, feasible macroscopically complete resection and clinically normal nodes; stage IV only with resectable pleural, liver, splenic, or abdominal-wall metastases Systematic pelvic and para-aortic lymphadenectomy after macroscopically complete cytoreduction vs no lymphadenectomy after macroscopically complete cytoreduction Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, quality of life, number of resected lymph nodes Systematic lymphadenectomy did not improve OS (65.5 vs 69.2 mo; HR 1.06, 95% CI 0.83–1.34) or PFS (25.5 mo in both groups) after complete resection with clinically normal nodes. It increased 60-day mortality (3.1% vs 0.9%) and repeat laparotomy (12.4% vs 6.5%)

records.title: JCOG0602 (Onda)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Primary surgery — debulking extent & chemotherapy timing · III · 2016
records.body: Clinically diagnosed FIGO 1988 stage III–IV ovarian, tubal, or peritoneal cancer, age 20–75 years, ECOG PS 0–3; cytology without diagnostic surgery; CA-125 >200 U/mL and CEA <20 ng/mL used to exclude digestive-tract origin; suspected breast or gastrointestinal primary excluded Primary debulking surgery → paclitaxel 175 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC6 q3w for 8 cycles vs 4 cycles of paclitaxel 175 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC6 q3w → interval debulking unless progression → 4 further cycles Primary: overall survival. Secondary: adverse events, frequency and duration of surgery, blood loss, blood/plasma/albumin infusions Neoadjuvant therapy reduced treatment invasiveness: fewer surgeries (0.86 vs 1.32 per patient), lower blood-plus-ascites loss (629 vs 3610 mL), and fewer grade 3–4 postoperative events after main surgery (4.6% vs 15.6%). This report contains no overall-survival result; its planned noninferiority analysis was later

records.title: GOG-0213 (Coleman)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Secondary cytoreductive surgery (platinum-sensitive relapse) · III · 2019
records.body: First platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian cancer after complete response to ≥3 first-line platinum cycles; disease-free interval ≥6 months; investigator-judged completely resectable disease; excluded diffuse carcinomatosis, ascites, extra-abdominal disease, or surgical unfitness Secondary cytoreductive surgery → 6 cycles of investigator-selected q3w platinum chemotherapy, with or without bevacizumab maintenance until progression/toxicity/withdrawal vs the same chemotherapy and optional maintenance Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, quality of life, physical functioning, surgical morbidity and mortality, treatment-related adverse events In investigator-selected resectable platinum-sensitive recurrence, secondary cytoreduction did not improve OS (50.6 vs 64.7 mo; HR 1.29, 95% CI 0.97–1.72) at a futility-released 197-death analysis. Secondary PFS was numerically longer (18.9 vs 16.2 mo; HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.66–1.01); complete resection occurred in 67% of operated patients

records.title: DESKTOP III (Harter/Du Bois)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Secondary cytoreductive surgery (platinum-sensitive relapse) · III · 2021
records.body: First platinum-sensitive relapse of epithelial ovarian cancer ≥6 months after first-line platinum, with positive AGO score: ECOG 0, complete initial resection and ascites <500 mL; CA-125 elevation alone was insufficient Secondary cytoreductive surgery → physician's-choice platinum chemotherapy vs physician's-choice platinum chemotherapy alone Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, quality of life, complete resection as prognostic factor, surgical complications up to 60 days In AGO-score-selected platinum-sensitive relapse, secondary cytoreduction improved OS (53.7 vs 46.0 mo; HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.59–0.96) and secondary PFS (18.4 vs 14.0 mo; HR 0.66, 95% CI 0.54–0.82). Complete resection was achieved in 75.5% of operated patients; 15.9% assigned no surgery crossed over after a later relapse

records.title: SOC-1 (Shi)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Secondary cytoreductive surgery (platinum-sensitive relapse) · III · 2021
records.body: First platinum-sensitive epithelial ovarian cancer relapse ≥6 months after first-line platinum and no more than 1 prior chemotherapy line, with complete resection predicted by iMODEL plus PET-CT; patients with iMODEL >4.7 and CA-125 >105 U/mL could enter by central PET-CT consensus Secondary cytoreductive surgery → 6 cycles of q3w paclitaxel/docetaxel plus carboplatin, with 2–3 additional cycles for partial response and optional bevacizumab/PARP inhibitor maintenance vs the same systemic treatment Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: treatment-free survival, safety, quality of life, iMODEL validation, compliance, subsequent anticancer therapy In iMODEL/PET-CT-selected platinum-sensitive first relapse, secondary cytoreduction improved PFS (17.4 vs 11.9 mo; HR 0.58, 95% CI 0.45–0.74). OS was interim (58.1 vs 53.9 mo; HR 0.82, 95% CI 0.57–1.19) and did not cross its prespecified boundary; crossover in the no-surgery group limits OS interpretation

records.title: GOG 111 (McGuire)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 1996
records.body: Stage III epithelial ovarian cancer with >1 cm residual disease after surgery or stage IV disease; no prior ovarian cancer chemotherapy; GOG PS 0–2 Cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m² plus cisplatin 75 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles vs paclitaxel 135 mg/m² over 24 h → cisplatin 75 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles progression-free survival, overall survival, clinical response, pathological response, toxicity Paclitaxel/cisplatin improved PFS (18 vs 13 mo; RR 0.7, 95% CI 0.5–0.8) and OS (38 vs 24 mo; RR 0.6, 95% CI 0.5–0.8) in the eligible randomized population. Clinical response among measurable disease was 73% vs 60%. Severe neutropenia, febrile neutropenia, alopecia and neuropathy were more frequent with paclitaxel/cisplatin

records.title: GOG 158 (Ozols)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2003
records.body: Optimally resected stage III epithelial ovarian cancer with no residual nodule >1 cm; no prior ovarian cancer chemotherapy; GOG PS 0–2 Cisplatin 75 mg/m² plus paclitaxel 135 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles vs carboplatin AUC7.5 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: toxicity, second-look laparotomy results Carboplatin/paclitaxel was noninferior to cisplatin/paclitaxel for PFS (20.7 vs 19.4 mo; RR 0.88, 95% CI 0.75–1.03), with OS 57.4 vs 48.7 mo (RR 0.84, 95% CI 0.70–1.02). Carboplatin increased grade 3–4 thrombocytopenia (19%/20% vs 3%/2%), whereas cisplatin increased gastrointestinal, metabolic and genitourinary toxicity

records.title: GOG 172 (Armstrong)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2006
records.body: Previously untreated stage III epithelial ovarian or primary peritoneal carcinoma after primary surgery with residual disease ≤1 cm; GOG PS 0–2 Paclitaxel 135 mg/m² IV over 24 h day 1 → cisplatin 75 mg/m² IV day 2 q3w for 6 cycles vs paclitaxel 135 mg/m² IV over 24 h day 1 → cisplatin 100 mg/m² IP day 2 plus paclitaxel 60 mg/m² IP day 8 q3w for 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: quality of life Intraperitoneal therapy improved PFS (23.8 vs 18.3 mo; RR 0.80, 95% CI 0.64–1.00) and OS (65.6 vs 49.7 mo; RR 0.75, 95% CI 0.58–0.97) among eligible patients. Only 42% received all assigned IP therapy; grade 3–4 gastrointestinal, neurologic, fatigue, metabolic, pain and infection events were more common, and 9 treatment-related deaths occurred (5 IP, 4 IV)

records.title: JGOG 3016 (Katsumata)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2009
records.body: Previously untreated FIGO II–IV epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary peritoneal cancer; ECOG 0–3; low-malignant-potential tumours and recent/active other malignancy excluded Paclitaxel 180 mg/m² IV over 3 h plus carboplatin AUC6 IV day 1 q3w for 6 cycles vs paclitaxel 80 mg/m² IV over 1 h days 1, 8 and 15 plus carboplatin AUC6 IV day 1 q3w for 6 cycles; 3 additional cycles for measurable-disease CR/PR after 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, response rate, adverse events Dose-dense paclitaxel improved PFS (28.0 vs 17.2 mo; HR 0.71, 95% CI 0.58–0.88) in eligible ITT patients. Three-year OS was 72.1% vs 65.1% (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.57–0.98), but OS was a secondary interim analysis. Grade 3–4 anaemia was more frequent (69% vs 44%), and toxicity caused more discontinuations

records.title: MITO-7 (Pignata)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2014
records.body: Chemotherapy-naive FIGO IC–IV epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary peritoneal cancer after initial surgery/staging; ECOG ≤2; excluded clinically relevant heart disease, contraindicating disorders, prior chemotherapy, or other malignancy Carboplatin AUC6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles vs carboplatin AUC2 plus paclitaxel 60 mg/m² weekly for 18 weeks Primary: progression-free survival, quality of life. Secondary: overall survival, toxic effects, objective response Weekly treatment did not improve PFS (18.3 vs 17.3 mo; HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.80–1.16); interim 24-month OS was also not improved. It produced more favourable quality-of-life trajectories and reduced grade 3–4 neutropenia (42% vs 50%), febrile neutropenia (0.5% vs 3%), thrombocytopenia (1% vs 7%), grade ≥2 neuropathy (6% vs 17%) and grade 2 alopecia (29% vs 59%); 3 chemotherapy-attributed deaths occurred

records.title: GOG-262 (Chan)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2016
records.body: Newly diagnosed untreated incompletely resected stage III or stage IV epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube or primary peritoneal cancer; later stage II/III with residual lesions ≤1 cm permitted; GOG PS 0–2 Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC6 q3w for 6 cycles vs paclitaxel 80 mg/m² days 1, 8 and 15 plus carboplatin AUC6 day 1 q3w for 6 cycles; optional bevacizumab from cycle 2 until progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: quality of life, toxic effects, overall survival Weekly paclitaxel did not improve PFS overall (14.7 vs 14.0 mo; HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.74–1.06). Among the 16% who elected no bevacizumab, the randomized weekly comparison favoured PFS (14.2 vs 10.3 mo; HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.40–0.95), with interaction P=0.047; nonrandomized bevacizumab choice limits inference. Weekly therapy caused more grade 3–4 anaemia and grade 2–4 neuropathy but less neutropenia; 14 deaths were considered at least possibly treatment related (6 vs 8)

records.title: ICON8 (Clamp)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2019
records.body: FIGO IC–IV epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal or fallopian-tube cancer; stage IC/IIA required high-risk histology; ECOG 0–2; primary, delayed, or no surgery permitted Carboplatin AUC5/6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles vs carboplatin q3w plus paclitaxel 80 mg/m² days 1, 8 and 15 q3w for 6 cycles vs weekly carboplatin AUC2 plus paclitaxel 80 mg/m² days 1, 8 and 15 q3w for 6 cycles Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: quality of life, toxic effects Neither weekly dose-dense regimen improved PFS over q3w treatment; restricted mean PFS was 24.9 and 25.3 vs 24.4 mo, with median PFS 20.8 and 21.0 vs 17.7 mo. Grade 3–4 toxicity was higher with weekly schedules (62% and 53% vs 42%), and longitudinal quality of life favoured q3w treatment

records.title: ENGOT-OV43/GOG-3036/KEYLYNK-001
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line chemotherapy — regimen & route · III · 2026
records.body: Newly diagnosed epithelial ovarian (non-mucinous, non-borderline), primary peritoneal or fallopian tube cancer; FIGO stage III or IV, first-line, after primary debulking surgery (within 7 weeks before chemotherapy) or planned interval debulking; no BRCA1/2 mutation on central tumour testing, enrolled regardless of PD-L1 status (CPS ≥10 hypothesis-tested subgroup); excluding germ cell tumours, prior PARP inhibitor or immune checkpoint inhibitor, CNS metastases, active autoimmune disease Carboplatin + paclitaxel (or docetaxel) per local standard for five cycles (one lead-in cycle before randomisation) with IV pembrolizumab 200 mg every 3 weeks for 35 cycles → maintenance pembrolizumab + oral olaparib 300 mg twice daily vs same chemotherapy + pembrolizumab → pembrolizumab + placebo maintenance vs placebo + chemotherapy → placebo maintenance; olaparib/placebo until discontinuation or up to 2 years; optional bevacizumab at investigator discretion; treatment until planned cycles, radiographic progression or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, blinded independent central review-assessed progression-free survival, progression-free survival 2, time to first subsequent therapy, time to second subsequent therapy, time to discontinuation of treatment, pathological complete response, global health status/quality of life by EORTC QLQ-C30 and EORTC QLQ-OV28 (change from baseline, time to deterioration), safety Pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy followed by pembrolizumab–olaparib maintenance significantly improved PFS versus chemotherapy in newly diagnosed BRCA non-mutated stage III–IV epithelial ovarian cancer. First interim analysis (median follow-up 30·1 mo): median PFS 23·7 vs 15·2 mo in CPS ≥10 (HR 0·63) and 22·1 vs 14·6 mo in ITT (HR 0·68); final analysis (49·6 mo) HR 0·66 and 0·71. Pembrolizumab alone did not improve PFS (CPS ≥10 HR 0·95; p=0·33), so OS was not formally tested; no OS improvement in either experimental group (ITT HR 1·04 pembrolizumab–olaparib and 1·06 pembrolizumab vs control). The control arm had no PARP inhibitor, so the benefit of pembrolizumab beyond olaparib cannot be isolated. Grade ≥3 treatment-related AEs 66% vs 56% vs 51%; treatment-related deaths four (1%) with pembrolizumab–olaparib and one (<1%) with pembrolizumab.
records.keywords: Vergote et al. Lancet Oncol 2026 (online ahead of print)

records.title: GOG 218 (Burger)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line antiangiogenic therapy · III · 2011
records.body: Previously untreated, incompletely resectable stage III epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after maximal debulking, with residual disease >1 cm initially and residual disease ≤1 cm permitted after amendment, or stage IV disease; GOG PS 0–2; no intestinal obstruction or clinically significant vascular-event history Carboplatin AUC6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles plus placebo through cycle 22 vs chemotherapy plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w cycles 2–6 then placebo vs chemotherapy plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w cycles 2–22; stop for progression, toxicity, completion, or withdrawal Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life, adverse events Bevacizumab throughout chemotherapy and maintenance improved PFS versus control (14.1 vs 10.3 mo; HR 0.717, 95% CI 0.625–0.824), whereas initiation only did not. OS was not improved at this cut. Bevacizumab increased grade ≥2 hypertension (22.9% vs 7.2%), gastrointestinal-wall disruption and grade ≥3 proteinuria; fatal adverse events were reported without treatment-causality attribution

records.title: ICON7 (Perren)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line antiangiogenic therapy · III · 2011
records.body: High-risk early-stage (FIGO I–IIA clear-cell or grade 3) or FIGO IIB–IV epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after surgery; ECOG 0–2; no further surgery planned Carboplatin AUC5/6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles vs the same chemotherapy plus bevacizumab 7.5 mg/kg IV q3w for 5–6 cycles → 12 additional cycles or until progression Primary: progression-free survival, overall survival. Secondary: biologic progression-free interval, response, toxicity, quality of life Bevacizumab modestly prolonged first-line PFS by 36-month restricted mean (21.8 vs 20.3 mo; difference 1.5 mo, 95% CI 0.1–2.9); the conventional HR was not meaningful because hazards were nonproportional. Updated OS was immature and not improved. Bevacizumab increased grade ≥2 hypertension (18% vs 2%), grade ≥3 thromboembolism (7% vs 3%), gastrointestinal perforation and treatment-related/treatment-and-disease deaths

records.title: SOLO-1 (Moore)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · III · 2018
records.body: Newly diagnosed FIGO III–IV high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer with germline or somatic BRCA1/2 mutation and complete/partial response after platinum chemotherapy without bevacizumab Olaparib tablets 300 mg orally twice daily until investigator-assessed progression; stop at 2 years if no evidence of disease, with blinded continuation permitted for partial response vs matching placebo on the same rule Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: second progression-free survival, overall survival, time to first and second subsequent therapy or death, quality of life Maintenance olaparib markedly prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.23–0.41; 3-year freedom from progression/death 60% vs 27%) in BRCA-mutated disease. OS was interim at 21% maturity. Anaemia was more common (grade 3–4, 22% vs 2%); AML occurred in 3/260 olaparib recipients, all >30 days after treatment ended

records.title: PRIMA (González-Martín)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · III · 2019
records.body: Newly diagnosed high-risk FIGO III–IV high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian, peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after response to first-line platinum; stage III required visible residual disease after primary debulking or inoperability, and neoadjuvant chemotherapy was permitted Niraparib orally once daily in 28-day cycles for 36 months or until progression; 300 mg initially, amended to 200 mg for baseline weight <77 kg or platelets <150,000/mm³ vs matched placebo on the same duration rule Primary: progression-free survival in HRD population, progression-free survival in overall population. Secondary: overall survival, time to first subsequent therapy, second progression-free survival, quality of life, safety Niraparib prolonged centrally reviewed PFS in HRD disease (21.9 vs 10.4 mo; HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.31–0.59) and overall (13.8 vs 8.2 mo; HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.50–0.76). OS was immature at 79 deaths. Grade ≥3 anaemia, thrombocytopenia and neutropenia were 31.0%, 28.7% and 12.8% vs 1.6%, 0.4% and 1.2%; adverse events caused dose reduction in 70.9% vs 8.2% and discontinuation in 12.0% vs 2.5%. An individualized starting dose was added during the study

records.title: PAOLA-1 (Ray-Coquard)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · III · 2019
records.body: Adults with newly diagnosed FIGO III–IV high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer, or other nonmucinous epithelial ovarian cancer with deleterious germline BRCA1/2 mutation; no evidence of disease or complete/partial response after platinum–taxane plus bevacizumab Olaparib 300 mg orally twice daily for up to 24 months plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV q3w for up to 15 months total, until progression, toxicity or other discontinuation vs matching placebo plus bevacizumab on the same duration rules Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, second progression-free survival, time to first subsequent therapy, quality of life, safety Adding olaparib to bevacizumab maintenance improved PFS overall (22.1 vs 16.6 mo; HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.49–0.72). The prespecified HRD-positive subgroup also had longer PFS (37.2 vs 17.7 mo; HR 0.33), but no interaction test established differential benefit; a post hoc HRD-negative-or-unknown analysis did not establish benefit (HR 0.92, 95% CI 0.72–1.17). Grade ≥3 anaemia was 17% vs <1%, and MDS/AML/aplastic anaemia occurred in 1% vs <1%; quality of life was maintained

records.title: ATHENA-MONO (Monk)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · III · 2022
records.body: Newly diagnosed stage III–IV high-grade epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after response to platinum doublet; R0 resection was permitted Rucaparib 600 mg orally twice daily from cycle 1 day 1 vs placebo; each in 28-day cycles with IV placebo q4w from cycle 2 day 1, until 24 months after IV-placebo initiation, progression, death, or unacceptable toxicity Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, objective response, duration of response, quality of life, safety Rucaparib improved investigator-assessed PFS in the ITT population (20.2 vs 9.2 mo; HR 0.52, 95% CI 0.40–0.68) and HRD-positive disease. OS data were immature. Grade ≥3 anaemia and neutropenia were more common, and treatment interruption/reduction was frequent

records.title: DUO-O
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · First-line maintenance — PARP inhibitors · III · 2026
records.body: Treatment-naive, newly diagnosed FIGO III–IV high-grade epithelial ovarian, primary peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer lacking a deleterious or suspected deleterious tumour BRCA mutation; planned platinum chemotherapy plus bevacizumab after upfront surgery or before interval debulking Carboplatin AUC5–6 plus paclitaxel 175 mg/m² q3w for 6 cycles with bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w → bevacizumab to 15 months vs the same plus durvalumab 1120 mg IV q3w → durvalumab to 24 months plus bevacizumab to 15 months vs the same plus durvalumab → durvalumab and olaparib 300 mg twice daily to 24 months plus bevacizumab to 15 months Primary: progression-free survival for durvalumab plus olaparib vs control in non-tBRCAm HRD-positive disease and the non-tBRCAm ITT population. Secondary: progression-free survival for durvalumab vs control, overall survival, progression-free survival 2, quality of life, safety Durvalumab without olaparib did not improve PFS versus control (20.6 vs 19.3 mo; HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.73–1.04). Durvalumab plus olaparib improved primary PFS in non-tBRCAm HRD-positive disease (37.3 vs 23.0 mo; HR 0.49) and the non-tBRCAm ITT comparison (24.2 vs 19.3 mo; HR 0.63). Interim ITT OS was formally tested and did not meet its criterion; no further testing occurred. Grade ≥3 events were 72% vs 62%, and one death was attributed to olaparib-related AML

records.title: Study 19 (Ledermann)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · II · 2012
records.body: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian, fallopian-tube, or primary-peritoneal cancer with high-grade serous features or a serous component after ≥2 platinum courses and complete/partial response to the latest regimen Olaparib capsules 400 mg orally twice daily continuously until progression vs placebo continuously until progression Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: time to progression, objective response, disease control, overall survival, quality of life, safety Olaparib maintenance prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (8.4 vs 4.8 mo; HR 0.35, 95% CI 0.25–0.49), with no evidence of treatment-effect heterogeneity across prespecified subgroups (global interaction P=0.15). Interim OS at 38% maturity was 29.7 vs 29.9 mo (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.63–1.39). Grade 3–4 adverse events were 35.3% vs 20.3%, with more nausea, fatigue, vomiting and anaemia

records.title: SOLO-2 (Pujade-Lauraine)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · III · 2017
records.body: Platinum-sensitive relapsed high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after ≥2 prior platinum lines and response to the latest; predicted/suspected deleterious BRCA1/2 mutation required and prior PARP inhibitor excluded; all randomized patients were germline BRCA-mutated Olaparib tablets 300 mg orally twice daily until disease progression or loss of benefit vs placebo until disease progression or investigator-determined loss of benefit Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, time to first and second subsequent therapy, time to treatment discontinuation, second progression-free survival, earliest progression or death, quality of life, safety Olaparib prolonged investigator-assessed PFS (19.1 vs 5.5 mo; HR 0.30, 95% CI 0.22–0.41). Final OS was 51.7 vs 38.8 mo (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.54–1.00) and missed its prespecified threshold; subsequent PARP inhibitor use was 10% vs 38%. At final follow-up, grade ≥3 anaemia was 21% vs 2% and MDS/AML 8% vs 4% (post-hoc RR 2.03, 95% CI 0.70–5.91). Fatal treatment-emergent events within the 30-day safety window were 4% vs 0, including six treatment-related MDS/AML deaths; later adverse-event deaths occurred in both arms
records.keywords: Lancet Oncol 2017;18:1274-1284   Lancet Oncol 2021;22:620-631 final OS analysis 33743851

records.title: NOVA (ENGOT-OV16, Mirza)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · III · 2016
records.body: Platinum-sensitive recurrent ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer with predominantly high-grade serous histology after ≥2 platinum regimens; progression >6 months after the penultimate platinum and complete/partial response to the latest; germline-BRCA and non-germline-BRCA cohorts Niraparib 300 mg orally once daily in continuous 28-day cycles until progression, unacceptable toxicity, death, consent withdrawal, or loss to follow-up vs placebo on the same rule Primary: progression-free survival in germline BRCA-mutated and non-germline-BRCA cohorts. Secondary: chemotherapy-free interval, time to first and second subsequent therapy, second progression-free survival, overall survival, quality of life, safety Niraparib prolonged PFS in germline BRCA-mutated disease (21.0 vs 5.5 mo; HR 0.27), HRD-positive non-germline-BRCA disease (12.9 vs 3.8 mo; HR 0.38), and the overall non-germline-BRCA cohort (9.3 vs 3.9 mo; HR 0.45). OS and time to second subsequent therapy were immature. Grade 3–4 events occurred in 74.1% vs 22.9%; follow-up recorded three MDS/AML deaths, including one investigator-assessed treatment-related death in each arm

records.title: ARIEL3 (Coleman)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · III · 2017
records.body: Platinum-sensitive recurrent high-grade serous or endometrioid ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after ≥2 prior platinum regimens; complete/partial response to the latest and progression >6 months after the penultimate platinum; latest platinum doublet ≥4 cycles required after amendment Rucaparib 600 mg orally twice daily until progression, death, toxicity, withdrawal, or study end vs placebo on the same rule Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: overall survival, quality of life, objective response, safety, population pharmacokinetics Rucaparib prolonged investigator-assessed PFS in BRCA-mutated (16.6 vs 5.4 mo; HR 0.23), HRD (13.6 vs 5.4 mo; HR 0.32), and ITT populations (10.8 vs 5.4 mo; HR 0.36). In the BRCA-mutated population, time to worsening in FOSI-18 disease-related symptoms did not differ (HR 1.24, 95% CI 0.82–1.86), stopping formal testing before immature OS. Grade ≥3 events were 56% vs 15%; fatal treatment-emergent events were 6 vs 2, including two treatment-related MDS/AML deaths with rucaparib

records.title: OReO/ENGOT-ov38
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — PARP maintenance (platinum-sensitive) · III · 2023
records.body: Platinum-sensitive relapsed non-mucinous epithelial ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after ≥2 platinum lines, response to ≥4-cycle latest platinum without bevacizumab, and one prior PARP inhibitor; BRCAm prior-PARP duration ≥18 months first-line or ≥12 months later-line, non-BRCAm ≥12 or ≥6 months Olaparib tablets 300 mg orally twice daily, or 250 mg twice daily if prior 300-mg intolerance, until objective radiological progression or while clinical benefit continued vs placebo on the same rule Primary: progression-free survival in BRCAm and non-BRCAm cohorts. Secondary: time to first and second subsequent therapy, overall survival, quality of life, safety Olaparib rechallenge modestly prolonged PFS in the separately randomized BRCAm cohort (4.3 vs 2.8 mo; HR 0.57, 95% CI 0.37–0.87) and non-BRCAm cohort (5.3 vs 2.8 mo; HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.26–0.71). Final BRCAm OS was 20.1 vs 20.9 mo (HR 0.88, 95% CI 0.52–1.53); non-BRCAm OS was truncated at 21% deaths with no further evaluation planned. Grade ≥3 events were 15% vs 5% and 21% vs 8% in the respective cohorts, with no fatal adverse events

records.title: OCEANS (Aghajanian)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · III · 2012
records.body: Measurable platinum-sensitive recurrent epithelial ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer progressing ≥6 months after frontline platinum; no prior chemotherapy for recurrence and no prior bevacizumab or other VEGF-pathway therapy Carboplatin AUC4 day 1 plus gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² days 1 and 8 q3w for 6 cycles, extendable to 10 with continued response, plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w → bevacizumab until progression/toxicity vs placebo plus the same chemotherapy → placebo on the same rule Primary: progression-free survival. Secondary: objective response, duration of response, overall survival, safety Adding bevacizumab improved PFS (12.4 vs 8.4 mo; HR 0.484, 95% CI 0.388–0.605) and objective response. At the second interim analysis, OS was 33.3 vs 35.2 mo (HR 1.027, 95% CI 0.792–1.331) with high censoring beyond 18 months. Grade ≥3 hypertension was 17.4% vs 0.4% and proteinuria 8.5% vs 0.9%; two delayed gastrointestinal perforations occurred, and one fatal adverse event occurred in each safety arm

records.title: GOG-0213 bevacizumab (Coleman)
records.subtitle: Ovarian Cancer · Recurrent — antiangiogenics & antibody-drug conjugates · III · 2017
records.body: Recurrent measurable/evaluable epithelial ovarian, primary-peritoneal, or fallopian-tube cancer after complete response to ≥3 first-line platinum cycles and disease-free interval ≥6 months; no more than one prior chemotherapy regimen; surgical-objective participation was separately randomized in a subset Paclitaxel 175 mg/m² plus carboplatin AUC5 IV q3w for 6 planned cycles, with up to 2 extra cycles for response, plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg q3w → bevacizumab until progression/toxicity vs the same chemotherapy alone Primary: overall survival. Secondary: progression-free survival, carboplatin/paclitaxel hypersensitivity, quality of life, objective response, safety The primary ITT OS comparison missed its criterion (42.2 vs 37.3 mo; HR 0.829, 95% CI 0.683–1.005); a post-hoc correction of misclassified platinum-free intervals gave HR 0.823 (95% CI 0.680–0.996).
